Second: [the lām] has its proper sense of cause, and the object of «سَمَّاعون» is omitted, i.e. listening much to your news and your talk in order to lie about it by adding, subtracting and altering — such as spreading alarming rumours that the believers had been killed in the raiding parties, as is reported of their disgraceful deeds.

His saying: {سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ}: this may be a repetition of the first; on this view His saying «لقوم» may be attached to the lie itself, i.e. they listen in order to lie for the sake of a people. The lām may also be attached to «سَمَّاعون» itself, i.e. listening much on behalf of a people who have not come to you, because out of their hatred they do not approach your assembly — and they are the Jews. «لم يأتوك» is in the position of the genitive because it is an adjective of «قوم».

His saying: {يُحَرِّفُونَ}: it may be an adjective of «سَمَّاعون», i.e. listeners who distort; it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «سَمَّاعون»; it may be resumptive with no position; it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they distort"; and it may be in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «قوم», i.e. "for a people who distort." «من بعد مواضعِه» I have treated thoroughly in al-Nisāʾ. «يقولون» is like «يحرفون», and it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «يحرفون». The conditional sentence in His saying {إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ} is the object of the saying; «هذا» is the second object of «أوتيتم», and the first stands in place of the agent. The fāʾ is [that of] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is obligatory because the apodosis is not fit to be a protasis; likewise the sentence in His saying {وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ}. In His saying {وَمَن يُرِدِ}, «مَنْ» is a fronted object, and it is conditional. His saying {فَلَن تَمْلِكَ} is its apodosis, and the fāʾ is likewise obligatory for the reason given. «شيئاً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or a maṣdar. «من الله» is attached to «تملكَ»; it is also said to be a ḥāl from «شيئاً», because it was originally its adjective. His saying {أولئك} is a mubtadaʾ, and {لَمْ يُرِدِ الله} is a verbal clause that is its khabar.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: {سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ}: it may be repeated for emphasis if it describes the hypocrites, and not repeated if it describes the Children of Israel. The parsing of its individual words was given above. It is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of a concealed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are listeners," and likewise «أكَّالون». In «للسحتِ», the lām admits the two views mentioned in His saying «للكذب».

«السَّحْتُ» is what is unlawful. It was so called because it removes blessing and effaces it. One says «سَحَته الله» and «أسحته», i.e. He destroyed it and did away with it. His saying, Exalted is He, {فَيُسْحِتَكُم} [Ṭā Hā: 61] has been read in both ways, from «سحته» and «أسحته». al-Farazdaq said:

1730 - وعضُّ زمانٍ يابنَ مروانَ لم يَدَعْ ... من المالِ إلا مُسْحَتاً أو مُجَلَّفُ
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, which left of wealth nothing but what is wiped out or what is barely remaining.)

[Translator's note: the source prints «إى» in the verse; the well-known wording is «إلا».] It is reported from al-Farrāʾ: "السُّحْت is the ravening of hunger," and this goes back to [the sense of] destruction.

Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read «السُّحْت» with a ḍamma on the sīn and a sukūn on the ḥāʾ; the rest with a ḍamma on both. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Khārija ibn Muṣʿab from Nāfiʿ, read it with a fatḥa and a sukūn on the ḥāʾ; ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr with a kasra and sukūn; and it has been read with two fatḥas. The two ḍammas are a noun for the thing destroyed; the ḍamma with sukūn is a lightening of this original form; the two fatḥas, and the kasra with sukūn, are also nouns for it. As for the form with a fatḥa on the sīn and sukūn on the ḥāʾ, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meant in the sense of the passive participle, like «الصيد» (hunting) in the sense of «المصيد» (game). It may also be a lightening of the form with [two] fatḥas, but this is weak.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ}: like His saying {كَيْفَ تُحْيِي الموتى} [al-Baqara: 260], which has been discussed. His saying: {وَعِنْدَهُمُ التوراة}: the wāw is circumstantial. «التوراة» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the adverb as its khabar (predicate); or the adverb may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) and «التوراة» its agent, because it depends on the one to whom the ḥāl refers. The nominal or verbal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. In His saying {فِيهَا حُكْمُ الله}, «فيها» is a fronted khabar and «حكم» a mubtadaʾ or an agent, as stated for «التوراة»; the clause is a ḥāl from «التوراة», or [only] the preposition and its noun are. «حكم» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it have no grammatical position, but be explanatory, [showing] that they have with them what makes them independent of seeking [your] judgement, as you say: "You have Zayd, who advises you and counsels you rightly; so what do you want with anyone else?" His saying {ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ} is conjoined to «يحكِّمونك», so it falls within the context of wonderment understood from «كيف».

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فِيهَا هُدًى}: it admits the two views mentioned on His saying {وَعِنْدَهُمُ التوراة}: «هُدَى» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) or an agent, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «التوراة». His saying {يَحْكُمُ بِهَا} may be a resumptive clause, or it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, either from the pronoun in «فيها» or from «التوراة». His saying {الذين أَسْلَمُواْ} is an adjective of «النبيون». He described them thus by way of praise and commendation, not by way of distinguishing, for all the prophets are Muslims [submitters]; He praised them with it only in the way attributes are applied to the names of Allah the Exalted. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is applied to the prophets by way of praise, like the attributes applied to the Eternal, Glorified is He, not to distinguish and clarify. By applying it, an allusion to the Jews is intended, [namely] that they are far from the religion of Islam, which is the religion of all the prophets of old and recent times, for the Jews are apart from it; and His saying {الذين أَسْلَمُواْ لِلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ} proclaims this," i.e. is proof of what he claimed.

His saying: {لِلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ}: there are three views on this lām. The most evident: it is attached to «يحكم», and on this view its meaning is specification, and it covers both the one for whom judgement is given and the one against whom it is given. For this reason some claimed that there is an ellipsis in the speech, its implied form being: "The prophets judge by it for those who are Jews and against them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others mentioned this. Second: it is attached to «أنزلنا», i.e. "We sent down the Torah for those who are Jews, the prophets judging by it." Third: it is attached to «هُدى» itself, i.e. "guidance and light for those who are Jews"; this involves separating the maṣdar from what it governs. On this view «للذين هادوا» may also be an adjective of «هدى ونور», i.e. guidance and light existing for those who are Jews. The first of these views is the one intended.

His saying: {والربانيون}: conjoined to «النبيون», i.e. the rabbāniyyūn — whose explanation was given in Āl ʿImrān — also judge according to what is in the Torah. «الأحبار» is the plural of «حَبْر», with a fatḥa or kasra on the ḥāʾ, meaning a scholar. Abū al-Haytham rejected the kasra, and al-Farrāʾ the fatḥa; Abū ʿUbayd allowed both and chose the fatḥa. As for «الحِبْر» with which one writes (ink), it is with a kasra only. The root basically denotes beautification and delight; that with which one writes was called «حِبْر» because it beautifies the script, and it is also said: because of its leaving a trace. The first is supported by His saying, Exalted is He, {أَنتُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُكُمْ تُحْبَرُونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 70], i.e. you will rejoice and be adorned.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said that «الربانيون» is [nominative] by an omitted verb, i.e. 'and the rabbāniyyūn and the rabbis judge by what they were entrusted to preserve'." End of quote. He means that since what the judging is related to differs, the two verbs are also made different: the prophets judge by the Torah, while the rabbis and rabbāniyyūn judge by what Allah entrusted them to preserve. This is far from correct, because what Allah entrusted them to preserve is what the Torah requires, so the prophets and the rabbāniyyūn judge by one and the same thing. Moreover, it will be shown that the pronoun in «استُحْفِظوا» refers to the prophets and those after them.

His saying: {بِمَا استحفظوا}: Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed three views on it. First: «بما» is a badal (substitute) of His saying «بها», with repetition of the governor because of the long separation. He said: "It is permissible even if [the separation] is not long," i.e. the repetition of the governor in the badal is permissible even if it is not long. I say: and even if there is no separation at all. Second: it is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "and the rabbāniyyūn judge by what they were entrusted to preserve," as I quoted from him above. Third: it is an object, i.e. they judge by the Torah because of their being entrusted with its preservation. [Translator's note: the source says «مفعول به» here, though the explanation given is causal.] This last view is the one al-Zamakhsharī inclined to, for he said: "«بما استُحْفِظوا»: by what their prophets asked them to preserve of the Torah, i.e. because of their prophets' asking them to preserve it from alteration and change." This is on the basis that the pronoun refers to the rabbāniyyūn and the rabbis, not the prophets, for he assumed the omitted agent to be "the prophets." He also allowed the pronoun in «استُحْفِظوا» to refer to the prophets, the rabbāniyyūn and the rabbis, assuming the agent for which [the deputy] stands to be the Creator, Exalted is He, i.e. "by what Allah entrusted them to preserve," meaning by what He charged them to preserve.

His saying: {مِن كِتَابِ الله}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مِنْ» in «مِنْ كتاب الله» is for explanation," meaning that it explains the genus left vague in «بما». For «ما» may be a nominal relative meaning «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "by what they were entrusted to preserve," or it may be maṣdariyya, i.e. "by their being entrusted to preserve." Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl from one of two things: either from the relative «ما» or from its omitted returning pronoun; this is open to question as to the meaning. His saying «وكانوا» falls within the scope of the ṣila (relative clause), i.e. and by their being witnesses over it, i.e. watchers so that it is not altered. «عليه» is attached to «شهداء», and the pronoun in «عليه» refers to «كتاب الله»; it is also said: to the Messenger, i.e. witnesses to his prophethood and his mission; and it is also said: to the ruling. The first is the evident one.

semin-durr:105-105.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ}: the majority read «أنفسكم» in the accusative, and it is accusative by way of ighrāʾ (incitement) through «عليكم», because «عليكم» here is an ism fiʿl (verbal noun of command), the implied form being "keep to yourselves," i.e. to their guidance and their protection from what harms them. So «عليكم» here governs a fāʿil (agent) in the nominative, its implied form being "عليكم أنتم"; for that reason a nominative may be conjoined to it, as in «عليكم أنتم وزيدٌ الخيرَ» ("keep, you and Zayd, to the good"), as though you said: "keep, you and Zayd, to the good."

The grammarians disagreed about the pronoun attached to it and its sisters, such as «إليك», «لديك» and «مكانك». The correct view is that it is in the position of a genitive (majrūr), as it was before the word was transferred to ighrāʾ; this is the school of Sībawayh. Al-Akhfash argued for it by what he related from the Arabs: «على عبدِ الله» with «عبد الله» in the genitive, and that is decisive on the question. Al-Kisāʾī held that it is in the position of an accusative, and this is far-fetched because of the accusative of what comes after the two of them — I mean «على» and what follows it — as in this verse. Al-Farrāʾ held that it is in the position of a nominative. I have verified these schools with their proofs at length in "Sharḥ al-Tashīl".

Abū al-Baqāʾ said — after making «كم» in the position of a genitive governed by «على» —: "unlike «رُوَيدَكم», for the kāf there is for address and has no position, since «رويد» has been used for the imperative addressed to someone present without the kāf of address; and likewise His saying, Exalted is He, {مَكَانَكُمْ} [Yūnus: 28]: «كم» is in the position of a genitive." I say: there is long discussion on this question; the correct view is that «رويد» sometimes has what follows it in the position of a genitive and sometimes in the position of an accusative, and this is not its place. I have presented earlier, in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, the disagreement over the permissibility of placing the governed word of this category before it.

Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym read «أنفسُكم» in the nominative, according to what the author of "al-Kashshāf" related from him. It is problematic, and it is explained on one of two views. Either as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «عليكم» as its khabar (predicate) placed before it, the meaning still being that of ighrāʾ, since ighrāʾ has come in the form of a nominal clause; of this kind is the reading of some {ناقةُ الله وسُقْياها} [al-Shams: 13], and this is a warning (taḥdhīr), which is the counterpart of ighrāʾ. The second of the two views: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «عليكم», because, as stated earlier, it stands in the place of the verb; except that emphasizing it with «النفس» without emphasizing it with a detached pronoun is anomalous. On this view the object is omitted, its implied form being "keep, you yourselves, to the soundness of your state and your guidance."

His saying: {لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the doubled rāʾ. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read {لا يَضُرْكم} with ḍamma on the ḍād and sukūn on the rāʾ; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read {لا يَضِرْكم} with kasra on the ḍād and sukūn on the rāʾ; and Abū Ḥaywa read {لا يَضْرُرُكم} with sukūn on the ḍād and ḍamma on the first and second rāʾ.

As for the reading of the majority, it admits two views. The first: that the verb in it is jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the command in «عليكم», and the rāʾ was given ḍamma only in harmony with the ḍamma of the ḍād; and the ḍamma of the ḍād is the vowel of the first rāʾ, transferred to the ḍād for the sake of assimilating it into the rāʾ after it, the original being {لا يَضْرُرْكم}. And the jussive may be not by way of being the answer to the command, but by way of being a resumptive prohibition, the working of it being as stated. Supporting the permissibility of the jussive here, in both senses mentioned — answer and prohibition — are the readings of al-Ḥasan and al-Nakhaʿī, for both are explicit in the jussive, though they admit the jussive either as answer or as prohibition.

The second view: that the verb is indicative (marfūʿ), being neither an answer nor a prohibition, but resumptive, brought to give information of that; it is supported by the reading of Abū Ḥaywa mentioned above.

As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, it is from {ضارَه يَضُوره}, like «صانَه يصونه»; and the reading of al-Nakhaʿī is from {ضاره يضيره}, like «باعه يَبيعه»; and the jussive in both is according to the two views stated for the reading of the generality. Abū al-Baqāʾ related «لا يَضُرَّكم» with fatḥa on the rāʾ; its explanation is as a jussive, the fatḥa being for lightness, and that is clear, the jussive likewise being according to the two views stated. All of these are dialects to which attention was drawn earlier in Āl ʿImrān.

And {مَّن ضَلَّ} is the fāʿil (agent). And «إذا» is an adverb governed in the accusative by «يَضُرُّكم», i.e. "the one who has gone astray does not harm you at the time of your being guided." It may also be conditional, its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being omitted because the speech indicates it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is unlikely that it is an adverb of «ضَلَّ», because the meaning is not sound with it." I say: because the meaning would become a negation of the harm coming from one who goes astray at the time of their being guided, and it might then be imagined that it does not negate for them the harm of one who went astray at a time other than that of their being guided; but this does not negate the soundness of the meaning altogether, as he stated.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِنْ عُثِرَ}: passive (mabnī lil-mafʿūl), and what stands in place of its fāʿil (agent) is the preposition-phrase after it, i.e. "if it is discovered that the two of them deserved the sin". One says: [عَثَر الرجلُ يعثُر] عُثوراً when he comes upon something that no one else has discovered; and أعثرتُه على كذا means "I made him discover it"; from this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: {أَعْثَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ} [al-Kahf: 21]. The lexicographers said: "Its origin is from" عَثْرة الرجل "which is falling (stumbling); that is because the one who stumbles only stumbles over something he did not see; when he stumbles over it, he discovers it and looks at what it is. So every matter that was hidden and was then discovered was said to be:" عُثِر عليه ". Al-Layth said:" عَثَر يَعْثُر عُثوراً: he came upon a matter that no one else came upon; and عَثَر يَعْثُر عَثْرَةً: he fell upon something. So he distinguished the two verbs by their two maṣdars (verbal nouns). Abū al-Baqāʾ distinguished between them otherwise, saying: "عَثَر, whose maṣdar is العُثور, means 'he discovered'; as for" عَثَر "in one's walking, speech and opinion, its maṣdar is العِثار." Al-Rāghib made the two maṣdars equivalent, for he said: "عَثَر الرجلُ بالشيء يَعْثُر عُثوراً وعِيثاراً: when he falls upon it; it is used figuratively of one who discovers a matter without seeking it; one says:" عَثَرْتُ على كذا ", and His words: {وكذلك أَعْثَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ} [al-Kahf: 21] mean: We made them come upon them without their seeking it."

The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَآخَرَانِ}: there are four aspects concerning it. [The first]: that it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "then the two witnesses are two others"; the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, entering upon the nominal clause, and the clause {يقومان} is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of آخران. The second: that it is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "then let two others bear witness"; Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. It has already been stated that the verb is not omitted on its own except in places that I mentioned at His words: {حِينَ الوصية اثنان} [al-Māʾida: 106]. The third: that it is a fronted khabar, and «الأَوْلَيان» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the implied form being: "the two nearest in the affair of the deceased are two others who stand in their place"; Abū ʿAlī mentioned this. He said: "And it would be like your saying:" تميمي أنا (a Tamīmī am I) ". The fourth: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and in that case there are possibilities for the khabar. One of them: His words {مِنَ الذين استحق}; and beginning with it [an indefinite] is permitted because it is specified by the description, namely the clause» يَقُومان «. The second: that the khabar is» يَقُومان «and» من الذين استحَقَّ «is a description of the mubtadaʾ; separating the description from what it describes by the khabar does no harm, and what also permits beginning with it is its reliance on the fāʾ of the apodosis. Abū al-Baqāʾ said, when he reported its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ:" Beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted here because «benefit» (informativeness) is obtained ". If he means that what permits it is the mere benefit, without considering any of the permitting conditions that I have mentioned, then this is not conceded. The third: that the khabar is His words «الأَوْليَان»; Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it, and his words «يَقُومان» and «مِن الذين استَحَقَّ» are both in the position of nominative as descriptions of «آخران»; it is also permissible for one of them to be a description and the other a ḥāl (circumstantial), the ḥāl coming from an indefinite noun because it is specified by the description. [Translator's note: the author announced four aspects for the khabar's possibilities but numbers the third possibility "the third" after "one of them" and "the second"; translated as written.]

There is a weakness in this aspect, in that when a definite and an indefinite noun come together, you make the definite the thing spoken about and the indefinite what is said about it; the reverse is very rare or a poetic licence, as in his saying:

182 - 9-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يكونُ مزاجَها عسلٌ وماءُ
(…its mixture being honey and water.)

[And as in his saying]:

183 - 0- وإنَّ حراماً أَنْ أسُبَّ مجاشِعاً ... بآبائي الشمِّ الكرامِ الخَضارمِ
(It is forbidden that I should revile Mujāshiʿ by my lofty, noble, generous forefathers.)

You will have understood from what preceded that the clause «يقومان» and the preposition-phrase {مِنَ الَّذينَ} are either in the position of nominative as a description of «آخَران» or as a khabar about it, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl: either from «آخران» itself or from the pronoun latent in «آخران». It is also permissible for {مِنَ الذين} to be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يَقُومان».

His words: {استحق}: the majority read «استُحِقَّ» as passive and «الأَوْليان» in the nominative. Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «اسْتَحَقَّ» as active, with «الأوليان» like the majority; this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and the Commander of the Believers ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them, and it is also related from Ibn Kathīr. Ḥamza and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «استُحِقَّ» as passive like the majority, and «الأَوَّلِين», the plural of «أَوَّل» as a sound masculine plural. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «اسْتَحَقَّ» as active and «الأوَّلان» in the nominative, the dual of «أَوَّل». Ibn Sīrīn read like the majority except that he put in the accusative الأوْلَيَيْن, the dual of «أَوْلى». And it was read «الأَوْلَيْنَ» with sukūn on the wāw and fatḥa on the lām, the plural of «أَوْلى», like الأعلَيْن as the plural of «أَعْلى». When Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj reached this place he said: "This is one of the most difficult places in the Quran in its iʿrab." I say: by my life, the true word is what Ḥadhām said [i.e. he spoke truly], for people's heads have spun in untangling this construction. I have striven — praise be to Allah the Exalted — and summarised the discussion of it in the best summary; and it is necessary to mention something of the meanings of the verse so as to be illuminated by it in the iʿrab, for the iʿrab is a servant of the meaning.

As for the reading of the majority, the nominative of «الأَوْلَيان» in it is on several aspects. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «آخران», the implied form being: "the two nearest in the affair of the deceased are two others"; its explanation has preceded. The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the two nearest", as though someone asked: «مَنِ الآخران» (who are the two others?) and it was said: "they are the two nearest". The third: that it is a badal (substitute) from «آخران», a badal in the sense of explaining what it replaces, as in «جاء زيدٌ أخوك»; this is weak in their view because substituting with derived words is rare. The fourth: that it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to «آخران», explaining the two others by the two nearest. If you say: the condition of ʿaṭf bayān is that the follower and the followed agree in definiteness and indefiniteness — besides which the majority hold that it does not occur with indefinites, contrary to Abū ʿAlī — and «آخران» is indefinite while «الأَوْلَيَان» is definite, I say: this is a valid question, but its permissibility is binding on al-Akhfash and binding on al-Zamakhsharī. As for al-Akhfash, he permits «الأَوْلَيان» to be a description of «آخران», as I will set out from him when I deal with this aspect; and agreement is a condition for the naʿt and what it qualifies, so if it is permitted in the naʿt let it be permitted in what resembles it, since there is no difference between them except that derivation is a condition in the naʿt.

As for al-Zamakhsharī, he does not stipulate that — I mean agreement — and he stated explicitly in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān that His words {مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [verse: 97] are a ʿaṭf bayān to His words {فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ}, while {آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ} is indefinite; but since it was specified by the description it came near to the definite, as I reported from him in its place. Likewise «آخَران» has been described with two descriptions, so it comes nearer to the definite than «آياتٌ بيناتٌ», inasmuch as that was described with one description. The fifth: that it is a badal from the fāʿil of «يَقُومان».

The sixth: that it is a description of «آخران»; al-Akhfash permitted this. Abū ʿAlī said: "Abū al-Ḥasan permitted something else in it, namely that" الأَوْلَيان "be a description of" آخران ", because when it was described it was specified, so on account of its being described and specified it was described with the description of definites." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is weak because it entails demolishing what they almost agreed upon: that an indefinite is not described by a definite nor the reverse." I say: there is no doubt that their disagreement in definiteness and indefiniteness is weak, yet they have committed it in places; among them is what al-Khalīl related: «مَرَرْتُ بالرجلِ خيرٍ منك» on one of the aspects in this question; and among them {غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِم} [al-Fātiḥa: 7] on the view that «غير» is a description of «الذين أنعمت عليهم»; and his saying:

183 - 1- ولقد أَمُرُّ على اللئيمِ يَسُبُّني ... فَمَضَيْتُ ثُمًّتَ قُلْتُ لا يَعْنيني
(I pass by the base man who reviles me, and I go on, then say: it does not concern me.)

and the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الليل نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النهار} [Yā Sīn: 37], on the view that «يَسُبُّني» and «نَسْلَخُ» are descriptions of what precedes them, since clauses are indefinites. These examples I have brought are the reverse of what we are dealing with, for in them the definite is interpreted as indefinite, while in our case we have treated the indefinite as definite; but what unites them is the disagreement. It is also possible that our case belongs among these examples, in that «الأَوْلَيَيْنِ», since two specific individuals are not intended by them, came near to the indefinite and so occurred as a description of it, while it [the indefinite] was itself specified. Thus there are two permitting factors in this: the nearness of the indefinite to the definite by specification, and the nearness of the definite to the indefinite by vagueness. What supports what I have said is the saying of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "The fifth is that it be a description of" آخران ", because though it is indefinite it has been described, and by الأَوْلَيان two particular individuals are not intended."

The seventh: that it is nominative as the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) of «استُحِقَّ»; however, everyone who parsed it so assumed an omitted muḍāf before it. The parsers' assumptions differed. Makkī said: "Its implied form is: the sin of the two nearest was deserved against them", and likewise Abū al-Baqāʾ; Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī preceded them to this assumption. Al-Zamakhsharī assumed it, saying: "of those against whom the summoning of the two nearest of them to testimony became due, because of their knowledge of the reality of the situation." Among those who held that «الأَوْلَيَيْنِ» is nominative by «استُحِقَّ» was Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, who then rejected it, saying: "because what is deserved can only be the bequest or something of it; as for the two nearest to the deceased, it is not possible that they be deserved so that استُحِقَّ be predicated of them." I say: Abū ʿAlī only rejected that according to the outward wording, for no one deserved the two nearest as he mentioned; but it is permissible to predicate «استُحِقَّ» of them by interpreting it with the omission of the muḍāf mentioned above.

This, which al-Fārisī rejected on its outward form, is what led people to implying that muḍāf; and al-Zamakhsharī's assumption of it as «انتداب الأوليين» (the summoning of the two nearest) is better than others' assumptions, for the meaning supports it. As for implying «الإِثم» (the sin), it is not apparent at all except by a far-fetched interpretation.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya also permitted «الأَوْلَيان» to be nominative by «استُحِقَّ», but the outward sense of his wording is that he did not assume a muḍāf; for he sensed al-Fārisī's objection mentioned above and contrived an answer to it. This is his text — he said, in summary: "«استُحِقَّ» here is taken as a metaphor, for it is not a real deserving, as with His words {استحقآ إِثْماً}; its meaning is only that they took control of the property by virtue of this deceased being alone and lacking his kin or the people of his religion, so their seizing of it was made a deserving figuratively. The meaning is: from the group that was absent and whose right it was to have its nearest kin present; when it was absent and this testator was alone, it deserved this situation, and these two witnesses not of the people of the religion and of the guardianship, and the affair of the two nearest [was] over this group; so the verb was made passive in this sense for concision. What strengthens this supposition is the verb's being made transitive by «على», since it was by power and imposition which the situation made possible; one does not say استحَقَّ منه or فيه except of a real deserving in its proper sense; as for «استحَقَّ عليه», it is by imposition, domination and borrowed deserving." End of quote. So he predicated «استحق» of «الأوْليان» without assuming a muḍāf, interpreting it as he mentioned; I have borne the length of his wording so that it may be clear. [Translator's note: the quoted passage from Ibn ʿAṭiyya is somewhat elliptical in the source ("and the affair of the two nearest over this group"); translated as written.]

Know that the nāʾib fāʿil of «استُحِقَّ» in the preceding aspects — I mean other than this aspect, which is its predication of «الأَوْلَيان» — is a pronoun referring to something preceding in wording or in context. Their expressions about it differed. Al-Fārisī, al-Ḥawfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī said: it is the pronoun of the sin (الإِثم), and the sin has preceded in His words {استحقآ إِثْماً}. Al-Fārisī and al-Ḥawfī also said: "What was deserved is the act of bequeathing (الإِيصاء) or the bequest (الوصية)." I say: implying the bequest (الوصية) is problematic, because when the verb is predicated of a feminine pronoun of any kind the tāʾ is obligatory except in poetic licence — and Yūnus does not restrict it to that — and it is not permissible to say that they implied the word الوصية [itself], because that would be an omission, and the fāʿil, in their view, is not omitted. [Translator's note: the source has «قالت» here, evidently a misprint for «قلت» (I say); translated as "I say".] Al-Naḥḥās said, approving the implying of الإِيصاء: "This is the best that has been said about it, because no particle is made a substitute for another particle" — meaning that he does not say that «على» means «في» nor «مِنْ», as has been said of both; this will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Al-Zamakhsharī gathered most of what I have said and reported of the iʿrab and meaning in the most concise wording, saying: "«آخران», i.e. two other witnesses who stand in their place, from those against whom it was deserved, i.e. [from those against whom] the sin was deserved; its meaning is: from those against whom the crime was committed, namely the family of the deceased and his kinsfolk; and الأَوْلَيان are the two most entitled to testimony because of their kinship and their knowledge. Their nominative is on [the implied] «هما الأَوْلَيان», as though it were said: and who are they? and it was said: the two nearest. It was also said: they are a badal from the pronoun in «يَقُومان» or from «آخران». And it is permissible that they be nominative by «استُحِقَّ», i.e. from those against whom the summoning of the two nearest of them to testimony became due, because of their knowledge of the reality of the situation."

His words {عَلَيْهِمُ}: there are three aspects concerning «على». The first: that it has its usual sense; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "As in your saying:" وَجَبَ عليه الاثمُ (the sin became binding upon him) "; and it has preceded from al-Naḥḥās that when he implied الإِيصاء he kept it in its usual sense and approved of that. The second: that it means» في «, i.e. the sin was deserved among them, so» على «occurred in the place of» في «, just as» في «occurs in its place, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النخل} [Ṭā Hā: 71], i.e. on the trunks; and as in his saying:

183 - 2- بَطَلٌ كأنَّ ثيابَه في سَرْحَةٍ ... يُحْذَى نِعالَ السِّبْتِ ليس بتوءمِ
(A hero, as though his clothes were on a tall tree; he is shod with sandals of tanned leather, not a twin.)

i.e. on a tall tree. Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed it, saying:" i.e. the bequest was deserved among them ". The third: that it means» من «, i.e. the sin was deserved from them; similar to it are the words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذَا اكتالوا عَلَى الناس} [al-Muṭaffifīn: 2], i.e. from the people. Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed it, saying:" i.e. the two nearest were deserved from them ". So when he made it mean «في» he assumed «استُحِقَّ» as predicated of the bequest, and when he made it mean «من» he assumed it as predicated of «الأَوْلَيان»; yet when he mentioned what stands in place of the fāʿil he mentioned only the pronoun of the sin and الأوليان. Some permitted «استُحِقَّ» to be predicated of the pronoun of the property, i.e. the inherited property was deserved against them; and this is close.

So it is established that there are five aspects concerning the nāʾib fāʿil of «استُحِقَّ». The first: «الأَوْلَيان». The second: the pronoun of الإِيصاء. The third: the pronoun of الوصية, which in meaning is like the one before it, and its difficulty has preceded. The fourth: that it is the pronoun of the sin. The fifth: that it is the pronoun of the property. I have not seen them permit «عليهم» to be what stands in place of the fāʿil, as in {غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِم} [al-Fātiḥa: 7]; it seems they saw no benefit in it.

As for the reading of Ḥafṣ, {الأَوْلَيان} is nominative [as fāʿil] of «استَحَقَّ» and its object is omitted. Some assumed it as «وصيتَهما» (their bequest), and al-Zamakhsharī assumed it as «أن يجرِّدوهما للقيام بالشهادة» (that they assign the two of them to bear the testimony), for he said: "Its meaning is: from the heirs against whom the two nearest among them in testimony have the right that they assign them to bear the testimony, and expose by it the lie of the liars." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«الأَوْلَيان» is nominative by «اسَتَحَقَّ»; that is, the meaning would be: from those against whom the two false witnesses claimed their property and estate; they were called the two nearest, i.e. the absence of people made them the nearest to the deceased and his estate, so they betrayed and wronged in it. Or the meaning is: from those for whom it was due that the two nearest be from among them, so استَحَقَّ means حَقَّ, like استعجب and عجب. Or استحقَّ means 'strove for and claimed as due', so the meaning is: from the people of whom two nearest were present, so the two claimed it against them, i.e. claimed it for them, strove in it and made it due by their oaths and their kinship." The Shaykh said, after relating from al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Muḥammad what I have presented from them: "Some said: the object is omitted, its implied form being: those against whom the two nearest claimed their bequest." I say: it is likewise omitted in the two views of Abū al-Qāsim and Abū Muḥammad, and I have explained what it is: for al-Zamakhsharī it is his saying «أَنْ يُجَرِّدُوهما للقيامِ بالشهادة», and for Ibn ʿAṭiyya it is his saying {ما لَهم وتَرِكَتَهم}. So his saying "Some said: the object is omitted" gives the false impression that he did not realise it was omitted in what preceded as well.

Among those who held that «استَحَقَّ» means the bare form «حَقَّ» is al-Wāḥidī, for he said: "استحقَّ here means حَقَّ, i.e. it became binding; and the meaning is: then two others from those upon whom the bequeathing became binding by his bequest among them, namely his heirs." This interpretation that al-Wāḥidī mentioned is clearer than the meaning that Abū Muḥammad mentioned on this aspect, and that is evident.

As for the reading of Ḥamza and Abū Bakr, the nāʾib fāʿil of «استُحِقَّ» is the pronoun of الإِيصاء, the bequest, the property or the sin, as has preceded. As for «الأَوَّلين», it is the plural of «أوّل», the counterpart of «آخِر», and there are four aspects concerning it. The first: that it is genitive as a description of «الذين». The second: that it is a badal from it, which is uncommon because it is derived. The third: that it is a badal from the pronoun in «عليهم»; what makes it acceptable here, though it is derived, is that what precedes it is unfit to be described; Makkī transmitted these last two aspects. The fourth: that it is accusative in praise; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it, saying: "The meaning of 'firstness' is precedence over strangers in testimony, because they are more entitled to it." He interpreted firstness as precedence over strangers only in keeping with what passed in his commentary on {أو آخرَان مِنْ غيرِكم}, that the two are from strangers, not from the unbelievers. Al-Wāḥidī said: "Its implied form is: from the first ones against whom the bequeathing or the sin was deserved; they were called «الأَوَّلين» only because they were first in mention. Do you not see that there preceded: {يِا أَيُّهَا الذين آمَنُواْ شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ} and likewise {اثنان ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ}, mentioned in the wording before His words: {أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ}." Ibn ʿAbbās used to prefer this reading and would say: "Do you see, if the two nearest were minors, how could they stand in their place?" He meant that if the two were minors they could not stand in the oath in the place of the two who swore falsely.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya took this direction, saying: "Its meaning is: from the people against whom their affair was deserved, i.e. they were overpowered in it; then He described them as being 'first', i.e. in mention in this verse."

As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, «الأولان» is nominative [as fāʿil] of «استَحَقَّ», for he reads it as active. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is used as proof by those who hold that the oath is returned to the claimant." He did not explain who the two first are; what is meant by them is the two mentioned first. This reading is like the reading of Ḥafṣ, so what was mentioned there is assumed in it, then whatever object is fitting is assumed.

As for the reading of Ibn Sīrīn, its accusative is in praise, and the genitive is not permissible in it, because [the genitive] would be either as a badal or as a description by a plural, while الأَوْلَيَن in his reading is a dual, so that is impossible in it. As for the reading «الأَوْلَيْن» like الأعلَيْن, Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it as an irregular (shādhdh) reading without attributing it, saying: "And it is read" الأَوْلَين ", the plural of الأَوْلَى, and its iʿrab is like the iʿrab of الأَوْلَين" — meaning in the reading of Ḥamza — and it has preceded that there are four aspects in it, and they apply here.

His words: «فيُقْسِمان»: conjoined to «يَقُومان», and the causation in it is evident. «لَشهادتُنا أحقُّ»: this clause is the response to the oath in His words «فيُقْسِمان». «ذلك أَدْنَى»: this clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive; what is pointed to is the preceding ruling in its detail, i.e. what was mentioned of the rulings is nearer to the testimony being given as it should. It was said: what is pointed to is the detaining after the prayer; and it was said: the making of the two witnesses swear. «أَنْ يأتوا»: its origin is «إلى أن يأتوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ also assumed it with «من», i.e. "nearer than that they come", and Makkī assumed it with the bāʾ, i.e. «بأَنْ يأتُوا»; neither is clear. Then the preposition was omitted, and the well-known disagreement arose [about the position of أنْ and its clause]. «على وجهها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يأتُوا»; it was also said: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from it [the testimony]; Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed it as «محقّقة وصحيحة» (verified and sound), which is an interpretation of meaning, because, as you have learned more than once, restricted [specific] verbs of being are not assumed in the like of this.

His words: {أَوْ يخافوا}: there are two aspects concerning its accusative. The first: that it is accusative by conjunction to «يَأْتوا»; and on this there are two interpretations of «أو». One: that it has its usual sense of one of two things, and the meaning is: that ruling is nearer to the testimony occurring as it should, or to fear of the oaths being returned to others so that their oaths fall away. The other interpretation: that it means the wāw, i.e. that whole ruling is nearer to their coming [with the testimony], and nearer to their fearing; this is understood from the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās. The second of the two aspects of the accusative: that it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after «أو», which means «إلا», as in their saying: «لألزمنَّك أو تقضيَني حَقِّي» (I will stick to you unless you pay me my due), its implied form being: «إلاَّ أَنْ تقضِيني». So «أو» is a conjunction in its usual sense, and the verb after it is accusative by an obligatorily implied «أَنْ», and «أَنْ» with what is in its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, that maṣdar being conjoined to a maṣdar imagined from the verb before it. So the meaning of «لألزمنَّك أو تقضيَني حقي» is: "there shall certainly be from me a sticking to you, or your paying of my due"; and likewise the meaning here, i.e. that is nearer to their coming with the testimony as it should be; and otherwise [وإلاَّ] they would fear the return of the oaths. Thus Ibn ʿAṭiyya assumed it, with a wāw before «إلا», which is contrary to the grammarians' assumption, for they assume «أو» only with the word «إلا» alone, without a wāw.

It is as though «إلا» in his wording, as the Shaykh understood it, is not the exceptive «إلا»; rather its origin is the conditional «إنْ» entering upon the negative «لا» and assimilated into it. For he said: "Or" أو "may mean" إلاَّ إنْ ", which is what Ibn ʿAṭiyya expressed with that wording, assuming it as a condition — whose verb is omitted — and an apodosis." End of quote. There is a point to consider in this from two angles. The first: that no one has held this, I mean that «أو» has the meaning of a condition. The second: that after ruling that it means «إلاَّ إنْ», he made it mean a condition whose verb is omitted.

{أَن تُرَدَّ} is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "or that they fear the returning of their oaths". «بعد أَيْمانهم» is either an adverb of «تُرَدَّ» or attached to an omitted [word] as a description of «أَيْمان». The pronoun in His words «يَأْتُوا» and what follows was made plural even though in meaning it refers to a dual, namely the two witnesses. It was said: it refers to the two kinds of witnesses; and it was said: rather it refers to witnesses among all people, its meaning being: that is more fitting and more appropriate that people should beware of betrayal and take care in their testimony for fear of disgrace and exposure through the return of the oath to the claimant. His words: {واتقوا الله}: He did not mention the object of the fear [taqwā], either because it is known, i.e. "fear Allah in your testimony and concerning those upon whom you have been made executors, by not purloining anything from them", since the story was for this reason; or with the intention of [simply] bringing about taqwā, so that it covers everything that is to be guarded against. Likewise the object of «اسمعوا»: if you wish, you may consider it omitted by restriction [to the verb itself] or by abbreviation, i.e. "hear His commands and prohibitions among the preceding rulings". How eloquently these two imperative clauses were brought! Blessed be Allah, the most truthful of speakers.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم}: the discussion of its parallel has preceded, and likewise {سَوَآءَ السبيل} [al-Nisāʾ: 155]. The majority read «قاسيةً», an active participle from «قسا يقسو». The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read — and it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] — «قَسِيَّةً», with fatḥa on the qāf, kasra on the sīn and a doubled yāʾ. People differed over this reading. Al-Fārisī said: "It is not originally among the words of the Arabs; it is only a foreign word that has been Arabised." He means that it is taken from their saying «دِرْهم قِسِيّ», i.e. adulterated: He likened their hearts, in their not being free of turbidity, to adulterated, impure dirhams. They cited the saying of Abū Zubayd:

171 - 1- لها صَواهِلُ في صُمِّ السِّلام كما ... صاحَ القَسِيَّات في أَيْدي الصياريفِ
(Its [hooves/pickaxes] ring on the hard rocks as the false coins ring in the money-changers' hands)

And another's saying:

171 - 2- وما زَوَّدوني غيرَ سَحْقِ عِمامةٍ ... وخمسَ مِئٍ منها قِسِيُّ زائفُ
(They gave me as provision only a worn-out turban and five hundred [dirhams], of which some were base and counterfeit)

The author of al-Kashshāf said: "And ʿAbd Allāh read «قَسِيَّة», i.e. bad and adulterated, from their saying «درهم قَسِيّ»; it is from «القسوة» (hardness), because pure gold and silver have softness in them, whereas the adulterated has hardness and dryness in it. «القسي» and «القاسح» — with the undotted ḥāʾ — are brothers in denoting dryness." Al-Mubarrad preceded him in this view, for he said: "The adulterated dirham is called «قَسِيّ» because of its hardness and toughness, due to the adulteration in it." This goes back to the first meaning; and «القاسي» and «القاسح» have one meaning. On these two views the word is Arabic. It was also said: rather, this reading agrees with the reading of the majority in meaning and derivation, because it is faʿīl for intensiveness, like «شاهد» and «شهيد», so likewise «قاسٍ» and «قسِيّ»; it is made feminine only in the sense of the group. Al-Hayṣam ibn Shaddākh read «قُسِيَّة», with ḍamma on the qāf and a doubled yāʾ. It was also read «قِسِيَّة» with kasra on the qāf by assimilation. [Translator's note: the source prints «قِسَّية».] The origin of the two readings is «قاسِوَة» and «قَسِيوة», because the derivation is from «القسوة».

His saying: {يُحَرِّفُونَ}: there are four views on this clause. [The first:] that it is resumptive, an explanation of the hardness of their hearts, because there is no hardness greater than inventing lies against Allah the Exalted. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «لعنَّاهم», i.e. We cursed them while they were characterised by distortion. The third — Abū al-Baqāʾ said it —: that it is a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «قاسية». He said: "It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from «القلوب», because the pronoun in «يُحَرِّفون» does not refer back to the hearts." What he said is open to consideration, because inasmuch as he permitted it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قاسية», he is bound to permit it to be a ḥāl from «القلوب», since the latent pronoun in «قاسية» refers to the hearts; so just as it is impossible for it to be a ḥāl from its overt noun, it is impossible for it to be a ḥāl from its pronoun. It is as though the obstacle he imagined is that the pronoun — the wāw in «يُحَرِّفون» — refers to the Jews as a whole, not to their hearts specifically, for hearts do not distort; only the owners of hearts distort. But this binds him in his permitting it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قاسية».

Someone may say: what is meant by the hearts is the persons themselves, and they were expressed by the hearts only because these organs are the seat of the distortion, i.e. it issues from them through their pondering it; so on this view it may be a ḥāl from «القلوب». The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «هم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak", meaning because a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is not permissible; but others permit it in a place like this, because the muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi. The majority read [«الكَلِم»] with fatḥa on the kāf and kasra on the lām, and it is the plural of «كلمة». Abū Rajāʾ read «الكِلْمِ», with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the lām, which is a lightening of the majority's reading; its origin is that he gave the kāf kasra by assimilation and then gave the ʿayn [i.e. the middle radical] sukūn for lightness. Al-Sulamī and al-Nakhaʿī read «الكلام» with an alif. «وعن مواضِعه»: its like has been mentioned in al-Nisāʾ.

His saying: {على خَآئِنَةٍ}: there are three views on «خائنة». One of them: that it is an active participle and the hāʾ is for intensiveness, like «راوية» and «نسَّابة», i.e. "on a treacherous person". The poet said:

171 - 3- حَدَّثْتَ نفسَك بالوفاءِ ولم تَكُنْ ... للغدرِ خائنةً مُغِلَّ الإصبَعِ
(You told yourself of keeping faith, yet you were not, for treachery, a betrayer with a thieving finger)

The second: that the tāʾ is for the feminine, and it is made feminine in the sense of «طائفة» (a party), «نفس» (a soul) or «فَعْلَة» (a deed) that is treacherous. The third: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «العافية» and «العاقبة»; this view is supported by the reading of al-Aʿmash: {على خيانة}. The origin of «خائِنة» is «خاونة», and of «خيانة» is «خِوانة», because of their saying «تَخَوَّن», «خَوَّان» and «هو أَخْوَن»; they were only modified in the way «قائمة» and «قيام» are modified. «منهم» is an adjective of «خائنة» if the adjective is intended by it; and if the maṣdar is intended by it, a muḍāf is supposed, i.e. "of some of their treacheries".

His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: accusative (manṣūb) as excepted. On that from which it is excepted there are four views. The most apparent of them: that it is the word «خائنة», and they are the persons mentioned in the preceding clause, i.e. you will not cease to discover those of them who betray, except the few, for they do not betray, so you do not discover it in them; these are ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Were it read in the genitive as a badal (substitute), it would be sound", meaning as a badal from «خائنة», since it is within the domain of non-affirmative speech. The second, mentioned by Ibn ʿAṭiyya: that it is the act, i.e. you will not cease to discover acts of treachery except a few acts. This is clear if by «الخيانة» is meant that it is an adjective of the implied «فَعْلة», as has preceded; but what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said is made unlikely by His saying after it «منهم». We have had its parallel in His saying {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 66], where al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. The third: that it is «قلوبهم» in His saying {وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَاسِيَةً}. The proponent of this view said: "What is meant by them is the believers, because the hardness has left their hearts." This is very far-fetched, because of His saying «لعنَّاهم». The fourth: that it is the pronoun in «منهم» in His saying, Exalted is He: {على خَآئِنَةٍ مِّنْهُمْ}; Makkī said this.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمِنَ الذين قَالُواْ}: there are five views on it. One of them — and it is the apparent one —: that «مِنْ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying «أخذنا». The correct supposition here is to say: its implied form is «وأَخَذْنا من الذين قالوا: إنَّا نصارى ميثاقهم», so you place «الذين» after «أَخَذْنا» and put «ميثاقهم» after it. It is not permissible to suppose «وأَخَذْنا ميثاقَهم من الذين», putting «ميثاقَهم» before «الذين قالوا» — even though that is permissible in so far as both are objects, each of which may be put first or later — because it entails the pronoun referring to something later in both wording and rank, which is not permitted except in limited places. A group stated this explicitly, among them Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose adjective stands in its place, the implied form being: «ومن الذين قالوا إنّا نصارى قومٌ أخذنا ميثاقهم» ("and among those who said 'We are Christians' are a people whose covenant We took"); so the pronoun in «ميثاقهم» refers to that omitted element. The third: that it is also a fronted khabar, but they supposed the mubtadaʾ to be a relative noun that was omitted while its ṣila (relative clause) remained, the implied form being: «ومن الذين قالوا: إنَّا نصارى مَنْ أخذنا ميثاقهم», so the pronoun in «ميثاقهم» refers to «مَنْ». The Kufans permit the omission of the relative noun, and we have had the discussion with them on that before. Makkī transmitted this doctrine of the Kufans and supposed it, according to them, as: «ومن الذين قالوا: إنَّا نصارى مَنْ أخذنا» [Translator's note: the source prints «إنَّ نصارى».]. This supposition does not entail that the omitted element is only a relative noun; rather the supposed «مَنْ» may be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, omitted while its adjective remains, so it would be like the first doctrine. The fourth: that «مِنْ» is attached to «أخذنا», as in the first view, except that that supposition — placing «من الذين» after «أخذنا» and before «ميثاقهم» — is not required; rather the supposition may be the reverse, in the sense that the pronoun in «ميثاقهم» refers to the Children of Israel, and the maṣdar in His saying «ميثاقهم» is a maṣdar of comparison, the implied form being: "and We took from the Christians a covenant like the covenant of the Children of Israel", as in your saying «أخَذْتُ من زيد ميثاق عمرو» ("I took from Zayd ʿAmr's covenant"), i.e. a covenant like ʿAmr's covenant. Al-Zamakhsharī began with this view, for he said: "We took from the Christians the covenant of those mentioned before them from the people of Moses", i.e. the like of their covenant to believe in Allah and the messengers. The fifth: that «من الذين» is conjoined to «منهم» in His saying, Exalted is He: «ولا تزال تَطَّلِعُ على خائنةٍ منهم», i.e. from the Jews; the meaning being: "and you will not cease to discover treachery from the Jews and from those who said 'We are Christians'"; and His saying {أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَهُمْ} would on this view be resumptive. This ought not to be permitted, for two reasons. One of them: the separation, which is not excusable. The second: that it is preparing the governor to govern something and then cutting it off from it, which is not permitted.

His saying: {بَيْنَهُمُ}: there are two views on it. One of them: that it is an adverb (ẓarf) of «أغرينا». The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «العداوة», so it is attached to an omitted element. It is not permissible for it to be an adverb of «العداوة», because a maṣdar's governed element does not precede it. «وإلى يوم القيامة»: Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be attached to «أغرينا», or to «العداوة», or to «البغضاء», i.e. "We stirred up among them until the Day of Resurrection enmity and hatred", or "they will be at enmity with one another until the Day of Resurrection", or "they will hate one another until the Day of Resurrection". On what Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted, the issue belongs to the chapter of al-iʿmāl (assigning government), and there would be a contention between three governors, and it would be a case of giving government to the third with omission from the first and second; the establishment of that has preceded. «أغرينا» is from «أغراه بكذا», i.e. he made it cling to him. Its origin is from «الغِراء» (glue), with which things are stuck, and its third radical is wāw, so the origin is «أَغْرَوْنا»; the wāw was changed into yāʾ only because it occurs as the fourth letter, as in «أغوينا». Of this is their saying «سَهْمٌ مَغْرُوُّ», i.e. an arrow made with glue. One says «غَرِيَ بكذا يَغْرى غَرَاء وغِراء», and when it is meant to be made transitive it is made transitive with the hamza, so one says «أغريته بكذا». The pronoun in «بينهم» may refer to «الذين قالوا إنَّا نصارى», or to the Jews mentioned before; a group held each view. This speech is conjoined to the speech before it in His saying: {وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ الله مِيثَاقَ بني إِسْرَآئِيلَ}, i.e. "Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We took from those who said …".

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {يُبَيِّنُ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسولنا», i.e. Our Messenger came to you in this state. «ممَّا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, because it is an adjective of «كثيراً». «ما» is a nominal relative noun, «تُخْفون» is its ṣila (relative clause), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "of that which you used to hide". [Translator's note: the source writes «من الذين كنتم تخفونه».] «ومن الكتاب» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun. His saying: {قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ مِّنَ الله نُورٌ} has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. The pronoun in «يبيِّن» and «يَعْفُو» refers to the Messenger; some have permitted it to refer to Allah the Exalted, and on this view His saying «يبيِّن» has no position in i'rab; it cannot be a ḥāl from «رسولنا» because of the absence of a linking element. The adjective of «كثير» is omitted because it is known, its implied form being: "of much of your sins"; and the omission of the adjective is rare. His saying: {قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ مِّنَ الله} has no position in i'rab because it is resumptive. «من الله» may be attached to «جاء», or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «نور»: an adjective of an indefinite noun was put before it, so it became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {يَهْدِي}: there are five views on it. The most apparent of them: that it is in the position of the nominative, because it is a second naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب»: He described it with a single word and then with a clause, which is the basic order. The second: that it is also an adjective, but of «نور»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. This is open to consideration, since the rule is that when followers come together the naʿt is put before the conjoined noun: you say «جاء زيدٌ العاقلُ وعمرو» ("the intelligent Zayd and ʿAmr came"), and you do not say «جاء زيدٌ وعمرو العاقل»; and also because there is ambiguity in it. The third: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كتاب», because the indefinite noun, having been specified by the adjective, has come close to the definite. By analogy with Abū al-Baqāʾ's view, it may be a ḥāl from «نور», just as it may be an adjective of it. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «رسولنا», as a badal (substitute) from the clause that occurs as a ḥāl of it, namely His saying «يبين». The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يبيِّن». Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these two, and what they involve of separation is not hidden, and also that there is in it something resembling preparing the governor to govern and cutting it off from it.

The pronoun in «به» refers to whichever of them «يَهْدي» is made a ḥāl from or an adjective of. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "For that reason it is singular", i.e. the pronoun in «به» was brought as singular although two things precede it, namely «نور» and «كتاب»; but since by the clause «يهدي» the ḥāl or description of one of them was intended, he made the pronoun singular. It was also said: the pronoun in «به» refers to the Messenger. It was also said: it refers to «السلام» [Translator's note: so in the source; possibly «الإسلام» (Islam) is intended.]. On these two views the clause «يهدي» is neither a ḥāl nor an adjective, because of the absence of a linking element. «مَنْ» is a relative noun or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; He observed its wording in His saying «اتَّبع», which is why He made the pronoun singular, and its meaning, which is why He made it plural in His saying {وَيُخْرِجُهُمْ}.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Muslim ibn Jundab and al-Zuhrī read «بهُ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ wherever it occurs; it has preceded that this is the original form. Al-Ḥasan read «سُبْل» with sukūn on the bāʾ, which is a regular lightening, as in their saying «عُنْق» for «عُنُق»; and this is more fitting here because it is a plural. It is the second object of «يهدي», on the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "to the paths"; the verification of its parallel has preceded. It may also be accusative as a badal (substitute) from «رضوانه»: either a badal of the whole from the whole, because «سبل السلام» are the good pleasure of the Creator, Exalted is He; or a badal of inclusion, because the good pleasure includes the paths of peace, or because they include the good pleasure of Allah the Exalted; or a badal of part from whole, because the paths of peace are part of the good pleasure. «بإذنه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يخرجهم», i.e. by His facilitation or by His command. The bāʾ is for the ḥāl, i.e. accompanied by His facilitation, or for causation, i.e. because of His command sent down to His Messenger.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِن بَحِيرَةٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), because the two well-known conditions are present. And «جَعَلَ» may be in the sense of «سَمَّى» (to name), transitive to two objects, one of them omitted, the implied form being: "Allah did not make — i.e. did not name — any animal a baḥīra." Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is in the sense of «شَرَعَ» (to legislate) and «وضع» (to lay down), i.e. Allah did not legislate it nor command it." Al-Wāḥidī said, after a long discussion: "So the meaning of 'Allah did not make any baḥīra' is: He did not make it obligatory nor command it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«جَعَلَ» in this verse cannot be in the sense of «خلق» (to create), because Allah created all of these things; nor in the sense of «صَيَّر» (to make into), because making-into requires a second object. So its meaning is: Allah did not institute nor legislate." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected all these transmitted views, on the grounds that the lexicographers did not count «شرع» among the meanings of «جَعَل»; he explained the verse as making-into (taṣyīr), with the second object omitted, i.e. "Allah did not make a baḥīra something legislated."

And «البَحيرة» is on the pattern «فَعِيلة» in the sense of «مَفْعولة» (passive), so the entry of the tāʾ of femininity on it is not according to rule; but since it came to be treated like non-derived nouns, it was made feminine. I have clarified this at His saying {والنطيحة} [al-Māʾida: 3]. Its derivation is from «البَحْر», and «البَحْر» is breadth (السَّعَة); from it is «بَحْرُ الماءِ» (the sea), because of its breadth.

The lexicographers disagreed greatly about what the baḥīra was among the Arabs. Abū ʿUbayd said: "It is the she-camel that has borne five litters, the last of them a male; then her ear is slit and she is left alone, so she is not ridden, not milked, and not driven away from pasture or water; and if an exhausted traveller met her he would not ride her." This was related from Ibn ʿAbbās, except that he did not mention a male at the end. Some said: "When the she-camel had borne five litters, they looked at the fifth: if it was a male they slaughtered it and ate it; and if it was a female they slit her ear and left her to graze and come to water, not ridden and not milked; this is the baḥīra." This was related from Qatāda. Some said: "The baḥīra is the female that is the fifth litter, as explained above, except that its flesh and its milk are not lawful for women; if she dies, she becomes lawful for them." Some said: "The baḥīra is the daughter of the sāʾiba" — the explanation of the sāʾiba will come — "so when the sāʾiba bore a female, they slit her ear and left her with her mother to graze and come to water, not ridden even by an exhausted traveller." This is the view of Mujāhid ibn Jabr. Some said: "It is the one whose flow — i.e. its milk — was withheld for the sake of the false gods (al-ṭawāghīt), so no one milks her." Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab held this. It was said: it is the one left in the pasture without a herdsman; Ibn Sīda said this. It was said: when she bore five females, they slit her ear and left her. Some said — and it is attributed to Masrūq —: "When she bore five or seven, they slit her ear." And it was said: "It is the she-camel that bears ten litters; then her ear is slit lengthwise into two halves, and she is left, not ridden, not milked, and not driven away from pasture or water; and when she dies her flesh is lawful for men but not for women." Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted this, and Abū al-Qāsim al-Rāghib said the same.

And it was said: the baḥīra is the male calf (السِّقْب): when it was born they slit its ear and said: "O Allah, if it lives then it is a stud-keeper's (قَنِيّ), and if it dies then it is slaughtered (ذَكِيّ)"; and when it died they ate it. [Translator's note: the source reads «نحروا أذنه» ("they slaughtered its ear"), apparently a slip for «بحروا أذنه» ("they slit its ear"); rendered by the latter sense.] The way to reconcile these many views is that the Arabs differed in their practices regarding the baḥīra.

As for the sāʾiba, it was said: when a man returned from a journey, or [wished to] give thanks for a blessing, he set a camel loose (سَيَّب), so it was not ridden, and what was mentioned for the baḥīra was done with it; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd. It was said: it is the she-camel that bears ten females, so she is not ridden and none drinks her milk except a guest or a child; al-Farrāʾ said this. It was said: it is what was left for their gods; a man would bring his livestock to the custodians (al-sadana) and leave it with them, and its milk would flow. It was said: it is the she-camel left so that a pilgrimage might be made on her; that was transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī. And it was said: it is the slave who is freed on condition that there be no walāʾ (clientage), no ʿaql (blood-money liability) and no inheritance attaching to him.

And «السائِبَة» here admits two views. The first: it is an active participle in its proper sense, from «ساب يَسِيب», i.e. to roam freely, like the flowing of water; and it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «سِبْتُه»; one says «سَيَّبْتُه فساب وانساب» ("I set it loose, so it went loose and roamed"). The second: it is in the sense of a passive participle, as in «عيشةٌ راضية» ("a pleasing life," lit. "a pleased life"); but the occurrence of «فاعِل» in the sense of «مَفْعول» is very rare, as in «ماء دافق» ("gushing water"). What ought to be said is that it is «فاعل» in the sense of "possessor of such-and-such," i.e. in the sense of relation (nasab), as in their saying «لابن», i.e. "possessor of milk"; and from it, on one of the two views, are «عيشةٌ راضية» and «ماء دافق», i.e. "possessing contentment" and "possessing gushing"; and likewise this one, i.e. "possessing roaming (سَيْب)."

And «الوصيلة» here is on the pattern «فَعِيلة» in the sense of «فاعِلة» (active), according to the explanation that will come, so the entry of the tāʾ is according to rule. The lexicographers disagreed about it: is it of the kind of sheep and goats, or of the kind of camels? Then they also disagreed after that. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the ewe that bears seven litters, two female kids at a time; and when at the last of them she bore a female kid and a male kid, it was said: 'she has joined her brother (وصلت أخاها),' so she was treated like the sāʾiba." Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the ewe: when she bore a male it was for their gods, and when she bore a female it was for them." Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is the ewe that bears seven litters; if the seventh was a female, the women derived no benefit from it at all, unless it died, in which case the men and the women ate it; if it was a male they slaughtered it and all ate it; and if it was a male and a female, they said: 'she has joined her brother,' so they left her with him, not slaughtered, and none but the men, not the women, benefited from her; if she died, the women shared in her with the men." Ibn Qutayba said: "If the seventh was a male it was slaughtered and the men, not the women, ate it, and they said: 'Exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives'; if it was a female she was left among the flock; and if it was a male and a female, then it is as in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās." And it was said: "It is the ewe that bears ten females in succession in five litters; then whatever she bore after that was for the males, not the females." Abū Isḥāq and Abū ʿUbayda held this, except that Abū ʿUbayda said: "And when she bore a male and a female together, they said: 'she has joined her brother,' so they did not slaughter him because of her."

And it was said: it is the ewe that bears five litters, or three; if it was a male kid they slaughtered it, if it was a female they kept her, and if it was a male and a female they said: "she has joined her brother." All of this is according to those who restrict it to the kind of sheep and goats. As for those who said it is of camels, they said: "It is the she-camel that bears a female as her first offspring, then follows it with the birth of another female with no male between them, so they leave her for their gods, and say: 'she has joined a female to a female with no male between them.'" [Translator's note: the source has «أنهى», an evident misprint for «أنثى» ("a female"); rendered accordingly.]

And «الحامي» is an active participle from «حَمَى يَحْمي», i.e. to protect/withhold. The lexicographers' explanation of it differs. From al-Farrāʾ: "It is the stallion to whose offspring's offspring a foal is born; then they say: 'he has protected his back,' so he is not ridden, not used, and not driven away from water or trees." Some said: "It is the stallion from whose offspring, males and females, ten females are produced"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya related that. [Translator's note: the source has «من يبن», an evident misprint for «من بين» ("from among").] Some said: "It is the stallion from whose loins ten litters are born; then they say: 'he has protected his back,' and they leave him like the sāʾiba as described above." This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd, and Abū ʿUbayda and al-Zajjāj inclined to it. It was related from al-Shāfiʿī that it is the stallion that covers in its owner's herd for ten years. And Ibn Zayd said: "It is the stallion for which seven females are produced in succession; then he protects his back and what was described above is done with him."

You have now learned the origin of the lexicographers' disagreement about these things: it is due to the differences among the practices of the Arabs and their corrupt opinions concerning them.

They recited concerning the baḥīra the saying [of the poet]:
184 - 5- مُحَرَّمَةٌ لا يَطْعَمُ الناسُ لحمَها ... ولا نحن في شيءٍ كذاك البحائرُ
(Made inviolable — people do not taste their flesh, nor do we in any way; such are the baḥāʾir.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed «184» in the source, while the neighbouring verses are numbered «181»; it is kept as written.]

And he recited concerning the sāʾiba the saying [of the poet]:
181 - 6- وسائبةٍ لله مالي تشكُّرا ... إنِ اللهُ عافَى عامراً أو مجاشعا
(My property shall be a sāʾiba for Allah, in thanksgiving, if Allah grants well-being to ʿĀmir or Mujāshiʿ.)

They recited concerning the waṣīla [a verse] of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
181 - 7- أجِدَّك أمَّا كنت في الناسِ ناعقاً ... تراعي بأَعْلى ذي المجازِ الوَصايلا
(By your earnestness! Were you not among people one who shouts at the flock, tending the waṣāʾil on the heights of Dhū al-Majāz?)

And they recited concerning the ḥāmī the saying [of the poet]:
181 - 8- حَماها أبو قابوسَ في عِزِّ ملكِه ... كما قد حَمَى أولادَ أولادهِ الفحلُ
(Abū Qābūs protected it in the might of his kingship, as the stallion has protected the offspring of his offspring.)

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَنَّ النفس بالنفس}: the verse. In «عليهم» the pronoun is for those who are Jews, and in «فيها» it is for the Torah. «أن النفس بالنفس»: «أنّ» with its noun and its khabar (predicate) is in the position of the accusative as the object of «كتبنا», the implied form being: "We prescribed for them the taking of a life for a life."

al-Kisāʾī read «والعينُ» and what is conjoined to it in the nominative; Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read all of it in the accusative; Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read the accusative in all except «الجروح», which they put in the nominative.

As for the reading of al-Kisāʾī, Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī accounted for it in three ways. First: the wāw conjoins a nominal sentence to a verbal sentence, so it conjoins sentences just as it conjoins single words. That is, His saying «والعين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بالعين» its khabar, and likewise what follows; and the nominal sentence is conjoined to the verbal one in His saying «وكتبنا». On this view it is the beginning of legislation and the statement of a new ruling not included in what was prescribed in the Torah. They said: it does not make the sentence share with what precedes it either in wording or in meaning. al-Zamakhsharī expressed this view as "resumption"; he said: "Or it is resumptive, and the meaning is: We made it obligatory upon them that a life is taken for a life, killed for it when it has killed it without right; and likewise the eye is gouged out for the eye, the nose is cut off for the nose, the ear is lopped or cut off for the ear, the tooth is pulled out for the tooth, and wounds are retaliation (qiṣāṣ), which is requital in kind." His implied form "a life is taken for a life" was anticipated by al-Fārisī, except that the latter assumed it in all the genitive phrases, i.e. "and the eye is taken for the eye," to the end. What al-Zamakhsharī assumed is very apt, for he assumed what each genitive phrase is attached to by what suits it: gouging for the eye, pulling out for the tooth, lopping for the ear, cutting off for the nose. However, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] seems to have disparaged it, since he assumed as the khabar to which the genitive phrase is attached a specific [notion of] being, whereas the rule in this is that only a general [notion of] being is assumed. He said: "al-Ḥawfī said: «بالنفس» is attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is 'is obligatory' or 'is established', and likewise «العين بالعين» and what follows; so he assumed the general [notion of] being, and the meaning is: its killing is established for the killing of the life." But before that he had said: "al-Zamakhsharī's saying should be taken as an explanation of the meaning, not an explanation of the parsing." Then he said: "So he — meaning al-Zamakhsharī — assumed something close to the general [notion of] being, namely 'taken'; for when you say «بعت الشياه شاةً بدرهم» (I sold the sheep a sheep for a dirham), the meaning is 'taken for a dirham'; and likewise 'the free for the free', i.e. taken."

The second way in al-Fārisī's account: the wāw conjoins a nominal sentence to the sentence in His saying {أَنَّ النفس بالنفس}, but in terms of meaning, not wording, since the meaning of "We prescribed for them that a life is for a life" is "We said to them: a life for a life." So the sentences fall under the prescribing in terms of meaning, not in terms of wording.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The wāw may be conjoining according to the meaning," and mentioned what was stated above; then he said: "Similar to it: since the meaning in His saying {يُطاف عليهم بكأسٍ من مَعين} is 'they are granted', «وحوراً عينا» was conjoined to it." So he compared this verse to that one because both share in regard to the meaning rather than the wording, and this is good. The Shaykh said: "This is conjunction by supposition (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum), since in His saying {أَنَّ النفس بالنفس} [the speaker] supposed «النفسُ بالنفسِ»," and he weakened it on the ground that conjunction by supposition is not subject to analogy.

al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this meaning, but expressed it in other terms; he said: "The nominative is [by conjunction] to the position of «أنَّ النفسَ», because the meaning is 'We prescribed for them: the life …', either by treating «كتبنا» as «قلنا» (We said), or because the meaning of the sentence «النفس بالنفس» is among the things on which writing falls, just as reading falls on it: you say «كتبتُ: الحمدُ لله» (I wrote: 'Praise be to Allah') and «قرأتُ: سورةٌ أنزلناها» (I read: 'A sūra We sent down'). That is why al-Zajjāj said: 'If «إنَّ النفسَ بالنفسِ» were read with a kasra, it would be correct'." The Shaykh said: "This is the second [view] in Abū ʿAlī's account, except that he departed from the technical terminology by making it a conjunction to the position, which it is not, because conjunction to the position is conjunction to the place [of an inflected element], which is restricted, and this is not of it. Do you not see that we do not say that «أنَّ النفسَ بالنفس» is in the position of the nominative, since what would require that is absent; rather, «أنّ» and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar whose wording and position are accusative, since the implied form is 'We prescribed for them the taking of a life'." I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not mean that «أنّ» and what falls within its scope are in the position of the nominative so that he conjoined the nominative to it, such that the Shaykh could bind him with [the fact] that its wording and position are accusative. He only meant that its noun's position was nominative before [«أنّ»] entered, so he took account of conjunction to that, as he took account of it with the noun of «إنَّ» with a kasra. This objection is not the Shaykh's own; Abū al-Baqāʾ anticipated him in it and he took it from him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may not be conjoined to «أَنَّ» and what it governs, because it and what it governs are in the position of the accusative." End of quote. It is worthless, for the reason given above.

Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma said: "The meaning of the statement is: We said to them: «النفسُ بالنفسِ». «العين بالعين» was construed according to this, because if «أنَّ» were omitted, the meaning would be sound with its omission just as it is sound with its presence, and «النفس» would be nominative. So «أنَّ» here has become like «إنَّ» with a kasra in that omitting it does not upset the sentence, and so conjunction to the position of its noun is permissible, just as it is permissible to the position of the noun of the kasra form. On this has been construed {أَنَّ الله بريءٌ مِّنَ المشركين وَرَسُولُهُ} [al-Tawba: 3]. Shaykh Abū ʿAmr — meaning Ibn al-Ḥājib — said: «ورسولُه» in the nominative is conjoined to the noun of «أنّ», even though it is with a fatḥa, because it has the status of the kasra form; and this is a point to which the grammarians have not drawn attention." [Translator's note: the source prints «برياء» in the verse and «أن الحاجب» for Ibn al-Ḥājib.] I say: On the contrary, the grammarians have drawn attention to this and disagreed about it: some allowed it, and that is correct. This occurs most often after «علم» (to know) or what has its meaning, as in his saying:
