1731 - وإلا فاعلموا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... بُغاةٌ ما بَقِينا في شقاق
(Otherwise, know that we and you are transgressors, as long as we remain in discord.)

and His saying {وَأَذَانٌ مِّنَ الله} [al-Tawba: 3], the verse, because «الأذان» means "announcement."

The third way: «العين» is conjoined to the latent (mustatir) nominative pronoun in the preposition phrase that serves as the khabar, the implied form being: "that the life is for the life — it and the eye," and likewise what follows; and the preposition phrase after it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) clarifying the meaning, since the nominative here is nominative as an agent through its conjunction to the latent agent. This was weakened on the grounds that these are permanent circumstantials, whereas the basic rule is that they be transitory; and that it entails conjunction to an attached nominative pronoun without separation between the two conjoined elements, without emphasis, and without separation by «لا» after the conjunction, as in His saying {مَآ أَشْرَكْنَا وَلاَ آبَاؤُنَا} [al-Anʿām: 148] — and this is not permissible according to the Basrans except out of poetic necessity. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Conjunction without emphasis was permissible, as in His saying {مَآ أَشْرَكْنَا وَلاَ آبَاؤُنَا} [al-Anʿām: 148]." I say: [there] the separation by «لا» between the conjunction and the conjoined element stood in place of the emphasis, so it is not parallel to it.

al-Fārisī [had a discussion with Sībawayh concerning His saying {ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا}, for Sībawayh makes the lengthening of the speech by «لا» a substitute for emphasis by the detached pronoun, just as] the speech is lengthened in their saying «حضر القاضيَ اليومَ امرأةٌ» (there came to the judge today a woman). al-Fārisī said: "This holds when it is before the conjunction; but when it comes after it, it does not take the place of the pronoun. Do you not see that if you said «حضر امرأةٌ القاضيَ اليومَ», the length of the speech would not suffice when it is in a place other than where it ought to occur?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Sībawayh's statement is sound on grammatical consideration, even if lengthening before the conjunction is more complete; for after the conjunction it has an effect, especially in this verse, because «لا» has bound the meaning, since a negation preceded it and it too negates [the association] of the fathers, so conjunction is possible."

Abū ʿUbayd chose the reading with all in the nominative, which is the transmission of al-Kisāʾī, because Anas reported it as the reading of the Prophet ﷺ. Anas also reported from him, upon him be peace, «أنْ النفسُ بالنفس», with «أَنْ» lightened and «النفس» in the nominative. There are two interpretations of it. First: «أَنْ» is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), omitted; «النفسُ بالنفس» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the lightened «أَنْ», as in His saying {أَنِ الحمد للَّهِ رَبِّ العالمين} [Yūnus: 10]; so the meaning is like the meaning of the doubled form. Second: it is the explicative «أَنْ», because it comes after what has the meaning of saying but not its letters, namely «كتبنا»; the implied form is "namely: a life for a life." This was preferred over the first because the first entails the lightened form occurring after a verb other than one of knowing, which is rare or disallowed. It may be said, however, that since «كتبنا» has the meaning of «قضينا» (We decreed), it comes close to the verbs of certainty.

As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and those with him, the accusative is on the noun of «أنّ» in wording, namely «النفس», and the preposition phrase after it is its khabar; «قصاصٌ» is the khabar of «الجروح», i.e. "and that wounds are retaliation." This is conjunction of sentences: we conjoin the noun to the noun and the khabar to the khabar, as in your saying «إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ وعمراً منطلق» (Zayd is standing and ʿAmr is departing), where you conjoined «عمراً» to «زيداً» and «منطلق» to «قائم». The prescription then covers all of it. However, there is in Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words what entails that «قصاص» is a khabar for all the accusatives together, for he said: "Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim read all of that in the accusative, and «قصاص» is the khabar of «أنّ»." Even though it is true that taking a life for a life and an eye for an eye is retaliation, here, by the indication of the parallelism, it has become specific to wounds; so [his statement] is open to question.

As for the reading of Abū ʿAmr and those with him, the accusatives are as stated for the reading of Nāfiʿ, but they did not put «الجروح» in the accusative, cutting it off from what precedes. There are four views on it: the three mentioned in accounting for the reading of al-Kisāʾī, whose explanation has been given; and fourth: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «قصاص», meaning that it is the beginning of legislation and the making known of a new ruling. Abū ʿAlī said: "As for «والجروحُ قصاص», whoever puts it in the nominative cuts it off from what precedes, and it admits these three views that we mentioned in the reading of whoever reads «والعينُ بالعين» in the nominative. «والجروحُ قصاص» may also be resumptive, not on the basis that it is among what was prescribed for them in the Torah, but by way of resumption and the beginning of legislation." End of quote. However, Abū Shāma said — before reporting these words from al-Fārisī —: "The third view, namely that it is conjoined to the pronoun in the khabar of «النفس», does not hold for the nominative of «الجروح», even if it is permissible for what precedes it. The reason is that the meaning is sound when you say 'taken — it — for the life' and 'the eye — it — is taken for the eye', but it is not sound [to say] 'and wounds are taken retaliation'. This is the meaning of my saying: 'Since His saying «الجروح قصاص» lacks the bāʾ in the khabar, it differs from the nouns before it, so the two were differentiated in case-inflection'." I say: what he said is clear, and many of the parsers did not notice it.

Some said: "«الجروح» was put in the nominative and not in the accusative following what precedes it only to distinguish between the general (mujmal) and the explained (mufassar)," meaning that His saying «النفسَ بالنفس والعينَ بالعين» is explained, not general, unlike «الجروح», which is general, since not every wound is subject to retaliation, but only one in which equivalence can be known and is possible, according to a well-known detailed treatment in the books of jurisprudence. Others said: the case-inflection was made different because of the difference and disparity of wounds, so the difference in it is like the difference alluded to. These two views have no sense; there is no necessary connection in any way between the difference in case-inflection and the difference in the rulings alluded to. I have mentioned them only to draw attention to their weakness.

Nāfiʿ read «والأذْن بالأذْن» — whether singular or dual, as in His saying {كَأَنَّ في أُذُنَيْهِ وَقْراً} [Luqmān: 7] — with a sukūn on the dhāl, which is a lightening of the ḍamma form, like «عُنْق» for «عُنُق» (neck); the rest read it with a ḍamma, which is the original. A muḍāf must be omitted in His saying {والجروح قِصَاصٌ}, either from the first or from the second, whether it is read in the nominative or the accusative; its implied form is: "and the ruling on wounds is retaliation," or "and wounds are subject to retaliation."

«القِصاص» is requital in kind (al-muqāṣṣa); it was discussed in al-Baqara. Ubayy read «النفس» and the four after it in the accusative, and «أنِ الجروحُ» with the addition of the light «أن» and «الجروحُ» in the nominative. On this reading it must be the lightened [«أنّ»], and it may not be the explicative one — unlike the reading of Anas from him, upon him be peace, mentioned above, with «أن» lightened and «النفس» in the nominative, where we allowed both views. That is because if you took it as explicative and made it conjoined to what precedes, it would be invalid, since «كتبنا» must be a governor because of the doubled «أنّ», but not a governor because of the explicative «أنْ»; and when its control over it is negated, its sharing with what precedes is negated, because where there is no governing there is no sharing. But if you make it the lightened one, its governing applies, and the governing entails sharing, in that the meaning of prescription falls on both.

Ubayy read: «فهو كفارتُه له» (it is his expiation for him), i.e. the giving in charity is an expiation, meaning the expiation he deserves, without anything being diminished from it; and it magnifies what he did, as in His saying {فَأَجْرُهُ عَلَى الله} [al-Shūrā: 40].

His saying: {فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ}: i.e. with the retaliation connected with the life, or the eye, or what follows it. «فهو», i.e. that giving in charity: the pronoun refers to the maṣdar (verbal noun) because its verb indicates it, as in His saying, Exalted is He, {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. On the pronoun in «له» there are three views. First — and it is the evident one —: it refers to the one who gives in charity, meaning the one entitled to retaliation, whether the injured person or the guardian, i.e. the giving in charity is an expiation for the one who gives up his right in charity. A large group of the Companions and those after them held this. Second: the pronoun means the offender, while the one giving in charity is, as stated, the one entitled to retaliation; the meaning is that when the entitled person gives [his right] in charity to the offender, that giving is an expiation for the offender, in that he is not held to account for it. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also said: «فهو كفارةٌ له», i.e. for the offender: when the holder of the right forgoes [it], what was binding on him falls from him." Ibn ʿAbbās, among others, held this. Third: the pronoun also refers to the one giving in charity, but what is meant by him is the offender himself. The meaning of his being one who gives in charity is that when he commits an offence and no one knows of it, and he makes it known himself, that confession is like a charity that effaces his sin and his offence. Mujāhid said this. It is related of ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr that he injured a man during his circumambulation, and the man did not know who had injured him, so ʿUrwa said to him: "I injured you, and I am ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr; if anything concerns you in it, here I am." On this interpretation, «تصدَّق» may be from «الصدَقة» (charity) or from «الصِدْق» (truthfulness).

I say: the first is clear; the second means that he takes truthfulness upon himself with effort, because that is something hard.

His saying: {وَمَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم}: «مَنْ» may be conditional, which is the evident view, or relative, with the fāʾ in the khabar redundant (zāʾida) because of its resemblance to a conditional. «هم» in His saying {هُمُ الكافرون} and its parallels is a separating pronoun (faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ. All of it is evident from what was said on its parallels.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ}: there are eleven aspects concerning its accusative. The first: that it is accusative by «اتقوا», i.e. "fear Allah on the day of His gathering the messengers"; al-Ḥawfī said this. This ought not to be permissible, because commanding them to taqwā on the Day of Resurrection cannot be, since it is not a day of obligation and testing. For that reason al-Wāḥidī said: "«اليوم» is not made accusative as an adverb of the fearing, because they were not commanded to fear on that day, but rather as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as in His words: {واتقوا يَوْماً} [al-Baqara: 48]." The second: that it is accusative by an implied «اتقوا», indicated by «واتقوا الله». Al-Zajjāj said: "It is carried on His words «واتقوا الله», then He said «يوم يجمع», i.e. and fear that day." So the mention of fearing in the first indicated fearing in this verse; and it is not accusative as an adverb of the fearing, because they were not commanded to fear on that day, but as mafʿūl bihi, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {واتقوا يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئاً} [al-Baqara: 48]. The third: that it is accusative by an implied «اذكروا» (remember). The fourth: by an implied «احذروا» (beware). The fifth: that it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from the Name of Majesty. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يوم يجمع» is a badal from the accusative in «واتقوا الله», and it is of the badal of inclusion, as though it were said: and fear Allah on the day of His gathering." End of quote. On this aspect a muḍāf must be omitted so that this expression of his is sound, for its outward sense is not good, because inclusion cannot be ascribed to the Creator, the Exalted, by whichever of the grammarians' doctrines on inclusion we explain it. The implied form is: "and fear the punishment of Allah on the day He gathers His messengers"; for the punishment includes its time, or its time includes it, or their governing word includes both, according to the disagreement over explaining the badal of inclusion. So the impossibility of these expressions in relation to the noble Name of Majesty has become clear to you. The Shaykh considered this aspect unlikely because of the long separation by two clauses; but it is not unlikely, for these two clauses complete the meaning of the first clause. The sixth: that it is accusative by «لا يَهْدي»; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. He will not guide them to the path of Paradise on that day, as is done with others." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. He will not guide them on that day to an argument or to the path of Paradise."

The seventh: that it is a mafʿūl bihi governed by «اسمعوا»; in that case a muḍāf must be omitted, because time is not heard. Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed it as: "and hear the report of the day He gathers". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned only these two aspects, beginning with the first of them. There is a point to consider in its being accusative by «لا يَهْدي», in that He does not guide them absolutely, neither on that day nor in this world — I mean those judged to be transgressors. In al-Zamakhsharī's assumption «لايهديهم إلى طريق الجنة» (He will not guide them to the path of Paradise) there is an inclination towards his doctrine that negating absolute guidance is not permissible of Allah the Exalted; for that reason he specified that to which guidance is given and did not mention anything else. What also made that easy in his view is its being on a day in which there is no obligation; as for in the abode of obligation, the Muʿtazilī does not permit negation of guidance absolutely to be attributed to Allah the Exalted at all.

The eighth: that it is accusative by «اسمعوا»; al-Ḥawfī said this. There is a point to consider in it, because they are not obliged to hear on that day, since what is meant by hearing is the hearing of obligation. The ninth: that it is accusative by an implied verb coming after, i.e. "on the day Allah gathers the messengers, such and such will happen"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The tenth — I say: it is permissible that the question be of the chapter of iʿmāl (the governing of competing verbs), for each of these three preceding governing words can validly govern it, as evidenced by the scholars' permitting that in it. The question would then be one in which three governing words compete, namely «اتقوا», «اسمعوا» and «لا يَهْدي», and it would be a case of the last one governing, because [the object] has been omitted from the first two; nothing in the grammatical craft prevents it. As for the meaning, I have already stated that the accusative of «يوم» by any of the three is not apparent, because the meaning rejects it; I only permitted it in keeping with what they said and permitted, especially Abū al-Baqāʾ, who mentioned nothing but its being accusative by «اسمعوا» or by «لايهدي»; likewise al-Ḥawfī permitted it to be accusative by «اتقوا» and by «اسمعوا». The eleventh: that it is accusative by «قالوا: لا علمَ لنا», i.e. the messengers said, on the day of their gathering and of Allah's saying to them "What response were you given?" [Translator's note: the source prints «اقولوا»; this appears to be a misprint for «قالوا» of the verse; translated accordingly.] The Shaykh chose this over everything preceding, and said: "It is the counterpart of what we said concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلاَئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الأرض خَلِيفَةً قَالُواْ أَتَجْعَلُ} [al-Baqara: 30]." And it is a good aspect.

His words: {مَاذَآ أُجِبْتُمْ}: there are four views concerning it. The first: that «ماذا» is like a single noun, in which the interrogative side predominates, and its position is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by what comes after it; the implied form being: "what response were you given?" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ماذا أُجِبْتُم» is accusative as its maṣdar, in the sense of: what response were you given? Had the answer been intended, it would have been said: بماذا أُجبتم" — i.e. had the speech given in answer been intended, it would have been said: بماذا (with what). An example of «ماذا» as a whole coming as a maṣdar is his saying:

183 - 3- ماذا يَغِيرُ ابنَتَيْ ربعٍ عويلُهما ... لا تَرْقُدانِ ولا بُؤْسَ لِمَنْ رَقَدا
(What does their wailing avail the two daughters of Rabʿ? They do not sleep, yet there is no misery for one who sleeps.)

The second: that «ما» is interrogative, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» is its khabar (predicate), being a relative meaning «الذي» because the two stated conditions are fulfilled, and «أُجِبْتُم» is its ṣila (relative clause), the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "what is that with which you were answered?"; so he omitted the returning pronoun. Al-Ḥawfī said this. This is not permissible, because it is not permissible to omit a genitive returning pronoun unless the relative is itself made genitive by a preposition like the preposition governing the returning pronoun, and their attachments are the same, as in «مررتُ بالذي مررتَ», i.e. «به»; and this relative is not genitive. Were you to say «رأيت الذي مررتَ», meaning «مررتَ به», it would not be permitted — unless it is claimed that it was omitted by stages: the preposition is omitted, so the verb reaches the pronoun directly, and then it is omitted, as in His words: {وَخُضْتُمْ كالذي خاضوا} [al-Tawba: 69] in one of its aspects, and His words: {فاصدع بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ} [al-Ḥijr: 94] in one of its two aspects. On the whole, it is weak. The third: that «ما» is genitive by an implied preposition, and when that was omitted it remained in the position of accusative; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it and weakened the aspect before it — i.e. «ذا» being a relative — for he said: "«ماذا» is in the position of accusative by «أُجِبْتُم», and the preposition is omitted; «ما» and «ذا» here are like a single noun. It is weak to make «ما» mean «الذي», because there is no returning pronoun here, and omitting the returning pronoun together with the preposition is weak." I say: as for his making the omission of the genitive returning pronoun weak, that is correct; its explanation and the drawing of attention to it have preceded. As for omitting the preposition and making its genitive noun accusative, that too is weak, not permissible except in poetic licence, as in his saying:

183 - 4- فَبِتُّ كأنَّ العائداتِ فَرَشْنَنِي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I spent the night as though the women visiting the sick had spread [thorns] for me…)

and his saying:

183 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأُخْفي الذي لولا الأَسَى لقَضاني
(…and I hide that which, were it not for grief, would have finished me.)

and his saying:

183 - 6- تَمُرُّون الديارَ ولم تَعُوجُوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You pass the dwellings and do not turn aside…)

The verification of that and the exception of the regular cases from it have preceded. So he fled from something weak and fell into something weaker. The fourth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its meaning is: with what did the nations answer?" So he made «ماذا» an allusion to that with which the answer was given, not to the maṣdar. Furthermore, this statement of his may be like what was related from al-Ḥawfī in making «ما» an interrogative mubtadaʾ and «ذا» its khabar as a relative, and attention has been drawn to its weakness. It may also be that «ماذا» as a whole is like an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «أُجِبْتُم» its khabar, the returning pronoun being omitted as he assumed; this too is weak, because the returning pronoun of a mubtadaʾ, when it is genitive, is not omitted except in places of which this is not one; were you to say «زيدٌ مررتُ» it would not be permitted. Since the weakness of these aspects is clear, the first is preferred.

The majority read «أُجِبْتم» as passive; and in the omission of the agent here there is an eloquence and rhetoric whose depth cannot be reached, since He confined the address to His messengers without anyone else being mentioned with them, to raise their standing, honour them and single them out. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ḥaywa read «أَجَبْتم» as active, with the object omitted, i.e. "what did you answer your nations when they denied you and harmed you?"; in it there is a rebuke to the nations, but it is not equal to the first in rhetoric.

His words: {إِنَّكَ أَنتَ عَلاَّمُ الغيوب} are like His words: {إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ العليم الحكيم} [verse: 32] in al-Baqara. The majority read «عَلاَّمُ الغيوب» in the nominative; it was read in the accusative, and there are aspects concerning that which Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] mentioned, namely: specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), the vocative, and a description of the noun of «إنَّ». He said: "It was read in the accusative on the view that the speech is complete at His words «إنك أنت», i.e. You are the One described by Your well-known attributes of knowledge and others; then «عَلاَّم الغيوب» is accusative by specification, or by the vocative, or it is a description of the noun of «إنَّ»." The Shaykh said: "It is on the omission of the khabar because the meaning is understood, so the speech is completed by what is implied in His words «إنك أنتَ», i.e. You are the One described by Your well-known attributes of knowledge and others." Then he said: "Al-Zamakhsharī said: then it is accusative…", and he quoted it to the end. So he claimed that al-Zamakhsharī assumed an omitted khabar for «إنك»; but al-Zamakhsharī does not intend that at all, nor does he approve of it. He only means that this pronoun, by being for Allah the Exalted, is what indicates those stated attributes, which are inseparable from it. This meaning is what rhetoric requires and what Abū al-Qāsim dived [for], not what the Shaykh assumed, giving the impression that he had brought it of his own accord.

By specification he means the accusative of praise, not the specification that resembles the vocative, for the condition of that is that it be medial. However, the Shaykh refuted Abū al-Qāsim's saying "it may be a description of the noun of «إنَّ»", on the grounds that its noun here is a pronoun of the person addressed, and a pronoun is not described at all according to the Basrans, while according to al-Kisāʾī only the third-person pronoun may be described, because of its vagueness, in their saying «مررت به المسكينِ», even though it can be interpreted as a badal. This is a clear refutation; though it could be said that by "description" he meant the badal, which is Sībawayh's expression — he uses "description" and means badal — so he has an example in his imam, and the consequence is shared: whatever is an answer on behalf of Sībawayh is an answer on his behalf. But there remains in it [the problem of] a badal with a derived word, which is easier than the first. I have not seen them interpret it according to the dialect of those who put both parts in the accusative with «إنَّ» and its sisters, as in his saying:

1837 - إنَّ العجوزَ خَبَّةً جَرُوزاً ... [and his saying]:
(The old woman is deceitful and voracious…)

183 - 8-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . إنَّ حُرَّا سَنا أُسْدا
(…our guards are lions.)

[and his saying]:

183 - 9- ليتَ الشبابَ هو الرَّجِيعُ على الفتى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Would that youth returned to the young man…)

[and his saying]:

184 - 0- كأنَّ أُذْنيه إذا تَشَوَّفا ... قادِمةً أو قَلَماً مُحْرَّفا
(As though his two ears, when they pricked up, were a front feather or a slanted reed pen.)

Had this been held, it would have been correct.

«عَلاَّمُ» is a form of intensification (mubālagha), so it governs what follows it in the accusative by implication. By this too al-Zamakhsharī is refuted, assuming the validity of describing the pronoun is conceded, inasmuch as it is indefinite, because its annexation is not pure [i.e. does not make it definite] while what it describes is definite. The majority read the ʿayn of «الغيوب» with ḍamma, which is the original; Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read it with kasra. The disagreement extends to other words, such as «البيوت والجيوب والعيون والشيوخ». All this has been set out in al-Baqara at the mention of {البيوت} [verse: 189], and each of these words will come, attributed to its reader, in its sūra, if Allah the Exalted wills. الغيب is made plural here, though it is a maṣdar, because of the variety of its kinds; and if what is meant by it is the absent thing, or we say it is lightened from the pattern فَيْعِل, as was established in al-Baqara, then it is clear.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَن يَمْلِكُ}: the fāʾ conjoins this clause to an implied clause before it, the implied form being: "Say: they have lied — or is the matter not so? — then who has power …?" His saying «من الله» admits two possibilities. The more apparent of them: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. The second, mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيئاً», meaning that it was originally an adjective of the indefinite noun, was put before it and so became accusative as a ḥāl; this is far-fetched or impermissible. His saying {فَمَنْ} is an interrogative of rebuke and affirmation, and according to the majority it indicates the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition after it. His saying {وَمَن فِي الأرض} is of the category of conjoining the general to the specific, so as to intensify the denial of divinity of the two of them; it is as though He stated them explicitly twice: once by mentioning them individually and once by their inclusion in the general term. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl from the Messiah, his mother and those on earth, or from «مَنْ» alone because of its generality. It may also be accusative as tawkīd (emphasis), like «كل»; some grammarians mentioned it among the words of tawkīd. His saying {يَخْلُق} is a clause with no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {فَلِمَ}: this fāʾ is the answer of an implied condition; this is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "If it is true that you are the sons of Allah and His beloved, then why do you sin and are punished?" It may also be like the fāʾ before it, in being a conjunction joining it to an implied clause, i.e. "you have lied — so why does He punish you?" The bāʾ in «بذنوبكم» is causal. «مِمَّن خلق» is an adjective of «بشر», so it is in the position of the nominative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ}: its parallel has preceded. His saying «على فترة»: there are three views on it. The most apparent of them: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاءكم», i.e. he came to you at a time of a lull in the sending of messengers and a break in revelation; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يبين», i.e. he explains while being in a lull. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in «لكم». On these two views it is attached to an omitted element. «من الرسل» is an adjective of «فترة», on the basis that the meaning of «من» is the beginning of the extent, i.e. a lull issuing from the sending of messengers. His saying: {أَن تَقُولُواْ}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī supposed it as "out of dislike that you should say", and Abū al-Baqāʾ as "for fear that you should say"; the first is better. His saying «يبيِّن»: it may be that no object at all is intended for it, the meaning being: he gives you explanation; or the object may be omitted, either because the wording indicates it — namely what preceded in His saying {يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيراً} [al-Māʾida: 15] — or because the situation indicates it, i.e. he explains to you that over which you used to differ. «ومن بشير» is the fāʿil (agent), «مِنْ» being added to it because the two conditions are present; «ولا نذير» is conjoined to its wording, and were it read in the nominative in consideration of its position, that would be permissible. His saying {فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ} is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "do not make excuses, for there has come to you …". The clauses after this have clear i'rab because of their parallels that have preceded.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {على أَدْبَارِكُمْ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «ترتدَّوا», i.e. do not turn back, reversing; it may also be attached to the verb itself before it. His saying: {فَتَنْقَلِبُوا}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: that it is jussive (majzūm) by conjunction with the verb of prohibition. The second: that it is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أنْ» after the fāʾ in answer to the prohibition. «خاسرين» is a ḥāl. Ibn Muḥayṣin read, here and throughout the Qurʾān, {يا قومُ} with ḍamma on the mīm, and it is also narrated as a reading from Ibn Kathīr. Its justification is that it is a dialect form in the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, like the reading {قل ربُّ احكمْ بالحق}; I have explained this issue before. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read {يا قوميَ ادخلوا} with fatḥa on the yāʾ.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {فَإِنَّا دَاخِلُونَ}: i.e. "then we will enter the land"; He omitted the object because it is indicated.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مِنَ الذين يَخَافُونَ}: this preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «رجلان». The object of «يخافون» is omitted, its implied form being: they fear Allah, or they fear the enemy, but Allah the Exalted made them firm through faith and trust in Him so that they said these words. The first supposition is supported by the explicit mention of the object in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: {يخافون الله}. These two interpretations are based on what is well known among the majority, namely that the two men who said that were of the people of Moses, and they are Joshua (Yūshaʿ) and Caleb (Kālib). It was also said: the two men were of the tyrants (al-jabbārīn), but Allah favoured them with faith, so that they said these words, urging them against their own people because of their enmity to them in religion. On this view the object of «يخافون» may be as preceded, i.e. they fear Allah or the enemy, the meaning being as preceded; or the object may be a pronoun referring to the relative noun, the nominative pronoun in «يخافون» being the pronoun of the Children of Israel, the implied form being: "of those whom the Children of Israel feared". Al-Zamakhsharī supported this interpretation by the reading of those who read «يُخافون» in the passive, and also by His saying {أَنْعَمَ الله عَلَيْهِمَا}, for he said: "The reading of those who read «يُخافون» with ḍamma is a witness for it, and so is «أنعم الله عليهما», as though it were said: of those who are feared." End of quotation. The mentioned reading is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid. Al-Zamakhsharī also put forward another possibility in this reading, namely that it is from «الإخافة» (causing fear), its meaning being: of those who are made to fear Allah through reminder and admonition, or whom Allah's threat of punishment makes fear. The reading also admits another view: that the meaning of «يُخافون» is: they are held in awe and revered, and people refer to them because of their excellence and goodness. Given these last two possibilities, there is no preponderance in this reading for the two men being of the tyrants. As for his saying "and likewise «أنعم الله عليهما»", i.e. in its also favouring their being of the tyrants, that is not apparent, because this description is shared between Joshua and Caleb and others whom Allah has favoured.

His saying: {أَنْعَمَ الله عَلَيْهِمَا}: there are five views on this clause. The most apparent of them: that it is a second adjective, so its position is the nominative; and here the more eloquent of the two usages was employed, in that the description by the preposition phrase was put before the description by the clause, because it is closer to the single word. The second: that it is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa); this too is apparent. The third: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَخافون»; Makkī said it. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «رجلان»; the ḥāl came from an indefinite noun because it is specified by the adjective. The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the preposition phrase, namely «مِنَ الذين», because it occurs as an adjective of a qualified noun. If you make it a ḥāl, «قد» must be implied with the past verb, according to a disagreement over the issue that has preceded.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا}: «ما» is a temporal maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya), and «داموا» is its ṣila (relative clause); it is the incomplete «دام» [of the kāna sisters], and its khabar (predicate) is the preposition phrase after it. This adverb is a badal (substitute) from «أبداً», and it is a badal of part from whole, because «الأبد» covers the whole of future time, and the tyrants' remaining in it is part of it. The apparent wording of al-Zamakhsharī allows it to be a badal of the whole from the whole or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — and [explicative] apposition may occur between two indefinite nouns, according to a discussion on it that has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أبداً» attaches the emphasised negation to long-extended time, and «ما داموا فيها» is an explanation of the matter." This wording allows it to be a badal of part from whole, because the badal of part from whole explains what is meant, as in «أكلت الرغيف ثلثه» ("I ate the loaf, a third of it"); it allows it to be a badal of the whole from the whole, for that is also an explanation and clarification of the first, as in «رأيت زيداً أخاك» ("I saw Zayd, your brother"); and it allows it to be an ʿaṭf bayān.

His saying: {وَرَبُّكَ}: there are four views on it. One of them: that it is nominative by conjunction with the latent (mustatir) agent in «اذهب»; that was permissible because of the emphasis by the pronoun. The second: that it is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and let your Lord go", so it would be a conjoining of clauses; I have previously transmitted this view and refuted it, and [shown] its contradiction of Sībawayh's explicit statement, at His saying, Exalted is He: {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الجنة} [al-Baqara: 35]. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, the wāw being circumstantial. The fourth: that the wāw is a conjunction and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is also omitted, and this clause has no grammatical position because it is a supplication, the implied form being: "and may your Lord help you". His saying: «ههنا قاعدون»: «هنا» alone is the adverb of place that is not inflected except by being made genitive with «مِنْ» and «إلى»; «ها» before it is for drawing attention, as with the other demonstratives; and what governs it is «قاعدون». It has been permitted that it be the khabar of «إنَّ» and «قاعدون» a second khabar, but that is far-fetched. Outside the Qurʾān, when an adverb fit to serve as a khabar comes together with another descriptive word, the adverb may be made the khabar and the descriptive word a ḥāl (circumstantial), or the khabar may be the descriptive word with the adverb accusative by it, as in this verse.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَفَّيْنَا على آثَارِهِم بِعَيسَى}: the meaning of «قَفَّينا» was given in al-Baqara, [namely] that it is from «قفا يقفو», i.e. he followed behind him. In His saying {على آثَارِهِم بِعَيسَى}, both prepositional phrases are attached to it, on the basis of its implying the meaning "We brought him upon their traces, following them." It was also stated there that the doubling in it is not for making it transitive, for a reason mentioned there. Its explanation is that «قفا» is transitive to one object before the doubling; the Exalted said: {وَلاَ تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ} [al-Isrāʾ: 36], where «ما» is a relative meaning «الذي» and is the object. The Arabs say «قَفا فلانٌ أثرَ فلانٍ», i.e. he followed him. If the doubling were for transitivity, it would take two objects, and the construction would be «ثم قَفَّيْنا هم عيسى بن مريم», with «هم» the second object and «عيسى» the first. But it has been given an implied meaning (taḍmīn), as stated above, and therefore it is made transitive by the bāʾ and «على».

al-Zamakhsharī said: "«قَفَّيْتُه» is like «عَقَّبْتُه» when you made him follow; then one says «قَفَّيْتُه بفلان», like «عَقَّبْتُه به», making it transitive to the second by adding the bāʾ. If you say: where is the first object? I say: it is omitted, and the adverbial phrase «على آثارهم» as it were takes its place, because when He made him follow on his trace, He made him follow him." His words here lean towards [the view] that the doubled «قَفَّيْته» is like the triliteral «قفوتُه», which he then made transitive by the bāʾ. Even though this is correct inasmuch as the pattern فَعَّل has occurred in the sense of the bare فَعَل, as with «قَدَّر» and «قَدَر», some claimed that a verb transitive to one object is not made transitive to a second by the bāʾ: you do not say, for «طعم زيدٌ اللحمَ» (Zayd ate the meat), «أطعمتُ زيداً باللحم». But the correct view is that it is rare, not impossible; some words of this kind have occurred. They said «صَكَّ الحجرُ الحجرَ» (the stone struck the stone) and then they say «صككتُ الحجرَ بالحجرِ» (I struck the stone with the stone); and «دفع زيدٌ عمراً» (Zayd pushed ʿAmr) and then «دَفَعْتُ زيداً بعمرو», i.e. I made him push him. So his words are either inadmissible or to be taken as the rare usage. I have pointed to the rejection of the claim that the object is omitted in cases like {وَقَفَّيْنَا} [verse 87] in al-Baqara, so let it be sought there.

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] took issue with his saying «فقد قَفَّى به إياه», in that he used the detached pronoun though able to use the attached one, so that he would say «قَفَّيْتُه به». He said: "If you said «زيدٌ ضربْتُ بسوطٍ إياه» (Zayd — I struck with a whip him), it would not be permissible except out of poetic necessity; rather [one says] «ضربتُه بسوط»." This is worthless, because that is of the type of His saying {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 1] and {وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 131]; its full treatment has been given.

The pronoun in «آثارهم» is either for the prophets, because of His saying {يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النبيون}, or for those on whom those rulings were prescribed. The first is more evident, because of His saying elsewhere: {بِرُسُلِنَا وَقَفَّيْنَا بِعِيسَى ابن مَرْيَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 27]. «مصدقاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عيسى». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida)," and he said the same about the second «مصدقاً». This is evident, for it is inherent in the messenger, and in the Injīl, which is a divine scripture, that they confirm [what came before].

«لِما» is attached to it. His saying {مِنَ التوراة} is a ḥāl, either from the relative, namely «ما» governed in the genitive by the lām, or from the pronoun latent in the adverbial phrase because it occurs as a ṣila (relative clause). It may also be explaining the genus of the relative.

His saying: {وَآتَيْنَاهُ}: two views are possible. First: it is conjoined to His saying {وَقَفَّيْنَا}, so it has no position, just as that to which it is conjoined has no position. Second: it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, conjoined to the first «مصدقاً», if the second «مصدقاً» is also made a ḥāl from «عيسى», as will come; and the clause may be a ḥāl even if the second «مصدقاً» is not a ḥāl from «عيسى».

His saying: {فِيهِ هُدًى}: «فيه» alone may be a ḥāl from «الإنجيل», with «هُدى» its agent, because when it depends on the one to whom the ḥāl refers it puts the agent in the nominative. Or «فيه» may be a fronted khabar (predicate) and «هدى» a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being a ḥāl. «ومصدقاً» is a ḥāl conjoined to the position of «فيه هدى» under both considerations: I mean the consideration that «فيه» alone is the ḥāl, so that you conjoin this ḥāl to it, and that «فيه هدى» is a nominal clause whose position is accusative and «مصدقاً» is conjoined to its position. Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this. However, this is outweighed for two reasons. First: the basic form of the ḥāl is to be a single word, and a prepositional phrase is closer to a single word than clauses are. Second: a nominal clause occurring as a ḥāl mostly comes with the wāw even if it contains a pronoun, so much so that al-Farrāʾ — followed by al-Zamakhsharī — claimed that this [omission of the wāw] is permissible only as an anomaly. That this «مصدقاً» is a ḥāl from «الإنجيل» is the evident view. Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib — followed by Abū al-Baqāʾ — allowed the second «مصدقاً» to be also a ḥāl from «عيسى», repeated for emphasis. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is somewhat awkward as regards the coherence of the meanings." I say: if we make «وآتيناه» a ḥāl from him, and conjoin this other ḥāl to it, I do not know what the awkwardness is from the stated standpoint.

His saying: {وَهُدًى}: the majority read it in the accusative, and it is a ḥāl, either from «الإنجيل», this ḥāl being conjoined to what precedes it, or from «عيسى», i.e. possessing guidance and admonition, or guiding; or he was made guidance itself, by way of hyperbole. al-Zamakhsharī allowed the two to be accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), making the governor His saying, Exalted is He, {آتيناه}. He said: "And [it is possible] that the two are accusative as objects of purpose, because of His saying {وليحكمَ}, as though it were said: 'For guidance and for admonition We gave him the Injīl, and for judging'."

Abū al-Baqāʾ and others allowed the governor to be «قَفَّينا», i.e. "We sent [him] following for guidance and admonition." If they are made objects of purpose, their being attributed to Allah the Exalted, not to the Injīl, ought to be assumed so that the accusative is valid, for its condition is that the object of purpose be one with its governor in agent and time. That is why, when the agent differed in His saying «وليحكم أهل الإنجيل», it was made to reach it by the lām; and also because it differed from it in time, since the time of judging is future while the time of the prophets is past — unlike guidance and admonition, which are concurrent in time with the giving.

«للمتقين» may be an adjective of «موعظة»; or the lām may be redundant (zāʾida), strengthening, and «المتقين» the object of «موعظة». The feminine tāʾ did not prevent it from governing, because it is built on it, as in his saying:

1732 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… and a fear of your punishment …) [Translator's note: the verse is only partially quoted in the source.]

The discussion of «الإنجيل», its derivation and al-Ḥasan's reading of it was given earlier, which makes repeating it unnecessary. al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim read «وهدى وموعظة» in the nominative; its justification is that it is the khabar of a concealed mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and it is guidance and admonition."

semin-durr:110-110.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذْ قَالَ الله}: there are aspects concerning it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «يوم يجمع». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: He rebukes the unbelievers by questioning the messengers about how they were answered, and by enumerating the great signs He manifested at their hands, which some of them denied, calling them sorcerers, while others exceeded the bound and made him and his mother two gods." [Translator's note: the source prints «إليهن», evidently a misprint for «إلهين» (two gods); translated accordingly.] When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this aspect, he interpreted «قال» in it as «يقول», [saying] that «إذ», though it is for the past, occurs here as a narration of a present state. The second: that it is accusative by an implied «اذكر» (remember). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is permissible that the implied form be: إذ يقول (when He says)", meaning that the past must be interpreted as future; this is as he held in the aspect before it. Likewise Ibn ʿAṭiyya interpreted it as «يقول», for he said: "Its implied form is: remember, O Muḥammad, when…; and «قال» here means «يقول», because the outward sense of this saying is that it is on the Day of Resurrection, as a preface to His words: {أَأَنتَ قُلتَ لِلنَّاسِ}." The third: that it is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is when He said"; al-Wāḥidī mentioned it. This is weak, because «إذ» is not freely inflected; likewise the view that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) with an implied «اذكر»; the verification of that has preceded — unless al-Wāḥidī means by its being a khabar that it is an adverb standing in place of a khabar, as in «زيدٌ عندك»; then it is permissible.

His words: {ياعيسى ابن مَرْيَمَ}: the discussion of the derivation and meanings of these words has preceded. «ابن» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عيسى», accusative because it is a muḍāf. This is a general, useful rule: when the single, definite vocative noun whose ḍamma is overt is described by «ابن» or «ابنة», and the ابن or ابنة occurs between two proper names, or two nouns identical in wording, and nothing separates ابن from what it describes, certain rulings apply to it. Among them: it is permissible to make the ḍamma-vocative follow the vowel of the nūn of «ابن», so that it takes fatḥa, as in «يا زيدَ بن عمرو، ويا هندَ ابنة بكر», with fatḥa or ḍamma on the dāl of «زيد» and «هند». If the ḍamma is implied, as in our case — for the ḍamma is implied on the alif of «عيسى» — is it to be assumed indeclinable on fatḥa by assimilation, as with the overt ḍamma? There is disagreement. The majority hold it impermissible, since there is no benefit in it: it was only for assimilation, and this meaning is absent with an implied ḍamma. Al-Farrāʾ permitted it, treating the implied like the overt, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him, for he said: "It is permissible that there be a fatḥa on the alif of «عيسى», because it has been described by «ابن» and stands between two proper names, and that there be a ḍamma on it; it is like your saying «يا زيد بن عمرو» with fatḥa or ḍamma on the dāl."

What the two of them said is not far-fetched, and it is supported by a question agreed upon by all: when the vocative is indeclinable on kasra, for example, as in «يا هؤلاء», they permitted two aspects in its description: the nominative and the accusative. They say «يا هؤلاء العقلاءِ والعقلاءُ», with the accusative or nominative of العقلاء. They said: the nominative is in consideration of that ḍamma implied on «هؤلاء», since it is a single definite noun, and the accusative is according to its position. So they took the implied ḍamma into account in agreement, even though it is absent from the wording. One might distinguish [the two cases] in that with «هؤلاء» we are compelled to assume that vowel because it is a single definite noun, so it is as though it were pronounced, unlike assuming the fatḥa here.

Al-Wāḥidī said concerning «يا عيسى»: "It is permissible that it be in the position of accusative [because it is in the intention of annexation; then he made ابن an emphasis of it; and everything] like this permits both aspects, as in «يا زيد بن عمرو»." And he recited:

184 - 1- يا حَكَمُ بنُ المنذرِ بن الجارودُ ... أنتَ الجوادُ بنُ الجوادِ بنُ الجودْ
سُرادِقُ المجدِ عليك ممدودْ ...
(O Ḥakam son of al-Mundhir son of al-Jārūd, you are the generous one, son of the generous, son of generosity; the pavilion of glory is spread over you.)

with the first [ابن] in the accusative or nominative, as we have explained. Al-Tibrīzī said: "The more apparent view in my opinion is that the position of «عيسى» is accusative, because you [make the noun together with its descriptive, when you annex it to the proper name,] like a single annexed thing." The Shaykh said: what these two said does not resemble the grammarians' speech at all; rather they say: the fatḥa is for assimilation, and the quiescent letter [the bāʾ of ابن] is not counted because it is a barrier that is not impenetrable. I say: al-Zamakhsharī — and [claiming] he is not one of the grammarians is to deny the self-evident — said at His words {إِذْ قَالَ الحواريون ياعيسى ابن مَرْيَمَ} [al-Māʾida: 112]: "«عيسى» is in the position of accusative by the assimilation of its vowel to the vowel of «ابن», as in your saying «يا زيدَ بنَ عمرو», and this is the widespread dialect; and it is permissible that it be with ḍamma, as in your saying «يا زيدُ بنَ عمرو». The evidence for it is his saying:

184 - 2- أحارِ بن عمروٍ كأني خَمِرْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O Ḥār[ith] son of ʿAmr, it is as though I were intoxicated…)

because truncation (tarkhīm) occurs only in a vocative with ḍamma." End of quote. So he needed to excuse himself for assuming the ḍamma, and cited the verse for it because it differs from the well-known dialect.

My saying "single" guards against the extended [vocative]. My saying "definite" guards against the indefinite, as in «يا رجلاً ابن رجل» when you do not intend a particular individual by it. My saying "whose ḍamma is overt" guards against the like of «يا موسى بن فلان» and the like of the noble verse. My saying "by «ابن»" guards against description by something else, as in «يا زيدُ صاحبَنا». My saying "between two proper names or two nouns identical in wording" guards against the like of «يا زيد بن أخينا». My saying "not separated" guards against the like of «يا زيدُ العاقلُ ابنَ عمرو». In all of these only the ḍamma is permissible. As for my saying "rulings": among them is what I mentioned of the permissibility of fatḥa by assimilation; among them is the omission of its alif in writing; and among them is the omission of its tanwīn outside the vocative, since the vocative has no tanwīn.

My saying "described" guards against ابن being a khabar rather than a description, as in «زيدٌ ابنُ عمرو». Is it permissible to make «ابن» follow [the vocative] so that it takes ḍamma, as in «يا زيد بنُ عمرو» with ḍamma on «ابن»? There is disagreement about it.

In His words {ابن مَرْيَمَ} there are three aspects. The first: that it is a description, as has preceded. The second: that it is a badal. The third: that it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). On the last two aspects, assuming the fatḥa by assimilation is not permissible by consensus, because ابن did not occur as a description, and it has preceded that this is a condition.

His words: {إِذْ أَيَّدتُّكَ}: there are aspects concerning «إذ». The first: that it is accusative by «نعمتي», as though it were said: remember when I bestowed favour upon you and your mother at the time of My supporting you. The second: that it is a badal from «نعمتي», a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion), as though it were in meaning an explanation of the favour. The third: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نعمتي»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The fourth: that it is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); Abū al-Baqāʾ also said this. I say: this is the second aspect — I mean the badal. The majority read «أيَّدتك» with doubled yāʾ, and others «آيَدْتُك»; the discussion of that, of who read it, and of what al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and the Shaykh said, has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara, so let it be consulted there.

His words: {تُكَلِّمُ الناس فِي المهد} to the end of it: this has also preceded in Āl ʿImrān, as has the benefit of His words: {فِي المهد وَكَهْلاً}; except that here there are some additions which must be dealt with. Ibn ʿAbbās read «فتنفخُها», omitting the preposition by extension. The majority read «فتكونُ» with the tāʾ dotted above, and Abū Jaʿfar dotted below [فيكون], i.e. "so the thing blown into becomes". As for the pronoun in «فيها», Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The views of the commentators about it are confused." Makkī said: "In Āl ʿImrān it refers to the bird, and in al-Māʾida it refers to the shape"; he said: "and the reverse of this is also valid." Others than Makkī said: "The masculine pronoun mentioned refers to the clay." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is not valid for this pronoun to refer to the birds, nor to the clay, nor to the shape, because the birds or the bird in whose shape the clay comes is not blown into at all; likewise there is no blowing into its particular shape; and likewise the clay is the clay in general, and there is no blowing into that." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun does not refer to the shape that is annexed [to the kāf], because it is not of his creating nor of his blowing into anything; likewise the pronoun in «فتكون»." Then Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The [right] way is that the feminine pronoun refers to what the verse necessarily implies, i.e. forms, figures or bodies, and the masculine pronoun refers to the created thing indicated by «تخلقُ»." Then he said: "And you may refer it to the meaning of 'likeness' that the kāf indicates, because the meaning is: when you create from clay the like of its shape; and you may refer it to the kāf itself, so that it is a noun outside poetry." End of quote.

This view is the very same as the one before it, for the kāf also means مِثْل (like); and its being a noun outside poetry was held by no one except al-Akhfash.

People found Makkī's statement above problematic, as I have related from Ibn ʿAṭiyya. It can be answered that by his saying "it refers to the bird" he does not mean the bird to which the shape is annexed, but the fashioned bird; the implied form being: "when you create from clay a bird in the form of the real bird, then blow into it, so it becomes a real bird". And by his saying "it refers to the shape" he does not mean the shape made genitive by the kāf, but the [shape] described by the kāf; the implied form being: "when you create from clay a shape like the shape of the bird, then you blow into it", i.e. into what is described by the kāf, whose creation was attributed to ʿĪsā. As for how a masculine pronoun could refer to a shape and a feminine pronoun to the bird — since his saying "the reverse of this is also permissible" leads to that — the answer is that it is permitted by interpretation: the shape is interpreted as a form (شكل) and the bird is interpreted as a shape (هيئة), so it is set right. It is a place calling for interpretation and deliberation. Here He said «بإذني» four times after four clauses, while in Āl ʿImrān [He said] «بإذن الله» twice, because there it is a place of informing, so concision was fitting, while here it is a setting of reminding of favour and bounty, so elaboration was fitting. His words «بإذني» are a ḥāl, either from the fāʿil (agent) or from the object.

His words: {إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here, in Hūd and in al-Ṣaff «إلا ساحر», an active participle; the rest read «إلا سحرٌ», a maṣdar (verbal noun), in all of them; the written form allows both readings. As for the reading of the majority, the pointing may be to the clear proofs he brought, i.e. "this that he brought of extraordinary signs is nothing but sorcery"; and the pointing may be to ʿĪsā, making him sorcery itself by way of intensification, as in «رجلٌ عدلٌ» (a man who is justice), or by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "nothing but a possessor of sorcery". Makkī restricted this aspect to the one pointed to being Muḥammad ﷺ, for he said: "It may be a pointing to the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, by assuming the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. this is nothing but a possessor of sorcery." [Translator's note: the passage that follows is printed in the source with a misplaced closing quotation mark; it appears to be the author's own comment.] I say: this is permissible [i.e. the omission], but the one pointed to is ʿĪsā, upon him be peace; how could the Prophet ﷺ be meant, when he was not in the time of ʿĪsā and the disciples so that they could point to him, except by a far-fetched interpretation? As for the reading of the two brothers, «ساحر» may be an active participle, the one pointed to being «عيسى»; and it may be that a maṣdar is meant by it, as in their saying «عائذاً بك» and «عائذاً بالله مِنْ شَرِّها» (in seeking refuge with You / with Allah from its evil), the one pointed to being what ʿĪsā brought of clear proofs and the Gospel. Makkī mentioned this, and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him; but al-Wāḥidī rejected it, for he said, after relating the two readings: "Both are good, because each of them is equal in that its mention has preceded; however, the preferred one is «سحر», because it can apply both to the event and to the person. Its application to the event is easy and frequent; its application to the person means 'possessor of sorcery', as in His words {ولكن البر مَنْ آمَنَ} [al-Baqara: 177], and they said «إنما أنت سيرٌ» and «ما أنت إلا سيرٌ» (you are nothing but travelling), and:

184 - 3-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنما هي إقبالٌ وإدبارُ
(…for she is nothing but coming and going.)"

I say: this supports what I stated earlier, that he applied the maṣdar to the person by way of intensification, as in «رجل عدل». Then he [al-Wāḥidī] said: "It is not permissible that by ساحر sorcery be meant. The pattern فاعِل has come meaning the maṣdar in a few words that are not many, as in «عائذاً بالله من شره», i.e. عياذاً, and as in «العافِية»; but these words have not become so numerous that analogy upon them is allowed."

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَخِي}: there are six views on it. The most apparent of them: that it is accusative (manṣūb) by conjunction with «نفسي», the meaning being: "and I have power over none but my brother, together with my power over myself, apart from others".

The second: that it is accusative by conjunction with the noun of «إنَّ», and its khabar (predicate) is omitted because the wording indicates it, i.e. "and my brother has power over none but himself". The third: that it is nominative (marfūʿ) by conjunction with the position of the noun of «إنَّ», since it comes after the khabar has been completed — there being disagreement on that, even though some have claimed consensus on its permissibility. The fourth: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar is omitted because of the aforementioned indication; He would then have conjoined a clause not emphasised to a clause emphasised by «إنَّ». The fifth: that it is nominative by conjunction with the latent pronoun in «أملك», the implied form being: "and my brother has power over none but himself"; that was permissible because of the separation by His saying {إِلاَّ نَفْسِي}. Al-Zamakhsharī, Makkī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ held this view. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this view on the ground that "it entails that Moses and Aaron have power only over the self of Moses alone, and the meaning is not so." This rejection is nothing, because the one who holds this view stated explicitly that the object is to be supposed after the conjoined agent; moreover the ambiguity is avoided, since it occurs to everyone's mind straight away that he has power over his own affair. The sixth: that it is genitive (majrūr) by conjunction with the yāʾ in «نفسي», i.e. "except myself and my brother's self". This is weak according to the rules of the Basrans, because of conjoining to the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition; what is involved in that has preceded.

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī reads with fatḥa on the yāʾ of «نفسي» and «أخي». Yūsuf ibn Dāwūd and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «فافرِقْ» with kasra on the rāʾ, and it is a dialect form: «فَرَق يفرِق» like «يضرِب». The rajaz poet said:

171 - 4- يا ربِّ فافرُقْ بينه وبيني ... أشدَّ مَا فرَّقْتَ بين اثنَيْنِ
(O Lord, separate him and me, more severely than You have ever separated two)

Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «فَفرِّقْ» with doubling, which goes against the written form [of the Muṣḥaf]. «بين» is governed by «افْرُق», and its due was not to be repeated in the conjunction — you say «المال بين زيد وعمرو» ("the wealth is between Zayd and ʿAmr") — but it was repeated only because of the need to repeat the preposition when conjoining to the genitive pronoun; and this supports the doctrine of the Basrans.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: that it is accusative (manṣūb) by «مُحَرَّمة», for it is narrated in the story that they entered it after the forty; so He restricted its prohibition to them to this period, and informed that they would wander, without explaining the extent of the wandering. On this view «يتيهون» admits two possibilities. One of them: that it is resumptive. The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم». The second view: that «أربعين» is accusative by «يتيهون», so He restricted the wandering to the forty, while the prohibition is unrestricted; it may then be permanent or interrupted — and that it was postponed for them. Each of the two possibilities has been held. It is narrated that none of those who were in the wandering entered it, and only their sons entered it; as for the fathers, they died. I do not know what led Abū Muḥammad Ibn ʿAṭiyya to permit that what governs «أربعين» be an implied verb explained by the later «يتيهون», nor what grammatical or semantic obstacle compelled him to it. The permissibility of pausing and starting at His saying «عليهم» and «يتيهون» is understood from the i'rab that has preceded.

«التِّيه» is bewilderment; of this is «أرضٌ تَيْهاء» ("a trackless land"), because of the bewilderment of the one who traverses it. He said:

171 - 5- بتَيْهاءَ قَفْرٍ والمَطِيُّ كأنها ... قَطا الحَزْن قد كانَتْ فراخاً بيوضُها
(In a trackless waste, the riding camels like sand-grouse of the rugged ground whose eggs had already become chicks)

One says «تاه يتيه» and «هو أَتْيَهُ منه», and «تاه يَتُوه» and «هو أتْوَهُ منه». So the saying of whoever says «يتيه» and «تَوَّهْتُه» is a case of overlapping (tadākhul) [of the two forms]. Similar to it is «طاح», in that both forms have been heard in its middle radical, and in that there is overlapping in it too: whoever says «يطيح» says «طَوَّحته» and «هو أَطْوَحُ منه».

«الأسى» is sorrow. One says «أَسِي» — with kasra on the ʿayn [middle radical] — «يَأْسَى», with fatḥa on it. The third radical of the word may be from wāw, which is the apparent view because of their saying «رجل أَسْوان» on the pattern of «سَكْران», i.e. much grieved; and they said in the dual of «الأسى»: «أَسَوان». The wāw in «أَسِيَ» was changed into yāʾ only because of the kasra before it. It may also be yāʾ, for «رجل أسْيان», i.e. much grieved, has been related; its dual on this view is «أَسَيان».

People customarily ask a question here, namely — as al-Zamakhsharī said —: "How do we reconcile His saying, Exalted is He: {فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ} with His saying: {الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ}?" He answered in two ways. One of them: that He prescribed it for them on condition that they strive, and they did not strive. The second: that the prohibition was limited to the period of the forty, and when it ended they entered it.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {بالحق}: there are three views on it. One of them: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اتلُ», i.e. recite that while you are clothed with the truth, i.e. with veracity.

The second: that it is a ḥāl from its object, namely «نبأ», i.e. recite their story clothed with veracity, agreeing with what is in the books of the earlier peoples, so that the proof of your messengership is established against them. The third: that it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «اتلُ», i.e. recite that with a recitation clothed with truth and veracity; this seems to be al-Zamakhsharī's choice, since he began with it. On all three views the bāʾ is for accompaniment, and it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element. Abū ʿAmr read with sukūn on the mīm of «آدم» before the bāʾ of «بالحق», and likewise every mīm that has a voweled letter before it and a bāʾ after it.

His saying: {إِذْ قَرَّبَا}: there are three views on it. One of them — al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ began with it —: that it is attached to «النبأ» itself, i.e. their story and account at that time; this is clear. The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from «نبأ», with the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "and recite to them the story, the story of that time"; this is how al-Zamakhsharī supposed it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What he mentioned is not permissible, because nothing is annexed to «إذ» except time, and «نبأ» is not time." The third — Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it —: that it is a ḥāl from «نبأ», and on this view it is attached to an omitted element; but this view is not clear. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is not an adverb of «اتلُ»." I say: because the verb is future and «إذ» is a past time, so how could they meet?

«القُرْبان» admits two possibilities. One of them — and al-Zamakhsharī held it —: that it is a noun for that by which one draws near [to Allah]. He said: "Just as «الحُلْوان» is a noun for what one gives as a gift. One says «قَرَّبَ صدقةً وتقرَّب بها» ('he offered a charity and drew near by it'), because «تقرَّب» is the reflexive-compliant form (muṭāwiʿ) of «قَرَّب». Al-Aṣmaʿī said: «تَقَرَّبوا قِرْفَ القِمَع» — so it is made transitive with the bāʾ so that it is in the sense of «قَرَّب»." That is, His saying {إِذْ قَرَّبَا قُرْبَاناً} calls for a compliant form for it, the implied form being: "when they offered it and drew near by it" — and this is far-fetched. The Shaykh said: "«تقرَّب بصدقة» is not the compliant form of «قَرَّب صدقة», because the agent of the two verbs is the same, whereas in compliance the agent differs: from one of them there is an action and from the other a being-acted-upon, as in «كَسَرْتُه فانكسر» ('I broke it and it broke') and «فَلَقْتُه فانفلق» ('I split it and it split'). «قَرَّب صدقته وتقرَّب بها» is not of this category, so it is a gross error." What the Shaykh said is open to consideration, because we do not concede this rule. The second possibility: that it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), then applied to the thing by which one draws near, like their saying «نَسْج اليمن» ("Yemeni weaving", i.e. cloth) and «ضَرْب الأمير» ("the prince's minting", i.e. coin). This is supported by its not being put in the dual although the place is one for the dual, because each of Qābīl and Hābīl had his own offering; so the basic form would be "when they offered two offerings", and it was not put in the dual only because it is originally a maṣdar. One who holds that it is a noun for that by which one draws near, not a maṣdar, may say: it was not put in the dual only because the meaning — as Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said — is: "when each of them offered an offering", like His saying, Exalted is He: {فاجلدوهم ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً} [al-Nūr: 4], i.e. each one of them.

His saying: {قَالَ لأَقْتُلَنَّكَ}, i.e. the one from whom it was not accepted said to the one from whom it was accepted. The majority read «لأقتلنَّك» with the heavy nūn, and this is the answer of an omitted oath; Zayd read it with the light nūn. His saying «إنما يتقبَّل الله»: its object is omitted because the meaning indicates it, i.e. their offerings and their deeds; and it may be that no object at all is intended for it, as in His saying: {فَأَمَّا مَنْ أعطى واتقى} [al-Layl: 5]. About this clause Abū Muḥammad Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Before it there is omitted speech, its implied form being: 'Why would you kill me when I have committed no crime, and I bear no guilt in Allah's accepting my offering and not yours?'" and he mentioned a great deal of speech. Another said: "There is a long omission in it", and mentioned something similar. There is no need to suppose all that, since the meanings understood from the drift of the speech are better when they are supposed briefly. The meaning here is: he said "I will surely kill you" out of envy over the acceptance of your offering, so he hinted to him that the cause of acceptance is piety. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how was His saying {إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ الله مِنَ المتقين} an answer to his saying «لأقتلنَّك»? I say: since it was envy of his brother over the acceptance of his offering that drove him to threaten him with killing, he said: you have only been brought low from the direction of your own self, because it has stripped itself of the garment of piety." End of quotation. This and the like is explanation of the meaning, not of the i'rab. It was also said: this clause is parenthetical between the speech of the killer and the speech of the one killed, and the pronoun in «قال» refers to Allah the Exalted, i.e. Allah said that to His Messenger; so He would have interposed His saying {إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ الله} between the speech of Qābīl, namely «قال لأقتلنَّك», and the speech of Hābīl, namely «لئن بَسَطْتَ» to its end. This is extremely far-fetched because of the disharmony of the composition.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
The lām in His saying: {لَئِن} is the lām that prepares for the oath (al-mūṭṭiʾa). His saying {مَآ أَنَاْ بِبَاسِطٍ} is the answer of the omitted oath; this is according to the established rule that when a condition and an oath come together, the first of them is answered, except in a case to which attention has been drawn before.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did the condition come in the form of the verb and the requital (jazāʾ) in the form of the active participle, namely His saying {لَئِن بَسَطتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي مَآ أَنَاْ بِبَاسِطٍ}? I say: to convey that he would not do this abominable thing that is characterised [in it]; for that reason he emphasised it with the bāʾ, which conveys emphasis of the negation." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] disputed with him over his saying that {مَآ أَنَاْ بِبَاسِطٍ} is "a requital of the condition". He said: "Because this is the answer of the oath, not of the condition." He said: "For if it were the answer of the condition, the fāʾ would be necessary in it, because it is negated by «ما» and the particle is one that makes the jussive; and it would also entail breaking that rule, namely that the first of them was not answered." This is nothing, because Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] called it a requital of the condition since it indicates the requital of the condition, and there is nothing objectionable in that — [the Shaykh being] keen that it be said: he has objected to al-Zamakhsharī. He also said: "Al-Zamakhsharī contradicted here what he mentioned in al-Baqara at His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ} [verse 145], where he made it the answer of the oath standing in place of the answer of the condition." He has a discussion with him there that I have previously cited from him in its place, so let it be consulted.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تَسْألوا». The grammarians disagreed about «أشياء» in five schools.

The first — the view of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Māzinī and the majority of the Basrans —: it is an ism jamʿ (collective noun) from the wording of «شيء», singular in form and plural in meaning, like «طَرْفاء» and «قَصْباء». Its original form is «شَيْئاء», with two hamzas with an alif between them, on the pattern «فَعْلاء» like «طَرْفاء». They found the meeting of two hamzas with an alif between them heavy, especially as it was preceded by a weak letter, namely the yāʾ; and this word circulated very frequently on their tongues, so they transposed the word by placing its lām (third radical) — namely the first hamza — before its fāʾ (first radical) — namely the shīn — and said «أَشْياء», so its pattern became «لَفْعاء»; and it was made a diptote because of the extended alif of femininity. This school was preferred on the grounds that nothing follows from it except transposition (qalb), and transposition is frequent in their language, as in «الجاه», «الحادي», «القِسِيّ», «ناءَ», «آدُر», «آرام», «ضِئاء» in the reading of Qunbul, and «أَيِس»; the originals being «وجه», «واحد», «قُووس», «نَأَى», «أَدْوُر», «أَرْآم», «ضياء» and «يَئِس». Some objected to this that transposition is contrary to the base rule, and that it has occurred only out of poetic necessity or in a small portion of speech; but this is refuted by the examples I have given. We do not deny that transposition is not regular; as for the anomalous and rare, it is like their saying «رَعَمْلي» for «لَعَمْري» and «شَواعي» for «شوايع». [The poet] said:
181 - 3- وكان أَوْلاها كِعابُ مُقامِرٍ ... ضُرِبَتْ على شَزَنٍ فهنَّ شَواعِي
(The first of them were like a gambler's dice, cast on a rough edge, so they scattered in all directions.)
He means «شوائع».
As for the schools that follow, difficulties are raised against them from which this school is free; for that reason the majority adopted it rather than any other.

The second school — held by al-Farrāʾ —: «أشياء» is the plural of «شيء», and the original of «شيء» is «شَيِّئ» on the pattern «فَيْعِل», like «لَيِّن»; then it was lightened to «شيء», just as they lightened «لَيِّن», «هَيِّن» and «مَيِّت» to «لَيْن», «هَيْن» and «مَيْت». Then he pluralized it after its lightening; its original is «أَشْيِئاء», with two hamzas with an alif between them, after a yāʾ, on the pattern «أَفْعِلاء». So two hamzas met — the lām of the word and the one of femininity — and the alif resembles the hamza, and the plural is heavy; so they lightened the word by changing the first hamza into a yāʾ because of the kasra before it, so two yāʾs met, the first of them with kasra; then they deleted the yāʾ that is the ʿayn (second radical) of the word for lightness, so it became «أَشْياء», and its pattern now, after the deletion, is «أَفْلاء»; and its being a diptote is because of the alif of femininity. [Translator's note: the source has «بعد الخلاف» ("after the disagreement"), apparently a slip for «بعد الحذف» ("after the deletion"); rendered by the latter sense.] This is the method of some, such as Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, in the morphological analysis of this school. Others, such as Abū al-Baqāʾ, said: when it became «أَشْيئاء», the second hamza, which is the lām of the word, was deleted, since it was through it that the heaviness arose, and the yāʾ with kasra was given fatḥa so that the alif of the plural would remain sound; so its pattern became «أَفْعاء».

The third school — held by al-Akhfash —: «أَشْياء» is the plural of «شَيْء» on the pattern of «فَلْس», i.e. not lightened from «شَيِّئ» as al-Farrāʾ says, but the plural of «شيء». He said that «فَعْل» is pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء», so it became «أَشْيِئاء» with two hamzas with an alif between them, after a yāʾ; then what was done in the school of al-Farrāʾ was done to it. [Translator's note: the source has «مذهب الفقراء», an evident misprint for «مذهب الفراء»; rendered accordingly.] The two methods mentioned from Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ in the morphological analysis of this school apply here too. Most authors report the school of al-Farrāʾ as being his and al-Akhfash's. Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ, al-Akhfash and al-Ziyādī said: the pattern of «أَشْياء» is «أَفْعِلاء», and its original is «أَشْيِئاء», like «هيِّن» and «أَهْوِناء», but it was lightened," then he gave the morphological analysis of the word to the end. And Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: the original of the word is «شَيِّئ» like «هَيِّن», then it was lightened by deletion," and he gave the analysis to the end. So these transmitted their two schools as a single thing, and the truth is what I have reported from them. What I have said is indicated by what al-Wāḥidī said, for he said: "Al-Farrāʾ in this word followed the school of al-Akhfash," except that he confused matters when he claimed that it is like «هَيْن» and «لَيْن», which were pluralized on «أَهْوناء» and «أَلْيِناء»; for «هَيْن» is a lightening of «هيِّن», and for that reason its pluralization on «أَفْعِلاء» was permissible, whereas «شَيء» is not lightened from «شَيِّئ» so as to be pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء».

These two schools — I mean the school of al-Farrāʾ and of al-Akhfash — although they are free from [positing] diptote status without a cause, have been rejected by people. Al-Zajjāj said: "This view is a mistake, because «شَيْء» is «فَعْل», and «فَعْل» is not pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء». As for «هَيِّن» and «لَيِّن», their original is «هَيين» and «لَيين», so they were pluralized [on] «أَفْعِلاء», just as «فعيل» is pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء», like «نصيب» and «أَنْصباء»." I say: this is very strange — I mean his making the original of «هيّن» to be «هَيين» on the pattern «فَعِيل», and likewise «لَيّن» and «لَيِين»; that is why he explicitly likened them to «نصيب». People say that the original of «هَيِّن» is «هَيْوِن», as the original of «ميِّت» is «مَيْوِت», then it underwent the well-known weakening; and the original of «لَيّن» is «لَيْيِن» with two yāʾs, the first with sukūn and the second with kasra, and the first was assimilated. Derivation supports them, for «الهيِّن» is from «هانَ يهون», and because when they pluralized it on «أَفْعلاء» they made the wāw appear, saying «أَهْوِناء».

Al-Zajjāj said: "Al-Māzinī debated al-Akhfash on this question, and said to him: 'How do you form the diminutive of «أشياء»?' He said: 'I say «أُشَيَّاء».' Al-Māzinī said: 'If it were «أَفْعال» [i.e. a broken plural], it would be returned in the diminutive to its singular, and one would say «شُيَيْئات», like «شُعَيْعات». And the consensus of the Basrans is that the diminutive of «أصدقاء», if it is for feminines, is «صُدَيِّقات», and if for masculines, «صُدَيِّقون».' And al-Akhfash was silenced." [Translator's note: the source reads «لو كانت أَفْعالاً» ("if it were afʿāl"), although al-Akhfash's claimed pattern is «أَفْعِلاء»; the forms «شُيَئْات» and «صُدّيَّقات» are spelled thus in the source and are rendered by the evident forms.]

I say: the elaboration of this is that when a broken plural is put into the diminutive, it is either one of the plurals of paucity — which are four on the correct view: «أَفْعِلة», «أَفْعُل», «أَفْعال» and «فِعْلة» — in which case it is put into the diminutive on its own form; or it is one of the plurals of multitude, in which case it is not put into the diminutive on its own form, on the correct view — and if anything of that occurs it is counted anomalous, like «أُصَيْلان», the diminutive of «أُصْلان», the plural of «أَصيل» — but rather it is returned to its singular.
