Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. «في الأرض» is attached to «فساد» itself, because you say «أفسد في الأرض» — except in the reading of al-Ḥasan with the accusative, if we explain it as accusative as a maṣdar, as Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned; for then it is not attached to it, because it is an emphasising maṣdar, and they have stated explicitly that the emphasising one does not govern. So «في الأرض» would be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «فساداً». The fāʾ in «فكأنما» in both places is the answer of the condition and its entry is obligatory. «ما» is a restraining particle (kāffa) for the particle of comparison; it is better here to call it "preparatory" (muhayyiʾa), because a verb occurs after it.

«جميعاً» is either a ḥāl or tawkīd (emphasis).

His saying: {بَعْدَ ذلك فِي الأرض}: this adverb and the preposition phrase after it are attached to His saying «لمُسْرِفون», which is the khabar of «إنَّ». The lām of the inceptive (lām al-ibtidāʾ) does not prevent that, as something separating the governor from its governed element placed before it, because its entry on the khabar is contrary to the basic rule, since its basic place is on the mubtadaʾ, and only the entry of «إنَّ» prevented that. «ذلك» points to the coming of the messengers with the clear proofs.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّمَا جَزَآءُ الذين}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «أن يُقَتَّلوا» and what is conjoined to it, i.e. their only requital is being killed, crucified or banished. His saying: {يُحَارِبُونَ الله}, i.e. they make war on His allies; this is how the majority supposed it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They make war on the Messenger of Allah, and making war on the Muslims has the ruling of making war on him." He means that the intent is to inform that they make war on the Messenger of Allah, and the name of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, was mentioned only to magnify and exalt the one who is warred against, like His saying: {إِنَّ الذين يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ الله}. The verification and supposition of that has preceded at His saying: {يُخَادِعُونَ الله والذين آمَنُوا} [al-Baqara: 9]. It was also said: the meaning of making war is opposing their rulings. On these views it is not entailed in His saying, Exalted is He: {يُحَارِبُونَ الله وَرَسُولَهُ} that the literal and the figurative are combined in a single word. Whoever permits that does not need any of these interpretations, but says: their making war on Allah the Exalted is taken in a sense that suits it, namely opposition, figuratively, and their making war on the Messenger is taken as fighting, literally.

His saying: {فَسَاداً}: there are three views on its accusative case. One of them: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they make war and strive for the sake of corruption; the conditions for the accusative are present. The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. and they strive in the land as corrupters, or as possessors of corruption, or they were made corruption itself for intensiveness — three well-known doctrines whose establishment has preceded. The third: that it is accusative as a maṣdar [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], i.e. it is a kind of the governor before it, for the meaning of «يَسْعَون» here is "they corrupt". In reality «فساد» is a noun of the maṣdar standing in the place of «الإفساد», the implied form being: "and they corrupt in the land by their striving, a corrupting". «وفي الأرض»: the apparent view is that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it, like His saying: {سعى فِي الأرض لِيُفْسِدَ} [al-Baqara: 205]. It has been permitted that it be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, because, had it come after it, it could be an adjective of it. It has also been permitted that it be attached to «فساداً» itself; this works only if we make «فساداً» a ḥāl; if we make it a maṣdar, that is impossible because it precedes it, and because the emphasising [maṣdar] does not govern. The majority read «أَنْ يُقَتَّلوا» and the two verbs after it with doubling, meaning multiplicity in relation to those on whom these acts fall. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muḥayṣin read them without doubling.

His saying «من خِلافٍ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «أيديهم» and «أرجلُهم», i.e. with an alternating cutting, meaning that his right hand and his left foot are cut off. «النفي» is expulsion. By «الأرض» here is meant [the land] in which they want to reside, or what is meant is "from their land", the «أل» being a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi according to those who hold this. His saying: {ذلك لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدنيا}: «ذلك» [likewise points to the aforementioned khabar], and it is a mubtadaʾ. His saying {لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ}: there are three views on it. One of them: that «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «خِزْيٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «في الدنيا» an adjective of it, so it is attached to an omitted element; or it is attached to «خزي» itself as its adverb; and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «ذلك». The second: that «خزي» is the khabar of «ذلك», and «لهم» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «خِزْي», because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

As for «في الدنيا», the two aforementioned views are permissible in it — its being an adjective of «خزي» or attached to it — and it may also be attached to the [verb of] settledness (al-istiqrār) to which «لهم» is attached. The third: that «لهم» is the khabar of «ذلك» and «خزي» is a fāʿil (agent); the preposition phrase here put the agent in the nominative because it leans on the mubtadaʾ. On this view «في الدنيا» admits the three views.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {إِلاَّ الذين تَابُواْ}: there are two views on it. One of them: that it is accusative (manṣūb) as excepted from those who make war. The scholars disagree about the highway robber who repents: do all the punishments fall away from him, or only the punishment for highway robbery, while what relates to property and the killing of souls does not fall away, its ruling rather being up to the owner of the property and the next of kin of the slain? The apparent view is the first. The second: that it is nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is His saying {أَنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ}, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "forgiving to them". Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this second view; in that case it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), meaning: but the one who repents is forgiven.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {وابتغوا إِلَيهِ الوسيلة}: there are three views on «إليه». One of them: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. The second: that it is attached to «الوسيلة» itself. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because it is in the sense of that by which one seeks access, which is why it governs what precedes it." He means that it is not a maṣdar (verbal noun), such that its governed element would be barred from preceding it. The third: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الوسيلة»; and that is not strong.

semin-durr:114-114.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً}: in «تكون» there is a pronoun referring to «مائدة», which is its noun. There are two possibilities for the khabar (predicate). The more apparent of them: that it is «عيد»; and «لنا» has two aspects in that case. The first: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عيدا», because it was originally a description of it. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of «تكون», according to those who permit it [kāna] to govern a ḥāl. The second possibility: that «لنا» is the khabar and «عيداً» a ḥāl, either from the pronoun of «تكونُ», according to those who hold that, or from the pronoun in «لنا», because it occurred as a khabar and so carries a pronoun. The clause is in the position of accusative as a description of «مائدة».

ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read {تَكُنْ} in the jussive as the response to the imperative in His words «أَنْزل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The two are the counterpart of {يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ} [Maryam: 6]", meaning the words of Allah the Exalted: {فَهَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنْكَ وَلِيّاً يَرِثُنِي}, in the nominative as a description and in the jussive as a response. But the two readings there are both mutawātir, while the jussive here is among the irregular (shādhdh) readings.

العِيد is derived from العَوْد (returning), because it returns every year; Thaʿlab said this from Ibn al-Aʿrābī. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "The grammarians say: the day of the ʿīd, because it returns with joy and happiness; and among the Arabs, because it returns with joy and sorrow. Everything that returns to one at a time is an ʿīd, so much so that they called the phantom [of the beloved] an ʿīd." Al-Aʿshā said:

184 - 7- فواكبدي من لاعجِ الحُبِّ والهَوى ... إذا اعتاد قَلْبي من أُمَيْمَة عيدُها
(Alas for my liver from the burning of love and passion, when her recurring phantom from Umayma visits my heart.)

i.e. her phantom. Taʾabbaṭa Sharran said:

184 - 8- يا عيدُ ما لكَ مِنْ شوقٍ وإيراقِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O recurring visitant, what longing and sleeplessness you bring…)

And he said:

184 - 9- عادَ قلبي من الطويلةِ عيدُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(A recurring longing for al-Ṭawīla returned to my heart…)

Al-Rāghib said: "العيد is a state that returns to a person repeatedly; العائدة is every benefit that comes back to a person through something; and from it is العَوْد for the aged camel: either because it returns repeatedly to travel and work, in which case it has the sense of an active participle, or because the years return to it and pass over it, in which case it has the sense of a passive participle." Imruʾ al-Qays said:

185 - 0- على لاحِبٍ لا يُهْتَدى بمنارِه ... إذا سافَه العَوْدُ النباطِيُّ جَرْجَرا
(On a clear, beaten track whose waymarks give no guidance; when the old Nabataean camel sniffs it, it groans.)

They made its diminutive «عُيَيْد» and its broken plural «أعياد», whereas analogy would be عُوَيْد and أَعْود, since the cause of changing the wāw into yāʾ has gone: it was changed only because of its being quiescent after a kasra, as in «ميزان». They said: they did that only to distinguish it from عود, wood.

His words: {لأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا}: there are two aspects concerning it. The first: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], because it occurs as a description of «عيداً». The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from the «نا» in «لنا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لأولنا وآخرنا» is a badal from «لنا» with repetition of the governing word." Then he said: "Zayd ibn Thābit and al-Jaḥdarī read لأُولانا وأُخْرانا, the feminine being according to the meaning of 'the community (الأمة)'." Abū al-Baqāʾ assigned each aspect to a particular case, for he said: "As for «لأولنا وآخرنا»: if you make «لنا» a khabar, or a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «تكون», then it is a description of «عيداً»; and if you make «لنا» a description of «عيد», then «لأولنا» is a badal from the genitive pronoun with repetition of the preposition."

I say: he only did that because if he makes «لنا» a khabar, «عيداً» is a ḥāl, and if he makes it a ḥāl, «عيداً» is the khabar; so on both assumptions he cannot make «لأولنا» a badal from «لنا», lest a separation between the badal and what it replaces be entailed, either by the ḥāl or by the khabar, namely «عيد» — unlike when «لنا» is made a description of «عيد». This is what appears to be his reason for assigning each to each. But it may be said: his saying "if you make لنا a description of عيداً, لأولنا is a badal" is also problematic, because the separation exists in it as well — especially since his statement cannot be taken literally, because «لنا» is not a description but a fronted ḥāl; however, he looked to the origin, the implied form being «عيداً لنا لأوَّلنا», so it is as though there were no separation. The apparent view is that the badal is permissible, and separation by the khabar or the ḥāl does no harm, because it is part of its completion and so is not foreign.

Know that a badal from a pronoun of someone present — whether first person or second person — of the type "whole from whole" is not permissible according to the majority of the Basrans; if you were to say «قمتُ زيدٌ», meaning yourself, or «ضربتُك عَمْراً», it would not be permitted. They said: because the badal is brought mostly for clarification, and the one present is distinguished by himself, so there is no benefit in a badal from him; this is close to their reasoning in forbidding describing it. Al-Akhfash permitted it absolutely, citing the outward sense of this verse and his saying:

185 - 1- أنا سيفُ العشيرةِ فاعرِفوني ... حُمَيْداً قد تَذَرَّيْتُ السِّناما
(I am the sword of the clan, so know me — Ḥumayd; I have mounted the highest summit.)

so «حُمَيْداً» is a badal from the yāʾ of اعرفوني; and the saying of another:

185 - 2- وشوهاءَ تَغْدو بي إلى صارخ الوغى ... بمُسْتَلْئِمٍ مثلِ الفنيق المُدَجَّلِ
(Many a long-faced mare carries me in the morning towards the battle-cry, [carrying] a mail-clad warrior like a stallion camel smeared with tar.)

and his saying:

185 - 3- بكم قريشٍ كُفينا كُلَّ مُعْضِلَةٍ ... وأَمَّ نهج الهُدى مَنْ كان ضِلِّيلا
(Through you, Quraysh, we were spared every grave difficulty, and whoever was much astray set out on the path of guidance.)

And in the ḥadīth: «أتينا النبيَّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نفرٌ من الأشعريين» (We came to the Prophet ﷺ, a group of the Ashʿarīs). The Basrans interpret all of that. As for the noble verse, it is according to the first aspect above. As for «حُمَيْداً», it is accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). As for «بمُسْتلئم», it is of the device of tajrīd (abstraction), something known to the rhetoricians; that is, he abstracted from himself a being characterised by such-and-such. As for «قريش», the narration is in the nominative, as a vocative given tanwīn by poetic necessity, as in his saying:

185 - 4- سلامُ اللَّهِ يا مطرٌ عليها ... وليسَ عليك يا مطرُ السَّلامُ
(The peace of Allah, O Maṭar, be upon her — but upon you, O Maṭar, be no peace.)

As for «نفرٌ», it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. نحن (we). Some forbade it unless the badal conveys emphasis and comprehensiveness, in which case it is permissible; and he cited this verse and the saying of another:

185 - 5- فما بَرِحَتْ أقدامُنا في مقامِنا ... ثلاثتِنا حتى أُزيروا المَنائِيَا
(Our feet — the three of us — did not leave our standing place until they were made to visit death.)

with «ثلاثتنا» in the genitive as a badal from «نا». There is no proof in it, because «ثلاثتنا» is a tawkīd (emphasis) treated like «كل».

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَفَحُكْمَ}: the majority read it with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, a sukūn on the kāf and a fatḥa (accusative) on the mīm, and it is a clear reading. «حكمَ» is a fronted object and «يبغون» a verb and agent, and it is what is asked about in meaning. On the fāʾ there are the two well-known views: is it placed after the hamza while originally preceding it, or is there before it a clause to which it conjoins what follows, the implied form being "Do they turn away from your judgement and seek the judgement of the Jāhiliyya?"

Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿraj, Abū Rajāʾ and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with the mīm in the nominative. There are two views on it. The more evident — and it is the well-known one among the parsers — is that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يبغون» its khabar (predicate), the returning pronoun to the mubtadaʾ being omitted, its implied form being «يَبْغُونه» (they seek it), treating the khabar like the ṣila (relative clause). However, some considered this reading a mistake, so that Abū Bakr ibn Mujāhid said: "This reading is a mistake," while others consider it weak without reaching the degree of a mistake. Ibn Jinnī said about Ibn Mujāhid's statement: "It is not so; rather, another construction is stronger than it. It has occurred in poetry; Abū al-Najm said:

1739 - قد أصبحَتْ أمُّ الخيارِ تَدَّعي ... عليَّ ذنباً كلُّه لم أَصْنَعِ
(Umm al-Khiyār has come to accuse me of a sin, all of which I did not commit.)

i.e. «لم أصنعه» (I did not commit it)." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is how it is transmitted, and with it the correct meaning is complete, because he wanted to declare himself free of all the sins; had he put «كل» in the accusative, the apparent sense of his words would be that he committed some of it." I say: this which Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] mentioned is a correct meaning, stated explicitly by the scholars of the sciences of meanings and eloquence (al-maʿānī wa-l-bayān). They cited as evidence for it his saying, upon him be peace, when Dhū al-Yadayn asked him, saying: "Has the prayer been shortened, or did you forget?" and he said: «كلُّ ذلك لم يكن» (none of that happened); he, upon him be peace, meant the negation of each and every item, and the fronting of «كل» conveyed this meaning. They said: had he said «لم يكن كلُّ ذلك» (not all of that happened), the speech would have admitted that some of it was not negated. This question is called "the generality of the negation" (ʿumūm al-salb), and its converse, as in «لم أصنعْ كلَّ ذلك» (I did not do all of that), is called "the negation of the generality" (salb al-ʿumūm). This is a useful question, so I have treated it thoroughly, even though some people have understood from Sībawayh something other than what I have mentioned to you.

Then Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is ugly — meaning omitting the returning pronoun from the khabar. The pronoun is omitted frequently only from the ṣila, and omitted less than that from the adjective; its omission from the khabar is ugly." But he gave the verse preference over this reading for two reasons. First: at the beginning of his saying there is no interrogative alif that calls for a verb, as there is in «أفحكم». Second: in the verse there is a compensation for the omitted hāʾ, namely the letter of prolongation (ḥarf al-iṭlāq), I mean the yāʾ in «أصنعي». So the reading of whoever reads «أفحكمُ الجاهلية يبغون» is weakened. What Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned in the second reason is talk not worth heeding. As for the first, it is close to correct, but it does not stand up as a ground for prohibiting or for deeming ugly; it stands only as a proof of something being better, or of something else being preferable to it.

Some mentioned a disagreement on this question regarding one type, and denied any disagreement — indeed reported consensus on its permissibility — regarding another type. He reported consensus where the mubtadaʾ is the word «كل» or something resembling it in generality and in needing [a complement]. As for «كل», [it is] as in «كلُّ رجلٍ ضربت» (every man I struck), and it is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir: {وكلُّ وعد الله الحسنى}. By what resembles «كل» he means something like «رجلٌ يقولُ الحقَّ انصرْ» (a man who speaks the truth — help), i.e. help him, for it is general and needs an adjective, just as «كل» is general and needs a muḍāf ilayhi. He said: "If the mubtadaʾ is not like that, the Kufans prohibit the omission of the returning pronoun and instead put the fronted [noun] in the accusative as an object, while the Basrans allow «زيدٌ ضربتُ», i.e. I struck him," and he mentioned the reading.

Some went to an extreme and said: "That is not permissible," without qualification, except out of poetic necessity, as in his saying:

1740 - وخالدٌ يَحْمَدُ ساداتُنا ... بالحقِّ، لا يُحْمَدُ بالباطلِ
(And Khālid — our chiefs praise [him] rightly; he is not praised falsely.)

He said: "Because it leads to preparing the governor to govern and then cutting it off from it." I have treated this question and what has been transmitted on it thoroughly in my book Sharḥ al-Tashīl, so you should turn to it.

The second of the two above-mentioned accounts is that «يبغون» is not the khabar of the mubtadaʾ but an adjective of an omitted noun it qualifies, and that omitted noun is the khabar; the implied form is: {أَفَحُكْمَ الجاهلية يَبْغُونَ} [i.e. a judgement they seek]. Omission of the returning pronoun here is more frequent, because, as stated, it is frequently omitted from the ṣila, less from the adjective, and less again from the khabar. This is what Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose, and it is a possible account. He compared it to His saying, Exalted is He, {مِّنَ الذين هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 46], i.e. "a people who distort," meaning in the omission of the qualified noun and the putting of its adjective in its place — otherwise the omitted element in the verse adduced as a parallel is a mubtadaʾ. He also compared it to his saying:

1741 - وما الدهرُ إلا تارتانِ: فمنهما ... أموتُ وأُخْرى أبتغي العيشَ أكدحُ
(Time is nothing but two turns: one of them, I die [in it]; and another, I seek a living, toiling.)

i.e. "a turn in which I die." al-Zamakhsharī said: "Dropping the returning pronoun from it is like dropping it in the ṣila, as in His saying {أهذا الذي بَعَثَ الله رَسُولاً} [al-Furqān: 41]; and from the adjective: «في الناس رجُلان: رجلٌ أهنْتُ، ورجلٌ أكرمت» (among people are two men: a man I humiliated and a man I honoured), i.e. a man I humiliated him and a man I honoured him; and from the ḥāl (circumstantial), as in «مررت بهند يضرب زيد» (I passed by Hind, Zayd striking [her])." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "If he means the comparison in omission and its goodness, it is not so, for the reason mentioned above; if he means in omission absolutely, it is granted."

al-Aʿmash and Qatāda read «أَفَحَكَمَ» with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the kāf and the mīm in the accusative. It is a singular by which the genus is meant, because the meaning is "the judges of the Jāhiliyya." In this reading a muḍāf must be omitted, which is the one stated explicitly in the mass-transmitted reading; its implied form is: "the judgement of the judges of the Jāhiliyya."

The readers other than Ibn ʿĀmir read «يَبْغُون» with the yāʾ of the third person, in sequence with the third-person nouns mentioned before. He read it with the tāʾ of address, by way of a shift (iltifāt), so as to be more effective in rebuking and restraining them and confounding them, since He confronted them with this question which people of insight disdain.

«حُكْماً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). His saying {لقوم}: there are three views on this [lām]. First: it is attached to «حكماً» itself, since the meaning is that Allah's judgement is in favour of the believer against the disbeliever. Second: it is explicative, and so is attached to an omitted element, as in «سُقْياً لك» (may you be watered) and {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23]; this is al-Zamakhsharī's opinion, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said something close to it, namely that the meaning is "He makes that clear and manifest to a people." Third: it means «عند», i.e. "in the view of [a people]"; and this is worthless. The object of «يوقنون» may be intended, its implied form being "they are certain of Allah and His judgement," or "of the Quran"; or it may not be intended, in the sense of the occurrence of certainty [as such]. al-Zajjāj inclined to this, for he said: "«يوقنون»: they perceive clearly Allah's justice in His judgement."

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). This clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive, brought as a reason for the preceding prohibition. al-Ḥawfī claimed that it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «أولياء»; the first is the evident view. The pronoun in «بعضهم» refers to the Jews and the Christians collectively, and the context makes clear that some Jews are allies of others [of them] and some Christians are allies of others [of them]. With this account there is no need, as some claimed, to assume an omission by which the meaning becomes sound, namely "some of the Jews are allies of others, and some of the Christians are allies of others." He said: "Because the Jews do not ally themselves with the Christians, and the Christians do not ally themselves with the Jews." Its answer has been given.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {فَتَرَى الذين}: the majority read «ترى» with the tāʾ of address, and «الذين» is the object. If the seeing is visual, or [a matter of] recognition — according to what Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted, and it is open to question — then the clause «يُسارعون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative; if it is mental, «يسارعون» is a second object. al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Waththāb read «فيَرى» with the yāʾ, and there are two interpretations of it. The more evident: the agent is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted — it is also said: to the seer as such — and «يُسارعون» stays as it is. Second: the agent is the relative itself, and the object is the clause in His saying {يُسَارِعُونَ}, on the interpretation that the maṣdar «أَنْ» is omitted, the implied form being "and the people in whose hearts is a sickness see that they hasten"; when «أَنْ» was omitted, [the verb] became nominative, as in his saying:

1742 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجري أَحْضُرُ الوَغى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who chide me for attending the battle …)

Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed this, but it is not regular, since according to the Basrans «أن» is not omitted except in places preserved [from usage]. Qatāda and al-Aʿmash read «يُسْرِعون», from «أسرع».

«يقولون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يسارعون»; «نخشى» is in the position of the accusative by the saying; and «أن تصيبنَا» is in the position of the accusative as the object, i.e. "we fear its striking us." «الدائرة» is an adjective that has become predominant [as a noun], whose qualified noun is not mentioned; its original is «داوِرَة», because it is from «دار يدور» (to turn).

His saying: {أَن يَأْتِيَ}: in the position of the accusative, either as the khabar (predicate) of «عسى», which is the opinion of al-Akhfash, or as an object, which is the opinion of Sībawayh, so as to avoid predicating an event of a concrete noun in your saying «عسى زيدٌ أَنْ يقومَ» (perhaps Zayd will stand). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «أن يأتي» to be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of the noun of «عسى»; this is open to question.

His saying: {فَيُصْبِحُواْ}: there are two views on it. The more evident: it is accusative, conjoined to «يأتِيَ», which is in the accusative by «أَنْ». What made this permissible is the presence of the causal fāʾ; without it, it would not be permissible, because what is conjoined to the khabar is a khabar, and «أن يأتي» is the khabar of «عسى» and contains a pronoun referring to its noun, while His saying {فَيُصْبِحُواْ} contains no pronoun referring to its noun, so the case ought to be inadmissible. But the fāʾ is causal, and it has made the two clauses like a single clause. This applies in the ṣila (relative clause), as in «الذي يطير فيغضب زيدٌ الذبابُ» (that which flies so that Zayd gets angry is the fly); in the adjective, as in «مررت برجل يبكي فيضحكُ عمرو» (I passed a man who weeps so that ʿAmr laughs); and in the khabar, as in «زيد يبكي فيضحك خالد» (Zayd weeps so that Khālid laughs). If the conjunction were other than the fāʾ, that would not be permissible. Second: it is accusative by a concealed «أَنْ» after the fāʾ in reply to a wish; they said: "Because «عسى» is wishing and hoping in respect of human beings." «على ما أسَرُّوا» is attached to «نادمين», and «نادمين» is the khabar of «أصبح».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ القلائد}: [i.e.] "nor those having garlands". It may also be that the garlands themselves are meant, which then involves an intensification of the prohibition against interfering with the garlanded sacrificial animal; for if He forbade interfering with its garland, then all the more fittingly would He forbid interfering with the sacrificial animal garlanded with it. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ}, because if He forbade displaying adornment, what then of the places of it on the limbs?

His saying: «ولا آمِّيْنَ» i.e. "and do not violate a people heading [for the House]". It may be by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "do not make lawful fighting a people" or "harming a people heading …". ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] and those who followed him read: «ولا آمِّي البيتِ», deleting the nūn and annexing the active participle to its governed word. «البيت» is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «آمّين», i.e. "heading for the House", and is not an adverb.

His saying: {يَبْتَغُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «آمِّين», i.e. "while those heading [there] are seeking bounty". This clause may not be an adjective of «آمّين», because when an active participle is qualified its governing power is annulled, according to the correct view; the Kufans disagreed on that. Al-Makkī parsed this clause as an adjective of «آمِّين», which is not good, for what preceded; it seems he followed the Kufans in that. Here there is a question, namely: why was it not said that it may govern before being qualified, as in this verse, by analogy with the maṣdar (verbal noun), which governs before being qualified, as in «يعجبني ضربٌ زيداً شديدٌ» ("A severe striking of Zayd pleases me")?

The majority read «يبتغون» with the tāʾ of address «[Translator's note: so in the text; the following words suggest that a sentence has dropped out, e.g. that the majority read «يبتغون» with yāʾ and that someone read «تبتغون» with tāʾ, since it is the tāʾ reading that is called awkward.]», as an address to the believers; and it is awkward because of His saying {مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ}; had address to the believers been intended, full correspondence would have been «تبتغون فضلاً من ربكم». «من ربهم» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb itself, or attached to an omitted word as an adjective of «فضلاً», i.e. "a bounty that is from their Lord". The disagreement about the ḍamma on the rāʾ of «رضوان» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān. If we attach «من ربهم» to an omitted word as an adjective of «فضلاً», then He has omitted the adjective of «رضوان» because what precedes indicates it, i.e. "and good pleasure from their Lord"; if we attach it to the verb itself, that is not needed.

His saying: {وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصطادوا}: it was read «أَحْللتم», which is a dialectal form of «حَلَّ»; one says «أحَلَّ من إحْرامِه» ("he left his iḥrām") as one says «حَلَّ». Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿImrān, Abū Wāqid, Nubayḥ and al-Jarrāḥ read with kasra on the conjunctive fāʾ; it is a weak, problematic reading. Al-Zamakhsharī explained it as the kasra on the fāʾ being a substitute for the kasra of the hamza at the start [of «اصطادوا»]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a problematic reading; part of its justification is that he paid regard to the kasra of the connecting alif when beginning with it, so he gave the fāʾ kasra out of regard for and in remembrance of the kasra of the connecting alif." Al-Shaykh said: "In my view it is not a pure kasra, but a pure imāla (inclination of the vowel), from imagining the presence of the kasra of the connecting hamza, just as they inclined the fāʾ of «فإذا» because of the presence of the kasra of the hamza."

His saying: {وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ}: the majority read «يَجْرِمَنَّكم» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from the triliteral «جرم». The meaning of «جَرَمَ» according to al-Kisāʾī and Thaʿlab is "to impel"; one says «جَرَمه على كذا», i.e. he impelled him to it. On this interpretation «جرم» takes one object, namely the kāf and mīm, and His saying {أَن تَعْتَدُواْ} is by dropping the preposition «على», i.e. "and let not your hatred of a people impel you to transgress against them"; so the well-known disagreement comes in about the position of «أَنْ». Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda inclined to this meaning. Its meaning according to Abū ʿUbayd and al-Farrāʾ is "to earn"; from it comes «فلان جريمةُ أهله» ("So-and-so is the earner of his family"). Also from al-Kisāʾī: «جرم» and «أجرم» mean "earned [something] for another". On this it admits two analyses: the first, that it takes one object; the second, that it takes two objects, as «كَسَب» does. In the noble verse, however, it can only take two objects, the first being the pronoun of address, and the second «أن تعتدوا», i.e. "let not your hatred of a people earn you transgression against them".

ʿAbd Allāh read «يُجْرِمَنَّكم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from the quadriliteral «أجرم». It is said: it has the sense of «جَرَم», as was transmitted above from al-Kisāʾī; and it is said: «أجرم» is transferred from «جرم» by the hamza of transitivity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«جَرَم» runs like «كسب» in taking one object and two. You say «جَرَمَ ذنباً», like «كَسبه» (he earned a sin), and «جرمته ذنباً», i.e. I earned it for him; and one says «أجرمته ذنباً», by transferring a verb taking one object, by the hamza, to two objects, as in your saying «أكسبته ذنباً». On this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولا يُجْرمنكم». The first of the two objects «[Translator's note: the text has «المعفولين», a misprint for «المفعولين».]» in both readings is the pronoun of those addressed, and the second is «أَنْ تعتدوا»." End of quotation.

The root of this material — as Ibn ʿĪsā al-Rummānī said — is cutting. «جرم» meaning "impelled to something" is because it cuts him off from other things; «جَرَم» meaning "earned" is because of devoting oneself exclusively to earning; and «جَرَم» meaning «حَقّ» ("became due/true") is because the truth is decided upon. Al-Khalīl said: {لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ النار} [al-Naḥl: 62], i.e. "it has truly become due". So said al-Rummānī; he thus posited a common meaning among these words, and in his view it is not a case of homonymy.

«شَنآنُ» means hatred; it is the maṣdar of «شَنِئ», i.e. he hated. Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, read «شَنْآن» with the nūn vowelless; the rest with fatḥa on it. They permitted each of them to be a maṣdar or an adjective, so much so that it is related that Abū ʿAlī said: "Whoever claims that faʿlān, when its middle radical is vowelless, is not a maṣdar has erred" — except that faʿlān with vowelless middle is rare among maṣdars, as in «لَوَيْتُه دينه لَيَّاناً» ("I put him off from his debt"), whereas it is frequent among adjectives, as in «سَكْران» and its kind; and faʿalān with fatḥa is rare among adjectives — they said «حمارٌ قَطَوان», i.e. slow-paced, and «تيس عَدَوان»; the poet said:

168 - 8-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كَتَيْسِ ظِباء الحُلَّبِ العَدَوانِ
(… like the running buck of the gazelles of al-Ḥullab.)

And like it is the saying of another — Abū Zayd recited it:

168 - 9- وقبلَك ما هابَ الرجالُ ظُلامتي ... وفَقَّأْتُ عينَ الأَشْوَسِ الأَبَيَانِ
(Before you, men feared [to do] me wrong, and I put out the eye of the scornful, defiant one.)

with fatḥa on the bāʾ and the yāʾ. Rather, the frequent case is for it to be a maṣdar, as in «الغلَيان» and «النزوان».

If by «الشنآن» with vowelless middle the adjective is meant, the meaning is: "and let not the hated one of a people impel you", «بغيض» here meaning «مُبْغض», the active participle of «أبغض», which is transitive; so faʿīl is in the sense of the agent, like «قدير» and «نصير». Its annexation to «قوم» on this view is an annexation of explanation, i.e. the hater from among them, and it is not annexed to an agent or an object — unlike when you construe it as a maṣdar, for then it is annexed to its object or its agent, as will come. The proponent of this view said: "One says «رجلٌ شَنْآن» and «امرأة شنْآنة», like «نَدمان» and «ندمانة»; and the analogy of this is that it be from a transitive verb." He also reported «رجل شنآن» and «امرأة شَنْأى», like «سَكْران» and «سكرى»; the analogy of this is that it be from an intransitive verb. There is nothing far-fetched in that, for they sometimes derive the intransitive and the transitive from one root «[Translator's note: the text has «واحة», a misprint for «واحدة».]»: they said «فَغَرْتُ فاه» and «فَغَر فُوه», i.e. "I opened it and it opened".

If the maṣdar is meant by it, it is clear; it is annexed to its object, i.e. "your hatred of a people", the agent being omitted; or it may be annexed to its agent, i.e. "a people's hatred of you", its object being omitted. The first is more apparent in meaning. The ruling of «شنآن» with fatḥa on the nūn, as maṣdar and adjective, is the ruling of the one with vowelless nūn; its explanation has preceded. Among instances of «شَنآن» with vowelless middle as a maṣdar is the saying of al-Aḥwaṣ:

169 - 0- وما الحبُّ إلا مَا تَلذُّ وتَشْتَهي ... وإنْ لامَ فيه ذو الشَّنَانِ وفَنَّدا
(Love is nothing but what you delight in and desire, even if the hater blames and reproaches you for it.)

He meant «الشنْآن» with vowelless nūn; he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the vowelless nūn and deleted the hamza; were it not for the nūn being vowelless, the transfer would not have been permissible. Were someone to say that the original is «الشنآن» with fatḥa on the nūn, and he lightened the hamza by deleting it entirely — as {إنها لاحْدى الكُبَر} [al-Muddaththir: 35] was read with the hamza of «إحدى» deleted — it would be a view by which the evidence falls, because of its being possible.

«الشنآن» with fatḥa is among what is anomalous with respect to the general rule. Sībawayh said: "Every maṣdar form on the pattern faʿalān with fatḥa on the middle radical, its verb is not transitive, unless something is anomalous, like «الشَّنآن»", meaning that it is a maṣdar on faʿalān with fatḥa, and yet its verb is transitive. Its verb is among the verbs with the most maṣdars: sixteen maṣdars have been heard for it. They said: «شَنِئَ يَشْنَأُ شَنْئَاً وشَنآناً», with all three vowels on the shīn; so these are six dialectal forms.

Ibn Waththāb, al-Ḥasan, and al-Walīd from Yaʿqūb read «يَجْرِمَنْكم» with the nūn vowelless, making it the light nūn of emphasis. The prohibition in wording is addressed to the hatred, but in meaning to those addressed, as in «لا أُرَينَّك ههنا» ("Let me not see you here") and {فَلاَ تَمُوتُنَّ إَلاَّ وَأَنْتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ} [al-Baqara: 132]. Al-Makkī said [this].

His saying, Exalted is He: {أَن صَدُّوكُمْ}: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read «إنْ» with kasra, and the rest with fatḥa. Whoever reads kasra takes it as conditional; the fatḥa takes it as the cause of the hatred, i.e. "let not your hatred of a people, because they turned you away from the Sacred Mosque, earn you" or "impel you"; and it is a clear reading.

People have found the reading of the two Abūs [Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr] problematic, in that the condition requires that the conditioned matter has not occurred, whereas the premise is that their turning [the believers] away from the Sacred House had already happened and occurred, and the revelation of this verse came some time after it: the turning away occurred in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya, which was the year six, and the verse was revealed in the year eight; moreover, Mecca was in their hands in the year of the Conquest, so how could they be turned away from it? Ibn Jurayj, al-Naḥḥās and others said: "This reading is objectionable", and they argued by the difficulty mentioned. But there is no difficulty in it. The answer to what they said is from two angles. The first: we do not grant that the turning away was before the revelation of the verse, for its revelation in the year of the Conquest is not agreed upon; al-Yazīdī mentioned that it was revealed before the turning away, so the turning away was an expected matter. The second: even if we grant that the turning away preceded its revelation, the meaning is: "if there occurs a turning away like the one that occurred at the time of al-Ḥudaybiya — or if they persist in that turning away that occurred from them — then let it not impel you". Al-Makkī said: "Its like according to Sībawayh is the saying of the poet — namely al-Farazdaq:

169 - 1- أتغضَبُ إنْ أُذْنا قتيبةَ حُزَّنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Are you angry if the two ears of Qutayba were cut off? …)

and that is something that had happened and occurred; its meaning is only: if the like of that occurs, the anger [would follow]; and the apodosis of the condition is what precedes it" — i.e. the apodosis is indicated by what precedes it, because the Basrans, except Abū Zayd, forbid fronting the apodosis. Al-Makkī also said: "Its parallel is that a man says to his wife «أنت طالق إنْ دخلت الدار» ('You are divorced if you enter the house') with kasra on «إن»: she is not divorced from him by her first entry [already past], because it is an awaited matter; but if he used fatḥa, she would be divorced from him, because it is a matter that has happened and occurred. So the fatḥa of «أن» is for what is the cause of something that has happened and occurred, and its kasra is only for an awaited matter; and both analyses are good according to their two meanings." In what al-Makkī said, the jurists distinguished between one who knows grammar and one who does not.

Supporting «[Translator's note: the text has «ويؤد», a misprint for «ويؤيد».]» the reading of the two Abūs is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «إنْ يَصُدُّوكم». Abū ʿUbayd said: "Ḥajjāj narrated to us from Hārūn, who said: Ibn Masʿūd read it" — and he mentioned it — "and he said: this can only be on a renewed turning away", i.e. if another turning away occurs like the one that preceded in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya.

The arrangement of these verses as they stand is of the utmost eloquence and clarity, and there is no fronting or postponing in them, as some claimed, saying: the original construction of the first verse is «غيرَ محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم، فإذا حَلَلْتم فاصطادوا», and the original construction of the second is {ولا آمِّينَ البيت الحرام يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلاً مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَاناً وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصطادوا وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ}; and he compared it to the verse of al-Baqara, meaning {إِنَّ الله يَأْمُرُكُمْ} [verse 67]. This is not needed, besides which fronting and postponing is, according to the majority, among the licences of poetry, so the Qurʾān must be kept free of it. Nor is the clause in His saying {وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصطادوا} parenthetical between His saying {ولا آمِّينَ البيت الحرام} and His saying {وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ}; rather, it is foundational and establishes a ruling, namely the lawfulness of hunting upon leaving iḥrām; a parenthetical clause conveys only emphasis and reinforcement, whereas this conveys a new ruling, as has preceded.

His saying: {أَن تَعْتَدُواْ}: it has preceded that it is among the dependents of «لا يجرمنكم», as a second object or by omission of the preposition. For whoever reads «إن صدوكم» with kasra, the condition and its implied apodosis are in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «قوم», i.e. "hatred of a people whose description is this". For whoever reads it with fatḥa, its position is genitive or accusative, because it is by the omission of the causal lām, as has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: let not the hatred of a people, because they turned you away, earn you transgression, nor impel you to it." Al-Shaykh said: "This is an explanation of meaning, not an explanation of i'rab, because it is impossible for the denotation of «جرم» to be 'impel' and 'earn' in a single use, because their requirements differ; so it is impossible for «[أن] تعتدوا» to be in the position of a direct object and in the position of an object by dropping of the preposition." What he said here is inconceivable to be imagined by anyone with the least insight into the craft, so that it should need pointing out.

The reading of al-Bazzī in the like of «ولا تَّعاوَنُوا» has preceded, and that the original is «تتعاونوا», then assimilated; the rest deleted one of the two tāʾs — [discussed] at His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث} [al-Baqara: 267].

semin-durr:95-95.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ}: in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تقتلوا». «حُرُمٌ» is the plural of «حَرام», and «حَرام» applies to one in iḥrām even if he is outside the sanctuary (al-ḥill), and to one in the sanctuary (al-ḥaram) even if he is not in iḥrām; the two are equal in the prohibition of killing game. Discussion of this word was given earlier.

His saying: {منكم}: in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «قَتَله», i.e. "being one of you." It has been said that «مِنْ» is explicative (li-l-bayān), but that is nothing, because the ruling on everyone who kills game is the same. If you say: this objection also applies to making it a ḥāl, I say: no implied contrary sense (mafhūm) was intended by that, such that if someone other than you killed it there would be no compensation upon him; because by the address another meaning was intended, namely emphasis in the prohibition of killing game.

His saying: {مُّتَعَمِّداً}: also a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «قَتَلَه». Whoever permits multiple ḥāls permits that here; and whoever forbids it says that «منكم» is explicative, so that the ḥāl is not multiplied. And «مَنْ» may be conditional — which is the apparent view — or relative, the fāʾ [then entering] because of its resemblance to the conditional; but there is no need for that, even though they did so in [other] places.

His saying: «فجزاء»: the fāʾ is that of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), or redundant because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to the condition. On the first, the clause after it is in the position of a jussive; on the second, in the position of a nominative. And what follows «مَنْ» is, on the first, in the position of a jussive, being the protasis; and on the second it has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause).

The people of Kufa read «فجزاءٌ مثلُ» with tanwīn on «جزاء», in the nominative, and «مثل» in the nominative. The rest of the Seven read it in the nominative, annexed to «مثل». Muḥammad ibn Muqātil read «جزاءً» with tanwīn in the accusative, and «مثلَ» in the accusative. Al-Sulamī read «جزاء» nominative with tanwīn, and «مثل» accusative. And ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read {فجزاؤُه}, «جزاء» nominative annexed to a pronoun, with «مثل» nominative.

As for the reading of the Kufans, it is because «مثل» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جزاء», i.e. "then upon him is a compensation qualified by being 'the like of what he killed'," i.e. equivalent to it. Makkī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others permitted «مثل» to be nominative as a badal (substitute). Al-Zajjāj mentioned a strange view, namely that «مثل» is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «جزاء», with «جزاء» being the mubtadaʾ (subject). He said: "The implied form is: then the compensation for that act is the like of what he killed." I say: this view is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «فجزاؤُه مثلُ»; except that it is better to take that omitted element as a pronoun referring back to the killed animal, not to take it as "the compensation for that act."

And «مثل» is in the sense of «مماثل» (equivalent); a group said this — al-Zamakhsharī and others — and that is the meaning of the word, for it has the force of an active participle. But Makkī imagined that «مِثْل» may be in a sense other than «مماثل», for he said: "«مثل» in this reading — meaning the reading of the Kufans — is in the sense of «مُماثِل», the implied form being: then a compensation equivalent to what he killed — meaning in value or in form, according to the disagreement of the scholars. If you took «مِثْل» according to its wording, the meaning would become: then upon him is a compensation like the killed game; whereas what is required of him is only the compensation for the killed animal itself, not a compensation for its like; because if he paid a compensation [for] the like of the killed animal, he would have paid the compensation for what was not killed, since he did not kill the like of the killed animal. So it is sound that the meaning is: then upon him is a compensation equivalent to the killed animal. For that reason the reading with annexation was considered unlikely by a group."

I say: «مثل» is always in the sense of «مُماثِل», so how can he say "if you took «مِثْل» according to its wording"? Moreover, his saying "the meaning would become … to the end": this difficulty he mentioned cannot be conceived to arise in this reading at all; people only mentioned it regarding the reading with annexation, as will come. It is as though he transferred this difficulty from the reading with annexation to the reading with tanwīn.

As for the reading of the rest of the Seven, a group considered it unlikely. Al-Wāḥidī said: "The compensation ought not to be annexed to «المِثْل», because upon him is the compensation for the transmitted animal, not the compensation for its like, for there is no compensation upon him for it since he did not kill it." [Translator's note: the source reads «المنقول» ("the transmitted"), evidently a misprint for «المقتول» ("the killed").] And Makkī said, after what I quoted from him: "For that reason the reading with annexation was considered unlikely by a group, because it requires a compensation for the like of the killed game." I say: no attention is to be paid to this judgement of unlikelihood, for most of the readers follow it. People have answered that with sound answers, and since these were hidden from those [scholars], they impugned what is mutawātir (mass-transmitted).

Among them: that «جزاء» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object for lightness, the original being: "then upon him is a compensation, the like of what he killed," i.e. that he give in compensation the like of what he killed; then it was annexed, as you say «عجبت من ضربٍ زيداً» ("I wondered at a striking of Zayd") and then «من ضرب زيدٍ»; al-Zamakhsharī and others mentioned it. The elaboration of that is that «الجزاء» here is in the sense of making good (al-qaḍāʾ), and the original is: "then upon him is that the killed game be compensated with its like from livestock"; then the first object was omitted because the speech indicates it, and the maṣdar was annexed to the second of them, as in your saying «زيدٌ فقيرٌ ويعجبني إعطاؤك الدرهمَ» ("Zayd is poor, and your giving the dirham pleases me"), i.e. your giving it to him.

And among them: that «مثل» is inserted (muqḥama), as in their saying «مِثْلُك لا يفعل ذلك» ("the like of you does not do that"), i.e. you do not do that; and like His saying, Exalted is He, {فَإِنْ آمَنُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَآ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ} [al-Baqara: 137], i.e. in what you have believed [in]; and like His saying {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ} [al-Shūrā: 11]; so «مثل» is redundant. But this is contrary to the base rule, so the answer is what I gave first.

And «ما» may be a nominal relative noun or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and the returning pronoun is omitted on both analyses, i.e. "the like of what he killed, from livestock."

For those who read «جزاء» in the nominative there are four views. The first: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "then upon him is a compensation." The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "then what is obligatory is a compensation." The third: it is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, i.e. "then a compensation is binding on him" or "is obligatory upon him." The fourth: it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «مثل»; it was stated above that this is the school of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj. It was also stated above that «مثل» is nominative in the reading of the Kufans on one of three views: naʿt, badal and khabar, where we said that «جزاء» is a mubtadaʾ according to al-Zajjāj.

As for the reading {فجزاؤه مثلُ}, it is also clear. As for the reading «فجزاءٌ مثلَ», with «جزاء» nominative with tanwīn and «مثل» accusative, it is on the basis of the tanwīn-bearing maṣdar governing its object — and it was stated above that the reading with annexation is from this — and it is the counterpart of His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14-15]. Its fāʿil is omitted, i.e. "then the compensation of one of you," or "of the killer," i.e. that the killer of the game give compensation. As for the reading «فجزاءً مثلَ» with both in the accusative, «جزاءً» is accusative as a maṣdar or as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «مثلَ» is its naʿt on both considerations, the implied form being: "then let him compensate with a compensation the like of…," or "then let him bring out a compensation," or "then let him be fined a compensation the like of…."

His saying: {مِنَ النعم}: there are three views on it. The first: it is a naʿt of «جزاء» absolutely, i.e. whether it is read nominative or accusative, with or without tanwīn; i.e. that compensation is of the kind of livestock. This view is not excluded in any case. The second: it is attached to «جزاء» itself, because it is a maṣdar; except that this is permissible only in the reading of those who annexed «جزاء» to «مثل», for nothing objectionable follows from it — unlike when you give it tanwīn and make «مثل» its naʿt, or a badal from it, or a khabar for it; for that is then excluded. Because if you make it qualified by «مثل», that is forbidden on two counts. The first: the qualified maṣdar does not govern, and this one has been qualified. The second: it is a maṣdar, so it is in the position of a relative noun, and the governed word is part of the completion of its ṣila; and it is established that the relative noun is not followed [by an appositive] until its ṣila is complete, lest it entail separation by a foreign element. And if you make it a badal, it entails following the relative noun before its ṣila is complete; and if you make it a khabar, it entails predicating of the relative noun before its ṣila is complete; and none of that is permissible. The third: mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ, namely that it is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun of the relative noun, for the implied form is: "then a compensation the like of that which he killed, while it is of livestock." This is a mistake, because what is qualified as being of livestock is only the compensation for the killed game; as for the game itself, it is not of livestock.

The majority read the ʿayn of «النَّعَم» with fatḥa, and al-Ḥasan read it with sukūn. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is a dialect." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He found the vowel on the guttural letter heavy, just as they said «الشَّعْر» for «الشَّعَر»."

His saying: {يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا}: in the position of a nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «جزاء», or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, or as a naʿt of «جزاء» for those who read it in the accusative. Abū al-Baqāʾ restricted its being a naʿt to the reading with tanwīn on «جزاء», and the ḥāl to the reading with its annexation; but there is no difference — rather the clause may be a naʿt or a ḥāl on both considerations, because when it is annexed to «مثل» it remains indefinite, since «مِثْل» does not become definite by annexation. Likewise Makkī restricted the naʿt to the reading with annexation of «الجزاء» to «مِثْل», for he said: "And «من النَّعم», in the reading of those who annexed «الجزاء» to «مِثْل», is a naʿt of «جزاء»; and it is good for [«من»] to be attached to the maṣdar, so that it is not a naʿt, the maṣdar merely being made transitive to «من النعم». And if you make it a naʿt, then «مِنْ» is attached to the omitted khabar, namely «فعليه»." [Translator's note: the source has «فعلية», evidently a misprint for «فعليه» ("then upon him").]

There are two objections to this statement. The first was given above, namely the restriction to the reading with annexation. The second: when he made «من النَّعم» a naʿt, he attached it to the omitted khabar, because of the notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār) it contains; and that is not so, because when a preposition-and-genitive phrase occurs as a naʿt, it is attached to an omitted element, and that omitted element is in reality the qualifier; whereas what he made the attachment-point of this naʿt is not in reality a qualifier of the thing qualified, but rather a khabar about it. Do you not see that if you said «عندي رجلٌ من بني تميم» ("I have a man of Banū Tamīm"), «مِنْ بني» is in reality attached to an omitted qualifier, not to your saying «عندي»? [Translator's note: the source has «مِنْ بين», evidently for «مِنْ بني».] It might be said — and it is very far-fetched — that he meant attachment in meaning: that is, what governs the thing qualified governs its naʿt, and «عليه» governs «جزاء», so it governs its naʿt; so the attachment is from this angle. But that only works where we make the khabar the governor of the mubtadaʾ, or say that the preposition-and-genitive phrase governs a fāʿil in the nominative even without support. I only mention these explanations because those who held such views are among those whose statements are not to be discarded altogether.

The alif in «ذوا» is the sign of the nominative of the dual. Discussion of the derivation of this word and its inflections was given earlier. The majority read {ذَوا} with the alif, and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq read «ذو» in the singular form. They said: "He does not mean singularity by that; rather he means: one who is of the people of justice judges it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And it was said: he meant the imām"; on this view, singularity is intended. And «منكم» is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt of «ذوا», i.e. the two are of your kind in religion. It may not be a naʿt of «عَدْل» because that is a maṣdar (verbal noun); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, meaning that the maṣdar is not of their kind, so how can it be qualified as being from among them?

His saying: {هَدْياً}: there are six views on it. The most apparent of them: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «به». Al-Zajjāj said: "It is accusative as a ḥāl, the meaning being: he judges it, intending that it be offered"; he means that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), not a concomitant one. Al-Fārisī said likewise, as in your saying «معه صقرٌ صائداً به غداً» ("he has a falcon, to hunt with it tomorrow"), i.e. intending to hunt.

The second: it is a ḥāl from «جزاء», whether it is read nominative or accusative, with tanwīn or annexed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«هَدْياً» is a ḥāl from «جزاء» for those who qualified it with «مثل», because the qualifier specified it, so it came close to the definite." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] restricted it likewise. This is not clear; rather the ḥāl-status is permissible absolutely, as stated above.

The third: it is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "he offers it as an offering (يُهديه هَدْياً)"; Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it.

The fourth: it is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī said this, except that Makkī said "as an explanation (ʿalā al-bayān)", which is tamyīz in meaning. It is as though both of them thought that it is a tamyīz of what is left vague in the "likeness," since there is nothing here fit for specification other than it. This is open to question, inasmuch as tamyīz only removes vagueness from entities, not from qualities; and this, as you see, only removes vagueness from a quality, because «الهَدْي» is a quality in meaning, since what is meant by it is «مُهْدَى» (something offered).

The fifth: it is accusative in accordance with the position of «مثل», for those who read it in the genitive, because its position is accusative through the maṣdar's implied governing of it, as was set out above.

The sixth: it is a badal (substitute) from «جزاء», for those who read it in the accusative.

And «بالغ الكعبة» is a naʿt of «هَدْياً», and it did not become definite by the annexation, because it governs «الكعبة» in the accusative by implication; like it is {هذا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [al-Aḥqāf: 24], and the saying of the other [poet]:
181 - 0- يا رُبَّ غابِطِنا لو كان يَطْلُبُكُمْ ... لاقَى مباعَدةً منكم وحِرْمانا
(Many a one who envies us — were he to seek you, he would meet with distance from you and deprivation.)
— in that the annexation in them is not genuine (ghayr maḥḍa). Al-Aʿraj read «هَدِيَّاً» with kasra on the dāl and a doubled yāʾ.

His saying: {أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ}: conjoined to His saying {فَجَزَآءٌ}, and «أو» here is for choice (takhyīr). It was transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is not for choice but for sequence (tartīb). This is on the reading of those who read «فجزاءٌ» in the nominative. As for those who read it in the accusative, al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: or what is obligatory upon him is an expiation. And you may supply: then upon him is that he compensate with a compensation, or an expiation, so you conjoin «كفارة» to «أَنْ يَجْزي»." He means that «عليه» would be a fronted khabar and «أَنْ يَجْزي» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and you conjoined «الكفارة» to this mubtadaʾ.

Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read {كفارة} annexed to what follows it, and the rest with tanwīn and with what follows it in the nominative. As for the reading of the group, it is clear, and «طعام» is nominative on one of three views. The first: it is a badal from «كفارة», since it is of its kind. The second: it is an explicative apposition (bayān) of it, as stated earlier; al-Fārisī said this, and the Shaykh rejected it on the grounds that the school of the Basrans restricts ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to definite nouns, not indefinites. I say: Abū ʿAlī differs on that and argues with proofs, among them: {شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ} [al-Nūr: 35], where «زيتونةٍ» is for him ʿaṭf bayān of «شجرة»; and likewise His saying, Exalted is He: {مِن مَّآءٍ صَدِيدٍ} [Ibrāhīm: 16], where «صديد» is for him a badal from «ماء». [Translator's note: the source says «بدل» here, though the context (arguing for ʿaṭf bayān with indefinites) suggests «بيان» was meant; translated as written.] But the badal is possible in both, so there is no proof for him, and the badal sometimes comes for explanation. The third: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is food," i.e. that expiation.

As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, its justification is that since the expiation was of different kinds — expiation by food, expiation by the equivalent compensation, and expiation by fasting — it was good to annex it to one of its kinds to make that clear; and annexation takes place on the slightest connection, as in [the poet's] saying:
181 - 1- إذا كوكبُ الخَرْقاءِ لاحَ بسُحْرَةٍ ... سهيلٌ أذاعَتْ غَزْلَها في القَرائبِ
(When the star of the clumsy woman — Suhayl — gleams at dawn, she scatters her spinning among her kinswomen.)
He annexed the star to her because of her rising [to work] at its appearance; so this is more fitting.

Al-Zamakhsharī justified it and said: "This annexation is explicative, as though it were said: or an expiation of the food of the poor, as in your saying «خاتمُ فضةٍ» ('a ring of silver'), meaning [made] of silver." The Shaykh said: "What he claimed is not of this category, because «خاتم فضة» is of the category of annexing a thing to its genus, and food is not a genus of expiation except by a very far-fetched extension of usage." End of quotation. I say: he ought to have said: "and expiation is not a genus of food," because «الكفارة» in the construction is the counterpart of «خاتم», in that each of them is the muḍāf to what follows it; so just as «خاتم» is what is annexed to its genus, it ought to be said, for the sake of the correspondence, that the expiation is not a genus of food. But that cannot be said, for the expiation, as stated above, is a genus of food, compensation and fasting. So the way to refute Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] is to say: the condition of annexation in the sense of «مِنْ» is that a part be annexed to a whole, on the condition that the name of the whole be true of the part, as in «خاتمُ فضة»; and «كفارة طعامٍ» is not so, rather it is the annexation of a whole to a part.

A group found this reading problematic on the grounds that the expiation is not for the food; it is only for killing the game. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and others said so; and its answer is what was given above.

The Seven did not differ over the plural «مساكين» here, though they differed in al-Baqara. They said: the difference between the two is that in killing game, feeding a single poor person does not suffice. However, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Aʿraj read «كفارة» with tanwīn and «طعام مسكين» in the nominative in the singular; they said: their intention is to express the genus, not singularity.

His saying: {أَو عَدْلُ}: conjoined to «فجزاء». The majority read the ʿayn with fatḥa, and Ibn ʿAbbās, Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and al-Jaḥdarī read it with kasra; I explained their meanings at the beginning of this work at His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ} [al-Baqara: 48]. And «ذلك» points to the food; its manner is mentioned in "al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr". And «صياماً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), because the meaning is "or the measure of that in fasting," so it is like your saying «لي مِلْؤُه عسلاً» ("I have its fill in honey"). The original of «صِياماً» is «صِواماً», and it was weakened for the reason known more than once.

His saying: {لِّيَذُوقَ}: there are six views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جزاء»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh said: "That only works where it is annexed to «مثل», or «جزاء» is given tanwīn and «مثل» is accusative." He gave as reason that if «مثل» is nominative it is a naʿt of the maṣdar, and when the maṣdar is qualified it does not govern — unless the governed word comes before its qualifier, as in «يعجبني الضربُ زيداً الشديدُ» ("the severe striking of Zayd pleases me"), which is permissible.

I say: likewise if he made it a badal too, or a khabar, because of what was stated earlier, that it entails following the relative noun, or predicating of it, before its ṣila is complete, and that is forbidden. The Shaykh's words convey explicitly that on the reading with annexation of «الجزاء» to «مثل», what Abū al-Qāsim said is permissible. And I say: that is not permissible either, because «ليذوقَ» is part of the completion of the maṣdar's ṣila, and His saying «أو كفارةٌ أو عَدْلٌ» has been conjoined to it, so it entails conjoining to the relative noun before its ṣila is complete; and that is not permissible — if you said «جاء الذي ضَرَبَ وعمروٌ زيداً» it would not be allowed, because of separating the ṣila — or parts of it — from the relative noun by a foreign element. So consider it, for it is a fine point.

The second: it is attached to an omitted verb indicated by the force of the speech, as though it were said: "he is requited with that so that he may taste." The third: it is attached to the implied "being settled" (al-istiqrār) before His saying {فجزاء}, since the implied form is "then upon him is a compensation, so that he may taste." The fourth: it is attached to «صيام», i.e. his fasting so that he may taste. The fifth: it is attached to «طعام», i.e. food so that he may taste. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned these three views, and they are very weak; the best of them is the first. The sixth: it is attached to «عَدْل ذلك»; the Shaykh transmitted it from some of the parsers and said — and it is as he said — "a mistake."

And «الوَبال» is an evil outcome and that whose harm is feared. Al-Rāghib said: "«الوابل» is rain with heavy drops; and in consideration of heaviness, a matter whose harm is feared is called «وبال». The Exalted said: {ذَاقُواْ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِمْ} [al-Ḥashr: 15]. And one says «طعامٌ وَبيلٌ» and «كلأ وبيل» (food / pasture) whose ill effect is feared. The Exalted said: {فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذاً وَبِيلاً} [al-Muzzammil: 16]." Another said: "«الوبال» in the language is the heaviness of a thing in what is disliked. One says «مرعىً وبيل» when it is found unwholesome, and «ماء وبيلٌ» when it is not found agreeable; and «استوَبَلْتُ الأرضَ»: I disliked the land, fearing its ill effect." And «الذوق» (tasting) here is an eloquent metaphor.

His saying: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional, the fāʾ being its apodosis, and «ينتقمُ» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then He takes retribution"; the jussive with the fāʾ is not permissible at all. And it may be relative, the fāʾ entering the khabar of the mubtadaʾ because it resembles the condition; so the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause after it is the khabar, and there is no need to supply a mubtadaʾ after the fāʾ, unlike the previous case. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The entry of the fāʾ was made good by the verb of the condition being past in form."

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ}: the discussion has preceded on «أنَّ» occurring after «لو», and that there are two doctrines on it. «لهم» is the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ», «ما في الأرض» is its noun, and «جميعاً» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of it or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it. There are two views on the accusative case of «مثلَه». One of them: that it is conjoined to the noun of «أنَّ», namely the relative «ما». The second: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); this is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī, and the objection to it and the answer will come.

«معه» is an adverb in the place of a ḥāl. The lām in «ليفتدوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [verb of] settledness to which the khabar «لهم» is attached. «به» and «مِنْ عذاب» are attached to the ransoming. The pronoun in «به» refers to the relative «ما». The pronoun was brought as singular although two things precede it, namely «ما في الأرض» and «مثلَه»: either because they are inseparable, so they have the ruling of a single thing; or because it was omitted from the second because what is in the first indicates it, as in the poet's saying:

172 - 2-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإني وقَيَّارٌ بها لَغَريبُ
(… then I and Qayyār are indeed strangers there)

i.e. "if they had what is on earth to ransom themselves with it, and its like with it to ransom themselves with it"; or because the pronoun is treated like a demonstrative, as in the poet's saying:

172 - 3- كأنَّه الجِلْدِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(As though it were … the skin …)

— and this has preceded in al-Baqara. «عذاب» is in the sense of «تعذيب» (punishing), and by its being annexed to «يوم», «يوم» departs from being an adverb. «ما» is negative and is the answer of «لو»; it came according to the more frequent usage, in that the negated answer is without lām. The clause of impossibility [i.e. the «لو» clause] is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ».

Al-Zamakhsharī made the singular pronoun in «به» due to another consideration, namely that the wāw in «ومثلَه» is the wāw of «مع» (accompaniment). After mentioning the two aforementioned views, he said: "The wāw in «ومثلَه» may be in the sense of «مع», so that what is referred to is single. If you say: then by what is the mafʿūl maʿahu made accusative? I say: by the verb that «لو» calls for, because the implied form is: 'if it were established that they had what is on earth'." He means that the ruling of what precedes the mafʿūl maʿahu, as regards the khabar, the ḥāl and the reference of the pronoun, is the ruling it would have if no mafʿūl maʿahu came after it. You say «كنتُ وزيداً كالأخ» ("I, together with Zayd, was like the brother"). He said:

172 - 4- وكان وإيَّاها كحَرَّان لم يُفِقْ ... عن الماءِ إذ لاقَاه حتى تَقَدَّدا
(He, together with her, was like a thirsty man who, when he met the water, did not desist from it until he burst)

So he said «كحَرَّان» in the singular and did not say «كحرَّانَيْنِ». And you say «جاء زيد وهنداً ضاحكاً في داره» ("Zayd came, together with Hind, laughing, in his house"). Al-Akhfash permitted it to be given the ruling of two conjoined nouns, meaning that the khabar, the ḥāl and the pronoun agree with it and with what comes after it, so you say «كنتُ وزيداً كالأخوين». One of them said: "What is correct is that it is permissible, though rare."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] refuted Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] and spoke at length with him, so his text must be quoted. He said: "As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying 'the wāw may be in the sense of «مع»' [it is not sound], because the implied form becomes: 'with its like with it', i.e. with the like of what is on earth together with what is on earth. If you make the pronoun in «معه» refer to «ما», «معه» would be a ḥāl from «مثلَه»; and if what is on earth is with its like, its like is necessarily with it, so there is no benefit in mentioning «معه», since the accompaniment of each of them with the other is inseparable. If you make the pronoun refer to «مثله», i.e. with its like together with that like, the meaning would be 'with two likes', and expressing this meaning with that wording is inarticulate (ʿiyy), since the well-ordered speech, if that meaning were intended, would be the construction «مع مِثْلَيْه» ('with its two likes'). As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying 'If you say …' to the end of the answer, this question does not arise, because we have shown the unsoundness of the wāw being the wāw of «مع». On the supposition that it does arise, this is based on his view that «أنَّ», when it comes after «لو», is in the position of the nominative as agent; so the implied form on this view would be: 'if the being of what is on earth together with its like were established for them to ransom themselves with it', and the pronoun would refer to «ما» only. What he mentioned is a derivation on his part from the doctrine of al-Mubarrad that «أنَّ» after «لو» is in the position of the nominative as agent, which is a less preferred doctrine; the doctrine of Sībawayh is that «أنَّ» after «لو» is in the position of a mubtadaʾ (subject). What appears in al-Zamakhsharī's words here and in his works is that he did not come across Sībawayh's doctrine on this issue. And on what is derived from al-Mubarrad's doctrine, it is not permissible for the wāw to be in the sense of «مع» with the implied «ثَبَتَ» governing it, because of what has preceded about the presence of the word «معه». And on the supposition of its absence it is still not sound, because «ثبت» does not put in the nominative the «ما» to which the pronoun refers; it only puts in the nominative a maṣdar formed from «أنَّ» and what follows it, namely 'being', since the implied form is: 'if the being of all that is on earth theirs, and its like with it, were established to ransom themselves with it'; and the pronoun refers to «ما», not to the being. So what puts the agent in the nominative is not what puts the mafʿūl maʿahu in the accusative; for if it were the same, it would entail that the establishment exists accompanying the like, whereas the meaning is about the being of what is on earth accompanying the like, not about the establishment of that accompanying the like. There is obscurity in this, and its explanation is: if you say «يعجبني قيامُ زيدٍ وعمراً» ('Zayd's standing, together with ʿAmr, pleases me') and make «عمراً» a mafʿūl maʿahu governed by «يعجبني», it follows that ʿAmr did not stand, and that the standing and ʿAmr pleased you; whereas if you make what governs it the standing, ʿAmr would be standing, and the pleasing would be connected with the standing accompanied by ʿAmr's standing. If you say: could «ومثلَه معه» be a mafʿūl maʿahu governed by what governs «لهم», since the meaning is upon that? I say: that is not sound, because of what we mentioned about the presence of «معه» in the clause; and on the supposition of its absence it is not sound, because they have stated explicitly that your saying «هذا لك وأباك» ('this is yours, together with your father') is barred in free usage. Sībawayh said: 'As for «هذا لك وأباك», it is ugly, because he has mentioned neither a verb nor a particle containing the meaning of a verb, such that it would become as though he had uttered the verb.' So Sībawayh made clear that the demonstrative and the preposition containing the meaning of settledness do not govern the mafʿūl maʿahu. [Translator's note: the source prints «فأصبح سيبويه»; «فأفصح سيبويه» ("Sībawayh made clear") is evidently meant.] Some grammarians permitted the preposition and the adverb to govern the mafʿūl maʿahu, as in «هذا لك وأباك», so his saying «وأباك» would be a mafʿūl maʿahu governed by the settledness in «لك»." End of quotation.

Despite this objection he mentioned, an answer to it may appear, namely that we say: we choose that the pronoun in His saying {معه} refers to «مثلَه», and the meaning becomes "with two likes", which is more emphatic than being with a single like; and his saying "an inarticulate construction" is a deficient understanding. A clause must be omitted before His saying {مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ}, its implied form being: "and they offered it" or "and they ransomed themselves with it", so that the mentioned sequence is sound, since non-acceptance does not follow from all that is on earth and its like with it being settled as theirs; non-acceptance follows only from offering and ransoming. The generality [of readers] read «تُقُبِّل» in the passive, its agent being omitted because of His greatness and because He is known. Yazīd ibn Quṭayb read «ما تَقَبَّل» in the active, [its agent] being the pronoun of the Creator, Blessed and Exalted is He.

His saying: {وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar (predicate) fronted before it, and «أليم» is its adjective, in the sense of «مُؤْلم» (painful). They permitted three views on this clause. One of them: that it is a ḥāl; there is weakness in this from the point of view of meaning. The second: that it is in the position of the nominative by conjunction with the khabar of «أنَّ»: He informed about those who disbelieve with two predicates: that if all that is on earth together with its like were settled as theirs and they offered it, it would not be accepted from them; and that they have a painful punishment. The third: that it is conjoined to the clause in His saying {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ}; on this view it has no grammatical position, because it is conjoined to what has no position.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَخْرُجُواْ}: it is like His saying {يُرِيدُ الله أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 28], which has preceded. The majority read «أن يخرجوا» in the active, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read «يُخْرَجوا» in the passive; the explanation of both is clear.

semin-durr:115-115.t:
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read {مُنَزِّلُهَا} with the doubled consonant. It was said that أَنْزَل and نَزَّل have the same meaning, and the verification of that has preceded. It was also said: the doubling is for multiplicity, for in the exegesis it is [reported] that it came down many times. As for نُنَزِّلُ, the verification of the disagreement about it has preceded.

The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَعْدُ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يكفر», and made indeclinable because it is cut off from annexation, since the origin is "after the sending down". «منكم» is attached to an omitted [word], because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَكْفُرْ». His words: {عَذَاباً}: there are two aspects concerning it. The more apparent of them: that it is a noun of the maṣdar meaning التعذيب (punishing), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the augment letters omitted, as in «عطاء» and «نبات» for «أعطى» and «أنبت»; its accusative is as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) on both stated assumptions. The second — Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it — that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), meaning he made the event a direct object for intensification; in that case its accusative is by resemblance to the direct object.
