What is accusative by resemblance to the direct object is, according to the grammarians, of three kinds: the governed word of the ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle), and the maṣdar and the adverb when extended. The maṣdar is as above; the adverb is as in «يوم الجمعة صُمتُه» (Friday, I fasted it), and from it is his saying:

185 - 6- ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سُلَيْماً وعامراً ... قليلٌ سوى الطعنِ النِّهالِ نوافِلُهْ
(Many a day we witnessed it, [against] Sulaym and ʿĀmir, whose spoils were few save thirsty spear-thrusts.)

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Had what is meant by العذاب been that with which one is punished, the bāʾ would have been necessary." I say: he only said that because the application of العذاب to that with which one is punished is frequent, so he feared that this would be imagined. No one may say: the origin was «بعذاب», then the preposition was omitted and its genitive noun became accusative; because that is regular only with «أَنْ», on condition that ambiguity is avoided.

His words: {لاَّ أُعَذِّبُهُ}: there are three aspects concerning the hāʾ. The most apparent of them: that it refers to «عذاب», which, as stated, means التعذيب; the implied form being: "I shall punish him with a punishing such that I do not punish anyone with the like of that punishing". The clause is in the position of accusative as a description of «عذاباً». This aspect is free of the strain you will see in the others. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this aspect — I mean its referring to the preceding «عذاباً» — he said: "On this there are two aspects in it. The first: on the omission of a preposition, i.e. I will not punish anyone with it. The second: that it is a mafʿūl bihi by extension." I say: as for his saying "the preposition was omitted", you have learned that it is not permissible except in what was excepted. The second of the aspects of the hāʾ: that it refers to «مَن» preceding in His words: {فَمَن يَكْفُرْ}, the meaning being: I will not punish anyone with the like of the unbeliever's punishment; and these two muḍāfs must be assumed for the meaning to be sound. Abū al-Baqāʾ said on this aspect: "There is an omission in the speech, i.e. I will not punish the unbeliever, i.e. the like of the unbeliever, i.e. the like of the unbeliever's punishment." The third: that it is the pronoun of the emphatic maṣdar, as in «ظَنَنْتُهُ زيداً قائماً» (I thought it — Zayd standing). When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this aspect he objected to himself, saying: "If you say: «لا أعذِّبه» is a description of «عذاب», and on this assumption nothing returns from the description to what is described —

it is said: since the second occurs in the place of the maṣdar, and the maṣdar is a genus, while «عذاباً» is indefinite, the first is included in the second, and the second includes the first; it is like «زيد نعم الرجل» (Zayd — what an excellent man!)." End of quote. So he made the link generality. What he mentioned, that the link is by generality, the grammarians mention only for the clause occurring as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject); for that reason Abū al-Baqāʾ compared it to «زيد نِعْم الرجل». This should not be taken as a basis for analogy, because in the khabar the link is achieved by things that are not permissible in a clause occurring as a description, and this is one of them. Moreover, this objection he mentioned applies to him in the second aspect, for the clause is a description of «عذاباً» and there is no pronoun in it [referring to it]. If it is said: there it is not a description, it is said: the meaning is corrupted by assuming it to be resumptive; and assuming that is sound, let it be resumptive here too. «أحداً» is accusative as an explicit direct object, and «من العالمين» is a description of «أحداً», so it is attached to an omitted [word].

semin-durr:116-116.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ قَالَ الله}: did this saying take place and finish, or will it take place on the Day of Resurrection? People have two views. Some said: when He raised him to Himself He said that to him; on this, «إذ» and «قال» keep their proper sense of the past, and this is the apparent view. Others said: He will say it to him on the Day of Resurrection; on this, «إذ» means «إذا», and «قال» means «يقول». [Translator's note: the source prints «إذا بمعنى إذا»; the first is evidently «إذ»; translated accordingly.] Its meaning «إذا» is easier than the view of Abū ʿUbayd that it is redundant (zāʾida), because the redundancy of nouns is not an easy matter.

His words: {أَأَنتَ قُلتَ}: the hamza entered upon the mubtadaʾ (subject) for a benefit that the rhetoricians have mentioned, namely: when the existence of an act is known and there is doubt about its attribution to a person, the noun whose attribution to the act is in doubt is placed immediately after the hamza; so one says «أأنت ضرب زيداً» (Is it you who struck Zayd?), for the striking of Zayd has occurred, and the doubt is only about its attribution to the one addressed. If there is doubt about the act's occurring at all, the verb is placed after the hamza, so one says «أضربْتَ زيداً» (Did you strike Zayd?), when you are not certain of the striking's occurrence but doubt it. In sum: the hamza is followed by what is in doubt. Coming to the noble verse: the interrogative in it is meant as reproach and rebuke to others than ʿĪsā, upon him be peace, namely those who took him and his mother as two gods; it entered upon the mubtadaʾ for the meaning I have mentioned, because the taking [as gods] has undoubtedly occurred. The lām in «للناس» is for conveying only. «اتخذوني» may mean «صَيَّر» (to make into), so it takes two objects, the second of which is «إلهين»; or it may be the one taking a single object, so «إلهين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «من دون الله» has two aspects. The more apparent of them: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the taking. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted — and began with it — that it be attached to an omitted [word] as a description of «إلهين».

His words: {سُبْحَانَكَ}, i.e. "a declaring free [of imperfection]"; its discussion has preceded in al-Baqara in full. What it relates to here is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī assumed it as: "Glory be to You, above having a partner." Ibn ʿAṭiyya assumed it as: "above this being said and uttered." The Shaykh preferred the latter because of His saying afterwards: {مَا يَكُونُ لي أَنْ أَقُولَ}. His words: {أَنْ أَقُول} are in the position of nominative, because they are the noun of «يكون», and the khabar (predicate) is in the preposition-phrase before it, i.e. "it is not fitting for me to say such". «ما» may be a relative or an indefinite noun described [by what follows]. The clause after it is either a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position, or a description, in which case its position is accusative. «ما» is accusative by «أقول» as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because it contains a clause, so it is the counterpart of «قلت كلاماً» (I said speech); on this, there is no need to interpret «أقول» as meaning "I claim" or "I mention", as Abū al-Baqāʾ did. In «ليس» there is a pronoun referring to «ما», which is its noun. There are two aspects concerning its khabar. The first: that it is «لي», i.e. "what is not established and fixed for me". On this, «بحق» has three aspects, of which Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned two. The first of them: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لي». He said: "The second: that it is a mafʿūl bihi, its implied form being: what is not established for me by reason of a right; so the bāʾ is attached to the omitted verb, not to the preposition-phrase itself, because abstract governors (al-maʿānī) do not govern the direct object."

I say: this is not good, because he assumed what the khabar is attached to as a restricted [specific] verb of being, then omitted it and kept what it governs. The third aspect: that His words «بحق» are attached to His words «عَلِمْتَه», the pause on this being at His words «لي», and the meaning: "then You knew it truly". This has been rejected on the grounds that the default is the absence of fronting and postponement; but that should not suffice in rejecting it. Rather, what prevents it is that what is governed by the condition or its apodosis does not come before the conditional particle — especially as what is related from the imams of the readers is pausing at «بحق» and beginning with «إنْ كنت قلتُه», and this is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, [so following it is obligatory]. The second aspect regarding the khabar of «ليس»: that it is «بحق». On this there are three aspects concerning «لي». The first: that it is for clarification (tabyīn), as in their saying «سُقْياً له» (may he be watered — [this is said] for him), so it is attached to an omitted [word]. [Translator's note: the source prints «يتبين»; the sense is "for clarification"; translated accordingly.] The second: that it is a ḥāl from «بحق», because if it were placed after it, it would be a description of it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "This is explained according to the view of those who permit fronting the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it." I say: people's disagreement about this and the evidence they brought have been presented to you. There is also in it the fronting of the ḥāl before its abstract governor: for «بحق» is the governor, since «ليس» cannot govern anything, even if we say that its sister «كان» may govern, because «ليس» has no event [meaning] by consensus. The third: that it is attached to «حق» itself, because the bāʾ is redundant and حَقّ means مُسْتحق (deserved), i.e. "what is not deserved by me".

His words: {إِن كُنتُ}: «كنت», though past in wording, is future in meaning; the implied form is: "if my claim to what was mentioned is proven true". Al-Fārisī assumed it with his saying: "If I now be [one who] said it in the past", because the condition and the apodosis occur only in the future. His words: {فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ}, i.e. "then Your knowledge of it has become clear and manifest", as in His words: {فَصَدَقَتْ} [Yūsuf: 26], {فَكَذَبَتْ} [Yūsuf: 27] and {فَكُبَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النار} [al-Naml: 90].

His words: {تَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِي}: this [verb] cannot be one of mere acquaintance (ʿirfān), because acquaintance, as I have stated, requires prior ignorance, or is restricted to knowing the essence without its states, according to what people have said. So the second object is omitted, i.e. "You know what is in my self as existing and brought into being in its reality; nothing of it is hidden from You". As for «ولا أعلم», even though it could be one of acquaintance, since it has become a counterpart to what precedes it, it ought to be like it. What is meant by النفس (self) here, according to what al-Zajjāj said, is that it is used to mean the reality of a thing; and the meaning of His words {تَعْلَمُ مَا فِي نَفْسِي} to the end is clear. He said: "The meaning is: You know what I conceal of my secret and my unseen, i.e. what is hidden and I have not shown; and I do not know what You conceal and do not reveal to us; so النفس is mentioned by way of correspondence and pairing (izdiwāj)." This is drawn from the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Zamakhsharī hovered around it, for he said: "You know what I know, and I do not know what You know." And He brought His words {مَا فِي نَفْسِكَ} by way of correspondence and matching with His words {مَا فِي نَفْسِي}; so it is like His words {وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ الله} [Āl ʿImrān: 54], and His words {إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ الله يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 14-15].

semin-durr:3-3.t:
The i'rab of {حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الميتة} has also preceded, and its origin «[Translator's note: so in the text («وأصلُها»); the sentence appears incomplete.]». Here He fronted the Majestic Name in His saying {وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ الله}, while it was postponed there, because in al-Baqara it is a verse-ending (fāṣila) or resembles a verse-ending, unlike here, for here conjoined items follow it.

«الموقوذة» is the one that was "waqadha-ed", i.e. struck with a stick and the like until it died; from «وَقَذَه», i.e. he struck him until he went limp. From it comes «وقَذَه النعاس», i.e. drowsiness overcame him; «ووقَذْه النعاس», i.e. overcame him «[Translator's note: this phrase is repeated in the text.]»; and «وقَذه الحُلُم», i.e. forbearance calmed him. It is as though the root indicates stillness and limpness.

«المُتَرَدِّيَة»: from «تَرَدَّى», i.e. fell from a height and perished. One says «ما يَدْري أين رَدَى», i.e. [he does not know] where he went; and «رَدَى» and «تَردَّى» mean "perished".

«النَّطيحة» is faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla (passive participle). By rights the tāʾ of the feminine should not enter it, as with «قتيل» and «جريح»; but it has been treated as a noun, or [it has the tāʾ] because what it qualifies is not mentioned — so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. There is a reservation about this, because they only add the tāʾ when what is qualified is not mentioned, to avoid ambiguity, as in «مَرَرْتُ بقتيلة بن فلان» ("I passed by the slain woman of the sons of so-and-so"), lest the masculine be confused with the feminine; here ambiguity is absent; moreover, the ruling for male and female in this is the same.

«وما أكل السَّبُعُ»: «ما» is in the sense of «الذي» and its returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "and what the beast of prey ate". The position of this relative noun is nominative, by conjunction to the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). This does not run according to its apparent sense, because what the beast of prey has eaten and finished cannot be slaughtered; that is why Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī said: "and what the beast of prey ate part of". Al-Ḥasan, al-Fayyāḍ and Abū Ḥaywa read «السَّبْع» with the bāʾ vowelless, which is a vowel-dropping of the ḍamma; fatḥa on both the sīn and the bāʾ is also transmitted. «السَّبُع» is every creature with fang and claw, like the lion and the leopard; it is applied also to birds with talons. The poet said:

169 - 2- وسِباعُ الطيرِ تَغْدُو بِطاناً ... تتخطَّاهُمُ فما تَسْتَقِلُّ
(And the birds of prey go forth in the morning gorged; they step over them and cannot rise [for fullness].)

His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ}: there are two views. The first: that it is a connected exception (muttaṣil). Those who hold it to be a connected exception differed: some of them said it is excepted from His saying {والمنخنقة} up to His saying {وَمَآ أَكَلَ السبع}. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The exception refers back to the one fallen, the one gored and the one eaten by the beast of prey"; his excluding the strangled one from it is not good. Some of them said: it is excepted from «ما أكل السَّبُع» only. The second view: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "but what you have slaughtered of others is lawful", or "eat it". It is as though this proponent held that these [animals] had reached death through these causes, or a state close to it, so their slaughter avails nothing in his view.

«التذكية» is slaughtering. «ذَكَت النارُ»: the fire rose high; «ذَكَى الرجلُ»: the man grew old. The poet said:

169 - 3- على أعراقهِ تَجْري المَذاكي ... وليس على تقلُّبِه وجُهْدِهْ
(The mature steeds run according to their lineage, not according to their bustle and effort.)

His saying: {وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النصب}: it too is nominative by conjunction to «الميتة». They differed regarding «النصب»: it is said they are stones on which they used to slaughter, so «على» here is clear; and it is said they are for the idols, because they are set up (tunṣab) to be worshipped. On this, «على» has two analyses. The first: that it is in the sense of the lām, i.e. "and what was slaughtered for the sake of the idols". The second: that it has its proper sense, but is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and what was slaughtered while being named over the idols"; so Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned. In it «[Translator's note: the text has «فهي», a misprint for «وفيه».]» is the well-known reservation, namely that he construed what it is attached to as something specific.

The majority read «النُّصُب» with two ḍammas. It is said: it is the plural of «نِصاب»; and it is said: it is a singular, as indicated by the saying of al-Aʿshā:

169 - 4- وذا النُّصُبَ المنصوبَ لا تَقْرَبَنَّه ... ولا تَعْبُدِ الشيطانَ واللَّهَ فاعبُدا
(And this erected stone — do not approach it; and do not worship Satan, but Allah worship.)

though there is another possibility in it. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read it with ḍamma on the nūn and the ṣād vowelless, which is a lightening of the first reading. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «النَصَب» with two fatḥas; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a noun in the sense of what is set up, like «القبَض» and «النقَص» in the sense of «المقبوض» and «المنقوص»." Al-Ḥasan [read] «النَّصْب» with fatḥa on the nūn and the ṣād vowelless; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the object. It may not be a lightening of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar's reading, because a fatḥa is not lightened [by dropping].

His saying: {وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بالأزلام}: «أن» and what is in its domain are in the position of the nominative by conjunction to «الميتة» «[Translator's note: the text has «المتية», a misprint.]». «الأزلام» are the divining arrows; their singular is «زَلْم» and «زُلْم», with fatḥa and ḍamma on the zāy. The divining arrows were shafts by which the Arabs sought to know what good and evil was allotted to them: on one was written "My Lord commanded me", on another "My Lord forbade me", and the other was blank. And it is said: they are the arrows of maysir, i.e. gambling; the reason for mentioning them along with these foods is that they used to be raised at the House together with them.

His saying: {ذلكم فِسْقٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The demonstrative refers to seeking divisions by the divining arrows specifically; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbās. And it is said: to all that preceded, because its meaning is "He has forbidden you consuming carrion, and so on", so the demonstrative refers to this implied [notion].

His saying: {اليوم يَئِسَ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: «اليوم» is an adverb in the accusative by «يئس», and the alif-lām in it is for a known reference (ʿahd). It is said: He meant by it the day of ʿArafa, which was a Friday in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage; this verse was revealed on it after the afternoon prayer. And it is said: it is the day of his entry, upon him be peace, into Mecca in the year nine; and it is said: eight. Al-Zajjāj said — and al-Zamakhsharī followed him — that it is not for a known reference, and no specific day is meant by "the day"; rather, He meant by it the present time and what is near it of past and coming times, as in your saying "Yesterday you were young, and today you are grey": you do not mean by "yesterday" the day before your day, nor by "today" the present time only. Similar is «الآن» in the poet's saying:

169 - 5- الآن لَمَّا ابيضَّ مَسْربتي ... وعَضَضْتُ مِنْ نابي على جِذْمِ
(Now, when the hair of my chest has turned white and I bite with my canine on a stump …)

and likewise the saying of Zuhayr:

169 - 6- وأَعلم ما في اليومِ والأمسِ قبلَه ... ولكنني عن علمِ ما في غَدٍ عَمِ
(I know what is in today and in yesterday before it, but I am blind to knowledge of what is in tomorrow.)

He did not mean by these their literal senses.

The majority read «يَئِس» with hamza; Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «يَيِس» with two yāʾs, without hamza, and it is also related from Abū ʿAmr. One says «يَئِس يَيْئَس» and «يَيْئِسُ», with fatḥa and kasra on the middle radical of the imperfect, the latter being anomalous. One also says «أَيِس», metathesized from «يئس», so its pattern is ʿafila; what indicates the metathesis is that it is not subjected to weak-letter change (iʿlāl), since if that were not assumed, the requirement for it — the weak letter being voweled and preceded by fatḥa — would have to be disregarded; but since it has the meaning of a word that is not subjected to iʿlāl, it remained sound.

«اليأس» is the cutting off of hope; it is the opposite of craving. «من دينكم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يئس», and [«من»] means the beginning of the extent; it is by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "of nullifying the matter of your religion". The discussion of His saying {اليوم أَكْمَلْتُ} is like that of «اليوم» before it. «عليكم» is attached to «أَتْممت»; it may not be attached to «نعمتي», even though its verb takes «على», as in {أَنعَمَ الله عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ} [al-Aḥzāb: 37], because a maṣdar's governed word does not precede it, unless it stands in its stead. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If you make it explicative, i.e. 'I have completed — I mean upon you —', it is permissible"; but there is no need for what he claimed.

His saying: {وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الأسلام دِيناً}: «رَضي» has two analyses. The first: that it takes one object, namely «الإسلام», and «ديناً» on this is a ḥāl. And it is said: it is made to contain the meaning of «صَيَّر» and «جَعَل» (to make), so it takes two objects, the first «الإسلام» and the second «ديناً». «لكم» admits two analyses: the first, that it is attached to «رضي»; the second, that it is attached to an omitted word, because it is a ḥāl from «الإسلام», but fronted before it.

His saying: «فمن اضطر»: discussion of this verse and what was read in it has preceded in al-Baqara, which makes repetition unnecessary. «في مَخْمَصَةٍ» is attached to «اضْطُرَّ». «المَخْمَصَة» is famine, because bellies become lean (takhmuṣ) from it, i.e. shrink; and it is a praiseworthy attribute in women: one says «رجلٌ خُمْصان» and «امرأةٌ خُمْصانة» (slender-waisted). From it comes «أَخْمَصُ القدمِ» (the hollow of the sole), for its thinness. It is used for hunger and «الغَرْث» (hunger); the poet said:

169 - 7- تَبيتون في المَشْتى مِلاءً بطونُكم ... وجارتُكم غَرْثَى يَبِتْنَ خمائصا
(You spend the winter nights with full bellies, while your neighbour-women spend the night hungry and lean.)

And another said:

169 - 8- كُلوا في بعضِ بطنِكُمُ تَعِفُّوا ... فإنَّ زمانَكم زمنٌ خَميصُ
(Eat to part of your belly and be abstinent, for your time is a lean time.)

The time was described thus by way of intensification, as in their saying "his day is fasting and his night is standing [in prayer]".

«غيرَ» is accusative as a ḥāl. The majority read «متجانِفٍ» with alif and undoubled nūn, from «تَجانَفَ»; Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Nakhaʿī read «مُتَجَنِّف» with doubled nūn and no alif. Abū Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is more intensive than «متجانف» in meaning, because the doubling of the middle radical indicates intensification and penetration into the meaning." «لإثم» is attached to «متجانف», the lām having its proper sense; and it is said: it is in the sense of «إلى», i.e. "not inclining to sin"; there is no need for that. The meaning and derivation of this word have preceded at His saying {فَمَنْ خَافَ مِن مُّوصٍ جَنَفاً} [al-Baqara: 182].

His saying {فَإِنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ} is a clause either in the position of the jussive or of the nominative, according to what is said about «من»; likewise the view on the fāʾ: it is either obligatory or permissible. On both construals the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "Allah is forgiving to him".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ}: discussion of «ماذا» and what has been said about it has preceded, so let it be consulted. His saying «لهم» is in the third person because the third-person pronoun preceded in His saying {يَسْأَلُونَكَ} [al-Baqara: 215]. Had it been said in the speech «ماذا أُحِلَّ لنا» ("What has been made lawful for us?"), it would have been permissible, by way of reporting the clause [verbatim], as in your saying «أقسم زيدٌ ليضربن» and «لأضربن» ("Zayd swore he would strike" / "I will strike"), in the third person and the first person; except that the first-person pronoun requires reporting what they said, just as «لأضربنَّ» requires reporting the clause sworn upon.

«ماذا أحِلَّ»: this interrogative suspends (ʿallaqa) the verb of asking, even though asking is not one of the verbs of the heart, because it is a cause of knowledge, and knowledge is suspended, so likewise its cause. The verification of the view on this has preceded in al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "In asking there is the meaning of saying; that is why «ماذا أُحِلَّ لهم» came after it, as though it were said: 'they say: what has been made lawful for them?'" There is no need to make asking contain the meaning of saying, given what preceded, that asking is suspended by an interrogative, as its effect [knowledge] is. Ibn al-Khaṭīb said: "Had it been a report of their speech, they would have said: 'What has been made lawful for them?', and it is known that this is false — they would not say it; they would only say: 'What has been made lawful for us?' Rather, the correct view is that it is not a report of their speech in their own wording, but an explanation of how the event was."

His saying: {وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ}: there are three analyses of this «ما». The first: that it is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», its returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "what you have taught"; its position is nominative, by conjunction to the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. "and the game of — or the catch of — what you have taught has been made lawful to you"; so this muḍāf must be omitted. The second: that it is conditional, so its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is His saying «فكُلوا». Al-Shaykh said: "This is more apparent, because it involves no implied word." The third: that it is also a relative noun, its position nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar (predicate) is His saying «فكُلوا»; the fāʾ entered only by likening the relative noun to the conditional noun.

His saying: {مِّنَ الجوارح} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Regarding the one it describes there are two analyses: the first, that it is the relative noun «ما»; the second, that it is the hāʾ referring back to the relative noun; and this is in meaning like the first. «الجوارح» is the plural of «جارحة», the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] being for intensification. They were so named because they mostly wound (tajraḥ) the game, or because they earn — «الجَرْح» is earning; from it comes {وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُم بالنهار} [al-Anʿām: 60]. «الجارحة» is an adjective treated as a noun, because what it qualifies is mostly not mentioned. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya read «عُلِّمتم» in the passive; its explanation is that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "and what Allah has taught you of the matter of the hunting animals".

«مكلِّبين» is a ḥāl from the agent of «عَلَّمتم». The meaning of «مكلِّبين» is training, habituating to the hunt, and accustoming. Al-Shaykh said: "The benefit of this ḥāl — even though it is emphatic of His saying «عَلَّمتم», so that it could be dispensed with — is that the teacher be skilled in teaching, adept at it, characterized by it." End of quotation. There is a reservation about his making this ḥāl emphatic; rather, it is foundational (muʾassisa).

This ḥāl was derived from the word «الكَلْب», this well-known animal, even though the hunting animals include others, even birds of prey, by giving it predominance (taghlīb), because hunting among the Arabs was mostly done with it. Or it was derived from «الكَلَب», which is avidity: one says «هو كَلِبٌ بكذا», i.e. avid for it, and «به كَلَبٌ», i.e. avidity; and this too seems to be derived from «الكَلْب», the animal, because of its avidity. Or it was derived [from] «الكَلْب» «[Translator's note: the preposition «من» is missing in the text.]» [in a wider sense], for «الكَلْب» is applied to the beast of prey too; from it is the ḥadīth: "O Allah, set upon him a dog of Your dogs", and the lion ate him. Al-Shaykh said: "This derivation is not sound, because the lion's being a dog is a description inherent in it, whereas «التكليب» is an attribute of the trainer; and the hunting animals are beasts of prey in themselves and dogs in themselves, not by the trainer's making." There is no substance under this rejoinder.

It was also read «مُكْلِبين» with the lām undoubled; faʿʿala and afʿala sometimes share one meaning, except that «كَلَّب» with doubling means "he trained them and habituated them to the hunt", while «أَكْلب» means "he became possessed of dogs". Al-Zajjāj, however, said: "One says «رجلُ مُكَلِّب»" — i.e. with doubling — "and «مُكْلِب»" — i.e. from «أكلب» — "and «كَلاَّب»" — i.e. with the lām doubled — "meaning one who owns dogs".

The answer clause here came as a verbal clause, while the question clause is nominal, namely «ماذا أُحِل؟». It is an answer to it in meaning, not in wording, since they do not «[Translator's note: the text has «مل», a misprint for «لم».]» correspond in kind.

His saying: {تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ}: there are four analyses. The first: that it is a resumptive clause. The second: that it is a clause in the position of the accusative as a second ḥāl from the agent of «عَلَّمتم»; Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade that, because he does not permit a governing word to govern two ḥāls; discussion of that has preceded. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «مُكَلِّبين», making it a ḥāl from a ḥāl, which is called "overlapping" (mutadākhila). On both preceding construals it is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because its meaning is understood from «عَلَّمْتُمْ» and from «مُكَلِّبين». The fourth: that it is a parenthetical clause; this is on making «ما» conditional, or a relative noun whose khabar is «فكلوا»; so it has been interposed between the condition and its apodosis, or between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar. If it is asked: is a fifth analysis permissible, namely that this clause be a ḥāl from «الجوارح», i.e. "of the hunting animals, while you teach them", since the clause contains a pronoun of the one described by the ḥāl? — the answer is that this is not permissible, because it would lead to separating this ḥāl from the one it describes by a foreign element, namely «مكلِّبين», which is a ḥāl from the agent of «عَلَّمتم».

His saying: {مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ}: «مِنْ» has two analyses. The more apparent: that it is partitive «[Translator's note: the text has «تبغيضية», a misprint for «تبعيضية».]», and it is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, which is the object of eating, i.e. "eat something of what they have held for you". The second: that it is redundant (zāʾida), which is analogous to the view of al-Akhfash. On the first, «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word; on the second, it has no attachment. «ما» is a relative noun or an indefinite qualified noun, and the returning pronoun is omitted on both construals, i.e. "[what] they held", as has preceded.

The nūn in «أمسكن» refers to the hunting animals. «عليكم» is attached to «أمسكن», and the sense of "upon" here is figurative.

His saying: «عليه»: regarding this hāʾ there are three analyses. The first: that it refers to the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from the verb, namely eating, as though it were said: "and mention the name of Allah over the eating"; supporting this is what is in the ḥadīth: "Mention the name of Allah, and eat from what is next to you." The second: that it refers to «ما عَلَّمْتم», i.e. mention the name of Allah over the hunting animals when sending them after the game; and in the ḥadīth: "When you send your dog and mention the name of Allah …". The third: that it refers to «ما أَمْسَكْن», i.e. mention the name of Allah [over] «[Translator's note: «على» appears to be missing in the text.]» whatever you reach in time to slaughter of what the hunting animals have held for you.

semin-durr:117-117.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مَآ أَمَرْتَنِي}: this is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), for «ما» is accusative by «قلت» (saying), because it and what is in its scope are in the interpretation of something said. Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed the saying as meaning mentioning and conveying. «ما» may be a relative or an indefinite noun described [by what follows].

His words: {أَنِ اعبدوا}: there are seven aspects concerning «أَنْ». The first: that it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in «به», the implied form being: "I said nothing except what You commanded me, namely that [they] worship"; an objection to this aspect will come. The second: that it is in the position of accusative by an implied «أعني» (I mean), i.e. he explained that which was commanded. The third: that it is in the position of accusative as a badal from the position of «به» in «ما أمرتني به», because the position of the genitive noun is accusative. The fourth: that its position is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), which is close in meaning to the accusative as a badal. The fifth: that it is in the position of genitive, because it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to the hāʾ in «به». The sixth: that it is a badal from «ما» itself, i.e. "I said nothing to them except: worship". The seventh: that «أَنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya); Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥawfī and Makkī permitted it. Among those who held it permissible that «أَنْ» be a badal from «ما», so that its position is accusative, or from the hāʾ, so that its position is genitive, is Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj; and he also permitted it to be explicative with no grammatical position. Some of these aspects al-Zamakhsharī rejected; Abū al-Baqāʾ rejected one aspect of them, namely its being explicative. As for al-Zamakhsharī, he rejected its being explicative except by an interpretation he mentioned, which will come, and [rejected] its being a badal from «ما» or from the hāʾ in «به». He said — may Allah have mercy on him: "«أنْ» in His words {أَنِ اعبدوا الله}: if you make it explicative, it must have something it explains, and that is either the verb of saying or the verb of commanding, and neither is right. As for the verb of saying, it is because clauses are quoted after it, and no explicative particle comes between it and what it quotes. As for the verb of commanding, it is predicated of the pronoun of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; were you to explain it with «اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم» it would not be right, because Allah does not say: worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. If you make it a badal, you must make it a badal either from «ما» in «ما أمرتني به» or from the hāʾ in «به», and neither is right; because the badal is what stands in place of what it replaces, and one does not say: 'I said nothing to them except that they worship Allah', i.e. I said nothing to them except His worship, because worship is not said. Likewise if you make it a badal from the hāʾ: for if you put «أن اعبدوا» in place of the hāʾ and said «إلا ما أمرتني بأن اعبدوا الله», the relative would remain without anything in its ṣila (relative clause) returning to it. If you say: what will you do? I say: the verb of saying is taken according to its meaning, because the meaning of «ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به» is: I commanded them only with what You commanded me; so its explanation by «أن اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم» becomes right. It is also permissible that «أَنْ» be maṣdariyya [lit. 'a relative'], conjoined as an explication of the hāʾ, not as a badal."

The Shaykh followed up his statement, saying: "As for his saying 'as for the verb of commanding…' to the end of the rejection, and his saying 'because Allah does not say: worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord': it was only not right because he made the clause and what follows it joined to the verb of commanding. It is right that the verb of commanding be explained by His words «اعبدوا الله», and that «ربي وربكم» be from the speech of ʿĪsā, by an implied «أعني», i.e. 'I mean my Lord and your Lord' — not as a description, which is how al-Zamakhsharī understood it, so that it was not right in his view. As for his saying 'because worship is not said', it is correct; but it is valid by the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. I said nothing to them except the saying You commanded me, the saying of worship of Allah, i.e. the saying that contains worship of Allah. As for his saying 'the relative would remain without anything in its ṣila returning to it', it is not necessary for every badal to take the place of what it replaces; do you not see that the grammarians permit «زيد مررت به أبي عبدِ الله», while if you said «زيدٌ مررت بأبي عبد الله» it would not be permitted except according to the view of al-Akhfash? As for his saying 'conjoined as an explication of the hāʾ', it is far-fetched, because ʿaṭf bayān is mostly with non-derived words, proper names. And what al-Zamakhsharī chose and others permitted is not valid, because it came after «إلا», and everything after the exceptive «إلا» must have a grammatical position, while the explicative «أن» has no grammatical position." End of quote.

I say: as for his saying that «ربي وربكم» is from the speech of ʿĪsā, it is as remote from understanding as anything can be. How would al-Zamakhsharī understand that, when the context and the meaning lead to «ربي» being a follower of the Name of Majesty? Nothing else springs to mind — rather, nothing else is acceptable. This is worse than what they say [in faulting a construction]: "it leads to preparing a governor to govern and then cutting it off". So the Shaykh's view comes down to «اعبدوا الله» being from the speech of Allah the Exalted and «ربي وربكم» from the speech of ʿĪsā, both of them explaining «أمرتَ», which is predicated of the Creator, the Exalted. As for his saying "it is valid by the omission of a muḍāf", there is some merit in it. As for his saying "the badal's taking the place of what it replaces is not necessary" and his citing what he mentioned, it is not conceded, because this is contradicted by their explicit statement that «جاء الذي مررت به أبي عبد الله», with «عبد الله» genitive as a badal from the hāʾ, is not permitted; they gave as the reason that it entails the relative remaining without a returning pronoun — besides the fact that we also have a disagreement about linking with an overt noun in the ṣila, which I have drawn attention to before. It suffices us that they frequently say in questions: "This is not permitted, because the badal takes the place of what it replaces", making that a preventive reason; anyone who has toiled with their discourse knows that, and were it not for fear of lengthiness I would have cited various questions of it.

As for his saying "everything after the exceptive «إلا»…" to the end, it is a correct statement, because it is an affirmation after a negation, so it requires that what precedes it govern what follows it.

In [the nūn of] «أَنْ» kasra is permissible, according to the rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and ḍamma by assimilation; its verification and attribution to those who read it have preceded at His words {فَمَنِ اضطر} [verse: 173] in al-Baqara. «ربي» is a naʿt (adjective), or a badal, or a ʿaṭf bayān, or cut off from following, in the nominative or the accusative; these are five aspects whose explanation has preceded.

His words: {شَهِيداً}: the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. «ما» is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-maṣdar), i.e. it is assumed as a maṣdar to which a time is annexed, and «دام» is its ṣila. It may be complete or incomplete. If it is complete, its meaning is residing, and «فيهم» is attached to it; it may also be attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "I was a witness over them for the duration of my residing among them"; so no accusative is needed here, and it is then fully inflected. If it is the incomplete one, it keeps the past form and is not content with a nominative, so «فيهم» is in the position of accusative as its khabar; the implied form being: "for the duration of my remaining settled among them". It has preceded that one says «دِمْتَ تَدام», like خِفْتَ تَخاف. His words: {كُنتَ أَنتَ الرَّقِيبَ}: «أنت» may be a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a tawkīd (emphasis). «الرقيب» was read in the nominative, as the khabar of «أنت», and the clause is the khabar of «كان», as in his saying:

185 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وكنتَ عليها بالمَلا أنْتَ أَقْدَرُ
(…and you were, in the open desert, the one most able over her.)

The derivation of {الرقيب} has preceded, and «عليهم» is attached to it. «على كلِّ شيء» is attached to «شهيد», fronted for the verse-ending.

semin-durr:118-118.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ العزيز الحكيم}: its counterpart has preceded. In the reading of the people and in their muṣḥafs it is «العزيزُ الحكيم», while in the muṣḥaf of Ibn Masʿūd — and a group read thus — it is «الغفورُ الرحيم». Someone who does not understand the speech of the Arabs has toyed with this verse and said: "What would have been fitting is only what is in the muṣḥaf of Ibn Masʿūd." It escaped him that the meaning is connected with both conditions together. What Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī said clarifies this; he transmitted this reading from one of the critics and then said: "When what this critic said is transmitted, its meaning becomes weak, for «الغفور الرحيم» would be exclusive to the second condition and have no connection with the first condition; whereas, as Allah sent it down and as the Muslims agreed upon reading it, it is known to relate to both conditions, the first and the last of them. For its summary is: if You punish them, You are the Mighty, the Wise; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise — in both matters, punishing and forgiving. So «العزيز الحكيم» is more fitting for this place because of its generality and because it combines the two conditions; and «الغفور الرحيم» would not be suited to bear the generality that «العزيز الحكيم» bears." I say: his statement has subtlety in it; for by his saying "it is known to relate to both conditions…" to the end, he does not mean that it is the response to both in grammatical terms, since that would be invalid in terms of Arabic grammar: the first [condition] has taken its response, namely «فإنهم عبادُك», which is a fitting response, for the servant is subject to his master's disposing of him as he wills. He only means by that that it relates to both in terms of meaning. People have discussed this verse at length beyond what this place can bear; I have only dealt with some of it because of its connection with the irregular (shādhdh) reading and irregular written form.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَيَقُولُ}: Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans read it with the wāw before «يقول», and the rest without it. However, Abū ʿAmr put the verb after the wāw in the accusative, while ʿAlī ibn Naṣr related from him the nominative, like the Kufans. So there are three readings: «يقول» without the wāw; «ويقولَ» with the wāw and the accusative; and «ويقولُ» with the wāw and the nominative.

As for the reading of whoever read «يقول» without the wāw, it is a resumptive sentence brought as the answer to an implied question: as though, after His saying, Exalted is He, {فَعَسَى الله أَن يَأْتِيَ بالفتح} up to His saying {نَادِمِينَ}, someone asked: "What did the believers say then?" and was answered by His saying, Exalted is He, {وَيَقُولُ الذين آمَنُواْ} to the end. This is clear. The wāw is absent in the codices of Mecca, Medina and Syria, and those who read so are the people of these codices, for those who read so are Ibn Kathīr the Meccan, Ibn ʿĀmir the Syrian and Nāfiʿ the Medinan; their reading agrees with their codices. This does not mean that they read so only because of the codex; rather, their transmission agreed with their codices, as I have explained more than once.

As for the reading with the wāw and the nominative, it is also clear, because it is a sentence with which a statement is begun; the wāw is resumptive, merely conjoining one sentence to another. The wāw is present in the codices of Kufa and the East, and those who read so are the people of this codex; the discussion is as above.

As for the reading of Abū ʿAmr, it is the one that requires extra consideration, and people disagreed about it in three ways. First: it is accusative, conjoined to «فيصبحوا» according to one of the two views mentioned on the accusative of «فيُصْبحوا», namely the second view, I mean its being accusative by a concealed «أَنْ» in reply to hope after the fāʾ, treating hope like wishing. On this there is a well-known disagreement between the Basrans and the Kufans: the Basrans disallow it and the Kufans allow it, citing as evidence the reading of Nāfiʿ: {لعله يزَّكى أو يَذَّكَّرُ فتنفعَه}, with «تنفعه» in the accusative, and the reading of ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ: «لعلي أبلغُ الأسبابَ أسبابَ السماواتِ فأطَّلِعَ», with «فأطَّلِعَ» in the accusative. The answer concerning the two noble verses will come in its place. This view — I mean conjoining «ويقول» to «فيصبحوا» — al-Fārisī stated, and a group followed him; Abū Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted it from him, and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥājib also mentioned it. Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma said after mentioning the above view: "This is a good view, which Shaykh Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥājib taught me, and I have not seen it from anyone else. They mentioned [other] views, all of them far-fetched and forced." End of quote. I say: this — as you have seen — is well known and transmitted from Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. As for his approving this view, it works only on the view of the Kufans, which is outweighed, as is established in the science of grammar.

Second: it is accusative, conjoined to the maṣdar (verbal noun) before it, namely «الفتح», as though it were said: "Perhaps Allah will bring the victory and [bring about] that they say," i.e. and the saying of those who believe. Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās mentioned this view, and compared it to the poet's saying:

1743 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتَقَرَّ عيني ... أحبُّ إليَّ مِنْ لُبْسِ الشُّفوفِ
(Wearing a woollen cloak with my eye content is dearer to me than wearing fine sheer garments.)

and the other's saying:

1744 - لقد كانَ في حَوْلٍ ثَواءٍ ثويتُه ... تَقَضِّي لُباناتٍ ويَسْأَمَ سائِمُ
(In a year of sojourn that I sojourned there was the fulfilment of needs, and [enough] for the weary to grow weary.)

This is rejected for three reasons. First: it leads to separating parts of the ṣila (relative clause) by something extraneous, because on his view «الفتح» is interpreted as «أَنْ» and the verb, the implied form being "that He bring that He give victory and that they say"; so the separation occurs by His saying {فيُصبحوا}, which is extraneous, since it is conjoined to «يأتي». Second: this maṣdar — namely «الفتح» — is not meant to be resolved into a maṣdar particle and a verb; rather, it is a maṣdar not meant thus, as in «يعجبني ذكاؤك وعلمك» (your intelligence and your knowledge please me). Third: even if its resolution into a maṣdar particle and a verb is granted, the meaning is not "Perhaps Allah will bring that those who believe say," for [the meaning] is plainly incompatible with that.

The third of the views on the accusative of «ويقول»: it is accusative, conjoined to His saying «يأتي», i.e. "Perhaps Allah will bring and [that] they say." al-Zamakhsharī held this and raised no objection to it. It has been rejected on the ground that it entails conjoining what cannot be a khabar (predicate) to what is a khabar. That is, His saying {أن يأتيَ} is the khabar of «عسى», and it is valid, because it contains a link referring to the noun of «عسى», namely the pronoun of the Creator, Exalted is He; but His saying «ويقول» contains no pronoun referring to the noun of «عسى», so how can it be validly made a khabar? Those who allowed it excused it in three ways. First: it is of the type of conjunction according to the meaning, the meaning being: "Perhaps [it will be] that Allah brings the victory and the saying of those who believe"; «عسى» is then complete (tāmma) because it is predicated of «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope, so it needs no link in that case. This is close to what they call "conjunction by supposition" (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum), as in {فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ الصالحين} [al-Munāfiqūn: 10]. Second: {أَنْ يأتي} is a badal (substitute) of the Name of Allah, not a khabar, and «عسى» is then complete, as though it were said: "Perhaps [it will be] that those who believe say." These two views are transmitted from Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. However, the second is not valid, because they have stated explicitly that «عسى», «اخلولق» and «أوشك», alone among their sisters, may be complete on condition that their nominative is «أن يفعل»; they said: so that there exist in form a predicate and a subject of predication, just as they said regarding «ظن» and its sisters that «أَنْ» and «أَنَّ» take the place of their two objects. Third: there is an omitted pronoun that makes valid the occurrence of «ويقول» as a khabar of «عسى», the implied form being "and those who believe say by Him," i.e. by Allah; then it was omitted because it is known. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, after relating the accusative of «ويقولَ» as conjoined to «يأتي»: "In my view, disallowing «عسى الله أن يقول المؤمنون» (perhaps Allah [will bring it about] that the believers say) is questionable, since Allah the Exalted makes them say that through His help and His making His religion prevail." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's statement on this resembles Abū al-Baqāʾ's statement, in that he assumed a pronoun referring to the noun of «عسى» by which the link becomes valid.

Some people multiply these views, bringing them to seven or more, by taking into account the [different] justifications of each of the three views I have mentioned to you; but their upshot does not go beyond three, namely the accusative by conjunction either to «أن يأتي», or to «فيصبحوا», or to «بالفتح». Their full treatment has been given to you.

His saying: {جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ}: there are two views on its accusative. The more evident: it is a corroborative maṣdar governed by «أَقْسموا», being of its meaning; the meaning is: they swore an oath of exertion in the swearing. Second — allowed by Abū al-Baqāʾ and others —: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as in their saying «افعَلْ ذلك جَهْدَك» (do that with all your effort), i.e. exerting yourself; its being definite in wording does not matter, for it is interpreted as indefinite, as I have mentioned to you. The grammarians have discussions on this question. The meaning here is: they swore by Allah exerting themselves in their oaths.

His saying: {إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ}: this clause has no grammatical position, for it is an explanation and report of the meaning of the oath, not of their words; for if it were a report of their words, it would have been said «إنَّا معكم» (we are with you). This is open to question, since you may say «حَلَفَ زيدٌ لأفعَلَنَّ» (Zayd swore: I will surely do) or «ليفعلنَّ» (he will surely do); just as you may say «لَيَفْعَلنَّ», one may say «إنهم لمعكم» as a report.

His saying: {حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ}: there are several views on it. First: it is a resumptive clause, the purpose of which is the Creator's, Exalted is He, informing of that. Second: it is an imprecation against them to that effect, and it is the saying of Allah the Exalted, as in {قُتِلَ الإنسان مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ} [ʿAbasa: 17]. Third: it is in the position of the accusative because it is part of the saying of the believers, and it admits two meanings like the two meanings in the resumptive [view], I mean its being a statement or an imprecation. Fourth: it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject), namely «هؤلاء». On this view His saying {الذين أَقْسَمُواْ} admits two views: one, that it is an adjective of the demonstrative, the khabar being «حَبِطَتْ أعمالُهم»; the other, that «الذين» is a first khabar and «حَبِطت» a second khabar, according to those who allow that. al-Zamakhsharī made «حَبِطَتْ أعمالُهم» convey wonderment. He said: "It contains the meaning of wonderment, as though it were said: How their deeds have come to nothing! How great their loss!" And while it is wonderment, he allowed it to be part of the saying of the believers, so that it is in the position of the accusative, or part of the saying of the Creator, Exalted is He; but he interpreted wonderment with respect to Allah the Exalted as [meaning] that it is something wondrous. He said: "Or [it is] from the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, as testimony against them that their deeds have come to nothing, and as wonderment at the evil of their state." Abū Wāqid and al-Jarrāḥ read «حَبَطت» with a fatḥa on the bāʾ; the two are dialectal variants, and this was mentioned earlier. In His saying, Exalted is He, {فأصبحوا}, the causal sense of this fāʾ is evident.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَن يَرْتَدَّ}: «مَنْ» is conditional only, since its effect is manifest, and His saying, Exalted is He, {فسوف} is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). It is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and regarding its khabar (predicate) there is the well-known disagreement. Those who do not require the return of a pronoun from the apodosis clause to the conditional noun hold to its apparent form; those who require it assume an omitted pronoun, the implied form being "Allah will bring a people other than them," with «هم» in «غيرهم» referring to «مَنْ» according to its meaning.

Ibn ʿĀmir and Nāfiʿ read «يَرْتَدِدْ» with two dāls. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is so in the Imām," meaning the script of the codex, without making that clear [i.e. which codex]. Others transmitted that each reader agreed with his codex, for in the codices of Syria and Medina it is «يرتدد» with two dāls, and in the rest «يرتدَّ». It was stated earlier that assimilation (idghām) is the dialect of Tamīm and keeping [the letters] distinct (iẓhār) is the dialect of the Ḥijāz; that the reason for keeping them distinct is the quiescence of the second [letter], whether due to the jussive or to the pause, and assimilation occurs only into a vowelled letter; and that the reason for assimilation is that this quiescent letter takes a vowel in some states, as in «رُدَّا», «رُدُّوا», «رُدِّي», «لم يَرُدَّا», «لم يَرُدُّوا» and «اردُدِ القومَ»; then «لم يردَّ» and «رُدَّ» were treated on that basis. So it is as though the Tamīmīs took account of this accidental vowel and the Ḥijāzīs did not. «منكم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يرتد», and «عن دينه» is attached to «يرتدَّ».

His saying, Exalted is He: {يُحِبُّهُمْ}: in the position of the genitive because it is an adjective of «قوم». On «يُحِبُّونه» there are two views. The more evident: it is conjoined to what precedes, and so is also in the position of the genitive; He thus described them with two attributes: that He, Exalted is He, loves them, and that they love Him. Second, allowed by Abū al-Baqāʾ: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in «يحبهم». He said: "Its implied form is: while they love Him." I say: Abū al-Baqāʾ assumed the word «هم» only to escape a difficulty, namely that whenever an affirmative imperfect occurs as a ḥāl, it must be free of the wāw, as in «قمت أضحك» (I stood up, laughing); «وأضحك» is not permissible. If anything [of this kind] occurs, it is interpreted as Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned, as in their saying «قمت وأصكُّ عينَه» (I stood up and I strike his eye) and his saying:

1745 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهنُهُمْ مالِكا
(… I escaped, and I leave Mālik to them as a pledge.)

i.e. "and I strike" and "and I leave them as a pledge," so the clause is interpreted as a nominal clause, and its being joined with the wāw becomes valid. But there is no necessity in the noble verse that calls for this, such that it should be resorted to; so it is an outweighed view. Allah the Exalted's love was put before their love because of its nobility and its precedence, since His love, Exalted is He, for them signifies His inspiring them to perform obedience and His rewarding them for it.

His saying: {أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى المؤمنين أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الكافرين}: these two are also adjectives of «قوم». Some adduced this verse as evidence for the permissibility of putting a non-explicit adjective before an explicit adjective, for His saying {يُحِبُّهم} is an adjective and it is non-explicit, because it is a clause interpreted as a single word, while His saying «أذلة» and «أعزة» are two explicit adjectives, because they are single words. As for other grammarians, they say: whenever an explicit adjective and an interpreted one come together, the explicit must be put first, except out of poetic necessity, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

1746 - وفَرْعٍ يُغَشِّي المَتْنَ أسودَ فاحِمٍ ... أثيثٍ كقِنْوِ النَّخْلة المُتَعَثْكِلِ
(And a mass of hair covering the back, black, coal-dark, thick, like the cluster of a date palm hanging in bunches.)

for he put his saying «يُغَشِّي», which is a clause, before «أسود» and what follows it, which are single words. According to the one who says this, one begins with the single word, then the adverbial phrase or its equivalent, then the clause; and on this pattern came His saying, Exalted is He, {وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَانَهُ} [Ghāfir: 28]. This verse is evidence against him, as is His saying, Exalted is He, {وهذا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ} [al-Anʿām: 92]. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "In it is evidence of the falsity [of the view] of whoever believes that qualifying by a noun must be put before qualifying by a verb except out of necessity," and then he mentioned the other verse. I say: there is nothing in these two noble verses that refutes the view of this speaker. As for this verse, His saying, Exalted is He, {يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ} may be a parenthetical clause, because it contains emphasis and reinforcement of the speech, and a parenthetical clause occurs between the adjective and what it qualifies, as in His saying, Exalted is He, {وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 76], where «عظيم» is an adjective of «قَسَم», and He separated them by His saying {لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ}. So likewise here He separated between His saying «بقوم» and their adjective, namely «أذلة» and «أعزة», by His saying {يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ}; on this view it has no grammatical position. As for {وهذا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ}, we do not grant that «مبارك» is an adjective; rather, it may be a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is blessed." Had he adduced as evidence for that two verses other than these two, it would have been stronger, namely His saying, Exalted is He, {مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ مُّحْدَثٍ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 2] and {وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ الرحمن مُحْدَثٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 5], where He put the qualification by the prepositional phrase before the qualification by the explicit [adjective]. It may [still] be said: we do not grant that «مِنْ ربهم» and «مِنَ الرحمن» are adjectives, since they may be two fronted circumstantials from the latent pronoun in «مُحْدَثٍ», i.e. "whose sending down is new, being from their Lord."

«أَذِلَّة» is the plural of «ذليل» in the sense of one who is gently inclined; what is not meant by it is the lowly one who is weak, submissive and abased. It may not be the plural of «ذَلُول», because «ذلول» is pluralised as «ذُلُل», not as «أَذِلّة», even though the words of some give that impression. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever claimed that it is from «الذُّل», the opposite of difficulty, has failed to notice that «ذَلُول» is not pluralised as «أَذِلّة»." «أَذِلّة» and «أَعِزّة» are plurals of «ذليل» and «عزيز», which are intensive forms. «أذلة» is made transitive by «على», although by origin it is made transitive by the lām, because of the meaning it implies of tenderness and kindness. The meaning is: inclining kindly towards the believers by way of humbling themselves before them and being modest. The meaning may also be that, despite their nobility, their high rank and their superiority over the believers, they lower their wings to them; similar is His saying, Exalted is He, {أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى الكفار رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ} [al-Fatḥ: 29]. Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these two views. The Shaykh said: "It is said: or because it is on the basis of the omission of a muḍāf, the implied form being 'in spite of their superiority over the believers', the meaning being that they humble themselves and submit to those over whom they have been given superiority, despite their nobility and high standing," and he mentioned the verse of al-Fatḥ. I say: this is exactly al-Zamakhsharī's statement, except that his saying "on the basis of the omission of a muḍāf" gives the impression that it is omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, whereas here he omitted the first «على» and omitted both the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi together; and I do not know what led him to that.

The description on the side of love came as a verbal clause because the verb indicates renewal and occurrence, and this is fitting, for their love for Allah the Exalted renews their acts of obedience and worship of Him at every moment, and Allah's love for them renews His reward and favour to them at every moment. The description on the side of humility towards the believers and harshness towards the disbelievers came as a noun indicating intensity, to indicate that this is firmly established and settled and that it is strong in them; for the noun indicates permanence and stability. He put the description of love from them and for them before describing them as «أذلة» and «أعزة» because the latter two arise from the two loves. And He put their description relating to the believers before their description relating to the disbelievers because it is more emphatic and more binding than it, and also because of the nobility of the believer.

The majority read «أَذِلَّةٍ» and «أَعِزَّةٍ» in the genitive as adjectives, as stated. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أَذِلَّةً وأَعِزِّةً» has been read in the accusative as a ḥāl." I say: the one who read «أَذِلَّةً» is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, except that instead of «أعزة» he read «غُلَظاءَ على الكافرين» (harsh towards the disbelievers), which is an explanation. It is a ḥāl from «قوم», and this is permissible even though «قوم» is indefinite, because it is close to the definite, having been specified by the adjective.

His saying, Exalted is He: {يُجَاهِدُونَ}: it admits three views. First: it is another adjective of «قوم», which is why it came without the wāw, just as the two adjectives before it came without it. Second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «أعزة», i.e. they are mighty while striving; so said Abū al-Baqāʾ. On this view it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أَذِلَّة», i.e. they are humble towards the believers while striving, i.e. striving in the way of Allah does not prevent them from humility towards the believers. Its being a ḥāl from the pronoun of «أعزة» is more evident than its being a ḥāl from what I mentioned, which is why it was not acceptable to make the case one of contention (tanāzuʿ). Third: it is resumptive, brought to inform that they strive in support of the religion of Allah the Exalted.

His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ يَخَافُونَ}: there are several views on it. First: it is conjoined to «يُجاهِدُون», so the views given for what precedes apply to it. Second: the wāw is circumstantial, and the one to whom the ḥāl refers is the agent of «يجاهدون». al-Zamakhsharī said: "I.e. they strive, and their state in striving is not the state of the hypocrites." The Shaykh followed him and did not object to him. This is open to question, because they have stated explicitly that the imperfect negated by «لا» or «ما» is like the affirmative in that the circumstantial wāw may not directly precede it, and this, as you see, is an imperfect negated by «لا» — unless it is said that that condition is not agreed upon. But the reason for which they disallowed the wāw directly preceding the affirmative imperfect is present in the imperfect negated by «لا» and «ما», namely: the affirmative imperfect is equivalent to an explicit noun, for when you say «جاء زيدٌ يضحكُ» (Zayd came laughing), [it is] equivalent to «ضاحكاً», and the wāw may not enter upon «ضاحكاً», so likewise what resembles it and is equivalent to it. This is present in the negated form, for your saying «جاء زيدٌ لا يضحك» (Zayd came, not laughing) is equivalent to «غيرَ ضاحك», and the wāw does not enter upon «غيرَ ضاحك». [Translator's note: the source here prints «جاز زيدٌ لا يضحكُ» in the first example, evidently for «جاء زيدٌ يضحكُ».] However, this is made problematic by their having stated explicitly that the wāw may enter upon what is negated by «لم» and «لمّا», even though, in your saying «قام زيد لم يضحكْ» (Zayd stood up, not having laughed), it is equivalent to «غيرَ ضاحك». An instance of the wāw entering is His saying, Exalted is He, {أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ الجنة وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُم} [al-Baqara: 214], and the like. Third: the wāw is resumptive, so what follows it is a resumptive clause, independent as a statement. By this the difference arises between this view and the view in which I allowed the wāw to be a conjunction while holding that «يجاهدون» is resumptive; and this is clear.

«اللَّوْمَة» is the single instance of «اللَّوْم» (blame). al-Zamakhsharī said: "In it and in its indefiniteness are two intensifications, as though it were said: they do not fear anything at all of the blame of anyone among the blamers." «لومة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its agent in meaning. If it is asked: may its object be omitted, i.e. "they do not fear the blame of a blamer [directed at] them"? The answer is that this is not permissible according to the majority, because a maṣdar delimited by the feminine tāʾ [of single instance] does not govern; if it were built on the tāʾ [inherently], it would govern, as in his saying:

1747 - فلولا رجاءُ النصر منك ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك قد كانوا لنا بالموارِدِ
(Were it not for hope of help from you and fear of your punishment, they would have been [lying in wait] for us at the watering places.)

[Translator's note: the source prints «فولا»; the intended word is «فلولا».] He made «رهبةٌ» govern because it is built on the tāʾ. A [maṣdar] delimited by the tāʾ may not govern except in a few instances of their speech, as in his saying:

1748 - يُحايي به الجَلْدُ الذي هو حازمٌ ... بضربةِ كَفَّيهِ المَلا وَهُو راكِبُ
(With it the hardy, resolute man revives [another], by striking the dust with his two palms while he is riding.)

He is describing a man who gave another man water to drink and so revived him with it, and performed dry ablution (tayammum) with dust. «المَلا» is dust. He put «الملا» in the accusative by «ضربة», which is a maṣdar delimited by the tāʾ. The original of «لائم» is «لاوِم», because it is from «اللَّوْم»; it was given the vowel-change like «قائم».

As for «ذلك», there are three views on what it refers to. The most evident: it is all the preceding attributes by which the people were described — love, humility, might, striving in the way of Allah, and the absence of fear of blame from anyone. This is admissible in a demonstrative, I mean that it occurs in the singular form while referring to more than one; its full treatment was given on His saying, Exalted is He, {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]. Second: it refers to Allah's love for them and their love for Him. Third: it refers to His saying «أَذِلَّة», i.e. gentleness and abandoning haughtiness. These two involve a specification that is not clear, and it seems that what led to it is the demonstrative coming in the singular. «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «فَضْلُ الله» its khabar. «يؤتيه» admits three views. The most evident: it is a second khabar. Second: it is resumptive. Third: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, as in His saying {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [Hūd: 72]. [Translator's note: the source cites this as Hūd: 89; the verse is Hūd: 72.]

semin-durr:119-119.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ}: the majority read it in the nominative without tanwīn, and Nāfiʿ in the accusative without tanwīn. Al-Zamakhsharī transmitted from al-Aʿmash «يوماً» in the accusative with tanwīn, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Shāmī «يومٌ» in the nominative with tanwīn; so these are four readings. As for the reading of the majority, it is clear, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of accusative by «قال» (saying). As for the reading of Nāfiʿ, there are aspects concerning it. The first: that «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ and «يوم» its khabar, as in the first reading; the adverb was only made indeclinable because of its annexation to the verbal clause, even though that [verb] is declinable. This is the doctrine of the Kufans, who cited this reading as evidence for it. As for the Basrans, they do not permit the indeclinability unless the clause annexed to begins with a past verb; and upon that is the saying of al-Nābigha:

185 - 8- على حينَ عاتبتُ المشيبَ على الصِّبا ... فقلتُ: أَلمَّا أًصْحُ والشيبُ وازعُ
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for [my] youthful folly, and said: Have I not yet come to my senses, while grey hair restrains?)

They explained this reading as «يوم» being accusative as an adverb, attached in reality to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "occurring, or will occur, on the day [truthfulness] benefits"; so this is equal in meaning to the explanation of the first reading, and of the second as well. Some of them explained it as «هذا» being accusative by «قال», pointing to the maṣdar (verbal noun), so its accusative is as a maṣdar. It was also said: rather it points to the report and the preceding stories, so the disagreement over its accusative applies: is it accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or as a maṣdar? — because whenever something understood as speech occurs after the verb of saying, as in «قلت شعراً وخطبة» (I said poetry and a sermon), this disagreement applies. On every assumption, «يوم» is accusative as an adverb by «قال», i.e. Allah said this saying, or these reports, at the time of the benefiting of the truthful; and «ينفع» is in the position of genitive by annexation. It has preceded what may be annexed to clauses, and that it is one of three things. [Translator's note: the source prints «قلت شهراً وخطبة»; «شهراً» (a month) is evidently a misprint for «شعراً» (poetry); translated accordingly.] As for the readings with tanwīn, its nominative is as a khabar, as in the reading of the majority, and its accusative is as an adverb, as in the reading of Nāfiʿ; except that the clause after it, in both readings, is in the position of a description of what precedes it, and the returning pronoun is omitted. It is the counterpart of the words of Allah the Exalted: {يَوْماً لاَّ تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئاً} [al-Baqara: 48]. So the position of this clause is either nominative or accusative.

His words: {صِدْقُهُمْ}: nominative as fāʿil (agent); this is the reading of the generality. It was read irregularly (shādhdh) in the accusative, and there are four aspects concerning it. The first: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. it benefits them because of their truthfulness; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that and the Shaykh followed him. This is not permissible, because one of the conditions of the accusative is lacking, namely the identity of the agent: the agent of the benefiting is other than the agent of the truthfulness. No one may say: "It is made accusative by «الصادقين», as though it were said: those who are truthful because of their truthfulness, so the identity of the agent is secured", because that leads to a thing being a cause of itself — though there is room for discussion in it. The second: by the dropping of the preposition, i.e. «بصدقِهم»; you have also learned what is in this, namely that omitting the preposition is not regular. The third: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, governed by the active participle in «الصادقين», i.e. those who were true to their truthfulness, by way of intensification, as in «صَدَقْت القتال» (I was true to the fighting), as though you had promised the fighting and did not belie it. What may strengthen this is its accusative as an object of purpose with the governor being the active participle before it. The fourth: that it is an emphatic maṣdar, as though it were said: those who are truthful with truthfulness, as you say «صَدَق الصدقَ». On all these aspects the agent of «ينفع» is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted. The words of Allah the Exalted: {رَّضِيَ الله عَنْهُمْ}: its meaning is supplication. The rest of the sūra is clear in its iʿrab from its counterparts that have preceded; and to Allah belongs praise.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ}: this verse and those after it are among the most difficult in the Quran in ruling, i'rab and exegesis. Scholars have never ceased to find them difficult and to shrink back from them, so much so that Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book called al-Kashf: "This verse, in its reading, its i'rab, its exegesis, its meanings and its rulings, is among the hardest and most difficult verses in the Quran." He said: "What it contains of the sciences could be expounded in thirty leaves or more." He said: "We have mentioned it with commentary in a separate book." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is the speech of one who did not attain certainty (lit. 'the coolness') in its exegesis, and that is evident from his book." Al-Sakhāwī said: "I have not seen any of the scholars whose discussion of it came out clear from its beginning to its end." Al-Wāḥidī said: "This verse and those after it are among the most abstruse things in the Quran in meaning and i'rab." I say: I seek the help of Allah the Exalted in explaining its i'rab, the derivation of its individual words, the morphology of its words, its readings and the understanding of its composition — what pertains particularly to this work. As for the rest of its sciences, we ask Allah for help in refining them in my book "Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAzīz", if Allah wills; and with Him is all power and strength.

The majority read {شهادةُ بينكم} with «شهادة» nominative, annexed to «بينكم». Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and al-Shaʿbī read it nominative with tanwīn, and «بينَكم» accusative. Al-Sulamī, and al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj in one transmission from them, read «شهادةً» with tanwīn in the accusative, and «بينَكم» accusative.

As for the reading of the majority, there are five views in explaining it. The first: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «اثنان». On this view the omission of a muḍāf is unavoidable, either from the first or from the second. Its implied form with [omission] from the first is: "the possessors of the testimony among you are two," i.e. the two holders of the testimony among you are two; and its implied form with [omission] from the second is: "the testimony among you is the testimony of two." We were only compelled to [posit] an omission from the first or the second so that mubtadaʾ and khabar would be true of one and the same thing, because testimony is an abstract notion while the two are concrete persons. The two analyses mentioned for the likes of «زيدٌ عدلٌ» ("Zayd is justice") — namely making him the very maṣdar for emphasis, or its standing for an active participle — do not apply here, because the meaning rejects them here. However, al-Wāḥidī transmitted from the author of "al-Naẓm" that he said: "«شهادة» is a maṣdar put in the place of nouns," meaning by the testimony the witnesses, just as one says «رجلٌ عَدْلٌ ورِضا» and «رجالٌ عدلٌ ورِضا وزَوْر»; "and if you take it in the sense of witnesses, it is on the omission of a muḍāf, and the meaning would be: the number of witnesses among you is two." He cited as evidence His saying {الحج أَشْهُرٌ} [al-Baqara: 197], i.e. the time of the Ḥajj: "were it not for that, «أشهر» would be accusative on the interpretation 'the Ḥajj is in months'." I say: on its apparent sense, he made the maṣdar the very witnesses for emphasis, and for that reason he illustrated it with «رجال عدل»; and this is open to question.

The second: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ too, and its khabar is omitted, indicated by the context of the speech; on this view «اثنان» is nominative through the maṣdar, which is «شهادة», the implied form being: "among what has been prescribed for you is that two shall testify." Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it thus, and it is one of the two views of al-Zajjāj, and it is very apparent. On these two views «إذا» is an adverb of «شهادة», i.e. "that there be testimony at the time death — i.e. its causes — is present." And on these views «حين الوصية» admits three views. The most acceptable of them: it is a badal (substitute) from «إذا»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. He said: "In its substitution for it there is a proof that the bequest is obligatory." The second: it is accusative by «الموت» itself, i.e. death occurs at the time of the bequest; and it must be interpreted as the causes of death, because at the time of actual death there is no bequest. The third: it is accusative by «حَضَر», i.e. the causes of death are present at the time of the bequest.

The third [of the five views]: «شهادةُ» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «إذا حضر», i.e. "the occurrence of the testimony is at the time of death's being present"; and «حين» is according to the three views just given concerning it. In this case it may not be an adverb of «الشهادة», lest it entail predicating of the relative [element] before its ṣila (relative clause) is complete, which is not permissible; you have learnt the explanation of that from what has passed. When the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] mentioned this view he did not point this out, which is surprising of him.

The fourth: «شهادة» is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «حين الوصية»; on this view «إذا» is accusative by «الشهادة». It may not be accusative by «الوصية», even though the meaning is according to that, because the governed word of the interpreted maṣdar does not precede it, according to the Basrans, even if it is an adverb; and also because it would entail placing the muḍāf ilayhi before the muḍāf, since fronting the governed word implies fronting the governor, and the governor cannot be fronted, so neither can its governed word. They did not permit fronting the governed word of the muḍāf ilayhi before the muḍāf except in a single case, namely when the muḍāf is the word «غير», and they recited:
181 - 9- إنَّ أمرأً خَصَّني عمداً مودَّتَه ... على التنائي لَعندي غيرُ مكفورِ
(A man who deliberately singled me out for his affection despite the distance is, with me, not unthanked.)
— so «عندي» is accusative by «مكفور». They said: because «غير» has the status of «لا», and with «لا» it is permissible to front the governed word of what follows it before it. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that at the end of al-Fātiḥa, and mentioned that «أنا زيداً غيرُ ضارب» ("I am not a striker of Zayd") is permissible, but not «أنا زيداً مثلُ ضارب».

On these last two views, «اثنان» is nominative on one of two views: either as fāʿil (agent), i.e. "two shall testify," indicated by the word «شهادة»; or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, also indicated by «شهادة», i.e. "the two witnesses are two."

The fifth: «شهادةُ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «اثنان» is a fāʿil that stands in place of the khabar; Abū al-Baqāʾ and others mentioned it, and it is the school of al-Farrāʾ.
