However, al-Farrāʾ took «الشهادة» as occurring in the place of an imperative verb, as though He said "let two testify," so he made it of the category of the maṣdar standing in for a verb of request; and it is like «الحمدُ لله» and {قَالَ سَلاَمٌ} [Hūd: 69] in terms of meaning. This is the school of some in the likes of «ضَرْبي زيداً قائماً» ("my striking Zayd [is when he is] standing"), who claim that the yāʾ is a fāʿil standing in place of the khabar; but this is a weak school which the grammarians rejected, restricting that to the adjective relying on a negation or interrogation, as in «[أ]قام أبواك». [Translator's note: the source has «قام أبواك» without an interrogative or negative particle; it stands for a construction like «أقائمٌ أبواك».] On this school, «إذا» and «حين» are two adverbs in the accusative according to what was established for them in [views] other than this one.

We have obtained from the foregoing that the nominative of «شهادة» is from a single aspect, namely being a mubtadaʾ, and that there are five views on its khabar, mentioned above in detail; that the nominative of «اثنان» is from five aspects: first, its being the khabar of «شهادة» with the interpretation mentioned; second, that it is the fāʿil of «شهادة»; third, that it is the fāʿil of an implied «يشهد»; fourth, that it is the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the two witnesses are two"; fifth, that it is a fāʿil standing in place of the khabar; and that «إذا» admits two views: either accusative as an adverb, or nominative as the khabar of «شهادة». All of this is clear from what I have summarized before. The reading of al-Ḥasan, with it nominative and with tanwīn, is explained by what was given for the reading of the majority, without difference.

As for the reading with the accusative, there are three views on it. The first — the view of Ibn Jinnī —: it is accusative by an implied verb, and «اثنان» is nominative by that verb, the implied form being: "let two establish the testimony among you"; al-Zamakhsharī followed him in this and mentioned it. The Shaykh rejected this on the grounds that the grammarians did not permit omitting the verb and keeping its fāʿil unless what precedes it intimates it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو والآصال رِجَالٌ} [al-Nūr: 36-37] in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr [i.e. «يُسَبَّحُ»], i.e. men glorify Him; and like it:
182 - 0- ليُبْكَ يزيدُ ضارعٌ لخصومةٍ ... ومُخْتَبِطٌ مِمَّا تُطِيح الطَّوائِحُ
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let] one humbled in a dispute [weep for him], and a beggar seeking favour, of those whom calamities have cast away.)
— and there is disagreement on whether this is to be applied by analogy or not; or [unless] it answers a negation, as in [the poet's] saying:
182 - 1- تَجَلَّدْتُ حتى قيل: لم يَعْرُ قلبَه ... من الوجدِ شيءٌ قلتُ: بل أعظمُ الوَجْدِ
(I bore up so firmly that it was said: "No grief has touched his heart"; I said: "Rather, the greatest grief [has].")
i.e. "rather the greatest grief touched it"; or it answers an interrogation, as in [the poet's] saying:
182 - 2- ألا هَلْ أتى أمَّ الحويرثِ مُرْسِلي ... نعم خالدٌ إنْ لم تُعِقْه العوائِقُ
("Has my messenger come to Umm al-Ḥuwayrith?" Yes — Khālid [has], unless hindrances have hindered him.)
i.e. "rather he came to her," or "will come to her." And what we are dealing with is none of these three things.

The second: «شهادةً» is a substitute for pronouncing a verb, i.e. it is a maṣdar standing in place of the verb, so it governs as the verb governs, the implied form being "let two testify"; so «اثنان» is a fāʿil of the maṣdar, because it stands in the place of the verb, or of that omitted verb, according to the disagreement on the root question. I only supplied it as "let two testify" (ليشهد اثنان), giving it as an imperfect verb joined with the lām of command, and did not supply it as an imperative verb on the form «افعل», as the grammarians supply it in the likes of «ضرباً زيداً» ("strike Zayd!"), i.e. «اضرِبْ», because this one has made an overt noun nominative, namely «اثنان», whereas the form «افعل» makes nominative only a latent (mustatir) pronoun, if the one commanded is singular. Like it is [the poet's] saying:
182 - 3-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَنَدْلاً زُرَيْقُ المالَ نَدْلَ الثَّعالِبِ
(… so snatch up the wealth, Zurayq, as foxes snatch!)
— «زريق» may be vocative, i.e. "O Zurayq"; and the second: it is nominative by «ندلاً», on the grounds that it occurs in the place of «ليندلْ» ("let him snatch"); its tanwīn was only dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, in the manner of [the poet's] saying:
182 - 4-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلا قليلا
(… nor one who remembers Allah except a little.)
[Translator's note: the source writes «يا زرق», evidently for «يا زريق». Also the tanwīn dropped "for the meeting of two quiescents" in the cited half-verse is that of «ذاكر»; the remark about «زريق» is as written.]

The third: «شهادةً» is a substitute for pronouncing a verb as well, except that this verb is declarative, even though that is less frequent than the request type, as in «حمداً وشكراً لا كفراً» ("praise and thanks, not ingratitude"); and «اثنان» too is a fāʿil of it, its implied form being "two testify a testimony." This is the best of the explanations given for the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
182 - 5- وقوفاً بها صَحْبي عليَّ مَطِيَّهم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(My companions halting their mounts there for my sake …)
«وقوفاً» is a maṣdar substituting for a declarative verb; it made «صحبي» nominative and «مطيهم» accusative, its implied form being "my companions halted." It was stated earlier that al-Farrāʾ, in the reading with the nominative, took «شهادة» as occurring in the place of a verb, and «اثنان» as nominative by it; and it was stated that this may be one of the cases where the fāʿil stands in place of the khabar. And «بينكم», in the reading of those who gave «شهادة» tanwīn, is accusative as an adverb, and it is clear.

As for the reading with the genitive in it, it is from the category of extended usage (al-ittisāʿ) with adverbs, i.e. by making the adverb as though it were the object of that verb. Like it is {هذا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ} [al-Kahf: 78], and His saying, Exalted is He: {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] for those who read it in the nominative. The Shaykh said: "Al-Māturīdī said — and al-Rāzī followed him — that the original is «ما بينكم», and «ما» was omitted. Al-Rāzī said: «بينكم» is an allusion to dispute, because witnesses are only needed at dispute; and omitting «ما» is permissible when it is evident; its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكَمْ} in the reading of those who read it in the accusative." The Shaykh said: "Omitting the relative «ما» is not permissible according to the Basrans; and with annexation, supplying «ما» is not sound at all. And His saying {هذا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي} is not a parallel of {لقد تقطَّع بينكم}, because this one is annexed, while that one remains adverbial, so the omission of «ما» can be imagined in it — unlike «هذا فراقُ بيني» and «شهادةُ بينكم», for the supplying of «ما» cannot be imagined in them, because the annexation removed it from adverbial status and made it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extended usage." I say: this which the Shaykh transmitted from the two of them was said in exactly these words by Abū ʿAlī al-Jurjānī. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "His saying «شهادةُ بينكم», i.e. «ما بينكم», and «ما بينكم» is an allusion to dispute and quarrelling; then He annexed the testimony to the dispute, because witnesses are only needed in the dispute occurring among people; and the Arabs annex a thing to a thing when it pertains to it through some cause, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِِ} [al-Raḥmān: 46], i.e. his standing before his Lord. And the Arabs often omit mention of «ما» and «مَنْ» in a place where they are needed, as in His saying {وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ} [al-Insān: 20], i.e. what is there, and His saying {هذا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ} and {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ}, i.e. what is between me, and what is between you." And the Shaykh's saying "the supplying of «ما» cannot be imagined in it … to the end" is to be rejected, because the state of annexation does not make it the ṣila of an omitted relative noun; and it does not follow from that [that one may not] supply it in terms of meaning, not in terms of i'rab, with regard to the original. As for the omission of the relative noun, its verification was given earlier.

His saying: {ذوا}: a naʿt (adjective) of «اثنين», i.e. "two possessors of justice"; and likewise His saying «منكم» is also a naʿt of «اثنين». His saying {أَوْ آخَرَانِ} is conjoined to «اثنين», and «من غيركم» is a naʿt of «آخَرَين». What is meant by «منكم» is "from your relatives and your kin," and by «من غيركم» "from Muslims who are not related." It was also said: «منكم» "from the people of your religion," and «من غيركم» "from the protected non-Muslims (ahl al-dhimma)." Al-Naḥḥās preferred the first and said: "This rests on a subtle point in Arabic, namely that the meaning of «آخر» in Arabic is 'of the kind of the first'. You say «مررت بكريمٍ وكريم آخر» ('I passed a noble man and another noble man'), but «وخسيس آخرَ» ('and another base man') is not permissible, nor «مررت بحمارٍ ورجلٍ آخرَ» ('I passed a donkey and another man'). So likewise here «أو آخَران» must be 'or two other just men', and unbelievers are not just."

The Shaykh rejected that and said: "As for the examples he mentioned, they are correct, because he illustrated with «آخَر» placed after, and made it a naʿt of something not of the kind of the first. But the verse is of the type in which «آخر» is placed before the qualifier, and «آخر» is included in the genus before it, and the qualifier of the first genus is not taken into account. You say «مررتُ برجلٍ مسلمٍ وآخرَ كافرٍ» ('I passed a Muslim man and another, an unbeliever') and «اشتريت فرساً سابقاً وآخرَ بطيئاً» ('I bought a swift horse and another, a slow one'); but if you placed «آخر» after in these two examples and said «مررتُ برجل مسلم وكافر آخر», it would not be permissible. The verse is not of this [latter] kind, because its construction is «اثنان ذوا عَدْل منكم أو آخران من غيركم», so «آخران» is of the kind of His saying «اثنان», especially if you supply it as 'two men', for «آخران» are of the kind of 'two men'; and the qualifier in His saying «ذوا عدل منكم» is not taken into account, even if it is different from His saying «من غيركم», just as the qualifier of the genus is not taken into account in your saying «عندي رجلان اثنان مسلمان وآخران كافران» ('I have two Muslim men and two others, unbelievers'); for it is not a condition of «آخر», when it comes first, that it be of the kind of the first together with the restriction of its qualifier. The speech of the Arabs came according to what I have mentioned. The poet said:
182 - 6- كانوا فريقين يُصْفون الزِّجاجَ على ... قُعْسِ الكواهلِ في أَشْداقِها ضَخَمُ
وآخَرين تَرَى الماذِيَّ فوقَهُمُ ... مِنْ نَسْجِ داودَ او ما أَوْرَثَتْ إرَمُ
(They were two parties: [one] leaning their spears on [camels] with arched withers and broad jaws; and others on whom you see shining mail of David's weaving, or what Iram bequeathed.)
The implied form is: 'they were two parties: one party — or people — who lean the spearheads (الزجاج)…', then he said: 'and others on whom you see the mail'; so «آخرين» is of the kind of your saying «فريقاً», and he did not take it into account with its qualifier in his saying «يصفون الزجاج», because he divided those mentioned into two parts differing in qualifier and one in genus." He said: "Few understand this distinction, let alone know it."
[Translator's note: the gloss of «يُصْفون الزِّجاجَ» follows the explanation of the verse; the phrase is obscure.]

His saying: {أو}: the apparent sense is that it is for choice (takhyīr); and that is clear on the view that the meaning of «من غيركم» is "from other than your relatives among the Muslims," i.e. the testator has the choice between having two of his relatives witness or two unrelated Muslims. It was said that «أو» is for sequence (tartīb), i.e. one does not turn away from two witnesses from among you except when they are lacking; and this only applies if we say «من غيركم» means "from other than the people of your religion."

His saying: {إِنْ أَنتُمْ}: «أنتم» is nominative by an omitted [verb] explained by what follows it, and it is the question of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the implied form being "if you travel (ضَرَبْتُم)"; when the verb was omitted the pronoun became detached. This is the school of the majority of the Basrans. Al-Akhfash among them and the Kufans held that a mubtadaʾ (subject) may occur after the conditional «إنْ», as they also permitted it after «إذا». So «ضربتم» has no grammatical position according to the majority, because it is explicative; and its position is nominative according to the Kufans and al-Akhfash, because it is a khabar (predicate). Like it are {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ المشركين استجارك} [al-Tawba: 6] and {إِذَا الشمس كُوِّرَتْ} [al-Takwīr: 1]. [Translator's note: the source has «مرفوعٌ محذوفٍ», evidently missing «بفعلٍ» ("by an omitted verb"); rendered accordingly.]

The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: {اثنان ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ أَوْ آخَرَانِ}. But the implied form of this apodosis depends on a disagreement about this condition: is it a restriction on the testimony as such, or a restriction on «آخران مِنْ غيركم» only? — meaning that it is not permissible, in testimony to a bequest, to turn to the protected non-Muslims except on the condition of journeying in the land, which is travel. If it is said that it is a condition on the testimony as such, then the implied form of the apodosis is: "if you journey in the land, let two from among you or from other than you testify." And if it is a condition on turning to two others from outside the religion, then the implied form is: "then have two others from other than you witness," or "then the witnesses are two others from other than you." So it has become clear that what indicates the apodosis is either the whole of His saying «اثنان ذوا عدل…» to the end, on the first view, or «أو آخران من غيركم» only, on the second view.

The fāʾ in «فأصابتكم» conjoins this clause to the condition itself.

His saying, Exalted is He: {تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا}: there are two views on it. The first: it is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt of «آخران»; on this view the conditional clause and what is conjoined to it are parenthetical between the naʿt and what it qualifies, for His saying «تَحْبسونهما» is a naʿt of His saying «آخران». Al-Fārisī, Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Ḥawfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this. Al-Fārisī clarified it with a particular wording, saying: "«تحبسونهما» is a naʿt of «آخران», and He interposed His saying {إِنْ أَنتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الأرض}. The parenthesis conveyed that turning to two others from outside the religion, or outside kinship — according to the disagreement of the scholars on it — is only in the necessity of travel and the arrival of death during it; and the apodosis of «إنْ» was dispensed with because of what preceded in His saying «آخران من غيركم»." I say: it has become clear from his words that he makes the condition a restriction on «آخران من غيركم» only, not a restriction on the testimony as such; so the implied form of the apodosis in his view is as stated: "then call two others from other than you to witness," or "then the two witnesses are two others from other than you."

The second: it has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive; al-Zamakhsharī held this. He said: "If you say: what is the place of His saying {تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا}? I say: it is the resumption of speech, as though it were said, after stipulating justice in the two: how shall we act if we have doubts about them? And it was said: you detain them." This which Abū al-Qāsim mentioned is more in accord with the craft [of grammar], because the first entails separating the naʿt from what it qualifies by long speech. He said "after stipulating justice" on the basis of his preferred view regarding His saying {أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ}, i.e. "or two just men from those unrelated."

The Shaykh said: "In His saying «إن أنتم ضربتم» to the end, there is iltifāt (a shift) from the third person to the second person, since if it had proceeded according to the wording «إذا حضَر أحدَكم الموتُ» the construction would have been 'if he journeys in the land and [death] befalls him'. The iltifāt only came in the plural because «أحدكم» means: when death is present to each one of you." This is open to question, because the address proceeds according to the style of the first address, from His saying {يِا أَيُّهَا الذين آمَنُواْ شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ} to the end. [Translator's note: the source has «أحكم», a misprint for «أحدكم»; rendered accordingly.]

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: then the calamity of death befalls you, having had the two of them witness the bequest." From Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: its implied form is "having made your bequest [to them]." Some said: "This is more fitting, because the executor (al-waṣī) takes an oath, whereas the witness does not take an oath."

The address in «تحبسونهما» is to those in authority, not to those addressed with death befalling them, because that is impossible in their case. And «من بعد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تحبسونهما». The meaning of «الحَبْس» is withholding. One says «حَبَسْتُ» and «أَحْبَسْتُ فرسي في سبيل الله» ("I dedicated my horse in the path of Allah"), so it is «مُحْبَس» and «حبيس». A water reservoir is called «حَبْس» because it holds it back. One also says «حَبَّست» with doubling, in the sense of "I made an endowment (وقَفْتُ) and dedicated it (سَبَّلْتُ)"; and the doubling may be for multiplicity in the act, as in «حَبَّسْتُ الرجال» ("I detained the men [many of them]"). [Translator's note: the source has «وأَحَبَسْتُ» and «سَبَلْتُ», read as «أَحْبَسْتُ» and «سَبَّلْتُ».]

The alif and lām in «الصلاة» admit two views. The first: it is for the genus, i.e. after any prayer whatever. The second — and it is the apparent one —: it is for the known (al-ʿahd); it was said: the ʿAṣr [prayer], and other things were said.

His saying: {فَيُقْسِمَانِ}: there are two views on this fāʾ. The more apparent of them: it conjoins this clause to the clause of His saying {تَحْبِسُونَهُمَا}, so it is in the position of a nominative or has no position, according to the disagreement given above. The second: it is the fāʾ of the apodosis, i.e. the apodosis of an implied condition. Al-Fārisī said: "If you wish, you may not make the fāʾ for conjoining a clause, but make it an apodosis, as in the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
182 - 7- وإنسانٌ عيني يَحْسِر الماءُ تارةً ... فيبدو، وتاراتٍ يَجُمُّ فيَغْرَقُ
(And the pupil of my eye — the water [of tears] recedes at times, so it appears; and at times it gathers, so it drowns.)"
Its implied form according to them is: "when it recedes, it appears"; and likewise in the verse: "when you detain them, they swear." Makkī said something similar, for he said: "The fāʾ may be the answer of a condition, because «تحبسونهما» means a command to do that, and it is the answer of the command which the speech indicates, as though it were said: when you detain them, they swear." I say: there is no need calling for any supplying of an omitted condition. Moreover, it would require omitting a mubtadaʾ before His saying {فَيُقْسِمَانِ}, i.e. "then they swear." Moreover, «تحبسونهما» was stated earlier to be a naʿt, so how can he make it in the sense of a command, when a request does not occur as a naʿt? [Translator's note: the source writes «إن تحبسوهما» here, evidently for «تحبسونهما»; and «تحسبونهما» in Makkī's quote for «تحبسونهما».] As for the verse that Abū ʿAlī recited, the grammarians explained it on the basis that «يَحْسِر الماءُ تارة» is a declarative clause, and even if there is no linking element in it, a clause containing a linking element has been conjoined to it with the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and the fāʾ of causation made the two clauses a single thing.

And «بالله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb of swearing; it was stated earlier that the verb of swearing may not be made overt except with it [the bāʾ], because it is the mother of the category. His saying: {لاَ نَشْتَرِي بِهِ} is the answer of the oath implied in «يُقْسِمان», so it was introduced as [an oath's answer] is introduced.

His saying: {إِنِ ارتبتم} is a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "if you have doubts about the two of them, then make them swear." This condition and its implied apodosis are parenthetical between the oath and its answer. This verse is not one of those in which a condition and an oath meet, so that the first of them is answered and the answer of the other is omitted because the first one's answer indicates it; because the condition of that question is that the answer of the oath be fit to be the answer of the condition, so that it stands in place of its answer, as in «واللهِ إن تقم لأكرمنَّك» ("By Allah, if you stand I will surely honour you"), since if you supplied "if you stand I will honour you" it would be sound. Here, the apodosis of the condition is not supplied as what is the answer of the oath; rather its apodosis is supplied as a separate part. Do you not see that its implied form here is "if you have doubts, make them swear"? And if you supplied it as "if you have doubts, then we will not sell," it would not be sound. So it happens here that a condition and an oath have met and the first of them has been answered and the answer of the other omitted, but it is not of that rule.

Al-Jurjānī said: "There is an omitted 'saying' there, its implied form being: they swear by Allah and say this saying in their oaths; and the Arabs often imply 'saying', as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [al-Raʿd: 23-24], i.e. saying: 'Peace be upon you'." I do not know what led him to imply this "saying." [Translator's note: the source has «الجرجان», read as «الجرجاني».]

His saying: «به»: there are three views on this hāʾ. The first: it refers back to Allah the Exalted. The second: it refers back to the oath. The third — the view of Abū ʿAlī —: it refers back to the distortion of the testimony; and this is strong in terms of meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It refers back to Allah, or the oath (القسم), or the swearing (الحَلْف), or the oath (اليمين), or the distortion of the testimony, or to the testimony, because it is speech." I say: his saying "or the swearing or the oath" has no benefit, since they are one thing. Likewise, whoever says that it refers back to Allah the Exalted must supply an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "we will not sell for the oath of Allah," or His swearing and the like, because that is not said of the Holy Essence. Makkī said: "It was said: the hāʾ refers back to the testimony, but it was made masculine because it is speech; as He said: {فارزقوهم مِّنْهُ} [al-Nisāʾ: 8], where He referred the hāʾ to what is divided, because 'the division' indicates that."

Is «الاشتراء» (buying) here kept to its literal sense, or is selling meant by it? Two views, the more apparent being the first. The explanation of that rests on the accusative of «ثمناً», which is accusative as an object. Al-Fārisī said: "Its implied form is: we will not buy with it something possessing a price; do you not see that a price is not bought, but only what possesses a price is bought?" He said: "Buying here is not in the sense of selling, even though that occurs in the language, because selling is a removal [of the thing] from the seller, and the meaning is not according to that; rather its meaning is holding fast to it and preferring it over the truth." The Shaykh transmitted these very words without attributing them to Abū ʿAlī.

Makkī said: "Its meaning is 'something possessing a price', because the price is not bought, but only what possesses a price is bought; and it is like His saying {اشتروا بِآيَاتِ الله ثَمَناً} [al-Tawba: 9], i.e. something possessing a price." Others said: "It does not need the omission of a muḍāf." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There is no omission in it, because the price is bought just as one buys with it; and it was said: the implied form is 'something possessing a price'." Some said: "«لا نَشْتري» means: we will not sell the covenant of Allah for some gain we take, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ الله وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 77]. So the meaning of {لاَ نَشْتَرِي بِهِ} is: we will not take and will not exchange; and whoever sells something has bought [its price]. The meaning of the verse is: we will not take a price for the covenant of Allah by selling it for some worldly good." Al-Wāḥidī said: "With this one can dispense with much of Abū ʿAlī's strained effort; and this is the meaning of the view of al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] and al-Jurjānī." [Translator's note: the source has «بغرضٍ» in the first instance and «بعَرَضٍ» in the second; both are rendered by the sense "gain / worldly good".]

His saying: {وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قربى}: the wāw here is like the one that preceded in His saying {أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ} [verse 170] in al-Baqara, in that it may be said to be conjunctive or circumstantial, and that the clause of impossibility [with «لو»] is a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to an implied ḥāl, as in «أعطُوا السائلَ ولو على فَرَسٍ» ("give to the beggar, even if he is on a horse"). So likewise here its implied form is: "we will not sell it for a price in any state, even if the state is such-and-such." The noun of «كان» is a pronoun implied in it, referring back to the one in whose favour testimony is given, i.e. "even if the one in whose favour testimony is given is a relative."

His saying: {وَلاَ نَكْتُمُ}: the majority read the mīm of «نكتُم» with ḍamma, on the basis that «لا» is negative. The clause admits two views. The first — and it is the apparent one —: it is conjoined to the answer of the oath, so it too is sworn upon. The second: it is a declaration from themselves that they do not conceal the testimony; this is supported by the reading of al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī «ولا نَكْتُمْ» as a prohibition. This reading came according to the less frequent usage, inasmuch as the entry of the prohibitive «لا» on a first-person verb is rare; and of it is:
182 - 8- إذا ما خَرَجْنا مِنْ دمشقَ فلا نَعُدْ ... بها أبداً ما دامَ فيها الجَراضِمُ
(When we leave Damascus, let us never return to it as long as the gluttons remain in it.)

The majority read «شهادة الله» with annexation, and it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it was annexed to Him, Exalted is He, because He is the One who commands it, and commands that it be preserved and not concealed or lost. ʿAlī, the Commander of the Faithful, Nuʿaym ibn Maysara, and al-Shaʿbī in one transmission read «شهادةً اللهَ», with tanwīn on «شهادة» and in the accusative, and the Name of Majesty in the accusative; and it is clear: «شهادة» is the second object, and the Name of Majesty is accusative [as the object], placed first for veneration, and it is the first [object]. The original is «ولا نكتُم اللهَ شهادةً» ("we will not conceal a testimony from Allah"), and it is like His saying {وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ الله حَدِيثاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 42]; it was only placed first here because of attention to it, for it is what is being spoken about. [Translator's note: the source says the Name is accusative «على التعظيم» ("for veneration"), and that "it was placed first for attention to it"; the referent of "it" (the testimony or the Name) is as ambiguous in the source as here.]

There is a second view on it — transmitted by al-Zahrāwī —: that the Name of Majesty is accusative by the dropping of the particle of oath, the implied form being "and we will not conceal a testimony, by Allah"; when the preposition was omitted, what is sworn by was made accusative. But there is no need for it, because it calls for the omission of the first object of concealing, i.e. "and we will not conceal from anyone a testimony, by Allah," and there is strain in that. Abū al-Baqāʾ also held this view, saying: "on the grounds that it is accusative by the verb of swearing, omitted."

ʿAlī, the Commander of the Faithful, al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «شهادةً» with tanwīn in the accusative, and «آللهِ» with prolongation of the alif — [the hamza] of interrogation, which entered for affirmation (taqrīr) and to make the swearers stop and take note; it is a substitute for the implied particle of oath. Whether the genitive is by it or by the omitted particle is a matter of disagreement.

Al-Shaʿbī, in one transmission, and others read «شهادهْ» with the hāʾ, pausing on it, then beginning «آللهِ», with the hamzat al-waṣl (connective hamza) made disjunctive and with prolongation of the hamza, on the basis that it is for interrogation in the sense given above, and with the Name of Majesty in the genitive. The disjunctive hamza serves as a substitute for the particle of oath in this noble Name specifically; you say «يا زيدُ آللهِ لأفعلن» ("O Zayd, by Allah, I will surely do it"). The things that substitute for the particle of oath in this noble Name specifically are three: the alif of interrogation, making the hamzat al-waṣl disjunctive, and the hāʾ of alerting, as in «ها اللَّهِ»; and with «ها» the hamza of the Name of Majesty may be either disjunctive or connective. Whether the genitive is by the implied particle or by the substitute — it was stated that there is disagreement on it. And if someone said that their saying «أللهِ لأفعلنَّ», with the genitive and the disjunctive hamza, is because it is a hamza of interrogation, his statement would not be rejected.

If it is said: when the hamza of interrogation enters on the hamzat al-waṣl that accompanies the lām of definition, or [that of] «ايمن» in oaths, the hamzat al-waṣl must remain, and then it is either softened (tusahhal) or changed into an alif; whereas this one has no hamzat al-waṣl remaining after it, so it must be a hamzat al-waṣl made disjunctive as a substitute for the particle of oath. The answer: they only changed the alif of waṣl, or softened it, after the hamza of interrogation in order to distinguish interrogation from statement; and here confusion is excluded, for the genitive in the Name of Majesty signals it, so there is no need for the hamzat al-waṣl to remain changed or softened. On this basis the reading «الله» and «آلله», short and long, may be interrogative; and this is a good explanation.

Ibn Jinnī said about this reading: "Pausing on «شهادهْ» with a quiescent hāʾ and starting the oath afresh is good, because starting it at the beginning of speech is more fitting for it and more awe-inspiring than its entering in the course of the statement." This reading — I mean «أللهِ» with a disjunctive alif without prolongation and with the Name of Majesty in the genitive — was transmitted from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim. And it was read «شهادةً اللهِ», with «شهادة» accusative with tanwīn and the Name of Majesty in the genitive with a connective hamza, on the basis that the genitive is by the implied particle of oath without any substitute for it, neither disjunction nor a hamza of interrogation; and this is peculiar to it [i.e. the Name of Allah].

His saying, Exalted is He: {إِنَّآ إِذَاً لَّمِنَ الآثمين}: this clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive. They declared of themselves that they would be among the sinners if they concealed the testimony; for that reason they brought «إذَنْ», which signals requital and answer. The majority read {لمن الآثمين} without transfer [of the vowel] and without assimilation. Ibn Muḥayṣin and al-Aʿmash read {لَمِلاَّثِمين}, assimilating the nūn of «مِن» into the lām of definition after transferring to it the vowel of the hamza in «آثمين»; he took account of the transferred vowel and so assimilated. It is the counterpart of the reading of those who read {عَاداً الأولى} with assimilation; there, if Allah wills, its verification will come; and with Him is strength.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ الله}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); and «رسولهُ» and «الذين» are conjoined to the khabar. al-Zamakhsharī said: A plurality has been mentioned, so why was it not said: «إنما أولياؤُكم»? He answered that guardianship (wilāya) belongs to Allah the Exalted by way of originality, and then it is strung into the same thread in being affirmed for His Messenger and for the believers; and had it been brought in the plural, so that it was said «إنما أولياؤُكم», there would be in the speech no principal and follower.
I say: Another possibility is that «وَلِيّ» is on the pattern faʿīl, and the scholars of the language have stated explicitly that faʿīl applies to the singular, the dual and the plural, masculine and feminine, in one single form; it is said: «الزيدون صديقٌ» and «هند صديقٌ». This is the same; the most that can be said is that it is placed first in the construction. al-Zamakhsharī and others gave this answer concerning His saying, the Exalted, {وَمَا قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدٍ} [Hūd: 89], and he mentioned the reason for it, namely its resemblance to maṣdars (verbal nouns); its verification will come later. Ibn Masʿūd read: «إنما مَوْلاكم», but that is an explanation, not a reading.
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يُقِيمُونَ الصلاوة}: there are five possibilities. The first: that it is nominative as an adjective of His saying «الذين آمنوا»; He described the believers by establishing the prayer and giving the zakāt, and He mentioned these two acts of worship rather than the rest of the branches of faith because they are the best of them. The second: that it is nominative as a badal (substitute) for «الذين آمنوا». The third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم الذين». The fourth: that it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to what precedes it; for everything that may be a badal may be an explicative apposition, except in what is excepted, which I have mentioned earlier. The fifth: that it is accusative by the implying of a verb; this possibility and the one before it belong to the category of cutting off from following (qaṭʿ ʿan al-tabaʿiyya).
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said, after reporting from al-Zamakhsharī only the two possibilities of badal and an omitted mubtadaʾ: "I do not know what prevented him from the adjective, since it is what comes first to the mind, and because the word substituted-from is in the intention of being discarded, which is not valid here, for it is the very adjective upon which the validity of the descriptions that follow it depends."
I say: We do not concede that the adjective is what comes first to the mind; rather the badal is what comes first. Moreover, describing by means of a relative noun is contrary to the original rule, because it is interpreted as a derived noun without being derived. And we do not concede that the substituted-from is in the intention of being discarded; that is what is transmitted from Sībawayh.
His saying: {وَهُمْ رَاكِعُونَ}: there are two possibilities for this clause. The more apparent: that it is conjoined to the preceding clauses, and so it is a ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. It was brought as a nominal clause, unlike those before it (He did not say «ويركعون»), out of concern for this description, because it is the most visible of the pillars of the prayer. The second: that the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and its owner is the wāw of «يُؤْتون»; and what is meant by rukūʿ (bowing) is humility, i.e. they give the charity while being humble towards the poor to whom they give. It is also possible that actual bowing is meant, as it is related of ʿAlī, Commander of the Believers, that he gave his ring in charity while bowing.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ}: «مَنْ» is a conditional in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). And His saying {فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ الله} may be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, and whoever does not require a pronoun to return to the conditional noun when it is a mubtadaʾ cites it as evidence. One may say: it was permissible only because what is meant by «حزب الله» is the very mubtadaʾ itself, so it falls under the repetition of the mubtadaʾ by its meaning; and there is a disagreement about it: al-Akhfash permits it. The implied form is: «ومَنْ يتولَّ اللهَ ورسولَه والذين آمنوا فإنه غالبٌ», and the overt noun was put in the place of the pronoun for a benefit, namely the honour of attaching the party (ḥizb) to Allah the Exalted. It is also possible that the apodosis is omitted because the speech indicates it, i.e. «ومَنْ يتولَّ اللهَ ورسولَه والذين آمنوا يَكُنْ من حزبِ الله الغالبِ» or «يُنْصَرْه» and the like, with His saying {فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ الله} indicating it. On these two possibilities there is no evidence in the verse against the requirement of a pronoun returning to the conditional noun. His saying {فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ الله هُمُ الغالبون} is in the position of the jussive if we make it the apodosis of the condition, and has no position if we make it an indication of the apodosis. His saying «هم» may be a separating pronoun (faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ with «الغالبون» as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ»; the discussion of the separating pronoun and its benefit has already preceded. And al-ḥizb is: a group in which there is harshness and severity; so it is a particular group.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ الذين اتخذوا دِينَكُمْ}: the verse. «الذين» with its ṣila (relative clause) is the first object of His saying {ولا تتَّخِذوا}, and the second object is His saying «أولياء»; «دينَكم» is the first object of «اتخذوا» and «هُزُوا» the second object. What is in «هُزْءاً» of readings and derivation has already preceded. His saying {مِّنَ الذين أُوتُواْ} has two possibilities. One: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its owner has two possibilities: one, that it is the first relative noun; the other, that it is the fāʿil (agent) of the second «اتَّخذوا». The second of the first two possibilities is that it is an explanation of the first relative noun, so «مِنْ» is for specifying the kind (bayān al-jins). And His saying {مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} is attached to «أوتوا», because they were given the Book before the believers; and what is meant by «الكتاب» is the genus.
His saying: {والكفار}: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «والكفارِ» in the genitive, and the rest read it in the accusative; both are clear. The genitive reading is a conjunction to the relative noun governed in the genitive by «من»; its meaning is that He forbade them to take as allies those who mock, and made clear that those who mock are two classes: the people of an earlier Book, namely the Jews and Christians, and the disbelievers who worship idols; although the name of disbelief applies to both groups, "the disbelievers" (al-kuffār) came to be used predominantly for the idol-worshippers, and "the People of the Book" for the Jews and Christians. al-Wāḥidī said: "The proof for this reading from the Revelation is His saying, the Exalted: {مَّا يَوَدُّ الذين كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب وَلاَ المشركين} [al-Baqara: 105]; they agreed on the genitive for «المشركين», conjoined to «أهل الكتاب», and it was not conjoined to the operator that governs the nominative." He means by that that He applied "the disbelievers" to the People of the Book and "the polytheists" to the idol-worshippers. What indicates that those meant by «الكفار» in the verse of al-Māʾida are the polytheists is the reading of ʿAbdullāh: «ومن الذين أشركوا». The reading of Abū ʿAmr was also given preference on account of proximity, since the word conjoined-to is near; and it was also given preference by the reading of Ubayy: «ومن الكفار», with «من» brought in.
As for the reading of the others, its explanation is that it is conjoined to the first relative noun, i.e. «لا تتخذوا المستهزئين ولا الكفار أولياء»; so it is like His saying, the Exalted: {لاَّ يَتَّخِذِ المؤمنون الكافرين أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ المؤمنين} [Āl ʿImrān: 28], except that this reading does not touch on informing of the mockery of the polytheists, though they too are mockers; He, the Exalted, said: {إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ المستهزئين} [al-Ḥijr: 95], and those meant by them are the polytheists of the Arabs. And because of the clarity of the genitive reading, Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib said: "Were it not for the agreement of the community on the accusative, I would have chosen the genitive, for its strength in meaning and for the nearness of the conjoined to what it is conjoined to."

semin-durr:58-58.t: The pronoun in {اتخذوها} may return to the prayer (al-ṣalāh), and that is the apparent sense; and it may return to the verbal noun understood from the verb, i.e. "they took the calling (al-munādāh)"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it, and there is remoteness in it, since nothing calls for it when what the pronoun can return to is stated explicitly, unlike His saying, the Exalted: {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. And His saying {ذلك بِأَنَّهُمْ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. "that mockery is established because of their lack of intellect."

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَلاَّ تَكُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr (al-Baṣrī) and the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it with ḍamma on the nūn (تَكُونُ), and the rest read it with fatḥa. As for the one who read it with ḍamma, for him «أَنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy «أَنَّ», and its noun is the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), omitted, its implied form being "annahu" (that it); «لا» is a negator, «تكون» is a complete verb (tāmma), «فتنةٌ» is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; and it explains the pronoun of the matter and affair. On this reading «حَسِب» here is for certainty, not doubt. Among its uses for certainty is the poet's saying:
178 - 0- حَسِبْتُ التقى والجودَ خيرَ تجارةٍ ... رَباحاً إذا ما المرءُ أصبحَ ثاقِلاً
(I reckoned piety and generosity the best of merchandise, in profit, when a man becomes weighed down [by age or burdens].)
That is: I was certain, because doubt is not fitting there. We were compelled to make it mean certainty in the noble verse only because the lightened «أَنْ» occurs only after certainty. As for his saying:
178 - 1- أرجو وآمُل أَنْ تدنُو مودتُها ... وما إخالُ لدينا منكِ تنويلُ
(I hope and aspire that her affection will draw near, though I do not think there will be any bestowal from you with us.)
its apparent sense is that it [the «أن»] is the lightened one, since it does not govern, and yet it occurs after «أرجو» and «آمل», which are not certainty. The answer is in two ways. The first: «أَنْ» is the subjunctive (nāṣiba) one, and it was merely left without effect (uhmilat) by analogy with the maṣdar «ما». The proof of this is that, had it been the lightened one, it would have been separated from the verbal clause by what we shall mention. This would then be like the saying of Allah the Exalted: {لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ الرضاعة} [al-Baqara: 233], and like his saying:
178 - 2- يا صاحبيَّ فَدَتْ نفسي نفوسَكما ... وحيثما كنتما لُقِّيتُما رَشَدا
(O my two companions, may my soul ransom your souls, and wherever you may be, may you meet with right guidance.)
أَنْ تَحْمِلا حاجةً لي خَفَّ مَحْمَلُها ... تستوجبا نعمةً عندي بها ويَدا
(That you carry a need of mine, light to carry, you will earn thereby a favour and a kindness from me.)
أَنْ تقرآنِ على أسماءَ ويحكما ... مني السلامَ وألاَّ تُشْعِرا أحدا
(That you two recite to Asmāʾ, woe to you both, my greetings, and that you let no one know.)
His saying «أَنْ تقرآن» is a badal (substitute) for «حاجة», and he left «أن» without effect. Similar is his saying:
178 - 3- إني زعيمٌ يا نُوَيْ ... قَةُ إن نجوْتِ من الرَّزاحِ
(I am guarantor, O little she-camel, if you escape from exhaustion,)
ونجوتِ من وَصَبِ العدو ... و [من الغدو] إلى الرَّواحِ
(and escape the enemy's hardship, and [the morning journey] to the evening journey,)
أَنْ تهبطين بلادَ قَوْ ... مٍ يَرْتَعُون من الطِّلاحِ
(that you will descend upon the land of a people who graze on the ṭilāḥ trees.)
However it is construed in the verses I have mentioned, one of two irregularities (shudhūdhayn) necessarily follows, each of which has been said to be possible: either leaving «أَنْ» without effect, or the lightened one occurring after something other than knowledge, with no separation between it and the verbal clause.
The second of the two answers: his hope and aspiration were so strong that they came close to certainty, so he treated them as certainty in this respect. As for the poet's saying:
178 - 4- عَلِموا أَنْ يُؤَمَّلون فجادُوا ... قبلَ أَنْ يُسْألوا بأعظمِ سُؤْلِ
(They knew that they were being hoped for, so they gave generously, before being asked, in answer to the greatest of requests.)
the apparent sense is that it is the lightened one, and the absence of separation is irregular; it is also possible that it is the subjunctive one, in which case its occurrence after knowledge is irregular and its being left without effect is irregular. So in the first there is one irregularity, namely the absence of separation, and in the second there are two: the occurrence of the subjunctive one after knowledge, and leaving it without effect by analogy with its sister «ما».
Here (in the verse) it came with what is obligatory according to some, or the better course according to others, namely the separation between the lightened «أَنْ» and its khabar when it is a verbal clause with a fully conjugating verb that is not an invocation. The separator is either a negation, as in this verse, or a particle of futurity (ḥarf tanfīs), as in His saying, the Exalted:
{عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُمْ مرضى} [al-Muzzammil: 20], and similar: "ʿalimtu an sawfa taqūmu" (I knew that you would stand); or «قد», as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَنَعْلَمَ أَن قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا} [al-Māʾida: 113]; or «لو», which is rare, as in His saying: {وَأَلَّوِ استقاموا} [al-Jinn: 16] and {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ الغيب} [Sabaʾ: 14]. I specified "verbal" to exclude the nominal clause, which needs no separator, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ الحمد للَّهِ رَبِّ العالمين} [Yūnus: 10] and as in his saying:
178 - 5- في فتيةٍ كسيوفِ الهندِ قد عَلِموا ... أَنْ هالِكٌ كلُّ مَنْ يَخْفَى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among youths like Indian swords, who knew that everyone who goes barefoot or wears sandals is perishing.)
And I specified "fully conjugating" to exclude the non-conjugating verb, which needs no separator, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سعى} [al-Najm: 39] and {وَأَنْ عسى أَن يَكُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 185]; and "not an invocation" to exclude the one that occurs as an invocation, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَّ غَضَبَ الله} [al-Nūr: 9] in the reading of Nāfiʿ.
As for the one who put «تكونَ» in the accusative, for him «أَنْ» is the one that puts the imperfect in the subjunctive, entering upon a verb negated with «لا»; and «لا» does not prevent what follows it from being governed by what precedes it, whether a subjunctive particle, a jussive particle or a preposition. The subjunctive is like this verse; the jussive is like His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ} [al-Anfāl: 73] and {إِلاَّ تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ الله} [al-Tawba: 40]; and the preposition is like: "ji'tu bi-lā zādin" (I came without provisions).
And «حَسِب» here is in its usual sense of supposition (ẓann). For the subjunctive «أن» does not occur after knowledge, just as the lightened one does not occur after anything else; and the occurrence of the subjunctive one after certainty is irregular, though that is explicit about it, as in his saying:
178 - 6- نَرْضَى عن الناسِ إنَّ الناسَ قد عَلِموا ... أَنْ لا يدانِيَنا من خَلْقِه بشرُ
(We are content with people; indeed people have known that no human of His creation comes near us.)
Nobody may say that "knowledge" here means supposition, since no necessity calls for that. The most frequent case after verbs of doubt is the subjunctive with «أَنْ», and for that reason there is consensus on the accusative in His saying, the Exalted: {أَحَسِبَ الناس أَن يتركوا} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2]. As for His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ} [Ṭā Hā: 89], the majority are for the nominative, because seeing applies to knowledge.
The upshot is that whenever it occurs after knowledge it must be the lightened one; when it occurs after what is neither knowledge nor doubt it must be the subjunctive one; and if it occurs after a verb that admits both certainty and doubt, two forms are allowed in respect of two considerations: if we take it as certainty we make it the lightened one and put what follows it in the nominative, and if we take it as doubt we make it the subjunctive one and put what follows it in the accusative. The noble verse is of this category, as is His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِم} [Ṭā Hā: 89] and His saying: {أَحَسِبَ الناس أَن يتركوا} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2]; but in the first it was read only with the nominative, and in the second only with the accusative, because the reading is a followed sunna. This is the precise formulation of the matter. I say it because some say that after verbs of doubt two forms are allowed, which gives the impression that it may be the lightened one while the verb before it remains in its meaning of doubt; but what he means is what I have told you, the formal possibility under the two considerations mentioned. Hence al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did the verb of supposition enter upon «أَنْ», which is for affirmation? I say: He placed their supposition, because of its strength in their breasts, in the position of knowledge." The reason requiring the lightened one after certainty, the subjunctive after other than it, and the two forms where there is hesitation is what they have mentioned: the lightened «أَنْ» indicates the firmness and settledness of the matter because it is for emphasis like the heavy one, and knowledge and its category are likewise, so it is fitting to place it after certainty because of the affinity between them. The proof of this is that it occurs in its heavy form after certainty, as in His saying, the Exalted:
{وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ الله هُوَ الحق المبين} [al-Nūr: 25], {أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ الله على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ} [al-Baqara: 106], {أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ الله لَهُ مُلْكُ السموات والأرض} [al-Baqara: 107], and so on. And the kind that does not indicate firmness and settledness is followed by the subjunctive one, as in His saying, the Exalted: {والذي أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِي} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 82], {نخشى أَن تُصِيبَنَا دَآئِرَةٌ} [al-Māʾida: 52], {فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 80], {أَأَشْفَقْتُمْ أَن تُقَدِّمُواْ} [al-Mujādila: 13], and so on. And the kind that admits both is followed sometimes by the lightened one and sometimes by the subjunctive one, as mentioned under the two considerations. On either assumption, I mean its being the lightened or the subjunctive one, it fills the place of the two objects according to the majority of the Basrans, and of the first object, with the second omitted, according to Abū l-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash), that is: "they supposed the absence of trial to be existent or occurring." Some grammarians reported that whoever reads the nominative should separate «أن» from «لا» in writing, because the implied pronoun «hā» (the pronoun of the matter) intervenes in meaning, while whoever reads the accusative should not separate them, there being no intervener between them. Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: "This may be admissible outside the muṣḥaf; as for the muṣḥaf, it was written only joined." End of quotation. I say: this expression contains looseness, since the word "joined" suggests that it is written «أنلا», with «أن» joined to «لا» in writing; it ought rather to be said: no form is written for it [the nūn], or a separate form is written for it. [Translator's note: the Arabic text of this last sentence is as printed; the intended sense is as rendered.]
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ}: in this book there are five aspects. The first: the wāw is a sign of the plural of the agent, just as the feminine tāʾ is attached to the verb to indicate the feminine of the agent, as in "qāmat Hind"; and this dialect also applies to the dual and the feminine plural, so one says "qāmā akhawāka" and "qumna akhawātuka", as in his saying:
178 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقد أَسْلَماه مُبْعَدٌ وحَميمٌ
(... and they both abandoned him, a distant one and a close kinsman.)
and his saying:
178 - 8- ولكنْ دِيافِيٌّ أبوه وأمُّه ... بِحَوْرانَ يَعْصِرنَ السَّليطَ أقاربُهْ
(But his father and mother are of Diyāf, in Ḥawrān; his relatives press the oil.)
Some argued from his saying, peace be upon him: "Angels succeed one another among you" (yataʿāqabūna fīkum malāʾikatun). The grammarians call this dialect the dialect of "akalūnī l-barāghīth" (the fleas ate me). But the more eloquent usage is that no sign be attached to the verb. The grammarians distinguished between the attachment of the feminine sign and that of the dual and plural signs in that the feminine sign is more obligatory, because femininity is in the very essence of the agent, unlike duality and plurality, which are not inherent.
The second aspect: the wāw is a pronoun referring to those mentioned, to whom the wāw of «حسبوا» refers, and «كثير» is a badal (substitute) for this pronoun, as you say: "ikhwatuka qāmū kabīruhum wa-ṣaghīruhum" (your brothers stood, the elder of them and the younger) and the like.
The third aspect: the wāw is also a pronoun and «كثيرٌ» is a badal for it. The difference between this aspect and the previous one is that the pronoun in the first aspect is explained by what precedes it, namely the Children of Israel, whereas in this aspect it is explained by what follows it. This is one of the places where a pronoun is explained by what follows it, namely when the thing explaining it is made a badal of it; it is a disputed question, whose treatment has already been given. The fourth aspect: the pronoun refers to those mentioned earlier, and «كثير» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Makkī gave two implied forms: one, "the blind and deaf are many of them"; the other, "the blindness and the deafness are many of them", the indication being His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ}. On his first implied form «كثير» applies to them, and «منهم» is an adjective of «كثير»; on the second «كثير» applies to the blindness and the deafness, not to them, and «منهم» is an adjective of it in the sense that it issued from them; and this second is not apparent. Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as: "those are many of them". The fifth aspect: «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ and the verbal clause before it is the khabar. It is not said that a verb, whenever it occurs as a khabar, must be placed later, for that is conditional on the agent being latent, as in "Zaydun qāma"; for if it were put first, "qāma Zaydun", it would be confused with the agent. If it is said: this too would be confused with the agent in the dialect of "akalūnī l-barāghīth", the answer is that it is a weak dialect to which we pay no heed. Abū l-Baqāʾ weakened this aspect for another reason, saying: "because the verb has occurred in its proper position, so nothing else is intended for it." There is room for objection in this, since we do not concede that it occurred in its proper position; it would have occurred in its proper position only if it were bare of a sign. Like this verse also is His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَسَرُّواْ النجوى الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 3].
The majority read «عَمُوا وَصمُّوا» with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the ṣād; the original is «عَمِيُوا» and «صَمِمُوا» like «شَرِبُوا», so the first was altered by elision and the second by assimilation (idghām). Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read «عُمُوا» and «صُمُّوا» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and ṣād, and with the mīm of «عَمُوا» lightened. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the implication of «ʿamāhum Allāh wa-ṣammahum», that is: He struck them and hit them with blindness and deafness, as one says «nazaktuhu» when you strike him with the spear (nayzak), and «rakabtuhu» when you strike him with your knee." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) did not object to him, although before that, after reporting the reading, he had said: "It follows the course of «zukima l-rajulu» (the man was afflicted with a cold) and «azkamahu Allāh», and «ḥumma» (he was feverish) and «aḥammahu Allāh»; one does not say «zakamahu Allāh» nor «ḥammahu», just as one does not say «ʿamaytuhu» nor «sammamtuhu»; these are verbs that came in the passive, whose agent is not named, and they are transitive triliteral; when they are built in the active they become intransitive, and if you want to build them in the active as transitive you introduce the hamza of transitivization, which is a strange type among verbs." End of quotation. His saying "just as one does not say «ʿamaytuhu» nor «sammamtuhu»" implies that the triliteral of these is not transitive, yet al-Zamakhsharī said, on the implication, «ʿamāhum Allāh wa-ṣammahum», thus using the triliteral as transitive. If what the Shaykh said is correct, then Abū l-Qāsim's words must be invalid, or vice versa.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «كثيراً» in the accusative, as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, though it has been mentioned more than once that for Sībawayh it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Makkī said: "Were you to put «كثيراً» in the accusative in ordinary speech, it would be permissible to make it an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: much blindness and deafness." I say: it is as though he had not come across it as a reading, or it was not sound in his view because of its irregularity.
As for His saying {فَعَمُواْ}, He joined it with «fa-», and His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ}, He joined it with «thumma»; and this is a fine meaning: immediately after the supposition, blindness and deafness befell them without delay, and He attributed both verbs to them, in contrast to His saying {فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وأعمى أَبْصَارَهُمْ} [Muḥammad: 23], because that concerns someone who had no prior guidance. And He attributed the good action to Himself in His saying {ثُمَّ تَابَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ}, and joined His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ} with the particle of delay as an indication that they persisted in error until the time of repentance.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تَنقِمُونَ}: the reading of the majority is with kasra on the qāf; the reading of al-Nakhaʿī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Ḥaywa is with fatḥa on it. These two readings are branches derived from the past tense, and there are two dialects in it: the more eloquent, which Thaʿlab reported in his Faṣīḥ, is «نَقَم» with fatḥa on the qāf, imperfect «يَنْقِم» with kasra; and the other is «نَقِم» with kasra on the qāf, imperfect «يَنْقَم» with fatḥa, which al-Kisāʾī reported. In His saying, the Exalted, {وَمَا نَقَمُواْ مِنْهُمْ} [al-Burūj: 8] it was read only with fatḥa.
His saying {إِلاَّ أَنْ آمَنَّا} is an object of «تنقمون» in the sense of "you dislike" and "you find fault with"; it is an incomplete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). «منا» is attached to it, i.e. "you dislike nothing from our side except faith." The original usage of «نَقَم» is that it is made transitive by «على»; you say «نَقَمْتُ عليه كذا». It was made transitive here by «مِنْ» for a meaning that I shall mention. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «"مِنَّا" is the second object of «تَنْقِمون», and what follows «إلا» is the first object; and it is not permissible for «منَّا» to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَنْ» and the verb, for two reasons: one, the advancing of the ḥāl before «إلاّ»; the second, the advancing of the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative; and the implied form is: do you dislike from us anything except our faith?» End of quotation.
In his saying "first and second object" there is something to consider, because the verbs that take two objects, one by themselves and the other by a preposition, are limited in number, such as «أمر», «اختار», «استغفر», «صَدَّق», «سَمَّى», «دعا» in its meaning, «زَوَّج», «نبَّأ» and «أنبأ», «خَبَّر», «أَخْبر» and «حَدَّث» when not implying the meaning of «أعلم»; in all of them dropping the preposition and using the accusative is permissible, and this is not one of them. As for his saying "and it is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl", he means that if the word «منا» had come after «أن آمنَّا», it would have been permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the interpreted maṣdar of «أَنْ» and its ṣila, and the implied form would become: "do you dislike anything except faith in the state of its being from us"; but it is impossible, given its advancing before «أن آمنَّا», for the two reasons mentioned. One of them is its advancing before «إلاَّ»; by this he means that the ḥāl is not advanced before «إلاَّ». And I do not know what prevents that, for when «منَّا» is made a ḥāl from «أَنْ» and what is within its scope, the operator of the ḥāl is implied, and the owner of the ḥāl is restricted; and when the owner of the ḥāl is restricted, advancing the ḥāl before it is obligatory. So it is said: «ما جاء راكباً زيد» and «ما ضَرَبْتُ مكتوفاً إلا عمراً»; «راكباً» and «مكتوفاً» are two ḥāls advanced obligatorily because their owners are restricted, and this is the same. And his saying "the second: the advancing of the ṣila before the relative": no ṣila has been advanced before a relative. The explanation: the relative is «أن», the ṣila is «آمنا», and «منَّا» is not attached to the ṣila but is the object of an implied word, which implied word is in reality governed in the accusative by «تَنْقِمون». I do not know what he imagined that he said what he said. Even so, it is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl, but not for what he mentioned; rather because it leads to the implied form becoming: "do you resent anything except our faith from us", whereas from the very word «إيماننا» it is understood that it is from us, so there is no benefit in it then.
If it is said: it would be an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), it is said: that is contrary to the original rule, and this is not one of its places; also, this resembles preparing a governor for work and then cutting it off from it, for «تَنْقِمون» demands this preposition with an evident demand. The majority read «وما أُنْزِل إلينا وما أُنْزِل» with the passive in both; Abū Nahīk read «أَنْزل، وأَنْزل» with the active; both are clear.
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ}: the majority read «أَنَّ» with fatḥa on the hamza; Nuʿaym b. Maysara read it with kasra. As for the reading of the majority, «أنَّ» in it may be in the position of the nominative, the accusative or the genitive. The nominative is from one angle only, namely that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The khabar is omitted, i.e. your wickedness is established and known to you, because you know that we are on the truth and you are on falsehood, except that the love of leadership and amassing wealth does not leave you, so that you would be fair." So he implied the khabar as postponed. The Shaykh said: "The khabar should be implied only as advanced, because, on the soundest view, one does not begin with «أَنَّ» except after «أمَا»." End. It may be said: what is not tolerated in verbal matters is tolerated in implied matters, especially as this runs in the manner of an explanation of meaning, and the aim is to show that khabar and how it would be pronounced; for it is said that he holds that beginning with «أنَّ» is permissible without restriction. So two possibilities arise in implying the khabar with regard to advancing and postponing.
As for the accusative, it is from six angles. The first: that it is conjoined to «أن آمَنَّا». This derivation was found problematic in that the implied form would become: "do you dislike anything except our faith and the wickedness of most of them", whereas they do not admit that most of them are wicked, so as to dislike it. It was answered: al-Zamakhsharī and others answered that the meaning is: "you resent nothing in us except the combination of our faith and your rebellion and your departure from faith"; as if it were said: "you disapprove of nothing in us except your opposition, in that we entered the religion of Islam while you are outside it."
al-Wāḥidī transmitted from some of them that this belongs to the category of correspondence and pairing (muqābala and izdiwāj); he means that when the Jews resented their faith in all the messengers, which is not a thing to be resented, He mentioned in contrast to it their wickedness, which is a thing to be resented; and the like of this is good in pairing. The speaker says: «هل تنقم مني إلا أني عَفَوْتُ عنك وأنك فاجر» ("do you resent anything in me except that I pardoned you and that you are a wrongdoer?"), and this is good for completing the meaning by correspondence. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning on this view is: you disliked our faith and your abstaining, i.e. you disliked our differing from you; and this is like your saying to a man: «ما كرهتَ مني إلا أني مُحَبِّبٌ للناس وأنك مُبْغَضٌ»" ("you dislike nothing in me except that I am endearing to people and you are hated"), even though he does not admit that he is hated.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «{وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ} is, according to most of the interpreters, conjoined to His saying {أَنْ آمَنَّا}, so that their being wicked is included in what they resent; and this has no tenable meaning.» Then he said after some discussion: «It is tenable only on the basis that the meaning of the dialogue is: do you resent anything in us except the totality of this situation, that we are believers and you are wicked; and {وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ} would be among what the speaker establishes for them. This is as you say to someone in dispute: "Do you resent anything in me except that I told the truth and you lied?", while he does not admit that he is a liar and does not resent that; but the meaning of your speech is: do you resent anything except the totality of this situation.» This is the sum of what al-Zamakhsharī and al-Wāḥidī answered.
The second angle of the accusative: that it is also conjoined to «أن آمنَّا», but there is an omitted muḍāf in the speech for the soundness of the meaning, its implied form being «واعتقادَ أن أكثركم فاسقون» ("and the belief that most of you are wicked"), which is a clear meaning, for the disbelievers do resent the believers' belief that they are wicked. The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "do you resent anything in us except faith, and you do not resent the wickedness of most of you." The fourth: that it is accusative as accompaniment (maʿiyya), the wāw being in the sense of «مع»; its implied form: "you resent nothing in us except faith, while most of you are wicked." Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī mentioned all of these angles. The fifth: that it is accusative by being conjoined to «أنْ آمنَّا», and «أن آمنَّا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) and so accusative, and this was conjoined to it; the original being: "do you resent anything except on account of our faith and on account of the wickedness of most of them." When the preposition was dropped from «أن آمنَّا» it remained accusative on one of the two well-known views; except that here it is said: the accusative is impossible because a condition of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi is missing, namely the sameness of the agent, and the agent here differs, for the agent of resenting is not the agent of believing; so the position of «أن آمنَّا» should be implied as genitive only, after the preposition's omission, and the well-known disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh about the position of «أنْ» when the preposition is dropped from it does not apply, for lack of sameness of agent. It was answered that although we make sameness of the agent a condition, we allow the belief in the accusative for «أَنْ» and «أَنَّ» when they occur as mafʿūl li-ajlihi after the preposition's omission, not because they are mafʿūl li-ajlihi, but because of their particularity, as such, of permitting the omission of the preposition owing to their length through the ṣila; and in this particular question there is a disagreement mentioned in its chapter. What indicates this is what al-Wāḥidī reported from the author of al-Naẓm; the author of al-Naẓm mentioned from al-Zajjāj a meaning, namely: "do you dislike anything except our faith and your wickedness", i.e. you disliked our faith while you know that we are on the truth, because you became wicked by remaining in your religion; and this is the meaning of al-Ḥasan's saying. On this basis the place of «أَنَّ» in His saying {وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ} must be accusative by the implying of the lām, in the interpretation «ولأنَّ أكثرَكم», the wāw being redundant (zāʾida); the author of al-Naẓm has stated explicitly what I have mentioned.
The sixth angle: that it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi of «تنقِمون», the wāw being redundant, as its statement has preceded. [Translator's note: the text says next "this fifth angle requires clarification so that its meaning be understood"; as written it follows the sixth angle, and the numbering in the source is kept as is.] The Shaykh said after mentioning what I have transmitted of the preceding angles from al-Zamakhsharī: "An eighth angle appears, and it may be the most preferable. It is that «نَقَم» originally is made transitive by «على»; you say «نَقَمت عليه»; then you build from it iftaʿala, and in that case it is with «من» and is made to imply the meaning of inflicting something disliked. He, the Exalted, said: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95]. What suits the implication in it is that whoever finds fault with a person's deed dislikes it and inflicts upon him something disliked on account of it. So here faʿala comes in the sense of iftaʿala, like «قَدَرَ» and «اقتدر»; therefore it was made transitive by «مِنْ» and not by «على», by which it should originally be made transitive. So the meaning becomes: you do not attain from us and do not inflict on us anything we dislike except that we believed, i.e. except because we believed." So «ان آمنَّا» would be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and «وأنَّ أكثركم فاسقون» would be conjoined to this reason; and this, God knows best, is the reason it is made transitive by «مِنْ» and not «على». End of what he said. He did not state explicitly whether it is then in the position of the accusative or the genitive, but the apparent state of his position is that he holds it to be in the position of the genitive, since he mentioned only the genitive angles.
As for the genitive, it is from three angles. The first: that it is conjoined to what is believed in. al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e. you resent nothing in us except faith in Allah and in what was sent down, and in that most of you are wicked", and this is a clear meaning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This has a sound meaning, because the believers' faith that the People of the Book who persist in disbelief in Muḥammad ﷺ are wicked is among what they resent." The second: that it is genitive by being conjoined to an omitted reason, its implied form being: "you resent nothing in us except faith, owing to your lack of fairness, your wickedness and your following your desires"; and what indicates it is the interpretation of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: «بفسقكم نَقَمتم علينا» ("you resented us because of your wickedness"), and it is reported «لفسقهم نَقَموا علينا الإِيمان» ("because of their wickedness they resented our faith"). The third: that it is in the position of the genitive by being conjoined to the position of «أنْ آمنَّا» if we make it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi and hold that «أنَّ» is in the position of the genitive after the preposition's omission; what is in that has already preceded in the fifth angle.
Thus, in His saying, the Exalted, {وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ} there result eleven angles: two in the case of the nominative with regard to implying the khabar, whether it is implied as advanced obligatorily or optionally, and what is in it has preceded; six angles in the accusative; and three in the genitive. As for the reading of Ibn Maysara, its explanation is that it is resumptive: He informed that most of them are wicked. It may also be accusative in position, by being conjoined to the object of the saying: He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say to them "do you resent..." to the end, and to say to them "most of you are wicked"; and it is a clear and evident reading.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ}: its meaning is "one of the three", and for that reason the majority forbade putting what follows it in the accusative; you do not say "thālithun thalāthatan" nor "rābiʿun arbaʿatan". They said: because it is an active participle and works like its verb, and here no verb can stand in its place, since one does not say "rabbaʿtu l-arbaʿata" nor "thallathtu l-thalāthata"; and also because it is one of the three, so it would have to govern itself. Thaʿlab permitted the accusative in such a case, and the majority rejected him with what I have told you. But when it is not of the same wording as what follows it, both forms are permitted: the accusative and the genitive construct, such as "rābiʿu thalāthatan" and, if you wish, "thalāthatin". Know that from one to ten an active-participle form may be derived, such as "wāḥid", and it may be formed before that, so one says ḥādī, thānī, thālith up to ʿāshir. It may then be used on its own, so one says "thālith" and "rābiʿ", just as one says "thalātha" and "arbaʿa" without mentioning the thing counted; or it may be used in the manner of active participles if something different in wording follows it, and that is only what is one rank below it, such as "ʿāshiru tisʿatin" and "tāsiʿu thamāniyatin"; it is not combined with what is two ranks below, such as "ʿāshiru thamāniyatin" or "thāminu arbaʿatin", and it is not combined at all with what is above it, so one does not say "tāsiʿu ʿashratin" nor "rābiʿu sittatin". Once this is established, it is given the ruling of the active participle, so it governs only under its conditions. But when it is combined with a term agreeing with it in wording, its genitive construct is obligatory, as in "thālithu thalāthatin" and "thānī ithnayni", and Thaʿlab's disagreement has been mentioned. It may also be built from eleven to nineteen, so one says "ḥādī ʿashar" and "thālith ʿashar"; it may be used on its own as I mentioned to you; and it may be used together with another term, which must be only an agreeing one, so one says "ḥādī ʿashara aḥada ʿashara" and "thāliths ʿashara thalāthata ʿashara", and one does not say "thāliths ʿashara ithnay ʿashara", although some disagreed. The ruling for the feminine is like its ruling in the explicit adjectives, so one says "thālitha" and "rābiʿa", "ḥādiyata ʿashrata", and "thālithata ʿashrata thalātha ʿashrata". It has many rulings which I treated fully in "Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl".
His saying: {وَمَا مِنْ إله}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in the mubtadaʾ because of the presence of the two conditions, namely that the discourse is not affirmative and that what it governs is indefinite. «إلهٌ» is a badal (substitute) for the position of «إلهٍ» governed in the genitive by the all-inclusive «مِنْ», because its position is nominative, as mentioned before. The implied meaning: "there is no deity in existence except a deity characterized by oneness". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «مِنْ» in His saying «مِنْ إله» is for all-inclusiveness, and it is the one implied with the «لا» of generic negation in your saying "lā ilāha illā llāhu"; the meaning is: "there is no deity at all in existence except a deity characterized by oneness, and He is Allah the Exalted." From this it follows that «مِنْ إله» is the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, and «إلا إلهٌ» is a badal on the position. Makkī said: "In ordinary speech the accusative is permissible: «إلا إلهاً», as an exception." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been read in the genitive as a badal for the word «إله», it would have been permissible in Arabic." I say: it is not as he said, because it would require «مِنْ» to be redundant in an affirmative context, since the negation is broken by «إلاَّ»; if you said "mā qāma illā min rajulin" it would not be allowed, and so too here. That is allowed only on the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash, for the Kufans stipulate only the indefiniteness of what it governs, and al-Akhfash stipulates nothing.
Makkī said: "Al-Kisāʾī preferred the genitive as a badal for the word «إله», but it is remote because «مِنْ» is not made redundant in an affirmative context." I say: if someone held that His saying «إلا إلهٌ» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the matter being one of the emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), as if it were said "mā ilāhun illā ilāhun muttaṣifun bi-l-wāḥid" (there is no deity except a deity characterized by the One), no objection would appear to him; but I have not seen them say it. There is room for consideration in it.
His saying: {لَيَمَسَّنَّ} is the answer to an omitted oath, and the answer to the condition is omitted because this indicates it. The implied form: "By Allah, if they do not desist, there will surely touch ...". This came according to the rule I established: when a condition and an oath come together, the answer is given to whichever of the two comes first, unless something with a khabar precedes them; the condition is sometimes answered regardless; and it was also mentioned earlier that the verb of the condition in that case is only past in form, or in meaning and not form, as in this verse. If it is asked: the one that comes first here is the condition, since the oath is implied and so its implied position is later; the answer is that had the oath been intended to be later in implication, the condition would have been answered; when the oath was answered it was known that it is implied as being first. Some expressed this by saying: "The preparatory lām of the oath is sometimes omitted while its ruling is observed, as in this verse, for the implied form is «wa-la-in lam»", as is explicitly stated in other places, such as His saying: {لَّئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ المنافقون} [al-Aḥzāb: 60]. Parallel to this verse is His saying: {وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ} [al-Aʿrāf: 23] and {وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 121]. It was mentioned earlier that this type of oath-answer must be met with the lām and one of the two nūns according to the Basrans, except for what I excepted for you. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «layamassahum ʿadhābun»? I say: putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun has a benefit, namely repeating the testimony against them of disbelief."
His saying: {مِنْهُمْ} is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Either from «الذين» or from the pronoun of the agent in «كفروا»." I say: the ruling does not change in meaning, because the pronoun of the agent is the relative itself, and the difference is verbal only. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «مِنْ» in His saying {لَيَمَسَّنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ مِنْهُمْ} is explicative, like the one in His saying {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان} [al-Ḥajj: 30].
