I say: on this view «منهم» is attached to an omitted element. If you say: on making it a ḥāl it is also attached to an omitted element, I say: the difference between them is that on making it a ḥāl it is attached to an omitted element which is in reality the ḥāl, whereas on this view it is attached to a verb explaining the first relative, as if it were said "aʿnī minhum" (I mean from among them), and «aʿnī» has no grammatical position because it is an explicative clause. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "«مِنْ» in «منهم» is partitive, that is: being of them, and the link is achieved by the pronoun, as if it were said: their disbeliever; not all of them remained in disbelief." End of quotation. He means: this is an implication on its being partitive, and it amounts to its being in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَلاَ يَتُوبُونَ}: its parallel has been mentioned repeatedly, with two views on it: the view of the majority is that the conjunction is, in implication, placed before the hamza; and the view of Abū l-Qāsim (al-Zamakhsharī) is that it remains as it is and a clause is omitted to which it is joined, the implied form being: "Will they persist in their disbelief, and so not repent?" The interrogative here has two views. The more apparent: it expresses wonder at their state: how can they not repent and seek forgiveness for this hideous statement? The second: it has the meaning of a command, and this is the view of Ibn Ziyād al-Farrāʾ, as if He had said: "Repent and seek forgiveness for these two statements", like His saying: {فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُّنتَهُونَ} [al-Māʾida: 91]. Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words imply that it is for urging (taḥḍīḍ); he said: "He, glorious and exalted, was gentle with them by urging them to repent and to seek forgiveness", meaning that in terms of sense; otherwise, understanding urging from this wording is not conceded. How could it be conceived that the conjunction separated the hamza from the «لا» that conveys urging? If you say: this poses a difficulty only on our view that the urging «ألا» is simple, not compound, so separation by a conjunction is not claimed in it; but if we say it is the interrogative hamza that entered upon the negating «لا» and the two together came to mean urging, then separation by a conjunction does no harm, since it is established for the negating «لا» that the interrogative hamza enters upon it; the answer is: it is not permissible at all, because that meaning has been shed and another meaning has arisen, namely urging, and permissibility in the original does not entail permissibility after a new meaning arises.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّا المسيح ابن مَرْيَمَ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ}: like His saying: {وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ} [Āl ʿImrān: 144]. And «قد خَلَتْ» is an adjective of it, as in the other verse. The meaning of restriction (ḥaṣr) has been mentioned. His saying: {وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and this clause has no grammatical position. «صِدِّيقَةٌ» is the feminine of «صِدِّيق», which is a form of intensification like «فَعّال» and «فَعُول», except that it does not work as the forms of intensification work, so one does not say "Zaydun shirrību l-ʿasala" as one says "sharrābu l-ʿasala", though analogy requires that it work. Is it from the triliteral «صَدَق» or from the doubled «صَدَّق»? Analogy requires the first, because forms of intensification are regular from the triliteral and not from the quadriliteral, from which only few came. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from taṣdīq (affirming as true)", and so did Ibn ʿAṭiyya, except that he made it a possibility; and this is clear from His saying: {وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَاتِ رَبَّهَا}, where He made explicit the doubled verb attributed to her.
His saying: {كَانَا يَأْكُلاَنِ الطعام} has no position, because it is resumptive and an explanation that the two of them are like the rest of humanity in needing what every generated body needs, whereas the true God is exalted above that. Some said: "It is a metonymy for their need to relieve themselves", and there is no need for that. His saying «كيف» is accusative by «نُبَيِّن» after it, and what is in it was mentioned at His saying {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28] and elsewhere; it cannot be governed by what precedes it, because it has the head of the sentence. This interrogative clause is in the position of accusative because it suspends (muʿallaqa) the verb before it. His saying: {ثُمَّ انظر أنى يُؤْفَكُونَ} is like the clause before it; «أَنَّى» means "how", «يُؤْفكون» governs «أنَّى», and «يُؤْفكون» means "are turned away".

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَا لاَ يَمْلِكُ}: «ما» may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which), or an indefinite noun that is described; the clause after it is then either a ṣila (relative clause), having no grammatical position, or an adjective, whose position is accusative. As for «ما» being applied to rational beings here, because Jesus and his mother are meant, there are several explanations. One: «ما» was used with a rational being intended because it is vague and applies to everything; so said Sībawayh. Or the kind was intended, as in His saying {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3], that is: the good kind. Or the rational together with the non-rational was intended, because most of what was worshipped besides [Allah] is non-rational, such as idols, statues, stars and trees; or [it applies to him because] he resembles it in his first state, since in his first state he is not described as having intellect, so how could he be taken as a god to be worshipped? In the repetition of the command in His saying «انظُرْ» ... «ثم انظر» there is an indication of the importance of looking; moreover the objects of the two lookings differ: the first is a command to look at how Allah the Exalted clarified and explained the signs to them so that there is no doubt or suspicion in them, and the second command is to look at how they were turned away from reflecting on them and believing in them, or at their being overturned from what was intended for them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of the delay (tarākhī) in His saying «ثم انظر»? I say: its meaning is what lies between the two wonders; he means that He explained the signs to them in a wondrous way, and that their turning away from them is more wondrous than that." End of quotation. He means that it is a matter of delay in rank, not in time, and similar is {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 1], which will come.
His saying: {والله هُوَ السميع العليم}: «هو» may be a second mubtadaʾ, with «السميعُ» its khabar and «العليمُ» a second khabar or an adjective, the clause being the khabar of the first; it may be a separating pronoun (faṣl), the details of which are known; and it may be a badal. The apparent view about this clause is that it has no grammatical position, but it is possible that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَعْبُدون», that is: "Do you worship other than Allah, when Allah is the one who deserves worship because He hears everything and knows it?" Al-Zamakhsharī's words tend to this, for he said: {والله هُوَ السميع العليم} is attached to «أتعبدون», that is: "Do you associate partners with Allah and not fear Him, when He is the one who hears what you say and knows what you believe? Do you worship the helpless when Allah is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing?" End of quotation. The link between the ḥāl and its owner is the wāw. The coming of these two attributes after this statement is perfectly fitting, for the All-Hearing hears what is complained to Him of harm and the request for benefit, and knows where both fall and how they come about.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {غَيْرَ الحق}: there are five aspects in it. The first: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "do not exceed bounds in your religion with an excess other than the truth", that is, a false excess; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the agent in «تَغْلُوا», that is: "do not exceed bounds, transgressing the truth"; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The third: it is a ḥāl from «دينكم», that is: "do not exceed bounds in it while it is false, but do exceed bounds in it while it is true"; this is supported by what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "Because excess in religion is of two kinds: a true one, which is to investigate its realities, to search into its remotest meanings, and to strive to attain its proofs; and a false excess, which is to overstep the truth and pass beyond it by turning away from the evidence." The fourth: it is accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). The fifth: as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) reported these two aspects from others and considered them remote, saying: "Furthest is the one who held that it is a connected exception, and the one who held that it is a disconnected exception and implies it as «lākin al-ḥaqqa fa-ttabiʿūhu» (but the truth, so follow it)." I say: the excepted-from is hard to specify; what appears is that it is His saying {فِي دِينِكُمْ}, as though it were said: "do not exceed bounds in your religion, except the true religion, for excess in it is permitted to you", and the meaning of excess in it is what was given in al-Zamakhsharī's explanation.
Al-Wāḥidī mentioned for it the ḥāl and the exception, saying: "The accusative of «غيرَ الحق» is in two ways. One: ḥāl and cutting off (qaṭʿ) from «الدين», as if it were said: 'do not exceed bounds in your religion, being in opposition to the truth', because they opposed the truth in their religion and then exceeded bounds in it by insisting upon it. The second: that it be accusative as an exception, so «الحق» is excepted from what is forbidden to be exceeded in, such that excess in what is true is permitted, in the sense of following it and holding firm to it." This is explicit in what I told you, that the excepted-from is «دينُكم».
The meaning of excess (ghuluww) was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. The apparent sense of these earlier analyses is that «تَغْلُوا» is an intransitive verb, and Abū l-Baqāʾ stated so explicitly; however the lexicographers explain it with a transitive meaning, for they said: its meaning is "do not exceed the limit". Al-Rāghib said: "Ghuluww is exceeding the limit. It is said when it concerns price: «ghalāʾ»; when it concerns measure and rank: «ghuluww»; and of an arrow: «ghalw»; and their verbs are all «ghalā, yaghlū»." On this basis «غير الحق» may be accusative as a direct object, that is: "do not exceed in your religion anything other than the truth". If we explain «تغلوا» as meaning "go far", from their saying «ghalā l-sahmu» (the arrow went far), it would be intransitive; so the one who said it is intransitive may have taken it from this and not from the first.
His saying: {كَثِيراً}: there are two aspects for its accusative. One: it is a direct object, and this is the view of most of the interpreters, who explain it as: "and they led many of them astray", or of the hypocrites. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar, that is, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "leading astray much"; and on this the object is omitted, that is: "they led others astray with much leading astray."

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن بني إِسْرَائِيلَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; its owner is either «الذين» or the wāw of «كفروا», and they are one in meaning. His saying: {على لِسَانِ دَاوُودَ وَعِيسَى}: what is meant by "tongue" is the organ, not the language; so said the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), meaning that the one pronouncing the cursing of these people is the tongue of these two prophets. The phrase «على لِسَانِ» came in the singular rather than the dual or plural, and he did not say «على لسانَيْ» nor «على ألسنةِ», because of a general rule, which is: whenever two parts, each single in its owner, are annexed to both of the owners without distinction, three forms are allowed for them: the plural wording, which is the preferred, followed by the dual according to some; and according to others the singular takes precedence over the dual. So one says "qaṭaʿtu ruʾūsa l-kabshayni" and, if you wish, "raʾsayi l-kabshayni", and, if you wish, "raʾsa l-kabshayni"; and from this is {فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا} [al-Taḥrīm: 4]. My saying "two parts" excludes two things that are not parts, like "dirhamikumā"; yet it has occurred: "min buyūtikumā wa-ʿamāʾimikumā wa-asyāfikumā" because there is no risk of confusion. My saying "single" excludes such as "the two eyes and the two hands"; as for His saying {فاقطعوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا} [al-Māʾida: 38], it is understood by consensus. And my saying "without distinction" excludes such as "I cut the heads of the two rams, the fat one and the lean ram", and this verse is of that kind, so only the singular is permissible. Some said: "and it is the preferred", that is, another is permissible. The verification of this rule was given in Sūrat al-Māʾida at length, so refer to it.
In my mind there is something about the organ being what is meant by "tongue", and this is supported by what al-Zamakhsharī said: "Allah sent down their cursing in the Zabūr on the tongue of Dāwūd and in the Injīl on the tongue of ʿĪsā", and the force of this refuses its being the organ. Then I saw that al-Wāḥidī mentioned two views from the commentators and preferred what I said. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means in the Zabūr and in the Injīl; the meaning is that Allah the Exalted cursed in the Zabūr whoever disbelieves among the Children of Israel, and likewise in the Injīl. It was also said: «on the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā» because the Zabūr is the tongue of Dāwūd and the Injīl is the tongue of ʿĪsā." This is explicit that what is meant by "tongue" is other than the organ. Then he said: "Al-Zajjāj said: it is possible that Dāwūd and ʿĪsā knew that Muḥammad is a prophet sent, and that they cursed whoever disbelieves in him." The view is the first; so al-Zajjāj's allowing that makes apparent that the organ is meant by "tongue", but this is not a view of the commentators. «على لسانِ» is attached to «لعن». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "as one says: «jāʾa Zaydun ʿalā farasin»." There is room for consideration in it, since the apparent sense is that it is a ḥāl. His saying «ذلك بما عَصَوْا» has had its parallel mentioned before. His saying {وَّكَانُواْ يَعْتَدُونَ}: in this defective clause there are two aspects, the more apparent being that it is joined to the ṣila of «ما», namely «عَصَوْا», that is: "that is because of their disobedience and their being transgressors". The second: it is resumptive, that is: Allah the Exalted informed about them of that. The Shaykh said: "What supports this is what comes after it as an elaboration of it, namely His saying {كَانُواْ لاَ يَتَنَاهَوْنَ}."

semin-durr:79-79.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {عَن مُّنكَرٍ فَعَلُوهُ}: attached to «يَتَناهَوْن», and «فعلوه» is an adjective of «منكر». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What is the meaning of describing the wrongdoing with «they did it», when prohibition does not come after the deed? I say: its meaning is that they did not forbid one another repeating a wrongdoing they had done, or a wrongdoing like one they had done, or a wrongdoing they intended to do, as you see the signs of plunging into immorality and its instruments being levelled and prepared. It is also possible that the meaning is: they do not desist and do not refrain from a wrongdoing they have done, but persist in it and continue. One says: «tanāhā ʿani l-amri» and «intahā ʿanhu» when he refrained from it."

semin-durr:80-80.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {لَبِئْسَ مَا}: and «بئسما قَدَّمَتْ»: the i'rab of its parallel has been given before, so there is no need to repeat it; here there is something further, because of the particularity of the construction, and you will learn it. His saying: {أَن سَخِطَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ}: there are several aspects for its position. The first: it is nominative as a badal (substitute) for the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), the makhṣūṣ having been omitted and its adjective set in its place; for «ما» is parsed as a complete, definite noun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of the verb of blame, the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm being omitted, and «قَدَّمت لهم انفُسُهم» is a clause in the position of nominative as an adjective of it. The implied form: "How evil is the thing, a thing their souls have sent forward for them"; so «أَنْ سَخِط اللهُ عليهم» is a badal for the omitted «thing». This is the school of Sībawayh, as its explanation preceded. The second: it is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm, and then the three well-known aspects apply. One: it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause before it is its khabar, the link on this view being generality according to those who make it so, or no link being needed because the clause is identical with the mubtadaʾ. Two: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, because when you say "biʾsa l-rajulu" you are asked: who is he? and you say: so-and-so, that is: he is so-and-so. Three: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the treatment of that has already been given. A group, such as al-Zamakhsharī, held that it is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm, and he mentioned nothing else; he said: {أَن سَخِطَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ} is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm, as if it were said: "How evil is their provision for the Hereafter: Allah's wrath against them", the meaning being: "what causes Allah's wrath". I say: in implying this muḍāf there are merits that are not hidden from one who reflects on it, for the very wrath attributed to the Creator, the Exalted, is not said to be the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm; rather what is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm is its causes. Al-Wāḥidī, Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ also held this, except that the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), after reporting this aspect from Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī, said: "This i'rab is sound only on the school of al-Farrāʾ and al-Fārisī in making «ما» a relative, or on the school of one who makes «ما» a tamyīz (specification) with «قَدَّمَتْ لهم» as its adjective; as for the school of Sībawayh, it cannot work." Then he mentioned Sībawayh's school.
The third aspect of «أَنْ سَخِطَ»: it is in the position of nominative as a badal for «ما», and Makkī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this, except that Makkī reported it from others, saying: "It was said: in the position of nominative as a badal for «ما» in «لبئس», on the view that it is definite." The Shaykh said, after reporting this aspect from Ibn ʿAṭiyya: "This is not sound, whether «ما» is complete or relative, because the badal takes the place of what it substitutes, and «أَنْ سَخِطَ» cannot be the fāʿil of «بِئْسَ», since the fāʿil of «بِئْس» is not «أَنْ» plus the verb." It is a clear objection as he said.
The fourth aspect: it is in the position of accusative as a badal for «ما» when it is said to be a tamyīz; Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. This is not permissible at all, because the condition of tamyīz according to the Basrans is that it be indefinite, and «أَنْ» with what is in its scope is, for them, among the most definite of definites because it resembles the pronoun, as its explanation has preceded; how, then, can it be a tamyīz, since the badal takes the place of what it substitutes? For the Kufans too this is not permissible, because they do not permit tamyīz with any definite, especially «أَنْ» plus the verb. The fifth: it is in the position of accusative as a badal for the pronoun governed in the accusative by «قَدَّمَتْ», which refers to «ما», whether relative or described, according to what has preceded; the implied form: "qaddamat-hu sukhṭa llāhi", like your saying "alladhī raʾaytu Zaydan akhūka" (the one I saw, Zayd, is your brother); there is a discussion of this in its place. The sixth: it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, as the implied form is «li-an sakhiṭa»; this follows the school of Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, because both claim that the position of «أَنْ» after the removal of the preposition is accusative. The seventh: it is in the position of genitive by that implied preposition; this follows the school of al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī, because both claim that the two are in the position of genitive, and this has been verified more than once. On this, the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm is omitted, that is: "How evil is what their souls have sent forward for them, their deed or their doing"; and the implied lām of cause is attached either to the clause of blame, that is: "the cause of their blame is Allah's wrath against them", or to an omitted element after it, that is: "because Allah's wrath came upon them, it was such-and-such (kayta wa-kayta)".

semin-durr:81-81.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ كَانُوا}: the apparent sense is that the noun of «كان» and the agent of «اتخذوهم» refer to «كثيراً» in His saying {ترى كَثِيراً مِّنْهُمْ}, and the accusative pronoun in «اتِّخذوهم» refers to «الذين كفروا» in His saying {يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الذين كَفَرُواْ}. Al-Qaffāl permitted that the noun of «كان» refer to «الذين كفروا», and likewise the accusative pronoun in «اتِّخذوهم», while the nominative pronoun in «اتخذوهم» refers to the Jews, and the Prophet meant is Muḥammad ﷺ; the implied meaning being: "had the disbelievers whom they befriend believed in Muḥammad and the Qurʾān, these Jews would not have taken them as allies". The first is preferable because the discourse is about "many" and not about the two befriended parties. The answer of «لو» here came in the most eloquent form, namely the lām not entering upon it because it is negated; similar is the saying of the other poet:
178 - 9- لو أنَّ بالعلمِ تُعْطَى ما تعيشُ به ... لَمَا ظَفِرْت من الدنيا بثُفْرُوْقِ
(Had you been given by knowledge what you live on, you would not have gained from the world even a date-stalk's cap.) [Translator's note: as printed, the second hemistich carries the lām «لَمَا» although the commentator presents the verse as an example of the answer without the lām; the text is translated as it stands.]
«ترى» may be from seeing with the eye, in which case those meant are contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; or it may be the knowing one, in which case the "many" are their predecessors, so the meaning of «ترى» is "you know their reports and stories through our informing you". On the first, His saying «يَتَولَّون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; on the second, it is in the position of accusative as the second object. His saying: {ولكن كَثِيراً مِّنْهُمْ}: this istidrāk (rectification) is clear from what has preceded. His saying «كثيراً» is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, because it stands for «كثيراً منهم» mentioned earlier, as though it were said: "you see many of them, but that many"; it does not mean "but many of that many are ungodly".

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ}: concerning the one addressed in «أنبئِّكُم» there are two views. The first, which most of the exegetes know no other than: that the People of the Book, whose mention has preceded, are meant. The second: that it is for the believers. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The exegetes proceeded in this verse on the basis that those to whom he was commanded to say «هل أنبئِّكم» are the Jews and the disbelievers who take our religion as mockery and sport; al-Ṭabarī said that, and he did not trace anything about it to an earlier authority; but the verse admits that the address is to the believers." End. On the view that it is addressed to the believers it is clear, and the comparative form (afʿal al-tafḍīl), I mean «بشرّ», is in its normal sense, for the implied form becomes: "Say: shall I inform you, O believers, of something worse than the condition of these wicked ones? Those are their predecessors whom Allah cursed", the reference by «ذلك» being to their condition. So Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied it; and he implied a muḍāf, namely «حال», so that the meaning is sound, since «ذلك» points to a singular; had it come without omitting a muḍāf it would have been said «بشرٍّ من أولئكم» in the plural. al-Zamakhsharī said: «"ذلك" points to the thing resented, and an omitted muḍāf is necessary before it or before «من»; its implied form: "worse than the people of that", or "the religion of him whom [Allah] cursed".» End. It is also permissible not to imply any omitted muḍāf, neither before nor after, and that is according to the dialect of those who point to the singular, the dual and the plural, masculine and feminine, with the demonstrative of the masculine singular; «ذلك» would then point to the persons mentioned before, who are the People of the Book, as if it were said «بشرٍّ من أولئك»; he means that the predecessors, who have it, are worse than the successors; and on this basis His saying {مَن لَّعَنَهُ} comes as an explanation of «ذلك» itself. But if it is the pronoun of the People of the Book, which is the view of the general body of exegetes, it is problematic and needs an answer.
The point of the problem is that the implied form becomes: "Shall I inform you, O People of the Book, of something worse than that", where «ذلك» is meant to be the thing resented, namely faith; and it is known that there is no evil at all in the religion of Islam. People have answered it. al-Zamakhsharī gave a statement by which he established the preceding problem, and he answered it, after saying: "If you say: recompense (mathūba) is specific to good-doing, so how did it fall on wrong-doing? I say: it was put in the place of punishment, so it is like the saying of the poet:
174 - 9- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... (their greeting to one another is a painful blow)
and of it is {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 21]." And the statement I mentioned to you is that he said: "If you say: those punished of the two groups are the Jews, so why were they made partners with them in the punishment? I say: the Jews, may they be cursed, claimed that the Muslims were astray and deserving of punishment, so it was said to them: he whom Allah cursed is worse in punishment, in truth and certainty, than the people of Islam in your claim and your contention." In his statement there is some connection, namely his saying "so why were they made partners with them", i.e. between the Jews and the believers; and his saying "of the two groups", by which he means the People of the Book addressed by «أنبِّئكم» and him whom Allah cursed and was angry with; and his saying "in the punishment", i.e. the one in whose place the recompense fell, so he explained it by the original sense; and others explained the recompense here as the return to Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection; and a benefit follows from the two explanations, which will appear to you shortly.
«مثوبةً» is accusative as tamyīz (specification), and its specified word is «شَرٌّ». Its derivation and pattern were discussed in al-Baqara, so refer to that. His saying {عِندَ الله} has two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «مَثُوبة» itself if we say it means "return", because you say «رَجَعْتُ عنده»; the "nearness" (ʿindiyya) here is figurative. The second: that it is attached to an omitted word because it is an adjective of «مثوبة», and it is in the position of the accusative, if we say it is a pure noun and not in the sense of return but in the sense of punishment.
The majority read {أُنَبِّئكم} with shadda on the bāʾ, from «نَبَّأ»; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb read «أُنْبِئُكم» without it, from «أنبأ»; they are two eloquent dialects. The majority also read «مَثُوبة» with ḍamma on the thāʾ and sukūn on the wāw; al-Aʿraj, Ibn Buraida, Nubayḥ and Ibn ʿImrān read «مَثْوبة» with sukūn on the thāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw; Ibn Jinnī counted it among the irregular forms, like their saying «فاكهة مَقْوَدَةٌ للأذى» with sukūn on the qāf and fatḥa on the wāw; he means that it was due that the vowel of the wāw be transferred to the quiescent letter before it and the wāw be turned into alif, so that «مثابة» and «مَقادة» would be said, as «مَقام» is said, whose original is «مَقْوَم».
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن لَّعَنَهُ}: concerning the position of «مَنْ» there are four possibilities. The first: that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هو مَنْ لعنه الله»; and Makkī implied an omitted muḍāf before it, saying: "its implied form is: the cursing of him whom Allah cursed." Then he said: It was also said: «مَنْ» is in the position of the genitive as a badal from «بشرّ», a badal of the thing from the thing, being the same thing. He ought to have implied an omitted muḍāf in this possibility too, as he implied it in the nominative case, because if he makes «شراً» refer to an abstract meaning, the implying is required in both places, and if he makes it refer to persons, he is required not to imply in either place. The second: that it is in the position of the genitive, as the explanation from Makkī has preceded. The third: that it is in the position of the accusative as a badal from the position of «بشر». The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb indicated by «أُنَبِّئكم», its implied form being «أُعَرِّفكم مَنْ لعنه الله» ("I shall make known to you him whom Allah cursed"); Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. «مَنْ» may be a relative, which is the apparent sense, or an indefinite noun with a description. On the first, the clause after it has no position; on the second it has a position according to what is judged for «مَنْ» by one of the preceding possibilities. He took it into account first by its form in "لعنه" and "عليه", then by its meaning in {مِنْهُمُ القردة}, then by its form in {وَعَبَدَ الطاغوت}, then by its form in {أولئك}; thus he combined four times of reference to it.
«جَعَل» here is in the sense of «صَيَّر» ("made into"), so «منهم» is in the position of the accusative as the second object, advanced before the first, attached to an omitted word, i.e. "He made the apes and the swine to be of them"; and al-Fārisī, in his book al-Ḥujja, made it in the sense of "created." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This from him, may Allah have mercy on him, is a Muʿtazilī inclination, because His saying {وَعَبَدَ الطاغوت} is implied as «ومَنْ عبد الطاغوت», and the Muʿtazila do not hold that Allah the Exalted makes anyone a worshipper of idols." End. What is fled from in "making into" is itself present in "creating", and the discussion of it has a place other than this, which I have dealt with in the great exegesis. The Shaykh made His saying, the Exalted, «مَنْ لعنَه الله» to the end a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, as an alert to the description by which their being worse in recompense came about, as if it were said: "Say: shall I inform you of something worse than that in recompense with Allah? You", i.e. they are you; and what indicates this meaning is His saying after it: {وَإِذَا جَآءُوكُمْ قالوا آمَنَّا}, so the pronoun is one; and he held that this is what the eloquence of the speech requires. Ubayy b. Kaʿb and ʿAbdullāh b. Masʿūd read: «مَنْ غَضِب الله عليهم وجعلَهم قردةً», which is clear.
His saying: {وَعَبَدَ الطاغوت}: in this verse there are twenty-four readings, two of them among the seven. They are «وعَبَد الطاغوتَ», where «عَبَد» is a past active verb with a pronoun in it returning to «مَنْ», as has preceded; this is the reading of the majority of the seven except Ḥamza. The second: «وعَبُدَ الطاغوتِ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ, fatḥa on the dāl and genitive on «الطاغوت»; it is the reading of Ḥamza, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb. Its explanation, as al-Fārisī said, is that «عَبُداً» is a singular meant for plurality, like His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَتَ الله لاَ تُحْصُوهَا} [Ibrāhīm: 34]; it is not the plural of «عبد», because there is among the plural patterns nothing like it. He said: "It has come on faʿul because that is a pattern meant for plurality and exaggeration, as in yaqiẓ and nadus, as if he had gone to every extreme in the worship of the Ṭāghūt." al-Zamakhsharī also answered with this meaning. He, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: "Its meaning is excess in servitude, like their saying «رجل حَذُر وفَطُن» for the one extreme in caution and sagacity", and he cited the verse of Ṭarafa:
175 - 0- أبني لُبَيْنَى إنَّ أمَّكُمُ ... أَمَةٌ، وإنَّ أباكُمُ عَبُدُ
(O sons of Lubayna, your mother is a slave-woman, and your father is an utter slave.)
Abū Isḥāq and Abū Bakr b. al-Anbārī preceded them both in this explanation. Abū Bakr said: "The bāʾ was given ḍamma for exaggeration, as they say «فَطُن» for the sagacious and «حَذُر» for the cautious; they give ḍamma to the middle letter for exaggeration. Aws b. Ḥajar said:
- أبني لُبَيْنَى إنَّ أُمَّكُمُ ... أَمَةٌ، وإنَّ أباكُمُ عَبُدُ
(the same verse)
so he gave the bāʾ a ḍamma." I say: he thus attributed the verse to Ibn Ḥajar [sic], but I have already stated that it is by Ṭarafa; among those who attributed it to Ṭarafa is the Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma. Abū Isḥāq said: "The explanation of Ḥamza's reading is that the noun is built on faʿul as you say «رجلٌ حَذُر», and its interpretation is that he is exaggerated in caution; so the interpretation of «عَبُد» is that he reached the utmost in obeying Satan, and it is as if this word is one single word indicating plurality, as you say to a people «عَبُد العَصا», meaning slaves of the stick." Abū ʿAlī took this and expanded it as I have mentioned from him, then said: "This pattern was permissible in «عَبْد» because it is originally an adjective, even if it has been used as nouns are used, which does not remove from it the ruling of the adjective, like al-abṭaḥ and al-abraq, used as nouns until they were pluralised as nouns in their saying abāriq and abāṭiḥ, like ajādil, plural of al-ajdal, and yet that did not remove from them the ruling of the adjective; what shows you that is that they made them diptotes, like aḥmar. And if «العبد» does not leave the adjective, there is no obstacle to building it on the pattern of adjectives, faʿul, like «يَقُظ»." I have elaborated the statement here because some people criticised this reading and ascribed to its reciter an error, such as al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, Abū ʿUbayd and Naṣīr al-Rāzī the grammarian, the companion of al-Kisāʾī. al-Farrāʾ said: "That is permissible only in the necessity of poetry", meaning the ḍamma on the bāʾ of «عَبُد», "but in the reading it is not." He also said: "If it is a dialect like ḥadhur and ʿajul, that is permissible and is a valid way; otherwise it is not permissible in the reading." al-Zajjāj said: "This reading is not the proper way, because «عَبُداً» is on faʿul and this is not among the patterns of the plural." Abū ʿUbayd said: "The meaning of «العَبُد» among them is only «الأعبُد», they mean the servants of the Ṭāghūt; and we have not found this to be authentic from any of the eloquent Arabs, that «العَبْد» is said as «عَبُد»; it is only «عَبْد» and «أَعْبُد»." Naṣīr al-Rāzī said: "This is an error on the part of the one who read it so; let him who read it so fear Allah, and let him ask the scholars about it until it is made clear to him that it is not permissible." I say: they have asked the scholars about that and found it sound in meaning, praise be to Allah the Exalted; and when a thing is transmitted by tawātur as Qurʾān, no attention is paid to the one who denies it, because there was hidden from him what was clear to others.
As for the irregular readings: Ubayy read «وعَبَدُوا» with the wāw of plurality, observing the meaning of «مَنْ»; it is clear. al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read, in the transmission of ʿAbbād, «وعَبْدَ الطاغوت» with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the dāl, sukūn on the bāʾ and accusative on the tāʾ of «الطاغوت». Ibn ʿAṭiyya derived it in two ways. One: that he intended «وعَبْداً الطاغوتَ», and dropped the tanwīn of «عبداً» because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in the verse:
175 - 1- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلا قليلا
(... nor one who remembers Allah except little.)
The second: that he intended «وعبَد» with fatḥa on the bāʾ as a past verb like the reading of the community, except that he put sukūn on the ʿayn in the manner in which another put sukūn on it in the verse:
175 - 2- وما كلُّ مغبونٍ ولو سَلْفَ صَفْقُهُ ... ... ... ... ...
(Not every one cheated, even if his bargain was earlier concluded ...)
with sukūn on the lām; and like it is the reading of Abū l-Sammāl: {ولُعْنوا بما قالوا} with sukūn on the ʿayn. I say: that is not like «لُعْنوا», because lightening a kasra is regular, unlike a fatḥa; and like «سَلْفَ» is the verse of another:
175 - 3- إنما شِعْريَ مِلْحٌ ... قد خُلْطَ بجُلْجُلانْ
(My poetry is only salt, mixed with sesame.)
in that he lightened the fatḥa. The Shaykh said, after relating the first derivation from Ibn ʿAṭiyya: "This derivation is not valid, because «عَبْداً» cannot govern «الطاغوت» in the accusative, as it is neither a maṣdar nor an active participle; the correct derivation is that it is a lightening of «عَبَدَ», like «سَلْف» for «سَلَفْ»." I say: had he mentioned both derivations from Ibn ʿAṭiyya and then objected to the first, it would have been fair, so that it not be imagined that the second derivation is his own. It may be said: «عَبْداً», because its wording carries the meaning of abasement and submission, indicates an omitted governor of the accusative for «الطاغوت», as if it were said: who worships this slave? and it was said: he worships the Ṭāghūt. And once it is established that the tanwīn of «عَبْد» was dropped, it is accusative by being conjoined to «القردة», i.e. "and He made of them a slave to the Ṭāghūt."
al-Ḥasan also read, in another transmission, like this reading, except that he put «الطاغوت» in the genitive; it is clear, for it is a singular meant for the genus, annexed to what follows. al-Aʿmash, al-Nakhaʿī and Abū Jaʿfar read «وعُبِد» as a passive, with «الطاغوتُ» nominative. ʿAbdullāh read likewise, except that he added to the verb the feminine tāʾ and read «وعُبِدَتِ الطاغوتُ»; and «الطاغوت» is used as masculine and feminine, He the Exalted said: {والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا} [al-Zumar: 17], and this has preceded in al-Baqara. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "al-Ṭabarī weakened this reading, but it is tenable", meaning the passive reading, and he did not state the point of weakness nor the explanation of the reading. The point of weakness is that the clause conjoined to the ṣila lacks a link tying it to the relative noun, since in «عُبِد الطاغوتُ» there is no pronoun returning to {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله}; if you said «أكرمت الذين أهنتُم وضُرِب زيدٌ», meaning that «وضُرِب» is conjoined to «أكرمت», it would not be permissible; so also this. As for its explanation, it is as Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī said: "The returning element is omitted, its implied form being «وعُبِد الطاغوتُ فيهم أو بينهم»" ("and the Ṭāghūt was worshipped among them").
Ibn Masʿūd, in the transmission of ʿAbd al-Ghaffār from ʿAlqama from him, read {وعَبُدَ الطاغوتُ} with fatḥa on the ʿayn, ḍamma on the bāʾ, fatḥa on the dāl and nominative «الطاغوت»; there are two derivations of it. One, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned: that being worshipped became for it like a habitual, well-known character or matter, so it is in the sense of faqiha, sharufa and ẓarufa. I say: he means by its being in their sense that jurisprudence and refinement became for it a habitual, well-known character; otherwise its meaning differs from the meanings of these verbs. The second, which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned: that it became worshipped besides Allah, like «أمُر», i.e. became an amīr; it is close to the first, although there is a subtle difference between them.
Ibn ʿAbbās, in the transmission of ʿIkrima from him, and Mujāhid and Yaḥyā b. Waththāb read: {وعُبُدَ الطاغوتِ} with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the bāʾ, fatḥa on the dāl and genitive «الطاغوت»; there are several views about it. One, the view of al-Akhfash: that «عُبُداً» is the plural of ʿabīd and ʿabīd is the plural of ʿabd, so it is a plural of a plural, and he cited:
175 - 4- أنسُبِ العبدَ إلى آبائِه ... أسودَ الجِلْدَةِ من قومٍ عُبُدْ
(Trace the slave to his fathers: black of skin, from a people of slaves.)
and al-Zamakhsharī followed him in that, meaning that ʿabīd, a plural, is in the position of raghīf as a singular, so it is pluralised as it is said raghīf and rughuf. The second, the view of Thaʿlab: that it is the plural of ʿābid, like shārif and shuruf, and he cited:
175 - 5- ألا يا حَمْزُ للشُّرُفِ النَّواءِ ... فهنَّ مُعَقِّلاتٌ بالفِناءِ
(O Ḥamza, [slaughter] for the old, fat she-camels; they are hobbled in the courtyard.)
The third: that it is the plural of ʿabd, like siqf and suqf, rahn and ruhun. The fourth: that it is the plural of ʿibād, and ʿibād is the plural of ʿabd, so it too is a plural of a plural like thimār, which is the plural of thamara and then is pluralised as thumur; this is because ʿibād and thimār, two plurals, are in the position of kitāb as a singular, and kitāb is pluralised as kutub; so likewise what is of its weight.
al-Aʿmash read «وعُبَّدَ» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, shadda on the bāʾ with fatḥa, and fatḥa on the dāl, «الطاغوت» in the genitive; it is the plural of ʿābid, like ḍurrab for the plural of ḍārib and khullaṣ for the plural of khāliṣ. Ibn Masʿūd also read, in the transmission of ʿAlqama: {وعُبَدَ الطاغوت} with ḍamma on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the bāʾ and the dāl, and «الطاغوتِ» genitive; its explanation is that it is a pattern of exaggeration like ḥuṭam and lubad, a singular generic noun meant for the plural, and the discussion of it is as for Ḥamza's reading, which has preceded.
Ibn Masʿūd also read, in the transmission of ʿAlqama: {وعُبَّدَ الطاغوتَ} with ḍamma on the ʿayn, shadda on the bāʾ with fatḥa, fatḥa on the dāl and accusative «الطاغوت»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya derived it as the plural of ʿābid, like ḍurrib for the plural of ḍārib, and he dropped the tanwīn of «عبدا» because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in the verse:
176 - 6- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلا قليلا
(... nor one who remembers Allah except little.)
He said: "Its like has already preceded", meaning the reading {وعَبْدَ الطاغوتَ} with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the dāl, sukūn on the bāʾ and accusative tāʾ, for which he mentioned two derivations, one this one, and the other of which is not possible, namely putting sukūn on the middle letter of the past verb. [Translator's note: the source numbers this verse 176 - 6, whereas the same verse appeared above as 175 - 1; the numbering is kept as it is in the source.] Burayda al-Aslamī, according to what Ibn Jarīr transmitted from him, read «وعابِد الشيطانِ» with accusative «عابد» and genitive «الشيطان» in place of «الطاغوت»; that is an explanation, not a reading. Abū Wāqid al-Aʿrābī read {وعُبَّاد} with ḍamma on the ʿayn, shadda on the bāʾ followed by an alif, and accusative dāl, and «الطاغوتِ» in the genitive; it is the plural of ʿābid, like ḍurrāb for ḍārib.
Some of the Basrans read «وعِبادَ الطاغوتِ» with kasra on the ʿayn, a lightened bāʾ followed by an alif, accusative dāl and genitive «الطاغوت». There are two views about it. One: that it is the plural of ʿābid, like qāʾim and qiyām, ṣāʾim and ṣiyām. The second: that it is the plural of ʿabd, and Sībawayh cited:
175 - 7- أتوعِدُني بقومِك يابنَ حَجْلٍ ... أُشاباتٍ يُخالُون العِبادَا
(Do you threaten me with your people, O son of Ḥajl, a rabble of mixed folk who are reckoned slaves?)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It may be the plural of «عَبْد», and rarely does «عِباد» come annexed to other than Allah the Exalted; and Sībawayh cited «أتُوْعِدُني», the verse. Abū l-Fatḥ said: he means the servants of Ādam, peace be upon him; and had he meant the servants of Allah, that would be nothing by which anyone is reviled, for all creation are servants of Allah." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This linking to Ādam is irregular and remote, and the objection remains; and this is not among what the poet imagined he intended; he meant only the slaves (ʿubayd) and the rhyme led him to «العباد», since it may be said of one whom someone owns in some way of ownership; and it has been mentioned that the Arabs of al-Ḥīra were called ʿibād because they entered obedience to Kisrā and his kingdom held them in subjection." I say: it has become well known on people's tongues that «عَبْد» annexed to Allah the Exalted is pluralised as «عِباد», and annexed to other than Him as «عبيد»; this is the general rule, and on it Abū Muḥammad built.
ʿAwn al-ʿUqaylī read, in the transmission of al-ʿAbbās b. al-Faḍl from him, «وعابِدُ الطاغوتِ» with ḍamma on the dāl and genitive «الطاغوت», like ḍāribu Zaydin. Abū ʿAmr said: its implied form is «وهم عابدُ الطاغوت». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "So it is a generic noun." I say: he means that he intended by «عابِد» a group. I say: it is possible that the origin of this reading is «وعابدو الطاغوت», the sound masculine plural of ʿābid, and when the wāw met the lām of definiteness it was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so the pronunciation became a dāl with ḍamma; and what supports this understanding is that Abū ʿAmr implied the mubtadaʾ as a plural, saying "its implied form: هم عابدو", unless they transmit from al-ʿUqaylī that he stated explicitly that his reading is in the singular, or heard him stopping at «عابد», or saw his codex with a dāl without a wāw; and then his reading would be like the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās: {وعابدو} with the wāw; and in sum the two readings are identical in wording, and the difference between them appears, according to what they said, only in pausal form or in writing.
Ibn ʿAbbās read, in another transmission of ʿIkrima, «وعابِدُوا» in the plural, and that has preceded. Ibn Burayda read «وعابد» with accusative dāl, like ḍāriba Zaydin, and it too is a singular meant for the genus. Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read: {وعَبَد الطاغوتِ} with fatḥa on the ʿayn, the bāʾ and the dāl and genitive «الطاغوت»; its derivation is that the original is «وعبدةَ الطاغوت», and fāʿil is pluralised as faʿala, like fājir and fajara, kāfir and kafara; so the feminine tāʾ was dropped because of the annexation, as in the verse:
175 - 8- قام وُلاها فسقَوْه صَرْخَدا
(Its governors rose and gave him Ṣarkhad wine to drink.)
i.e. wulātuhā, and as in the verse:
175 - 9- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... وأَخْلَفُوك عِدَ الأمرِ الذي وَعَدُوا
(... and they failed you in the promise of the matter they had promised.)
i.e. ʿidata l-amr; and of this is {وَإِقَامَ الصلاوة} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 73], i.e. iqāmati l-ṣalāt. It is also possible that «عَبَد» is a generic noun for ʿābid, like khādim and khadam, and in that case there is no dropping of the feminine tāʾ for annexation. It was also read «وعَبَدَة الطاغوت» with the tāʾ retained, which indicates the dropping of the tāʾ for annexation in the reading before it; its explanation has preceded, that fāʿil is pluralised as faʿala, like bārr and barara, fājir and fajara.
ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr read «وأعْبُد الطاغوت», the plural of ʿabd, like fals and aflus, kalb and aklub. Ibn ʿAbbās read «وعبيد الطاغوت», also the plural of ʿabd, like kalb and kulayb. He said [the poet]:
176 - 0- تَعَفَّق بالأَرْطَى لها وأرادَها ... رجالٌ فَبَذَّتْ نبلَهُمْ وكَلِيبُ
(He concealed himself among the arṭā trees for her, and men sought her, but she outstripped their arrows and Kulayb.)
It was also read «وعابدي الطاغوت». ʿAbdullāh b. Masʿūd read «ومَنْ عَبَدوا». These are twenty-four readings, and «وعابد الشيطان» should not have been counted among them because it is an explanation, not a reading. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Some of the transmitters said about this verse that it is a permission, not a reading", meaning that when the transmissions in this verse became numerous, some of them thought that it was said by way of permissibility and not that it was transmitted from anyone; this should not be said nor believed, for its people transmitted it only as readings which they recited to those from whom they learned; this is unlike «وعابد الشيطان», for it contradicts the noble written text.
The way of controlling the reading in this word, after the readers are known, is to say: seven readings with «عَبَد» as a past verb, namely: وعَبَد، وعَبَدُوا، ومَنْ عَبَدوا، وعُبِد، وعُبِدَت، وعَبُدَ، and وعَبْدَ, on our saying that the bāʾ was made quiescent for lightening like «سَلْفَ» for «سَلَف»; nine readings with it as a broken plural, namely: وعُبُدَ، وعُبَّد with the genitive «الطاغوت»، وعُبَّد with its accusative، وعُبَّاد، وعِباد، وعَبَدَ with the tāʾ dropped for annexation، وعَبَدَة، وأَعْبُد، وعبيد; six with the singular: وعَبُدَ، وعُبَدَ، وعابدَ الطاغوت، وعابدُ الطاغوت with ḍamma on the dāl، وعابد الشيطان، وعَبْدَ الطاغوت; and two with the sound plural: وعابِدوا with the wāw and وعابدي with the yāʾ. On the reading as a verb, two possibilities are permissible for the clause: one, that it is conjoined to the ṣila before it, the implied form being «مَنْ لعنَه الله وعَبَد الطاغوت»; the second, that it is not within the scope of the ṣila but is on the implying of «مَنْ», i.e. «ومَنْ عَبَد», and the reading of ʿAbdullāh with the overt «مَنْ» indicates it; except that this, as al-Wāḥidī said, leads to omitting the relative noun and leaving its ṣila, which is forbidden to the Basrans and permitted to the Kufans; all of this will come in His saying, the Exalted: {وقولوا آمَنَّا بالذي أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 46], i.e. «وبالذي أُنزل». On the broken-plural reading it is accusative, conjoined to «القردة والخنازير», i.e. "He made of them the apes, and ʿibād, ʿubbād and ʿubayd"; on the singular reading likewise; and the accusative is also possible in it from another angle, namely conjunction to «مَنْ» in {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله} if we say that it is accusative in the manner whose treatment has preceded, it being meant for the genus; and in some of them it is read in the nominative, such as «وعابدُ الطاغوت», and it has preceded that Abū ʿAmr implies a mubtadaʾ for it, i.e. «هم عابدُ», and what is in that has preceded; and in my view it may be nominative by being conjoined to «مَنْ» in His saying, the Exalted, {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله}, and what indicates that is that they allowed these two possibilities for the reading of ʿAbdullāh «وعابدُو» with the wāw; so this is like it.
As for the reading of the sound plural, whoever read it with the yāʾ, it is accusative by conjunction to «القردة», and two other possibilities are permissible for it: one, that it is accusative by conjunction to «مَنْ» in {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله} if we say that its position is accusative, as has passed; the second, that it is genitive, also by conjunction to {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله}, if we say that it is in the position of the genitive as a badal from «بشرِّ», as its clarification has preceded. These are clear possibilities, difficult to derive, and Allah knows best. And whoever read it with the wāw, his nominative is either on the implying of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم عابدُو الطاغوت», or a conjunction to «مَنْ» in His saying, the Exalted: {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله}, as has preceded.
His saying, the Exalted: {أولئك شَرٌّ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar; «مكاناً» is accusative as tamyīz; he attributed the evil to the place while it belongs to its people, as a metonymy for their extremity in that. «شرّ» here is in its normal comparative sense, and what it is compared with has two possibilities. One: that they are the believers; so it is said: how can that be said when the believers have no evil at all? It was answered with two answers. One, which al-Naḥḥās mentioned: that their place in the Hereafter is worse than the place of the believers in this world, because of the "evil" that befalls them in it, meaning worldly cares, need, hardship, hearing harm and being wronged at their hands. He said: "This is the best of what has been said about it." By my life he spoke truly, for the believer often meets harm and tastes of need every bitterness and gall. The second of the two answers: that it is by way of descent to the opponent's level and conceding to him his claim, as a compelling argument against him, as if it were said: worse than their place in your claim; this is close to correspondence (muqābala) in meaning. The second of the two possibilities: that what is compared with is a group of the disbelievers, i.e. those cursed ones, those who earned wrath, of whom apes and swine were made, the worshippers of the Ṭāghūt, are worse in place than others among the disbelievers who did not combine these blameworthy qualities.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ الناس}: the i'rab of this was given before, in such as His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ الناس على حياوة} [al-Baqara: 96], which makes repetition unnecessary. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement)", but that is nothing; rather it is the lām with which an oath is met. «أشدَّ الناس» is the first object, and «عداوةً» is accusative as tamyīz (specification). «للذين» is attached to it [to «عداوةً»], strengthened by the lām since it is secondary in governing to the verb; and its being feminine with tāʾ does no harm, because it is built upon it, so it is like his saying:
179 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . .
ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك. . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(... and fear of your punishment ...) [Translator's note: only this fragment of the verse is given in the source.]
«للذين» may also be an adjective of «عداوة», attached to an omitted element, with «اليهودَ» as the second object. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is possible that «اليهود» is the first and «أشدَّ» the second, and this is the apparent view, since the aim is that Allah the Exalted informs about the Jews and the polytheists that they are the most intense of people in enmity to the believers, and about the Christians that they are the nearest of people in affection to them; the aim is not to inform about the most intense and nearest of people as being of the Jews and Christians. If it is said: whenever the two are equal in definiteness and indefiniteness, the first object must come first and the second last, as is obligatory in the mubtadaʾ and khabar, and this is of that kind; the answer is: that is obligatory only where there is confusion; but when evidence indicates it, advancing and postponing are permitted, and from it is his saying:
179 - 1- بَنُونا بنو أبنائِنا، وبناتُنا ... بنوهُنَّ أبناءُ الرجالِ الأباعدِ
(Our sons are the sons of our sons, but our daughters' sons are the sons of distant men.)
Here «بنو أبنائنا» is the mubtadaʾ and «بَنُونا» is its khabar, because the meaning rests on likening the children of the sons to sons; and similar is the saying of the other:
179 - 2- قبيلةٌ ألأَمُ الأحياءِ أكرمُها ... وأَغْدُر الناسِ بالجيرانِ وافِيها
(A tribe: the most ignoble of the living is its noblest, and the most treacherous of people to neighbours is its most faithful.)
«أكرمُها» is the mubtadaʾ and «ألأمُ الأحياءِ» is its khabar; likewise «وافيها» is a mubtadaʾ and «أغدرُ الناس» its khabar, and the meaning rests on this; and the verse is of this kind in what I have told you."
His saying: {والذين أَشْرَكُواْ} is conjoined to «اليهود», and what is said of the second clause is as what is said of the one before it. «ذلك بأنَّ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and its explanation has preceded; «منهم» is the khabar of «أنَّ» and «قسيسين» is its noun; «أن» with its noun and khabar is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the bāʾ with its genitive noun here is the khabar of «ذلك». «القسيسين» is the plural of «قِسِّيس» on the pattern fiʿʿīl, which is a form of intensification like «صِدِّيق», as already mentioned; here it means the chief and worshipper of the Christians. Its origin is from «taqassasa l-shayʾa» when one follows it and seeks it by night; one says «taqassastu aṣwātahum», that is, I followed them by night. The chief of the Christians is called «qiss» and «qissīs», and the guide by night «qasqās» and «qasqas»; so said al-Rāghib. Another said: «al-qass», with fatḥa on the qāf, is following a thing, and from it the scholar of the Christians was named, for his pursuit of knowledge. Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj said:
179 - 3- أَصْبَحْنَ عن قَسِّ الأذى غَوافِلا ... يَمْشِين هَوْناً خُرُداً بَهالِلا
(They became heedless of the pursuit of harm, walking gently, bashful, noble.)
One says «qassa l-athara» and «qaṣṣahu» also with ṣād; and one says «qass» and «qiss», with fatḥa and kasra on the qāf, and «qissīs». Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed that it is non-Arabic, an Arabized loanword. Al-Wāḥidī said: "The Arabs have spoken of «al-qass» and «al-qissīs»," and al-Māzinī recited:
179 - 4- لو عَرَضَتْ لأيْبُلِيٍّ قَسِّ ... اشعثَ في هيكلهِ مُنْدَسِّ
(Had she appeared before an ʾAybulī [monk], a priest, disheveled, hidden in his temple,)
حَنَّ إليها كحنينِ الطَسِّ ...
(he would have yearned for her as the cup yearns ...)
and he recited from Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt:
179 - 5- لو كان مُنْفَلَتٌ كانت قساوسةٌ ... يُحْيِيهم الَّهُ في أَيْديهم الزُّبُرُ
(Had there been any escape, there would be priests whom Allah gives life, with the scriptures in their hands.)
This is the lexicographers' discussion of «al-qissīs». Then he said: "ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: «The Christians lost the Injīl and what is in it, and there remained of them a man called qissīs», meaning that he remained on his religion and did not change it; so whoever remained on His guidance and religion was called «qissīs». Quṭrub said: «al-qass» and «al-qissīs» is the scholar in the language of the Romans. Waraqa said:
179 - 6- لما خَبَّرْتَنا مِنْ قولِ قَسٍّ ... من الرهبانِ أكرُه أَنْ يَبُوحا
(When you told us of the words of a priest among the monks, which I dislike to be divulged.)
On this, «al-qass» and «al-qissīs» are among the words in which the two languages coincide." I say: this strengthens Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view. The lexicographers did not report for this word «al-quss», with ḍamma on the qāf, either as a maṣdar or as an adjective. As for Quss ibn Sāʿida al-Iyādī, it is a proper name, so it may be among what is changed by way of becoming a proper name, its origin being «qass» or «qiss» with fatḥa or kasra as Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported; Quss ibn Sāʿida was the most learned of the people of his time, and he is the one of whom he, peace be upon him, said: "He will be raised as a community by himself." As for the plural of «qissīs», it is a sound plural, as in the noble verse. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Had it been pluralized as «qusūs», it would have been right, because the two are of one meaning", meaning «qiss» and «qissīs». He said: "«Al-qissīs» is also pluralized as «qasāwisa»; they pluralized it on the pattern of «mahālaba», the original being «qasāsisa»; the sīns multiplied, so one of them was replaced by a wāw", and they recited Umayya's «لو كان مُنْفَلَتٌ كانت قساوسةٌ» (the verse). Al-Wāḥidī said: "«Al-qusūsa» is the maṣdar of «al-qiss» and «al-qissīs»." I say: it is as though he made this maṣdar derived from this noun, like «al-ubuwwa», «al-ukhuwwa» and «al-futuwwa» from the words «ab», «akh» and «fatā»; I had earlier mentioned that «al-qass» with fatḥa is originally the maṣdar and that the scholar was named by it for intensification; and I do not know what led the one who said it is Arabized to do so, given the existence of its meaning in the Arabs' language as you have learned from what preceded.
«الرُّهْبان» is the plural of «rāhib», like «rākib» and «rukbān», «fāris» and «fursān». Abū l-Haytham said: "«Ruhbān» may be singular and may be plural", and he recited, for its being singular, the poet's saying:
179 - 7- لو عايَنَتْ رهبانَ دَيْرٍ في القُلَلْ ... لأَقْبَلَ الرُّهبانُ يَعُدُوا ونَزَلْ
(Had she seen the monk of a monastery on the peaks, the monk would have come running and descended.)
Had it been a plural he would have said «yaʿdūna» and «nazalū», with the plural pronoun. But there is no proof in this, because a singular pronoun may return to an explicit plural when it is interpreted as one, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنعام لَعِبْرَةً نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ} [al-Naḥl: 66], where the hāʾ in «بطونه» refers to «الأنعام»; and he said:
179 - 8- وطابَ البانُ اللِّقاحِ وبَرَدْ
(And the milk of the milch camels became sweet and cold.)
where in «بَرَدْ» there is a pronoun that refers to «أَلْبان»; and they said: "He is the best of the youths and the most beautiful of him." And the other said:
179 - 9- لو أنَّ قوميَ حين أَدْعُوهمْ حَمَلْ ... على الجبالِ الشُّمِّ لانهدَّ الجَبَلْ
(Had my people, when I call them, been loaded onto the lofty mountains, the mountain would have collapsed.)
and other examples that would take long to mention. Among the instances of its coming as a plural is the verse, and in the noble Qurʾān it occurs only as a plural. Kuthayyir said:
180 - 0- رُهْبانُ مَدْيَنَ والذين عَهِدْتُهُمْ ... يبكون من حَذَرِ العقابِ قُعودا
(The monks of Madyan and those I knew, weeping, seated, from fear of punishment,)
لو يَسْمعون كما سَمِعْتُ كلامَها ... خَرُّوا لِعَزَّةَ رُكَّعاً وسُجودا
(had they heard her speech as I heard it, they would have fallen down for ʿAzza in bowing and prostration.)
It was said: there is no proof in this because he said «والذين», so it is possible that the pronoun was pluralized because of this plural and not because «ruhbān» is a plural. More explicit than this is Jarīr's saying:
180 - 1- رُهبانُ مَدْيَنَ لو رَأَوْكِ تَنَزَّلُوا ... والعُصْمُ مِنْ شَعَفِ العَقُولِ الفادِرِ
(The monks of Madyan, had they seen you, would have come down, and the mountain goats from the peak of the high refuge.)
Ibn al-Haytham [Translator's note: earlier cited as Abū l-Haytham; the source's text varies] said: "If the singular «ruhbān» is pluralized as «rahābīn» and «rahābina», it is permissible, and if you say «ruhbāniyyūn» it is right, as if you attributed it to monasticism (rahbāniyya); and «rahbāniyya» is from «rahba», which is fear." Al-Rāghib said: "«Ruhbān» may be singular or plural; whoever makes it singular pluralizes it as «rahābīn», and «rahābina» as a plural is more fitting", meaning that this pattern predominates in the plural, like «al-farāzina», «al-mawāzija» and «al-kayālija». Al-Layth said: "«Al-rahbāniyya» is the maṣdar of «al-rāhib», and «al-tarahhub» is devotion in a hermitage." This resembles the earlier discussion that «al-qaswasa» is a maṣdar of «al-qass» and «al-qissīs», and there is no need for this, since «al-rahbāniyya» is a maṣdar in itself, from «al-tarahhub», which is devotion, or from «al-rahab», which is fear; hence al-Rāghib said: "«Al-rahbāniyya» is the excess of one who undertakes devotion out of extreme fear." The derivation of this root was given at His saying {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40].
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ} is conjoined to the «أنَّ» governed in the genitive by the bāʾ, that is: "that is because of what preceded and because they are not arrogant."

semin-durr:83-83.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا سَمِعُواْ}: «إذا» is conditional, its answer being «تَرى», which is what governs it. This conditional clause has two aspects. The more apparent: its position is nominative, conjoined to the khabar of the second «أنَّهم», namely «لا يستكبرون», that is: "that is because some of them are such-and-such, and because they are not arrogant, and because, when they hear ..."; so the wāw joins a single term to its like. The second: the clause is resumptive, that is, the Exalted informed about them of that. The pronoun in «سمعوا» apparently refers to the Christians mentioned before, because of their generality; it was also said that it refers only to some of them, namely those who came from Abyssinia to the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "because not all Christians are like that."
«ما» in «ما أُنْزل» may be a relative or an indefinite noun that is described. «ترى» is of sight, so His saying «تَفيض من الدمع» is a clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
It was read irregularly «تُرى» in the passive, with «أعينُهم» in the nominative. Overflowing was attributed to the eyes for intensification, although what overflows is their tears and not they themselves, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
180 - 2- ففاضَتْ دموعُ العينِ مني صَبابةً ... على النَّحْرِ حتى بَلَّ دَمْعِيَ مَحْمِلي
(The tears of the eye overflowed from me out of longing onto the breast, until my tears wet my sword-strap.)
The intention is intensification in describing them as weeping; or the meaning is that their eyes fill until they overflow, because overflowing arises from filling, as in his saying:
180 - 3- قوارِصُ تأتيني وتَحْتَقِرُونها ... وقد يَمْلأَ الماءُ الإِناءَ فَيَفْعُمُ
(Stinging words come to me, which you belittle; yet water may fill a vessel until it brims over.)
Abū l-Qāsim tended to these two meanings, for he said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «تَفيض من الدمع»? I say: its meaning is that they fill with tears until they overflow, because overflowing is when the vessel fills until what is in it rises over its sides; so he put overflowing, which results from filling, in the place of filling, and this is putting the effect in the place of the cause; or you intend intensification in describing them as weeping, so you make their eyes as though they overflow of themselves, that is: they flow with tears because of weeping, as in your saying «damaʿat ʿaynuhu damʿan»."
«من الدمع» has four aspects. The first: it is attached to «تفيض», «مِنْ» having the meaning of the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), the meaning being: they overflow from the abundance of tears. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the agent in «تفيضُ»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said both, and he implied the ḥāl as "filled with tears". There is room for consideration in it, because that is a restricted being (kawn muqayyad), which is not permitted, so what remains is to imply an unrestricted being, i.e. "overflowing, being from tears", and the meaning is not that; so holding it to be a ḥāl is not fitting. If it is asked: is it permissible, according to the Kufans, that «من الدمع» be a tamyīz, since they do not stipulate the indefiniteness of the tamyīz, the origin being "overflowing tears", like your saying "tafaqqaʾa Zaydun shaḥman" (Zayd burst with fat), and so it is among what is accusative after the completion of the sentence? The answer is that this is not permissible, because when the tamyīz is transferred from the agent function, the entry of «مِنْ» upon it is barred, even if it is implied with it; one cannot say "tafaqqaʾa Zaydun min shaḥmin"; and this one, as you see, is governed in the genitive by «من», so it cannot be a tamyīz. Yet Abū l-Qāsim, in Sūrat Barāʾa, made it a tamyīz in His saying, the Exalted: {تَوَلَّوْا وَّأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدمع} [al-Tawba: 92], and his text must be quoted so you may know it. He, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: "«تفيضُ من الدمعِ» is like your saying «tafīḍu damʿan», and it is more eloquent than your saying «yafīḍu damʿuhā», because the eye is made as though it were overflowing tears itself; «من» is explicative, as in your saying «afdīka min rajulin» (I would ransom you, as a man), and the position of the preposition and its genitive noun is accusative as tamyīz." In it are the two obstacles you have learned, namely its being definite and its being governed in the genitive by «من» while being an agent in origin; further explanation of this will come. On this, this verse is, for him, like that one, and this is the third aspect. The fourth: «مِنْ» has the meaning of the bāʾ, that is: "they overflow with tears"; its having the meaning of bāʾ is a weak view, and they also counted among it His saying, the Exalted: {يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ} [al-Shūrā: 45], that is, «bi-ṭarfin»; just as the bāʾ comes with the meaning of «min», as in his saying:
180 - 4- شَرِبْنَ بماءِ البحرِ ثم ترفَّعَتْ ... متى لُجَجٍ خُضْرٍ لهنَّ نَئيجُ
(They drank of the sea water, then rose from green depths, with a roar of theirs.)
that is, «min māʾi l-jarr». [Translator's note: the source reads «ماءِ الجر», probably a scribal slip for «ماء البحر», "sea water".]
His saying: {مِمَّا عَرَفُواْ مِنَ الحق}: the first «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range and is attached to «تَفِيضُ»; the second may be for explaining the kind, that is, it explains the kind of the relative before it, and it may be partitive. Abū l-Qāsim clarified this to the utmost, saying, may Allah have mercy on him: "If you say: what is the difference between «مِنْ» and «مِنَ» in His saying {مِمَّا عَرَفُواْ مِنَ الحق}? I say: the first is for the beginning of the range, in that the tears began and arose from knowing the truth, being on account of it and because of it; and the second is to explain the relative, which is «ما عرفوا», and it admits the meaning of partition, in that they knew part of the truth and it made them weep and affected them; so how would it be if they knew all of it, read the Qurʾān and comprehended the Sunna?" End of quotation. He did not address what the two prepositional phrases are attached to, though it can be taken from the force of his words, and we shall add clarification. The first «مِنْ» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الدمع», that is: "while it arises and begins from knowing the truth", which is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's saying "in that the tears began and arose from knowing the truth"; and it cannot be attached to «تفيض», lest two identical particles, in wording and in meaning, be attached to one governor, for «مِنْ» in «من الدمع» is for the beginning of the range as mentioned; unless it is held that «مِنْ» in «من الدمع» is explicative, or has the meaning of the bāʾ, in which case it may be allowed, though its meaning is not as clear as the first.
As for «من الحق»: if it is made explicative, it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "I mean, from such-and-such"; if it is made partitive it is attached to «عَرَفوا», which is the meaning of his saying "they knew part of the truth".
Abū l-Baqāʾ said of «من الحق» that it is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun of the relative, that is: "from what they knew, being of the truth". The «من» in His saying, the Exalted, {مِمَّا عَرَفُواْ} may be causal, that is: the overflowing of their tears is because of their knowing the truth, and this is supported by al-Zamakhsharī's saying "on account of it and because of it". So four aspects result for the first «مِنْ», and weakness or prohibition in the third, as mentioned; and for the second «مِنْ» four also: two with respect to its meaning, whether «من» is of beginning or of cause, and two with respect to what it is attached to, whether «تفيض» or an omitted element as a ḥāl from the tears; and for the third, five: two with respect to its meaning, whether explicative or partitive, and three with respect to what it is attached to, whether an omitted «أعني», or «عَرَفوا» itself, or it is a ḥāl and so is attached to an omitted element as well, as Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned.
His saying: {يَقُولُونَ}: there are three aspects in it. One: it is resumptive and so has no position; Allah the Exalted informed about them of this fine statement. Two: it is a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in «أعينهم», and it is permissible for the ḥāl to come from the muḍāf ilayhi because the muḍāf is a part of it, so it is like His saying, the Exalted: {مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَاناً} [al-Ḥijr: 47]. Three: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «عَرَفوا», with «عرفوا» governing it. The Shaykh said, when reporting its being a ḥāl: "So said Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ, and neither made clear the owner of the ḥāl nor its governor." I say: as for Abū l-Baqāʾ, he did make clear the owner of the ḥāl, for he said: «يقولون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the agent in «عَرَفوا», so he made it explicit; and once the owner of the ḥāl is known, its governor is known, since the governor of the ḥāl is the governor of its owner; so the apparent sense is that he came across a corrupt copy of Abū l-Baqāʾ's i'rab from which what I mentioned dropped out. Then the Shaykh rejected its being a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أعينهم», with words to the effect that the ḥāl does not come from the muḍāf ilayhi even if the muḍāf is a part of it, and considered it an error, referring the explanation to some of his works; and he also rejected its being a ḥāl from the agent of «عرفوا», because it would require restricting their knowing the truth to this state, whereas they knew the truth in this state and others. He said: "So it is preferable that it be resumptive." As for what he considered an error, the discussion with him on this question belongs to a place other than this; and as for his saying "it would require restriction", the answer is that this ḥāl was mentioned only because it is the noblest of their states, so it came out as praise of them. His saying «ربَّنا آمنَّا» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying, and likewise {فاكتبنا} up to His saying {الصالحين}.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا جَآءُوكُمْ}: the nominative pronoun refers to the Jews contemporary with the Prophet; in that case an omitted muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "and when their descendants or their offspring come to you", because those of whom apes and swine were made did not come. It is also permissible not to imply an omitted muḍāf, on the basis that His saying {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله} to its end is an expression for those addressed in His saying {يَا أَهْلَ الكتاب}, and is a case where the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, as if it were said "you"; so the Shaykh said, and there is something to consider in it, for an implied muḍāf is necessary in His saying, the Exalted: {وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ القردة}, its implied form being "and He made of your fathers or your predecessors or of your kind", because the contemporaries were not themselves the ones made into those; so whether he takes it from what he mentioned or not, an omitted muḍāf is necessary.
His saying, the Exalted: {وَقَدْ دَّخَلُواْ بالكفر}: this is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. Concerning its governor there are two possibilities. One, with which Abū l-Baqāʾ began: that it is «قالوا», i.e. "they said so while entering as disbelievers and leaving as disbelievers"; there is something to consider in it, since the meaning rejects it. The second: that it is «آمنَّا», and this is clear, i.e. "they said 'we believe' in this state." «قد» in «وقد دَخَلُوا» and «وقد خَرَجُوا» is to bring the past near to the present. al-Zamakhsharī said: "And for another meaning, which is that the signs of hypocrisy were evident on them, and the Messenger, peace be upon him, was expecting Allah the Exalted to disclose what they concealed, so the particle of expectation entered; and it is attached to His saying «قالوا آمنا», i.e. they said that while this was their state." By his saying "it is attached" he means the ḥāl; and the force of his statement gives that the owner of the ḥāl and its governor is the clause reported by the saying. «بالكفر» is attached to an omitted word because it is a ḥāl from the agent of «دَخَلوا», so it is a ḥāl within a ḥāl, i.e. "they entered accompanied by disbelief", i.e. with disbelief with them, like their saying «خرج زيدٌ بثيابه» and the reading of those who read {تَنْبُتُ بالدُّهْن}, i.e. "and in it is the oil"; of it is what al-Aṣmaʿī cited:
176 - 1- ومُسْتَنَّةٍ كاسْتنانِ الخَرُو ... فِ قد قَطَعَ الحَبْل بالمِرْوَدِ
(And a galloping one, galloping like a lamb, has broken the rope, with its pin still in it.)
i.e. "and its pin is in it"; likewise «به» too is a ḥāl from the agent of «خرجوا».
His saying {وهم} is a mubtadaʾ and «قد خَرَجُوا» its khabar, and the clause is also a ḥāl, conjoined to the ḥāl before it. The first came verbal and the second nominal as an alert to their excess of self-destruction in disbelief: for it was proper for them, on entering to the Messenger, peace be upon him, to believe, because of what they saw of the beauty of his bearing and his majesty and what appeared at his noble hands of extraordinary acts and miracles; for that reason one of the disbelievers said: "I saw the face of one who is not a liar." When that did not take effect in them, He emphasised their second disbelief by presenting the clause as nominal, its beginning a noun and its khabar a verb, so that the predication in it is twice. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His saying «وهم» is a clarification from the possibility, in the expression, that a people enter with disbelief and then believe, and another people leave while they are disbelievers, so that it would apply to all, whereas they entered with disbelief and left with it; so Allah removed the possibility by His saying «وهم قد خَرَجوا به», i.e. they themselves, in person." al-Wāḥidī preceded him to this meaning and Ibn ʿAṭiyya expanded it. al-Wāḥidī said: "«وهم قد خَرَجوا به»: He emphasised the speech with the pronoun, singling them out for disbelief and distinguishing them from others." Some of them said: "The meaning of «هم» is emphasis in ascribing disbelief to them, and the denial that anything from the Messenger obliged their disbelief by way of bad treatment of them; rather he was gentle with them and treated them with the best treatment. So the meaning: they are the ones who left with disbelief by their own choice, not that you are the one who caused them to remain in disbelief." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form may be «وقد كانوا خَرَجُوا به»", and there is no sense in this interpretation.
The wāw in His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُواْ} admits two possibilities. One: that it is a conjunction of a ḥāl clause to its like. The second: that it is itself the wāw of ḥāl, and on this the noble verse contains evidence for those who permit multiple ḥāls for one single owner of the ḥāl without conjunction or badal, except in the comparative, as in «جاء زيدٌ ضاحكاً كاتباً»; on the first, that is not permissible except by conjunction or badal; and this is similar to the disagreement about multiple khabars.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وترى}: it may be of sight, in which case «يُسارعون» is a ḥāl; or it may be a verb of knowing or thinking, in which case «يسارعون» is accusative as the second object.
«منهم» is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «كثيراً», attached to an omitted word, i.e. "being of them" or "established among them". Abū Ḥaywa read «العِدوان» with kasra. «وأَكْلِهم»: this is a maṣdar annexed to its agent, and «السحتَ» is its object; what is in it has already preceded. As for His saying «لبئسما», the ruling of «ما» with «بئس» and «نِعْم» has also preceded at the beginning of this book, which makes repetition unnecessary.

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لَوْلاَ}: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and its meaning is reproach. al-Jarrāḥ and Abū Wāqid read «الِّربيُّون» in place of «الربانيين». Ibn ʿAbbās read «بئسما» without the lām of oath. «قولِهم» is a maṣdar annexed to its agent, and «والإِثْمَ» is its object.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
Abū l-Sammāl read «ولُعنوا» with sukūn on the ʿayn, and what made the lightening good here is that it is a kasra between two ḍammas; and like it is the saying of another:
176 - 2- لو عُصْرَ منه البانُ والمسكُ انعصَرْ
(Were ban-oil and musk squeezed from it, they would flow out.)
The apparent sense is that the pronoun in «كانوا» refers to the rabbis and monks; it may also refer to the earlier ones.
And His saying, the Exalted, reporting from the Jews: {يَدُ الله مَغْلُولَةٌ} has two views. One: that it is a pure statement.
