Some of them claimed that it is on the implying of a hamza of interrogation, its implied form being «أيدُ اللَّهِ مغلولةٌ؟» ("Is the hand of Allah fettered?"); they said that when He tightened their livelihood; but there is no need for this implication. «بما قالوا»: the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "they were cursed because of their saying", and «ما» is a maṣdar; it may also be a relative noun, with the returning pronoun omitted. The fettering of the hand and its spreading here is a metaphor for miserliness and generosity, even though there is no hand or limb there, and the speech of the Arabs is full of that. The Arabs said: «فلانٌ ينفق بكلتا يديه» ("so-and-so spends with both hands"). He said:
176 - 3- يداك يدا مجدٍ، فكفٌّ مفيدةٌ ... وكفٌ إذا ما ضُنَّ بالمالِ تُنْفِقُ
(Your two hands are hands of glory: one palm that bestows benefit, and one palm that spends when wealth is withheld.)
And another, namely Abū Tammām, said:
176 - 4- تعوَّد بَسْطَ الكفِّ حتى لَوَ أنَّه ... دعاها لقَبْضٍ لم تُطِعْه أنامِلُهْ
(He grew accustomed to spreading the palm, so that were he to call it to clench, his fingertips would not obey him.)
The Arabs used this metaphor also where there is no hand at all; of it is the saying of Labīd:
176 - 5- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... إذْ أصبحَتْ بيدِ الشَمالِ زِمامُها
(... when the reins of the morning came to be in the hand of the north wind.)
And another said:
176 - 6- جادَ الحِمَى بَسْطُ اليدين بوابلٍ ... شَكَرتْ نداه تِلاعُه ووِهادُهْ
(The preserve was lavished upon with a spreading of both hands, with a heavy downpour; its upland channels and its hollows gave thanks for its bounty.)
And they said: «بَسَطَ اليأسُ كفَّيه في صدري» ("despair spread its two palms in my chest"), and despair is an abstraction, not a physical thing, yet they gave it two palms figuratively. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is the hand dual in «بل يداه مبسوطتان» whereas in «يَدُ اللَّهِ مغلولةٌ» it is singular? I say: so that the rebuttal of their saying and the denial of it be more eloquent and more indicative of affirming the utmost generosity for Him and negating miserliness from Him; for the utmost that a generous person gives of his wealth with his own person is to give it with both hands together; so he built the metaphor on that." His saying {غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَلُعِنُواْ} may be a pure statement, and may be meant as an invocation against them. In the codex of ʿAbdullāh: «بُسُطان»; it is said «يدٌ بُسُط» on the pattern of «ناقة سُرُح» and «أُحُد» and «مِشْية سُجُع», i.e. spread out in generosity; and ʿAbdullāh read «بسيطتان»; it is said «يد بسيطة», i.e. released in generosity.
His saying: {يُنفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ}: in this clause there are five possibilities. The first, which is the apparent: that it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. The second: that it is in the position of the nominative because it is a second khabar for «يداه». The third: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «مبسوطتان». On these two possibilities a implied pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ, or to the owner of the ḥāl, is necessary, i.e. «ينفق بهما», and omitting the like of that is rare.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«ينفق كيف يشاء» is resumptive, and it is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the hāʾ", meaning in «يداه», "for two reasons: one, that the hāʾ is annexed-to; the second, that the khabar separates between them; nor is it permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the two hands, since there is no pronoun in it returning to them." I say: his saying "one, that the hāʾ is annexed-to" is no obstacle, for what is forbidden is the coming of a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi only when the muḍāf is not a part of the muḍāf ilayhi, or like a part of it, or a governor in it, and this is of the first kind, so there is no obstacle in it. And his saying "the second: that the khabar separates between them" is also no obstacle; of it is {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [Hūd: 72], if we say that «شيخاً» is a ḥāl from the demonstrative, the governor in it being the alerting particle. And his saying "since there is no pronoun in it" – it has preceded that the returning element is implied, i.e. «ينفق بهما».
The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «يداه»; and there is disagreement in it, I mean the coming of a ḥāl from a mubtadaʾ; the point of the prohibition is that the governor in the ḥāl is the governor in its owner, and the governor in its owner is an abstract matter, not a verbal one, namely inceptiveness (ibtidāʾ), and this is on one of the views about the governor in the mubtadaʾ. The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «يداه», and no regard is paid to what Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade, because of the validation of that which has preceded.
«كيف» in a construction like this is conditional, as in «كيف تكون أكون»; the object of «يشاء» is omitted, and likewise the apodosis of this condition is omitted, indicated by the verb preceding «كيف»; the meaning: "He spends as He wills to spend, He spends; and He spreads in the heaven as He wills to spread it, He spreads it". So the object of «يشاء», which is «أَنْ» and what follows, was omitted, and it has preceded that the object of «يشاء» and «يريد» is not mentioned except when it is strange. He also omitted the apodosis of «كيف», which is the later «ينفق» and the later «يبسط», because the first «ينفق ويبسط» indicate it, which is like your saying «أقوم إنْ يقم زيد». It is not permissible that the earlier «ينفق» govern «كيف», because it has the front of the speech, and what has the front of the speech is not governed except by a preposition or a muḍāf. al-Ḥawfī said: "«كيف» is a question about a state, and it is accusative by «يشاء»." The Shaykh said: "It cannot be understood here as a question about a state." I say: it has been discussed at length at His saying {يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الأرحام كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 6], and we mentioned what people have said about it.
His saying: {مَّآ أُنزِلَ}: «ما» here is a relative noun, in the position of the nominative, because it is the agent of His saying {وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ}; it is not permissible for «ما» to be a maṣdar with «إليك» standing in the place of the agent of «أُنْزل», the implied form being «وليزيدَنَّ كثيراً الإِنزالُ إليك», because the thing sent down itself would not be known, whereas what increases them is the thing sent down, not the act of sending down itself.
His saying «منهم» is an adjective of «كثيراً», attached to an omitted word; «طغياناً» is a second object of «يَزيد»; and His saying {إلى يَوْمِ القيامة} is attached to «أَلْقينا»; it may also be attached to His saying «والبغضاء», i.e. the mutual hatred among them is until the Day of Resurrection. It is not permissible for it to be attached to «العداوة», lest separation between the maṣdar and its object by a foreigner, namely the conjoined word, be necessarily entailed; and on this the question cannot be one of competition (tanāzuʿ), because its condition is the dominion of each of the two governors, and the first governor here, if given dominion over the disputed word, would not be permitted, because of the forbidden thing mentioned. Some have transmitted that competition is permitted in the two verbs of wonder, with the obligation of giving effect to the second, because no separation is made between the verb of wonder and its object; and this is like it, i.e. giving effect to the second governor is obligatory, and it is outside the analogy of competition; its like has preceded for you. The difference between ʿadāwa and baghḍāʾ is that enmity is everything publicly known from which action and war arise, whereas hatred does not go beyond the souls. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and the Shaykh said: "Enmity is more specific than hatred, because every enemy is hated, and one may hate one who is not an enemy."
His saying: {لِّلْحَرْبِ}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «أوقدوا», i.e. "they kindled it for the sake of war". The second: that it is an adjective of «نارا», attached to an omitted word. Is the kindling literal or figurative? Two views. «أطفأها الله» is the apodosis of «كلما», and it is also literal or figurative according to what has preceded. His saying {فَسَاداً} [al-Māʾida: 33]: its like has already preceded, and that it may be a maṣdar by meaning, in which case you have two considerations: one, returning the verb to the meaning of the maṣdar; the second, returning the maṣdar to the meaning of the verb; and that it may be a ḥāl, i.e. "they strive with the striving of corruption", or "they corrupt with their striving a corruption", or "they strive as corrupters"; and that it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "they strive for the sake of corruption". The pronoun in «بينهم» may refer to the Jews alone because they are diverse sects and branching factions, and it may refer to the Jews and the Christians because their mention has preceded in His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ اليهود والنصارى} [al-Māʾida: 51], and because the two classes are included in His saying: {قُلْ ياأهل الكتاب} [al-Māʾida: 59]. The alif and lām in «الأرض» may be for the genus and may be for a known referent.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا لَنَا لاَ نُؤْمِنُ}: «ما» is interrogative, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and «لنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar, the implied form being: "What thing has settled for us?"; and «لا نؤمن» is a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya). The parallel of this verse and the discussion of it were given before, and some said that it is an obligatory ḥāl without which the meaning is incomplete, as in {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49]; what I said about it was mentioned, which makes repetition unnecessary. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said here: "It is the intended point, and in mentioning it lies the benefit of the speech, just as you say «jāʾa Zaydun rākiban» to someone who said: did Zayd come walking or riding?"
His saying: {وَمَا جَآءَنَا}: there are two aspects for the position of «ما». One: it is genitive, conjoined to the Majestic Name, that is: "in Allah and in what has come to us"; on this His saying «من الحق» has two possibilities. One: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «جاءنا», that is: "it came while being of the kind of the truth". The other possibility: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range, and by "the truth" the Creator, the Exalted, is meant, and «مِنْ» is then attached to «جاءنا», as you say "jāʾanā fulānun min ʿindi Zaydin". The second: its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is His saying {مِنَ الحق}, and the clause is in the place of a ḥāl; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, and the implied form becomes: "Why do we not believe in Allah, when what has come to us is of the truth?" "The truth" may mean the Qurʾān, for it is true in itself, and it may mean the Creator, the Exalted, as was mentioned before; and what governs it is the settledness included in the meaning of «لنا».
His saying: {وَنَطْمَعُ}: in this clause there are six aspects. The first: its position is accusative, conjoined to what is reported by the saying before it, that is: "they say such-and-such and they say «we hope»", and this is a fine meaning. The second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-phrase which occurs as the khabar, namely «لنا», since it includes settledness, so it raises the pronoun and governs the ḥāl; Abū l-Qāsim held this, for he said: "The wāw in «ونطمعُ» is the wāw of the ḥāl. If you say: what governs the first ḥāl and the second? I say: what governs the first is the sense of the verb in the lām, as if it were said: what thing has befallen us, while not believing?; and in the second, the sense of this verb, but restricted by the first ḥāl, because if you removed it and said «mā lanā wa-naṭmaʿu» it would not be speech." There is room for consideration in these words, namely his saying "because if you removed it, etc.", because if we remove it and bring «نطمع», we do not bring it joined to the conjunction but bare of it, so that it takes the place of the first; do you not see that the grammarians, when they put the conjoined in the place of the one conjoined to, put it bare of the conjunction? And I saw in some copies of al-Kashshāf: «mā lanā naṭmaʿu» without a wāw joined to «نطمعُ», but this too is not sound, because if you said «mā lanā naṭmaʿu» it would be speech, as in His saying, the Exalted {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49], for «نطمع» would be in the position of a single term which is a ḥāl, as if you said "mā laka ṭāmiʿan" and "mā lanā ṭāmiʿīna". The Shaykh rejected this aspect on two counts. One: a governor does not call for more than one ḥāl when its owner is single, without a badal or conjunction, except the comparative, on the correct view. The second: it would require the wāw to enter upon an affirmative imperfect, which is not permitted except by interpretation, implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and we hope".
The third: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «نؤمن», so the two ḥāls are nested. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ونطمع» may be a ḥāl from «لا نؤمن», in the sense that they denounced themselves for not affirming the oneness of Allah while hoping, along with that, to be in the company of the righteous." This has what was mentioned of the wāw of the ḥāl entering upon the affirmative imperfect, and Abū l-Baqāʾ, when he permitted this aspect, implied a mubtadaʾ before «نطمع» and made the clause a ḥāl from the agent of «نؤمن» to escape this difficulty, saying: "It is possible that the implied form is «wa-naḥnu naṭmaʿu», so the clause would be a ḥāl from the agent of «lā nuʾminu»."
The fourth: it is conjoined to «لا نؤمن», so it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from that latent pronoun in «لنا», its governor being the governor of the ḥāl before it. If you say: this is the second aspect given above, and you mentioned from the Shaykh there that he forbade two ḥāls for one owner and that it would require the wāw to enter upon the imperfect, so what is the difference between this and that? The answer is that what is forbidden is the multiplicity of ḥāls without a conjunction, and this wāw is a conjunction; and what is barred for the imperfect is the entry of the wāw of the ḥāl upon it, and this is a conjunction, not a wāw of the ḥāl; so the difference between them arises from the wāw, since in the second aspect it was the wāw of the ḥāl and in this aspect the wāw of conjunction. Although this is clear, it may be hidden from many who are in training in i'rab. When Abū l-Qāsim reported this aspect, he showed two fine meanings for it, saying, may Allah have mercy on him: "and that it be conjoined to «لا نؤمن», in the sense: why do we combine the Trinity with hope for the company of the righteous?, or in the sense: why do we not combine the two by entering Islam, since it is not fitting for a disbeliever to hope for the company of the righteous?"
The fifth: it is a resumptive clause. The Shaykh said: "The best and easiest is that it be a resumptive report from them that they hope for Allah's favour upon them by admitting them with the righteous, the wāw conjoining this clause to the clause «وما لنا لا نؤمن»." I say: this meaning and the meaning of its being conjoined to what is reported by the saying before it are one thing, for in it is the report about them of their saying such-and-such.
The sixth: «ونطمعُ» is conjoined to «نؤمن», that is: "Why do we not hope?" The Shaykh said here: "There appears to me an aspect other than what they mentioned, which is that it be conjoined to «نؤمن», the implied form being: «why do we not believe and not hope», so there is in that a denunciation of the absence of their faith and the absence of their hope despite their ability to attain the two things: faith, and hope of entering with the righteous." I say: his saying "other than what they mentioned" is not as he said; rather Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, saying: «ونطمعُ» may be conjoined to «نؤمن», that is: "why do we not hope?", so he made explicit its conjunction to the verb negated by «لا»; the most that can be said is that the Shaykh added to it in elaboration.
As for aspiration (ṭamaʿ), al-Rāghib said: "It is the soul's inclination toward a thing out of desire for it." Then he said: "Since most ṭamaʿ comes from passion, it was said: ṭamaʿ is a stain, and ṭamaʿ soils the hide." The Shaykh said: "Ṭamaʿ is close to hope (rajāʾ). One says from it: ṭamiʿa, yaṭmaʿu, ṭamaʿan. He, the Exalted, said {خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً} [al-Sajda: 16], and «ṭamāʿa» and «ṭamāʿiya», like «karāhiya»; he said:
180 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
طَماعيةً أَنْ يغفرَ الذنبَ غافرُهْ
(... in hope that the forgiver will forgive the sin.)
So the doubling in it is an error. Its active participle is «ṭamiʿ», like «fariḥ» and «ashir»." The Shaykh reported nothing else, and al-Rāghib reported «ṭamiʿ» and «ṭāmiʿ»; it should be that this is in two respects, like their saying «fariḥ» for one whose nature it is and «fāriḥ» for one in whom joy is newly arisen.
His saying: {أَن يُدْخِلَنَا}: that is, «fī an», so its position is accusative or genitive, as mentioned more than once. «مع» is in its usual sense of accompaniment; it was also said that it means «في», and there is no need for that, as the meaning stands on its own while the word stays in its original sense.

semin-durr:85-85.t: Al-Ḥasan read {فآتاهم}: from «ātāhu kadhā», that is, he gave him; the well-known reading is preferable, because «ithāba» (rewarding) in it alerts that this is for the sake of a deed, in contrast to «īʾtāʾ» (giving), which may be for a deed or otherwise. His saying {جَنَّاتٍ} is the second object of «أثابَهم» or of «آتاهم», according to the two readings. «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «جنات». «خالدين» is a ḥāl of anticipated state (ḥāl muqaddara). His saying {وذلك جَزَآءُ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; «ذلك» points to the reward or the giving. «المحسنين» may be a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, the original being «wa-dhālika jazāʾuhum», and their noble description was mentioned only to alert that this trait is what brings about their reward with good; or it may be meant as every doer of good, so they are included first and foremost.

semin-durr:88-88.t: His saying, the Exalted: {حَلاَلاً}: there are three aspects in it. The most apparent: it is a direct object, that is, "eat something lawful"; on this aspect there are two views on the preposition-phrase, namely His saying {مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ}. One: it is a ḥāl from «حلالا», because in origin it is an adjective of an indefinite noun, and when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. The second: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range in eating, that is: "begin your eating of the lawful from that which Allah has provided for you". The second of the aspects mentioned: it is a ḥāl from the relative or from its omitted returning pronoun, i.e. «razaqakumūhu», so what governs it is «رزقكم». The third: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "lawful eating", and there is some looseness in it.

semin-durr:65-65.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ أَنَّ}: the discussion of the like of this construction has already preceded.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لأَكَلُواْ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ}: the object of eating here is omitted by way of limitation, i.e. "this act would have been found from them", and «من فوقهم» is attached to it, i.e. "they would have eaten from both directions". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«من فوقهم» is an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. «لأكلُوا رِزْقاً كائناً مِنْ فوقِهم»." His saying «منهم» is an advanced khabar, «أمةٌ» a mubtadaʾ and «مقتصدةٌ» its adjective; and according to the view of al-Akhfash it is permissible for «أمة» to be an agent of the preposition-phrase. His saying: {مِّنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ مُّقْتَصِدَةٌ وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ} is a variety in the detailing: in the first clause He gave information by the preposition and its genitive noun and described the mubtadaʾ with moderation, whereas in the second clause He described the mubtadaʾ with «منهم» and gave information about it with the clause of His saying {سَآءَ مَا يَعْمَلُونَ}. That is because the first group is praised, so they were described with moderation and it was reported of them that they are among the People of the Book, for the description is more binding than the khabar, since when they accept Islam this name leaves them; as for the second group, they were described as being of the People of the Book, for the description is more binding, and they are disbelievers and so of them, and He reported of them with the blaming clause, for the khabar is not binding, and some of them may accept Islam and the reporting of that leaves them.
«ساءَ» here admits three possibilities. The first: that it is wonder, as if it were said «ما أسوأ عملَهم» ("how evil is their deed"); al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only this possibility, but when the grammarians listed the forms of wonder they did not count «ساء» among them; if he meant it in terms of meaning and not in terms of the wonder that has a chapter in grammar, it is close. The second: that it is in the sense of «بِئْس» and so indicates blame, as in His saying, the Exalted: {سَآءَ مَثَلاً القوم}; on these two views «ساءَ» is non-conjugating, because the verbs of wonder, praise and blame are not conjugated. The third: that it is the conjugating «ساء» as in sāʾa yasūʾu, and of it are {لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ} [al-Isrāʾ: 7] and {سِيئَتْ وُجُوهُ الذين كَفَرُواْ} [al-Mulk: 27]; the conjugating one is transitive, He the Exalted said: {لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ}; so where is the object of this one? It was said: it is omitted, its implied form being «ساء عملُهم المؤمنين»; and the one in the sense of «بئس» must have a specified noun (mumayyiz), which is omitted here, its implied form being «ساء عملاً الذي كانوا يعملونه». «الحرب» is feminine, and originally a maṣdar, and the discussion of it has preceded in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ياأيها الرسول}: He addressed him with the noblest human attributes. His saying: {بَلِّغْ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ}, though he had already conveyed! al-Zamakhsharī answered that the meaning is: "all that was sent down to you", i.e. whatever was sent down, not watching anyone in conveying it and not fearing that something disliked will reach you. Ibn ʿAṭiyya answered with something close to it, saying: "He commanded His Messenger to convey it in full completeness, because he had already conveyed." Others besides them answered that the meaning is continuity, as in His saying: {يا أَيُّهَا النبي اتق الله} [al-Aḥzāb: 1] and {يَا أَيُّهَا الذين آمَنُواْ آمِنُواْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 136]. I mention this only because it benefits a question that is coming.
His saying: {ما} may be a noun in the sense of «الذي»; it is not permissible for it to be an indefinite with a description, because he is commanded to convey everything, as has passed, and the indefinite does not suffice for that, for its implied form would be «بَلِّغْ شيئاً أُنزل إليك». In «أُنزل» there is a nominative pronoun returning to «ما», which stands in place of the agent. It may, though remotely, be that «ما» is a maṣdar, and on that there is no pronoun in «أُنزل», because the maṣdar «ما» is, on the sound view, a particle, so something must stand in the place of the agent, namely the preposition-phrase after it, and on this the implied form is «بَلِّغِ الإِنزالَ»; but the sending down is not conveyed, for it is an abstract meaning, unless it is intended that the maṣdar falls in the position of the direct object. It is also possible that the meaning is "make known by conveying the sending down", in which case it is a maṣdar in its normal sense.
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ}, i.e. "if you do not do the conveying". He omitted the direct object and did not say «وإن لم تبلِّغْ فما بَلَّغت», for the reason that has preceded in His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ} [verse 24] in al-Baqara. The apodosis must differ from the protasis for the benefit to be obtained, and whenever the two are identical the speech is flawed; if you said «إن أتى زيد فقد جاء», it would not be permissible. The apparent sense of His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ} is that the protasis and the apodosis are identical, for the meaning apparently comes to: "if you do not do, you have not done". People have answered that with answers, the soundest of which is what the master Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī said. He gave two answers. One: that if he did not comply with Allah's command in conveying the messages and concealed all of them, it would be as though he had not been sent as a messenger, which would be a hideous matter whose hideousness is not hidden; so it was said: "if you do not convey the least thing, even one word, you are like one who committed the hideous act which is the concealment of all of it", just as the killing of a soul was magnified in His saying: {فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ الناس جَمِيعاً} [al-Māʾida: 32]. The second: that what is meant is: "if you do not do that, you incur what the concealment of the whole revelation requires of punishment", so the cause was put in the place of the effect; and it is supported by: "Then Allah revealed to me: If you do not convey My messages, I shall punish you."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya answered and said: "That is: if you leave anything, you have left everything, and what you conveyed becomes unreckoned; so the meaning of «وإن لم تفعل» is «وإن لم تستوفِ» ('if you do not complete')." Like this is the saying of the poet:
176 - 7- سُئِلْتَ فلم تبخَلْ، ولم تُعْطِ نائلاً ... ، فسِيَّان لا حمدٌ عليك ولا ذَمٌّ
(You were asked and did not withhold, and you gave no gift; so it is the same: no praise be on you and no blame.)
i.e. "you did not give what is counted as a gift"; otherwise the verse would be self-contradicting. He means by self-contradiction that he said «فلم تبخل», which implies that he gave something, so his saying after that «ولم تُعْطِ نائلاً», if one did not imply a gift worth reckoning, would be contradictory. There is something to consider in it, for his saying «لم تبخل ولم تُعْطِ» do not converge on one single locus so as to contradict each other; so it does not follow, from the absence of the implication that Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied, that the verse is false. By what I have mentioned, the corruption is made clear of the saying of one who claimed that this verse is one in which three governors compete: «سُئِلت» and «تَبْخَلْ» and «تُعْطِ»; for his saying «ولم تَبْخَلْ», on this speaker's view, has dominion over «طائل» [sic], as if it were said «فلم تبخل بطائل», and if he did not withhold it, then he gave and bestowed it, which contradicts his saying after that «ولم تُعْطِ نائلاً». [Translator's note: the source reads «طائل» here, whereas the verse as quoted has «نائلاً».]
Ibn al-Khaṭīb al-Rāzī invalidated the preceding answer and chose an answer of his own, saying: "The majority answered with «if you do not convey one of them, you are like one who did not convey anything», and this is weak, because as for one who leaves a part and brings a part, if it is said that he left everything it would be false; and if it is said that the measure of the offence in leaving a part is like the offence in leaving everything, that is the impossible and the barred; so this answer falls. The soundest in my view is to say: this answer came out on the principle of the saying:
176 - 8- أنا أبو النجمِ وشِعْري شِعْري
(I am Abū l-Najm, and my poetry is my poetry.)
and its meaning is that my poetry has reached in perfection, eloquence and solidity a point where, whenever it is said 'it is my poetry', its praise has reached the utmost limit beyond which there is no increase; and this speech gives complete exaggeration from this angle. So also here, as if He said: 'if you do not convey His messages, you have not conveyed His messages', meaning that the leaving of conveyance cannot be described by a threat greater than that he left the conveyance; so that was an alert to the utmost of threat and warning."
The Shaykh said: "What he used to weaken the answer of the majority does not weaken it, because he said 'if it is said that he left everything, it would be false', and they did not say that; they said only that some of them are not more deserving of delivery than others, so if you do not deliver, it is as though you neglected delivering all of them, just as one who does not believe in some of them is like one who does not believe in all of them, because each of them pleads with what the others plead with, and their being so is in the ruling of one single thing, and one single thing is not conveyed and not conveyed, believed and not believed; so that conveying of some became unreckoned." I say: this elegant speech, I mean that by which the answer to al-Rāzī's objection was given, is the speech of al-Zamakhsharī; he took it and transferred it here.
The remainder of al-Zamakhsharī's speech is that he said, after his saying "not believed": "And on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him: 'If you conceal one verse, you have not conveyed My messages.' And it is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: 'Allah sent me with His messages and I was distressed by them, so Allah revealed to me: If you do not convey My messages, I shall punish you; and He guaranteed me protection, so I became strong.'" The Shaykh said: "As for what he mentioned, that the measure of the offence in leaving a part being like the offence in leaving everything is impossible and barred, there is no impossibility in it, because Allah the Exalted may attach to a small sin a great punishment and the reverse." Then he gave the example of the thief who takes by stealth: his hand is cut off and he returns what he took; and of the usurper: what he took is taken from him without cutting.
al-Wāḥidī said: "That is: if he leaves conveying some, he is like one who did not convey, because his leaving some nullifies the conveying of what he conveyed, and his offence in concealing some is like his offence in concealing all, in that he deserves punishment from his Lord; and Allah forbid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conceal anything of what Allah revealed to him. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'Whoever claims that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed anything of the revelation has made a great slander against Allah; and Allah the Exalted says: {ياأيها الرسول بَلِّغْ}. Had the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed His saying, the Exalted: {وَتُخْفِي فِي نِفْسِكَ مَا الله مُبْدِيهِ}' [al-Aḥzāb: 37], the verse." This is close to the preceding answers. This is what I have come across of answers in this noble verse. The like of this verse, in the preceding question, is the sound ḥadīth from ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb: "So whoever's emigration was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger", for the apodosis itself is the protasis itself; and they answered it by saying an implication by which difference is obtained, saying: "its implied form: whoever's emigration was to Allah and His Messenger in intention and purpose, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger in ruling and law"; and al-Rāzī's answer, which he chose, may also apply to it.
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr, read «رسلاتِه» in the plural, and the rest «رسالتَه» in the singular. The explanation of the plural is that he, peace be upon him, was sent with various kinds of message, such as the fundamentals of tawḥīd and the rulings in their different kinds. The singular is clear, because the annexed generic noun covers all of that; one of the messengers said: {أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالاَتِ رَبِّي} [al-Aʿrāf: 62], and another said: {رِسَالَةَ رَبِّي} [al-Aʿrāf: 79], having regard to the two meanings.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ} to the end: the i'rab of that and the derivation of the individual words were given in Sūrat al-Baqara. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «عَقَدْتُمُ» with the qāf lightened and no alif after the ʿayn; Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir read «عاقدتم» on the pattern fāʿaltum; and the rest read «عَقَّدتم» with the qāf doubled. As for the lightening, it is the original; as for the doubling, it admits several explanations. One: it is for intensification (takthīr), because the ones addressed are a group. The second: it is equivalent to the simple form, thus agreeing with the first reading, like «qaddara» and «qadara». The third: it indicates the corroboration of the oath, as in "By Allah, than whom there is no god but He". The fourth: it indicates the reinforcement of resolve by commitment. The fifth: it is a compensation for the alif in the other reading, and I do not know what its meaning is; and it cannot be for the repetition of the oath, for the expiation is due even with a single time.
Abū ʿUbayd was bold toward this reading and discredited it, saying: "The doubling is for repetition, time after time, and I am not safe from this reading entailing the dropping of expiation for a single oath, since it was not repeated." People held him mistaken in that and mentioned those earlier meanings, so the reading is sound in recitation and meaning, and praise be to Allah.
As for «عاقدت», it may be equivalent to the simple form, like «jāwaztu l-shayʾa» and «juztuhu». Al-Fārisī said: «عاقَدْتم» admits two things. One: that it be equivalent to «faʿala», like «ṭāraqtu l-naʿla» and «ʿāqabtu l-liṣṣa». The other: that it be the form fāʿaltu which calls for two parties, so the meaning is "by what you have made oaths binding upon", and he made it transitive with «ʿalā» when it was in the sense of «ʿāhada» (to covenant); He said {بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهِ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10], just as He made {نَادَيْتُمْ إِلَى الصلاة} [al-Māʾida: 58] transitive with «ilā», while its usual form is to say «nādaytu Zaydan», as in {وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِن جَانِبِ الطور} [Maryam: 52], since it was in the sense of «daʿawtu ilā kadhā» (I called to such-and-such); He said {مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى الله} [Fuṣṣilat: 33]. Then it was extended: the preposition was dropped and the verb was transferred to the object, then the returning pronoun from the ṣila to the relative was dropped since it became {بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ الأيمان}, as it was dropped in His saying {فاصدع بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ} [al-Ḥijr: 94]. I say: he, may Allah have mercy on him, wants to show the meaning of mufāʿala, so he brought these parallels for inclusion of meaning (taḍmīn) and for the gradual omission of the returning pronoun; the meaning is: "by what you have made oaths binding upon" and "you have made the oaths binding upon it", so he attributed the making of the covenant to the oaths metaphorically. One could say: we may not need a returning pronoun at all, so as to need this great effort, by making «ما» a maṣdar and the object omitted, its implied form being: "by your making oaths binding with others", that is, "by your covenanting oaths with others", and we are spared another metaphor, which is attributing the covenant to the oaths, for in this aspect the covenant is attributed to others, which is a literal attribution; and a group stated this aspect explicitly.
The Shaykh criticized Abū ʿAlī's words, saying: "His saying that it is like «ṭāraqtu l-naʿla» and «ʿāqabtu l-liṣṣa» is not like it, because you do not say «ṭaraqtu» nor «ʿaqabtu», whereas you say «ʿāqadtu l-yamīna» and «ʿaqadtuhā»." This is not binding on Abū ʿAlī, because he means that it is like it in that mutual participation by two parties, in the sense of fāʿala, is negated of it as it is negated of «ʿāqabtu» and «ṭāraqtu»; as for its also being said in this case in such a way, that does not harm it in the comparison.
He also said: "To imply the omission of the preposition and then the pronoun by gradation is remote, and it is not parallel to «فاصدَعْ بما تؤمر», because «amara» is transitive sometimes by itself and sometimes with a preposition, even if the original is the preposition; moreover, «ما» in «فاصدَعْ بما» need not be in the sense of «alladhī»; rather the apparent view is that it is a maṣdar, and likewise here the better course is that it be a maṣdar, in contrast with the maṣdar, namely «al-laghw» (idle talk)."
In Sūrat al-Nisāʾ His saying, the Exalted, {والذين عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ} [verse 33] and «عَاقَدْت» preceded, and I mentioned to you what is in them, so there are three readings in the well-known, and in that one two readings; and I had mentioned that «ʿaqqadat» with doubling was reported from Ḥamza in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, so there would be three readings in it also, but it is a strange coincidence, for Ḥamza is among those who lighten in this sūra, and the doubling is reported from him in al-Nisāʾ. [Translator's note: the sentence "فصارَ في ثلاث قراءاتٍ في المشهور" is rendered as it stands; "in" and "that one" refer to the two sūras.]
His saying, the Exalted: {فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعَامُ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. There are four aspects for the pronoun in «فكفارته». The first: it refers to the breach (ḥinth) which the flow of the speech indicates, although it was not mentioned, that is: "so the expiation of the breach". The second: it refers to «ما» if we make it a nominal relative, with a muḍāf omitted, that is: "so the expiation of its violation"; so al-Zamakhsharī implied it. The third: it refers to the contract (ʿaqd), because of the earlier verb indicating it. The fourth: it refers to the oath (yamīn), although feminine, because it has the sense of "swearing" (ḥalf); Abū l-Baqāʾ stated these two, and they are not apparent. «إطعامُ» is a maṣdar annexed to its object, equivalent to a particle and an active verb, that is: "its expiation is that the one who breaks the oath feeds ten", and the agent of a maṣdar is often omitted; there is no necessity calling for implying it with a passive verb, i.e. "that ten be fed", because in that there is a disagreement already pointed out. On the first, the position of «عشرة» is accusative; on the second, its position is nominative as the one whose agent is not named. This has a benefit that appears in the follower: when you say "yuʿjibunī aklu l-khubzi", if you imply it as active you follow «الخبز» in the genitive by wording and in the accusative by position, and if you imply it as passive you follow it in the genitive and the nominative; so you say "yuʿjibunī aklu l-khubzi wa-l-samni, wa-l-samna, wa-l-samnu". In the ḥadīth: "He forbade the killing of the snake «al-abtar» and «dhū l-ṭufyatayn»", with «dhū» in the nominative in the sense: that the abtar be killed. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is good to imply it, that is the maṣdar, by a verb whose agent is named, because what precedes and what follows it is address." I say: this is an indication that strengthens that, because the meaning is: "so its expiation is that you feed, O you who swear"; and I had told you that implying it with the active is the preferable, even if no indication were found, because it is the original.
His saying: {مِنْ أَوْسَطِ}: two aspects. One: it is in the position of nominative as a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ which what precedes explains, its implied form being "their food is from the middle of", so that the speech is complete at His saying {مساكين}; further clarification of this will come soon, if Allah the Exalted wills. The second: it is in the position of accusative because it is an adjective of the second object, the implied form being: "provision or food being of the middle of"; as for the first object, it is «عشرة», to which the maṣdar is annexed; and «ما» is a nominal relative, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "from the middle of that which you feed". Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it governed in the genitive by «مِنْ», saying: "that from which you feed". There is room for consideration in it, because it is a condition of the returning pronoun governed in the genitive, for omission, that the two particles and the two attachments be identical; and the two particles here, though alike, namely «مِنْ» and «مِنْ», differ in governor, for the second «مِنْ» is attached to «تُطْعِمُون» and the first is attached to an omitted element, namely unrestricted being, because it occurs as an adjective of the omitted object. It may be said that, since the verb is directed to His saying {مِنْ أَوْسَطِ}, it is as though it were governing it, and we implied an object only by the necessity of the craft. If you say: the relative is not governed in the genitive by «مِنْ», it is governed only by annexation, the answer is that what is annexed to the relative is like the relative in that, as in "murra bi-ghulāmi lladhī marartu" (it was passed by the servant of him by whom you passed).
«أهليكم» is the first object of «تُطْعِمُون», and the second is omitted as mentioned, i.e. "you feed it to your families". «أهليكم» is a sound plural, and it lacks one of the conditions, namely that it not be a proper noun nor an adjective; what made it good is that it is often used in the manner of "deserving of such-and-such" in their saying "huwa ahlun li-kadhā", meaning "he deserves it", so it resembled the adjectives and was pluralized as they are. The Exalted said {شَغَلَتْنَآ أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا} [al-Fatḥ: 11] and {قوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَاراً} [al-Taḥrīm: 6]. In the ḥadīth: "Allah has «ahlīn»." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, who are they? He said: "The reciters of the Qurʾān; they are the people of Allah and His elect." His saying «أهلُوا الله» is a plural whose nūn is dropped for annexation; it may also be singular, in which case it is written «أهلُ الله», so it is one in wording.
Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq read «أهالِيكم» with sukūn on the yāʾ, and there are two explanations of it. One: «أهالي» is a broken plural of «ahla», so it is irregular by analogy, like «layla» and «layālī». Ibn Jinnī said: "«Ahāl» is on a par with «layāl»; their singulars are «ahlāt» and «laylāt»; and the Arabs say «ahl» and «ahla», the poet said:
180 - 6- وأَهْلَةُ وُدٍّ قد سُرِرْتُ بوُدِّهم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And a kin of affection, with whose affection I was gladdened ...)
And by the analogy of Abū Zayd's statement you would make it a plural of an implied singular, like «aḥādīth» and «aʿārīḍ»; and to this points Ibn Jinnī's saying «ahl is on a par with layālī», their singulars being «ahlāt» and «laylāt»." This may be by way of transmission, and it may be by way of analogy as Abū Zayd says.
The second: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) of «ahl». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "like «al-layālī» as plural of «layla» and «al-arāḍī» as plural of «arḍ»." His saying "as plural of layla and plural of arḍ" means the lexical plural, because a collective noun is a plural in meaning; he does not mean that it is technically the plural of «layla» and «arḍ», for he has supposed it to be a collective noun, so how would he make it a plural in the technical sense?
The analogy of Jaʿfar's reading would be to give the yāʾ a fatḥa for its lightness, but he likened the yāʾ to the alif and so implied the vowel in it, which is frequent in verse, as in al-Nābigha's saying:
180 - 7- رَدَّتْ عليه أقاصِيه ولَبَّده ... ضَرْبُ الوليدةِ بالمِسْحاةِ في الثَّأَدِ
(Its far parts restored to it, and it was matted down by the girl's striking with the spade in the damp ground,)
and the saying of the other:
180 - 8- كأنَّ أيدِيهنَّ بالقاعِ القَرِقْ ... أيدي جوارٍ يتعاطَيْنَ الوَرِقْ
(As though their feet on the smooth level ground were the hands of girls passing silver coins.)
That has been treated more fully than this.
His saying, the Exalted: {أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ}: two aspects. One: it is joined to «إطعام», that is: "its expiation is feeding ten, or clothing those ten". The second: it is joined to the position of «من أوسط»; so said al-Zamakhsharī, and what he said works only on an aspect that preceded in His saying «من أوسط», namely that «من أوسط» be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being "their food is of the middle", the speech being, for him, complete at His saying {عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ}, and then he began another report that the food is of the middle of such-and-such. But if we say «من أوسط» is the second object, joining «كسوتهم» to it is impossible because of their disagreement in i'rab.
The majority read «كِسوتهم» with kasra on the kāf. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab read it with ḍamma; it was mentioned in al-Baqara that they are two dialects, both for the maṣdar and for the thing clothed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "like «al-qidwa» and «al-quḍwa», and «al-iswa» and «al-uswa»", except that the one who read it with ḍamma in al-Baqara was Ṭalḥa, and they did not mention him here, nor did they mention these here.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «أو كأُسْوَتِهم» with the kāf of the genitive entering upon «أُسْوة». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "meaning: or the like of what you feed your families, whether in plenty or in scarcity, not reducing them below the measure of their provision, but sharing equally among them. If you say: what is the position of the kāf? I say: nominative: its implied form: «or their food like their share», meaning: like the likeness of their food, if they do not feed them the middle." End of quotation. It was mentioned earlier that he makes «من أوسط» nominative in position as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, so the kāf for him is nominative, joined to «مِنْ أوسطِ». Abū l-Baqāʾ said something close to this, for he said: "The kāf is in the position of nominative, that is: «or like the share of your families»." The Shaykh said: "It is in the position of accusative, joined to the position of «مِنْ أوسط», because for him it is the second object."
Yet this reading removes clothing from the expiation, and people have agreed that it is one of the three options; but the holder of this reading may say: "Clothing is derived from the Sunna." But if consensus were established that the basis of clothing in the expiation is the verse, then rejecting this reciter would be valid.
His saying: {أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ} is joined to «إطعامُ», and it is a maṣdar annexed to its object, and what is said of it is as what is said of «إطعامُ عشرة» regarding the permissibility of implying it with an active or a passive verb and what was said about that. His saying {فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ} is like His saying in al-Nisāʾ {فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ} [verse 92], and that has been treated carefully before.
His saying: {إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is accusative as an adverb of time and its governor is «كفارة», that is: that feeding, or what is joined to it, expiates for you the breach of the oath at the time of your swearing." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And that which is mentioned is an expiation; and had it been said «tilka kaffāratu», it would have been right, in the sense of those things, or the feminine is for the expiation; and the meaning is: «when you swore and broke [it]», so he left out the mention of the breach because it is known that the expiation becomes due by the breach of the oath, not by the swearing itself." What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is necessary, namely implying the breach; hence Abū l-Baqāʾ was faulted for his saying: "The governor of «إذا» is «kaffāratu aymānikum», because the meaning is: that expiates your oaths at the time of your swearing." It was said to him: the expiation does not take place at the time of the swearing, so how can what does not occur in it govern the adverb? The apparent sense of the verse is that «إذا» is purely adverbial, with no conditional meaning, which is not its predominant use; it may also be conditional, its answer being omitted according to the Basrans' rule, indicated by what preceded, or being the very preceding clause according to Abū Zayd and the Kufans, the implied form being: "when you swore and broke it, that is the expiation for the sin of your oaths", like their saying "you are a wrongdoer if you do". The kāf in His saying {كذلك يُبَيِّنُ} is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar according to the majority of the parsers, that is: "Allah makes His signs clear with a clarification like that clarification"; and for Sībawayh it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of that maṣdar, as has been known more than once.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والصابئون}: the majority read it with the wāw, and so it is in the codices of the cities. For its nominative there are nine possibilities. The first, which is the view of the majority of the people of Basra, al-Khalīl and Sībawayh and their followers: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, because the khabar of the first indicates it, the intention being to postpone it; and the implied form is: "Indeed those who believed and those who were Jews – whoever believes in them... to its end – and the Sabians likewise"; and like it: «إن زيداً وعمروٌ قائمٌ», i.e. «إنَّ زيداً قائم وعمرو قائم». If we do that, is the omission from the first, i.e. the khabar of the second is the one retained, the implied form being «إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ وعمروٌ قائم», with the first «قائم» omitted, or the reverse? Two well-known views; each of them has occurred. He said:
176 - 9- نحنُ بما عِنْدنا وأنت بما ... عندك راضٍ والرأيُ مختلفُ
(We, with what we have, and you, with what you have, are content, and opinion differs.)
i.e. «نحن راضون»; and the reverse is his saying:
177 - 0- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... فإني وقَيَّار بها لَغَريبُ
(... for I and Qayyār here are strangers.)
The implied form being «وقيارٌ بها كذلك». If it is said: why is it not permissible that the omission be from the first here too? The answer is that this would entail the lām entering the khabar of a mubtadaʾ not abrogated by «إنَّ», which is rare and occurs only in the necessity of poetry; so in the verse these two implications are permissible on this derivation. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«والصابئون» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar omitted, the intention being to postpone it from what is within the scope of «إنَّ» of its noun and khabar, as if it were said: 'indeed those who believed, those who were Jews and the Christians – their ruling is thus – and the Sabians likewise.'" And Sībawayh cited as evidence for that:
177 - 1- وإلاَّ فاعلَمُوا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... بُغاةٌ ما بَقِينا في شِقاقِ
(Otherwise know that we and you are rebels so long as we remain in dissension.)
i.e. "know that we are rebels and you likewise." Then he said after some discussion: "If you say: His saying «والصابئون» is a conjoined word that must have something it is conjoined to, so what is it? I say: it, together with its omitted khabar, is a clause conjoined to the clause of His saying {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ} to its end, and it has no position, just as the one it is conjoined to has no position. If you say: advancing and postponing are only for a benefit, so what is it? I say: its benefit is the alert that the Sabians are accepted in repentance if faith and righteous action are sound from them; so what is the supposition about others? That is because the Sabians are the clearest of these enumerated in error and the most severe in rebelliousness; and they were called Sabians only because they 'inclined away' (ṣaba'ū) from all religions, i.e. went out; just as the poet advanced his saying «وأنتم» as an alert that those addressed are deeper in the description of rebellion than his own people, where he hastened with it before the khabar which is «بُغاةٌ», lest his people enter into rebellion before them though they are deeper in it than they and firmer of foot. If you say: if it had been said «والصابئين وإياكم», the advancing would have been achieved? I say: if it were said so, it would not be advancing in any respect, because there is no displacement from its place in it; one says 'advanced' and 'postponed' of what is displaced, not of what stays in its place; and this clause runs in the manner of a parenthetical clause."
The second possibility: that «إنَّ» is in the sense of «نعم» and so is a particle of response, and in that case it has no position; and on this what follows it is nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, and what follows that is conjoined to it in the nominative, and the khabar of all of it is His saying {مَنْ آمَنَ} to its end. That it is in the sense of «نعم» is a weaker view, which some grammarians held, and they made of it His saying, the Exalted: {إِنْ هذان لَسَاحِرَانِ} [Ṭāhā: 63] in the reading of those who read it with the alif (hādhāni); there is a long discussion about the verse which will come in its place, God willing. They also made of it the saying of ʿAbdullāh b. al-Zubayr: «إنَّ وصاحبُها», in answer to one who said to him "may Allah curse the she-camel that carried me to you", i.e. «نعم وصاحبُها» ("yes, and her owner"); and they made of it the saying of another:
177 - 2- بَرَزَ الغواني في الشبا ... بِ يَلُمْنَني وألومُهُنَّهْ
ويَقُلْنَ شَيْبٌ قد عَلا ... كَ وقد كَبِرْتَ فقلتُ إنَّهْ
(The beauties came forth in youth, they blame me and I blame them; and they say: 'Grey hair has come upon you, and you have grown old'; so I said: «إنَّهْ».)
i.e. «نعم», the hāʾ being for pausing. It was answered that the noun and the khabar are omitted in the saying of Ibn al-Zubayr, and the word conjoined to the noun remains as an indication of it, the implied form being «إنها وصاحبها معلونان» ("she and her owner are cursed"), and the implied form of the verse «إنه كذلك»; and on the supposition that it is in the sense of «نعم», it is not valid to make it that here, because nothing preceded it for it to be an answer to, and «نعم» does not occur as the beginning of speech, but only as an answer to a question, so that it is an affirmation of it. One might say: "It is possible that there is an implied question there, and they have mentioned that in many places, among them His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ أُقْسِمُ} [al-Qiyāma: 1] and {لاَ جَرَمَ} [Hūd: 22]; they said: it may be a rebuttal to one who says such-and-such."
The third possibility: that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «هادوا», i.e. "they were Jews, they and the Sabians"; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī, and his pupils al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj rejected it. al-Zajjāj said: "It is an error from two angles. One of them: that the Sabian, in this view, shares with the Jew in Judaism, and that is not so, for the Sabian is other than the Jew; and if «هادوا» is made in the sense of 'they repented', from His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّا هُدْنَآ إِلَيْكَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 156], not from Judaism, so that the meaning is 'they repented, they and the Sabians', then the exegesis has come otherwise, because the meaning of «الذين آمنوا» in this verse is only belief with their mouths, since He means the hypocrites, for it is a description of those who believed with their mouths while their hearts did not believe; then He mentioned the Jews and the Christians and said: whoever of them believes in Allah has such-and-such, making them Jews and Christians; and had they been believers, it would not have been necessary to say «مَنْ آمنَ فلهم أجرهم»." I say: this is according to one of the two views, I mean that «الذين آمنوا» are believers in hypocrisy. Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib rejected it by another point, namely the absence of emphasis on the pronoun that is conjoined-to. I say: this does not bind al-Kisāʾī, because his school does not make that a condition, though the sound view is the condition; yes, it binds al-Kisāʾī in that he held a view that the sound proofs reject, and Allah knows best.
This view was reported by Makkī from al-Farrāʾ, as others reported it from al-Kisāʾī, and he rejected it by what has preceded; so it may be that al-Farrāʾ used to agree with al-Kisāʾī and then withdrew, or that he disagreed with him and then returned to him; and in sum two views are possible in the question.
The fourth possibility: that it is nominative by coordination to the position of the noun of «إنَّ», because before its entry it was nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and when it entered upon it, it did not change its meaning but emphasised it; the most that can be said is that it acted in it verbally, and for that reason it and «أنَّ» were singled out for the fatḥa [Translator's note: the source text reads «بالتفح», which appears corrupt; «بالفتح» is presumed], "but according to a view, with that and not with the rest of its sisters" [Translator's note: the sentence is garbled in the source], because the meaning of inceptiveness remains in it, unlike layta, laʿalla and kaʾanna, for these passed to wishing, hoping and comparison. al-Farrāʾ ran the chapter as one, and permitted that in layta and laʿalla, and cited:
177 - 3- يا ليتني وأنتِ يا لميسُ ... في بلدٍ بها أنيسُ
(O would that I and you, Lumays, were in a land where there is company.)
He brought «أنت», a nominative pronoun, in coordination to the yāʾ in «ليتني». Do appositives other than conjunction run in the same course in that? al-Farrāʾ and Yūnus held that it is permissible, and made of it His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بالحق عَلاَّمُ الغيوب} [Sabaʾ: 48], where the nominative of «عَلاَّم» in their view is as an adjective of «ربي» by position; and they reported «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون». Sībawayh declared mistaken whoever of the Arabs said «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون», for he said: "Know that some of the Arabs err, saying «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون»". People took him to task for that, in that he declared mistaken the people of the language, who are the originators or the receivers from the originator; and it was answered that they are mistaken in relation to the generality of the Arabs. In sum, people have rejected this school, I mean the permissibility of the nominative by conjunction to the position of the noun of «إنَّ» absolutely, I mean before the khabar and after it, whether the case-ending of the noun is hidden or apparent. Some reported consensus on the permissibility of the nominative by position after the khabar, and it is nothing. In sum there are four schools in the question: the school of the verifiers: prohibition absolutely; the school of some: a distinction, so that before the khabar it is barred and after it is permissible; the school of al-Farrāʾ: if the case-ending of the noun is hidden, that is permissible because of the removal of the verbal dislike, and it was reported from their speech: «إنك وزيد ذاهبان»; the fourth, the school of al-Kisāʾī: permissibility absolutely, and he cites the apparent senses of His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ والذين هَادُواْ} the verse, and the saying of Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī:
177 - 4- فَمَنْ يَكُ أمسى بالمدينةِ رحلُه ... فإني وقَيَّارٌ بها لغريبُ
(Whoever's baggage has come to rest in Medina, I and Qayyār here are strangers.)
and his saying:
177 - 5- يا ليتنا وهما نَخْلُو بمنزلةٍ ... حتى يَرى بعضُنا بعضاً ونَأْتَلِفُ
(O would that we and they two were alone at a station, until some of us saw others and we became reconciled.)
and his saying:
177 - 6- وإلاَّ فاعلموا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... ... ... ...
(Otherwise know that we and you ...)
the verse, and his saying:
177 - 7- يا ليتني وأنتِ يا لميسُ
(O would that I and you, Lumays...)
and their saying «إنك وزيدٌ ذاهبان». All of these may serve as evidence for al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ together; and al-Kisāʾī should adduce evidence for the permissibility of that with the case-ending of the noun apparent, such as «إنَّ زيداً وعمروٌ قائمان». al-Zamakhsharī rejected the nominative by position, saying: "If you say: why do you not claim that its nominative is by conjunction to the position of «إنَّ» and its noun? I say: that is not valid before the khabar is completed; you do not say «إنَّ زيداً وعمرو منطلقان». If you say: why is it not valid, when the intention is to postpone it, as if you said «إنَّ زيداً منطلق وعمرو»? I say: because when I make it nominative I make it nominative on the position of «إنَّ» and its noun, and the governor in their position is inceptiveness, so it must be the governor in the khabar, since inceptiveness comprises the two parts in its operation, just as «إنَّ» comprises them in its operation; so if you made «الصابئون», with the intention of postponement, nominative by inceptiveness while you had made the khabar nominative by «إنَّ», you would have applied two different nominative-governors to them." What he rejected with is clear, except that his speech suggests that he permits that after the khabar is completed, and it has preceded that some reported consensus on its permissibility.
The fifth: al-Wāḥidī said: "In the verse there is a fourth view, of Hishām b. Muʿāwiya: that the khabar of «إنَّ» is implied and «الصابئون» is begun anew, the implied form being «إنَّ الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا يُرْحَمُون» ('will be shown mercy') on the view of those who say they are Muslims, and «يُعَذَّبون» ('will be punished') on the view of those who say they are disbelievers; so the khabar is omitted since its place is known, as it is omitted from His saying: {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بالذكر} [Fuṣṣilat: 41], i.e. «يُعاقَبون» ('will be punished')." Then al-Wāḥidī said: "This view is close to the view of the Basrans, except that they imply the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and make «مَنْ آمن» the khabar of «إنَّ», whereas this is the reverse of that, for he made «مَنْ آمَن» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and omitted the khabar of «إنَّ»." I say: it is as he said, and I drew attention to that in my first statement that some of them imply the omission from the first and some reverse it.
The sixth: that «الصابئون» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, like the school of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, except that postponement is not intended for this mubtadaʾ; so the difference between it and the school of Sībawayh is the intention of postponement and its absence. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also weak, because of the necessity of omission and separation in it", i.e. because of what is entailed in combining omission and separation; and he does not mean by that that the place is among the places of necessary omission, since the Qurʾān must be recited as it was sent down, even if that place in other than it permits mention and omission.
The seventh: that «الصابئون» is accusative, and it came only in the dialect of Banū l-Ḥārith and others who make the dual with alif in every case, as in «رأيت الزيدان ومررت بالزيدان»; Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib and Abū l-Baqāʾ reported that. It is as if the doubt of this speaker, weak as it is, is that he saw the alif as the sign of the nominative of the dual, and in this dialect it is made to serve for nominative, accusative and genitive; and likewise the wāw is the sign of the nominative of the sound plural, so it remains in the accusative and genitive as the alif remained; and this is weak, indeed corrupt.
The eighth: that the sign of the accusative in «الصابئون» is the fatḥa of the nūn, the nūn being the letter of declension, as it is in «الزيتون» and «عربون». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it is said: Abū ʿAlī permitted that only with the yāʾ and not with the wāw, it is said: others have permitted it, and analogy does not repel it." I say: he alludes to a question, namely that al-Fārisī permitted, in some sound plurals, which are those that run in the course of broken plurals, like banīn and sinīn, that the case-ending alight on their nūn, on the condition that that be with the yāʾ specifically and not the wāw, so that «جاء البنينُ» is said. He said:
177 - 8- وكان لنا أبو حسن عليٌّ ... أباً بَرّاً ونحنُ له بنينُ
(And Abū Ḥasan ʿAlī was for us a dutiful father, and we are his sons.)
and in the ḥadīth: «اللهم اجْعَلْها عليهم سنيناً كسنينِ يوسف» ("O Allah, make them years like the years of Yūsuf"). And he said:
177 - 9- دعانيَ مِنْ نجدٍ فإنَّ سنينَه ... لَعِبْنَ بنا شِيباً وشَيَّبْنَنا مُرْدَا
(Leave me alone from Najd, for its years played with us when grey and turned us grey when beardless.)
So he retained the nūn in annexation. When this reading came and was explained by the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa of the nūn, and the one famous for this view is only al-Fārisī, Abū l-Baqāʾ asked this question and answered that others permit it even with the wāw, and made out that analogy does not refuse it. I say: analogy does refuse it, and the difference between it when it is with the yāʾ and when it is with the wāw is evident, which I have verified in my Sharḥ al-Tashīl. Yes, if it is used as a name, being a sound masculine plural, five possibilities are permitted in it, the first of which is that it be declined by vowels with the wāw and become the like of «الَّذُوْن», so that it is said «جاء الزيدون ورأيت الزيدون ومررت بالزيدون», like «جاء الذون ورأيت الذون ومررت بالذون»; this is when it is used as a name; but as long as it is a plural I do not know of what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned; and whoever affirms is a proof against whoever denies, especially with his precedence in knowledge and time.
The ninth: Makkī said: "«الصابئون» was made nominative only because «إنَّ» showed no effect in «الذين», so the conjoined word remained in its original nominative before the entry of «إنَّ» upon the sentence." I say: this is exactly the school of al-Farrāʾ, I mean that he permits conjunction to the position of the noun of «إنَّ» when no case-ending shows in it, except that the wording of Makkī does not apparently agree with this.
Ubayy b. Kaʿb, ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān, ʿĀʾisha, al-Jaḥdarī, Saʿīd b. Jubayr and a group read «والصابئين» with the yāʾ, and the author of al-Kashshāf reported it from Ibn Kathīr, but that is not well known from him. This reading is clear in derivation, by conjunction to the form of the noun of «إنَّ», and although it contradicts the script of the codex, it is a slight contradiction and has parallels, such as the reading of Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr of {سراط} and its kind with sīn, and like the reading of Ḥamza in one transmission of it with zāy, while it is written with ṣād in the rest of the codices, and like the reading of all of {إيلافهم} with yāʾ, while the writing is without it in all of them.
al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Zuhrī read {والصابِيُون} with kasra on the bāʾ followed by a pure yāʾ, which is a lightening of the hamza, like the reading of those who read {يَسْتهزِيُون} with a pure yāʾ, and Nāfiʿ's reading has preceded in al-Baqara. As for «النصارى», it is accusative by conjunction to the form of the noun of «إنَّ», and there is no need to claim that it is nominative by what made «الصابئون» nominative, because of the difficulty of that.
His saying, the Exalted: {مَنْ آمَنَ}: two possibilities for «مَنْ». One: that it is conditional, and His saying «فلا خوفٌ» to its end is the apodosis, and on this «آمن» is in the position of the jussive by the condition and «فلا خوف» in the position of the jussive as its apodosis, the fāʾ being necessary. The second: that it is a relative and the khabar is «فلا خوف», the fāʾ having entered because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to the condition; «آمَنَ» on this has no position because it occurs as ṣila, and «فلا خوفٌ» is in the position of the nominative because it occurs as khabar, and the entry of the fāʾ would be permissible if it were in other than the Qurʾān. On these two possibilities the position of «مَنْ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; and on its being a relative it may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal from the noun of «إنَّ» and what is conjoined to it, or a badal from the conjoined word only; and this depends on the disagreement about «الذين آمنوا»: are the real believers meant by them, or believers in hypocrisy? On each of the preceding suppositions the returning element from this clause to «مَنْ» is omitted, its implied form being «مَنْ آمَنَ منهم», as He stated explicitly in another place; and the i'rab of the rest of the clause has already preceded.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كُلَّمَا جَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ}: the discussion of «كلما» has already preceded at length, which makes repetition unnecessary. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«كلما جاءهم رسول» is a conditional clause that occurs as an adjective of «رسلاً», and the returning element is omitted, i.e. «رسول منهم»." Then he said: "If you say: where is the apodosis of the condition? For His saying {فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُواْ وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ} cannot stand in for the apodosis, because a single messenger cannot be two groups, and because it is not good to say «إن أكرمت أخي أخاك أكرمت»? I say: it is omitted, indicated by His saying {فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُواْ وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ}, as if it were said: 'whenever a messenger came to them they opposed him'; and His saying {فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُواْ} is a resumptive answer to one who says: how did they treat their messengers?" The Shaykh said: "«كلما» is not a condition; rather «كلَّ» is accusative as an adverbial and «ما» is a maṣdar adverbial; and the Arabs do not use the jussive with «كلما» at all. And even granting that «كلما» is a condition, what he mentioned is no obstacle. As for the first, the «رسول» meant is the genus and not one particular person, so its division into two groups is valid, as in «لا أصحبك ما طَلَعَ نجمٌ», meaning the genus of stars; and as for the second, he means that advancing the object of the apodosis before it is not permitted; and what he forbade was forbidden only by al-Farrāʾ alone, while others permitted it; and this is granting that «كلما» is a condition; but if we proceed on the basis that it is adverbial, there is no need to excuse that, and advancing the object of the verb governing in «كلما» is not barred; you say «كلما جئتني أخاك أكرمتُ»." I say: this is clear from the fact that it is not a condition, and this wording is frequent in the wording of the jurists rather than the grammarians. In the wording of Abū l-Baqāʾ there is what suggests what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "«وكَذَّبوا» is the apodosis of «كلما»; «فريقاً» is an object of «كَذَّبوا», and «فريقاً» is accusative by «يقتلون»; he advanced the object of «يقتلون» only for the harmony of the verse endings, and advanced the object of «كَذَّبوا» to suit what follows."
al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was one of the two verbs brought in the past and the other in the imperfect? I say: «يقتلون» was brought as a rendering of the past state, regarding the killing as monstrous, and bringing that hideous state to mind out of wonder at it." End. It may be said: why was the state of denial not also rendered, so that the verb would come in the imperfect for that? It is answered that the monstrousness of the killing and its hideousness is greater than the monstrousness of denial; also, once it was brought in the imperfect, it suited the verse endings.

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رِجْسٌ}: a khabar about these things mentioned before. It is asked: how can a singular be predicated of a plural? Al-Zamakhsharī answered that it rests on an omitted muḍāf, that is: "the matter of wine and such-and-such"; he mentioned that when he dealt with the pronoun in «فاجتنبوه», as will come. Abū l-Baqāʾ likewise implied it, saying: "because the implied form is: «the doing of these things»." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said, after relating al-Zamakhsharī's words: "There is no need for this; rather the judgement that these four themselves are an abomination is more eloquent than implying this muḍāf, as in {إِنَّمَا المشركون نَجَسٌ} [al-Tawba: 28]." It is a fine statement. Abū l-Baqāʾ also answered that «رجس» may be the khabar of «الخمر», and the khabar of the conjoined items is omitted because the khabar of the first indicates them. I say: on this, it may also be a khabar of the last, with the khabar of what precedes it omitted because the khabar of what follows it indicates it; for we have in such as His saying, the Exalted, {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62] both of these implications, and their verification has been given more than once.
«الأنصاب» is the plural of «naṣb», mentioned at the beginning of the sūra, and «الأزلام» was also mentioned. As for «al-rijs», al-Rāghib said: "It is the filthy thing; a man is «rijs», men are «arjās»." Then he said: "It was also said: «rijs» and «rijz» are for a violent sound; one says «baʿīr rajjās» for a camel of violent roaring, and «ghamām rājis» and «rajjās» for a cloud of violent thunder." Al-Zajjāj said: "It is a name for every detestable, ugly deed. One says «rajisa» and «rajasa», with kasra and with fatḥa on the jīm, «yarjusu rijsan» when he did an ugly deed; and the best of it [Translator's note: the source reads «وأصلح من الرِّجْس», which appears corrupt; rendered as it stands] is from «al-rajs» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, which is the intensity of the sound of thunder. He said:
180 - 9- وكلُّ رَجَّاسٍ يسوقُ الرَّجْسا ...
(And every roaring one drives the thunder ...)
Ibn Durayd distinguished between «rijs», «rijz» and «rikṣ», making «rijs» evil, «rijz» punishment, and «rikṣ» filth and stench; then he said: «rijs» is said of the two." It results from this that it is a name for the filthy, stinking thing, or that in origin it is a maṣdar.
His saying: {مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشيطان} is in the position of nominative because it is an adjective of «رجس»; and the hāʾ in «فاجتنبوه» refers to the «rijs», that is: "so avoid the abomination which He reported of what preceded, wine and what follows it." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It refers to the act", meaning the one he implied as muḍāf to wine and what follows it, and al-Zamakhsharī tended to this too, saying: "If you say: to what does the pronoun in «فاجتنبوه» refer? I say: to the omitted muḍāf, or the practising of the two, or the like; therefore He said {رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشيطان}." It was mentioned earlier that the better view is that these things were made the very abomination, for intensification.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الخمر}: four aspects. The first: it is attached to «يوقع», that is: "He causes these two things between you in the matter of wine", that is, because of drinking it; «في» conveys causality, as in his saying, peace be upon him, "A woman entered the Fire because of a cat" (fī hirratin). The second: it is attached to «البغضاء» because it is a maṣdar defined by «al». The third: it is attached to «العَداوة». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«في» may be attached to «العداوة» or to «البغضاء», that is: that you be hostile and hate one another because of drinking wine." On what he mentioned, the matter is one of competition (tanāzuʿ), which is the fourth aspect, except that there is a difficulty in that, namely that the two competing words should each be fit to govern; and this first governor, «العداوة», if it were made to govern the disputed item, would require separation between the maṣdar and its object by an outsider, namely the conjoined term. It may be said that in some forms of tanāzuʿ the governing by the second is obligatory, and that is in the two verbs of wonder when they compete for an object, and this has been treated fully in al-Baqara.
His saying: {فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُّنتَهُونَ}: this interrogative has the meaning of a command, that is: "desist". Therefore when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb understood the imperative sense he said: "We have desisted, O Lord, we have desisted, O Lord." This is also indicated by the explicit imperative being joined to it in His saying «وأطيعوا», as if it were said: "Desist from drinking wine and from such-and-such, and obey". So the coming of this interrogative clause, headed by a noun about which an active participle is predicated, indicating the firmness and settledness of the prohibition, is more eloquent than an explicit command. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why were wine and maysir combined with the anṣāb and azlām at first, and then the two were mentioned alone at the end? I say: because the address is to the believers, and He forbade them only what they were practising of drinking wine and playing maysir, and the mention of the anṣāb and azlām is to reinforce the prohibition of wine and maysir and to show that all of that is of the deeds of the people of the Jāhiliyya and the people of polytheism." End of quotation. Something else appears, namely that He did not single out wine and maysir for mention at the end, but mentioned with them something that entails the absence of the anṣāb and azlām, as though He had mentioned all of them at the end. Its explanation is that He said: "in wine and maysir, and it turns you away from the remembrance of Allah", by worshipping the anṣāb or by slaughtering upon them for the idols, according to the interpretation given at the beginning of the sūra, "and from prayer", by your preoccupation with the azlām, whose interpretation was also mentioned. So the remembrance of Allah and the prayer both point to the anṣāb and azlām, and this is a fine aspect.

semin-durr:93-93.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا مَا اتقوا}: an adverb of time, governed by what is understood from the preceding clause, which is «ليس» and what is within its scope; the implied form: "they are not sinful and are not held to account at the time of their piety". It may be a pure adverb, or it may have the sense of a condition, its answer being omitted or having preceded, as mentioned.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ}: the answer of an omitted oath, that is: "By Allah, He will surely test you"; it was mentioned earlier that the lām and one of the two nūns are obligatory in such an answer. His saying {بِشَيْءٍ} is attached to «ليبلونَّكم», that is, "He will surely try you with something". His saying {مِّنَ الصيد} is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «شيء», so it is attached to an omitted element. «مِنْ» is apparently partitive, because He did not forbid the game of those not in iḥrām, nor the game of the non-sacred area, nor the game of the sea. It was said: it is to explain the kind. Makkī said: "It was said that «مِنْ» is to explain the kind: when He said «بشيء» it was not known of what kind it is, so He explained and said «من الصيد», as you say «la-uʿṭiyannaka shayʾan min al-dhahab» (I shall surely give you something of gold)." Abū L-Baqāʾ began with this aspect, then said: "It was also said that it is partitive." Its being explicative is open to consideration, because the correct view is that it is not explicative, and the one who says it is explicative stipulates that the item explained by it be defined by the generic «al», as in {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان} [al-Ḥajj: 30]; so said Ibn ʿAṭiyya too, and al-Zajjāj is the source of it, for he said: "This is as you say: «la-amtaḥinannaka bi-shayʾin min al-rizq» (I shall surely test you with something of provision), and as the Exalted said {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان}."
His saying: {تَنَالُهُ} is in the position of genitive because it is a second adjective of «شيء». Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted that it be a ḥāl, either from «الصيد» or from «شيء», although it is indefinite, because it was described and so became specific. The Shaykh considered it remote that it be a ḥāl from «الصيد», the ground of the remoteness being that it is not the one about which the discourse is. The majority read {تناله} with the dotted-above letter (tāʾ) for the feminine of the plural, and Ibn Wathāb and al-Nakhaʿī with the dotted-below letter (yāʾ), because its femininity is not real. As for His saying {ثُمَّ اتَّقَواْ وَآمَنُواْ ثُمَّ اتَّقَواْ} [al-Māʾida: 93], people have two views on it. One: it is a case of emphasis, and the conjunction does no harm in that, as in His saying, the Exalted, {كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ} [al-Takāthur: 3-4], so much so that Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik makes this verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī), which has a chapter in grammar. The second: it is not for emphasis but for founding something new (taʾsīs), except that he made the difference arise by implying the attached elements; among them that the implied form is: "they feared Allah, avoiding polytheism, and believed with complete faith, then feared Allah and believed", that is, "then they held firm to the earlier piety and faith and continued in this state, then feared Allah, then reached the utmost in piety and went deep into it, did good to people and shared with them from their wealth." Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī tended to this in words close to this meaning.
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَعْلَمَ الله}: the lām is attached to «لَيبلونَّكم», and the meaning is "that it may be distinguished" or "that it may appear to you"; its verification was given in al-Baqara, and this is called the lām of «kay» (purpose). Some read «لِيُعْلِم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, from «aʿlama»; on this reading the first object is omitted, i.e. "that Allah may make His servants know", and the second object is His saying {مَن يَخَافُهُ}, so «aʿlama» is transferred by the hamza of transitivization from «ʿalima», which is transitive to one object in the sense of «ʿarafa». His saying {بالغيب} is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «يَخافُه», that is: "fears Him in association with the unseen"; its meaning was given in al-Baqara.
Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted three aspects in it. One: what I mentioned. The second: it is a ḥāl from «مَنْ» in «من يخافه». The third: the bāʾ has the meaning of «في», and «الغيب» is a maṣdar standing in the place of «ghāʾib» (absent), that is: "fears Him in the place hidden from creation"; on this it is attached to the very verb before it, whereas on the first two it is attached to an omitted element, as is known.
